items.statement: NTPC plans to award 13.6 GW of thermal capacity by FY27, in addition to 11.16 GW already under construction.
items.quote: We are actively considering awarding thermal capacity to the tune of 13.6 GW by the financial year 2026-27. This is in addition to 11.16 GW thermal capacity already under construction.

items.statement: Renewable capacity addition guidance: 3 GW in FY25, 5 GW in FY26, 8 GW in FY27, reaching 19.4 GW operational by FY27.
items.quote: The current year, the capacity addition expected is 3 GW. Next year, it will be 5 GW. And the year next, it will be 8 GW. So, by FY27 operational capacity will be 19.4

items.statement: Group capex incurred in H1 FY25 was INR 17,474 crores vs INR 13,204 crores in H1 FY24; stand-alone capex was INR 14,040 crores vs INR 7,959 crores.
items.quote: In H1 FY 25, we have incurred a group capex of INR 17,474 crores as compared to INR 13,204 crores in the corresponding previous period. While on a stand-alone basis, NTPC has incurred a capex of INR 14,040 crores as compared to INR 7,959 crores in the corresponding previous period.

items.statement: Thermal PLF declining due to rising renewable generation; thermal plants will play subservient role to renewables during daytime.
items.quote: PLF has a bearing on what is the demand rather than …. it's no longer an efficiency parameter. It is more to do with what is the system demand. And with more renewables coming into the space, increasingly, the thermal energy may find a lesser PLF because it will be playing a role of subservient to the renewable energy during the daytime.

items.statement: FGD policy changes are a national-level decision; NTPC is fully hedged under cost-plus regulation and remains unaffected.
items.quote: Even if it is introduced, altered, withdrawn, as far as the company is concerned, it operates on a cost-plus principles, and we are completely hedged against this kind of a situation. So, this is a completely national-level policy decisions, and the company per se remains unaffected because we are entirely into a cost-plus business.

items.statement: NTPC Green Energy IPO process proceeding as planned; hoped to conclude by Q3 FY25, no valuation decided yet.
items.quote: we are still in the process, and we are hopeful that we will be going ahead as per our plan

items.statement: Nuclear: Mahi Banswara (4x700 MW) first concrete pour expected March 2026, first unit criticality FY31-32, all four units by FY32.
items.quote: Our Mahi Banswara's first milestone, first pour of concrete is expected in March 2026. Our first unit would approach to criticality in financial year 2031-32. All the 4 units will be commissioned by FY32.

items.statement: Pump storage hydro: 1 GW already under execution, 2.8 GW ordered from Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra, 4.2 GW in pipeline, targeting ~8 GW at NGEL.
items.quote: Already, 1 GW PSP, our subsidiary is doing. And 2.8 GW, from Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra, we have got the order for going ahead. Another 4.2 GW is in the pipeline. So expected is around 8 GW PSP, we'll be able to get at NGEL.

items.statement: Stand-alone PAT Q2 FY25 INR 4,649 crores (+19.66% YoY); H1 FY25 PAT INR 9,160 crores (+15.2% YoY).
items.quote: NTPC's profit after tax for Q2 FY25 is INR 4,649 crores as against INR 3,885 crores in the corresponding quarter of previous year, registering an increase of 19.66%. On a half yearly basis, PAT is INR 9,160 crores as against INR 7,951 crores in H1 FY24, registering an increase of 15.2%.

items.statement: Average coal price fell 5.46% YoY to INR 3,584/ton in Q2 FY25; revenue declined only 0.66% due to cost pass-through.
items.quote: The average price of coal was INR 3,791 per ton in the last year. Now it is INR 3,584, thereby a reduction of INR 207 per ton with a reduction of 5.46%. Compared to this, the revenue reduction is only 0.66%.

items.statement: Coal production target raised from 40 MMT in FY25 to ~67 MMT by FY29 for fuel security.
items.quote: It is planned to enhance estimated NTPC Group coal production from 40 million metric ton in FY25 to about 67 million metric tons up to FY29.

items.statement: Regulated equity: stand-alone INR 89,430 crores (+7.67% YoY), consolidated INR 105,049 crores (+5.5% YoY) as of Sep 2024.
items.quote: Stand-alone regulatory equity for Power and Mining business as on 30th September 2024 was INR 89,430 crores, which was INR 83,059 crores in the previous year, registering a growth of 7.67%. On a consolidated basis, the consolidated regulated equity as on 30th September 2024 was INR 105,049 crores, which is 5.5% over last year's figure of INR 99,611 crores.

items.statement: First interim dividend declared at INR 2.50 per share for FY25.
items.quote: The Board has declared the first interim dividend of INR 2.50 per share for the financial year 2024-25.

items.statement: Tehri PSP (1,000 MW) expected to commission all four units by December 2024.
items.quote: These projects are expected to commission in this quarter, by December, all the four units.

items.statement: Wind installations expected around 5 GW for FY25, 6-7 GW for FY26, and 9-10 GW yearly thereafter
items.quote: Our expectation is that wind installations will be around 5 GW for this financial year FY'25, 6-7 GW for FY'26 and then increase to anywhere between 9-10 GW yearly.

items.statement: Order book exceeds 5 GW at 5.1 GW, all firm orders with financial commitments, executable in 18-24 months
items.quote: With the largest ever order book of 5.1 GW, we now have clear visibility of the orders that need to be tentatively executed over the next 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity being ramped from 3.1 GW to 4.5 GW across tower, blade, and nacelle by end of FY25
items.quote: currently it’s about 3.1 GW which we have now ramped up to about 4.5 GW across all components of tower, blade and nacelle. So, that’s what our manufacturing capacity on a per annum basis wou ld be

items.statement: WTG gross margin in mid-to-late teens, OMS gross margin about 65%, WTG EBITDA margin ~7% expected to increase, OMS EBITDA margin ~40% to maintain trajectory
items.quote: we continue to maintain t hat the WTG gross margin will be in the mid-to-late teens, whereas the OMS business gross margin will be about 65

items.statement: India's renewable energy journey just starting with robust power demand from industrialization, urbanization, e-mobility
items.quote: We believe India's renewable energy journey is just starting with power demand to remain robust on account of t, industrialization, urbanization, E-mobility, etc.

items.statement: Order book 75% from C&I and public sector, only ~24% from large PPAs, reducing dependence on grid PPAs
items.quote: if you look at our mix of orders, which we have given in our presentation, that 75% of our order book is from C&I and public sector, only about 24% or so is from the big PPAs.

items.statement: Competition intensifying with more players entering, but company prepared and will not compromise margins
items.quote: competition has always been there and would continue to be there. We are absolutely conscious about that, and we know that we need to be completely prepared and constantly keep sharpening our model, reducing our cost, but I can repeat that we will not compromise on our margins when we take our orders

items.statement: Renom acquisition consolidated for 25 days in Q2, added ~2.9 GW fleet across wind, BoP, and solar segments
items.quote: The acquisition of Renom has added significantly to our fleet s trength of close to 2.9 GW across wind, BoP and solar segments

items.statement: Corporate office and non-core assets monetized for 440 crores
items.quote: Additionally, we successfully monetize our corporate office and non-core assets for 440 crores.

items.statement: One Earth sale-leaseback results in ~4 crores monthly P&L charge, subleasing efforts underway to reduce this
items.quote: When we divested O ne Earth sale and leaseback transaction, we confirm that there will be an approximate 4 cro res per month charge on account of the One Earth transaction in the P&L

items.statement: ESOP non-cash charge of 32 crores in Q2, will continue till FY26
items.quote: Rise in employee costs is also attributable to non-cash provisi ons of about 32 crores on account of ESOPs that were granted to employees

items.statement: NTPC 1.166 GW order supply contract to complete within 17 months from NTP, supplies starting end of Q3, mainly from Q4
items.quote: NTPC order, there are differe nt contracts, supply contract is expected to be completed within I think 17 months from the NTP. NTP has already started. Actual supplie s would commence probably by Suzlon Energy Limited October 28, 2024 end of this quarter but signifi cantly mainly starts from Q4

items.statement: Pondicherry plant already started production, ramping up; Daman capacity also increasing significantly
items.quote: Pondicherry we already started production there. As Himanshu mentioned for the previous question that we will reach gradually from now onwards to 4.5 GW before this year ends in all segments, whether it is tower or blade or the nacelle.

items.statement: SE Forge expanding into non-wind sectors (defence, railways) and exports, orders expected to materialize in 4-5 months
items.quote: We already received a few orders which will materialize into revenue maybe in next four t o five months because in SE Forge what happens is whenever the order comes, you develop that mode l, it takes time before we start producing

items.statement: Next turbine model on drawing board, will launch at right time when current model saturates
items.quote: On the Turbine make, ye s, today is just 144 is what is significantly being produced. But as I mentioned in the previous calls that the wind turbine business is the movement, roll out one model, next model is already on t he drawing board

items.statement: Balance sheet cleanup approved by board to remove legacy reserves and negative items, process to take 6-7 months
items.quote: As part of the board release today, you would have seen that We are looking at reorganizing the balance sheet. There are quite a few legacy Suzlon Energy Limited October 28, 2024 reserves and negative items that are there in the balance sheet . The board has approved the cleanup of that

items.statement: Management does not provide specific financial guidance; suggests using six-to-nine-month trends for modeling
items.quote: we don't give a guidance. The H1 numbers are up and you take more than three months rather than taking a quarter. Go for a longer tenure, six or nine months. It can give you a sense on directionally how it is going.

items.statement: Bond issuances picked up strongly in Q2 FY25; H2 expected to be quite good with tailwinds from infrastructure spend and rural consumption
items.quote: We have seen bond issuances pick up very well in Q2. We do expect that H2 bond issuances will be quite good. It also is a function of many factors, including how the economy grows, the governments spend on infrastructure, a pickup in rural consumption since we have had good monsoons.

items.statement: Margins expected to improve quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year in absolute terms; ratings margin trajectory to continue via process and technology improvements
items.quote: But that said, in absolute terms, I mean, we expect the margins to keep improving, quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year.

items.statement: Pricing strategy maintained at reasonable levels with focus on growth segments; competitive intensity higher in commoditized bank loan ratings, lower in bond issuances where flight to quality prevails
items.quote: Pricing is a function of many things. Bond issuances, usually, in the market, they tend to prefer the better rating agencies and we are one of those. So it does help us. And then again, when we look at the growth segments, one has usually seen that growth segment, the pricing is better.

items.statement: Non-ratings focus is product and advisory-led in risk management (Model Risk, EWS, ECL, Climate Risk); ESG ratings launched on issuer-pays model; D2K acquisition strengthening risk offerings
items.quote: our focus will be product and advisory led not so much actually consulting. The product that we will be concentrating on will be products which are linked or allied to risk management, which is where our, expertise lies.

items.statement: Knowledge services face automation risk but offset by moving up value chain and adding new projects; near-term growth moderated after rapid expansion
items.quote: Now, what essentially the way this industry plays out, eventually you will lose some of the projects due to automation but as an entity or as an organization, we will also keep on moving on the value chain and keep on building capabilities in other segments.

items.statement: Technology spends increasing and will continue; compensation benchmarking was a one-time spike now normalized
items.quote: As far as technology is concerned, we have been looking at technology quite closely over the last couple of years. And our spends in technology, have been increasing and that will continue to be the case.

items.statement: Capital allocation reviewed periodically with board; dividend payouts increased in recent years; endeavor to maximize shareholder returns
items.quote: We evaluate capital allocation on a periodic basis and have discussions with our board. And you would have seen that, I mean in the last few years, as you rightly said, we have increased the dividend payout and w e continue to evaluate and have a discussion with the board

items.statement: ESG ratings license received end of April; first rating released a month ago; working on a couple of mandates with positive response across segments
items.quote: We have already released one rating which was about a month ago and we are working on a couple of mandates. The response is quite positive. The interest is coming in across segments and we are quite optimistic about this business.

items.statement: GDP growth estimated at 7% for FY25 amid downside risks from commodity prices and geopolitical tensions
items.quote: we estimate India's GDP growth to print at 7%t in financial year 2025 amid downside risks owing to a significant increase in global commodity and crude prices on the back of an escalation in geopolitical tensions in the region.

items.statement: Exploring non-Moody's clients domestically and internationally; brought in sales accelerators and consultants for GTM strategy; expect good movement in next 3-4 quarters
items.quote: we are already here exploring various opportunities with non- Moody clients, both domestically as well as internationally. W e have brought in several sales accelerators and international consultants who are helping us with the GTM strategy to expand our services

items.statement: No regulatory restrictions on Indian rating agencies operating abroad; current focus remains primarily on India for ratings business
items.quote: I don't believe there are any regulatory restrictions. As we did have a subsidiary in Lanka till very recently, which we have, which business we have wound up. We have presently an operation in Nepal.

items.statement: D2K acquisition completed end of last calendar year; full-year revenue roughly INR 19-20 crores; not yet 100% subsidiary, integration ongoing
items.quote: since we do not disclose that separately, we will not be able to share that to ensure that we maintain parity of information across all stakeholders. But you can get the last year's number from the website and it is roughly around INR19 crores or INR20 crores full year

items.statement: Market share stable in chosen segments; selective approach avoids very small entities; focus on segments where fee-paying ability is above threshold
items.quote: Our market share is quite stable. As we have been mentioning in the previous calls and various commentaries, which we have put out. We are very selective in a sense that we look at that segment where the pricing or where the fees, the ability of the company to pay the fees is above a certain threshold.

items.statement: MSME credit ratings under evaluation; no plans yet; need to understand scale and traction
items.quote: We just we are evaluating we need to see whether -- we need to understand the scale that it might entail and for that matter what -- how much traction it will have. So we are in the process of evaluating but we don't have any plans yet.

items.statement: Targeting 10% to 15% revenue growth for FY25 on consolidated basis with EBITDA margin around 12%
items.quote: So, basically just to sum it sir, 10% to 15% revenue growth for FY'25 on a consolidated basis with EBITDA margin of around 12%? Keyur Gajjar: That's what we are targeting.

items.statement: Expect MDF margin of 13% to 14% to be maintained for FY25
items.quote: We would like to just maintain that overall MDF margin which we are thinking so whatever we have achieved as of now 13% to 14% which we will maintain for this financial year.

items.statement: Laminate margins expected to improve next financial year due to Jumbo laminate project with 14% to 16% margins
items.quote: Now, after having this new project into place, the overall margin will definitely improve because the Jumbo product has a margin in the range of 14% to 16%, and the way we are planning next financial year will definitely have a sizable turnover in terms of this particular product.

items.statement: Jumbo Laminate project in Gandhinagar on track for operations by end of Q4 2025, adding 2.8 million sheets annually
items.quote: The Jumbo Laminate project in Gandhinagar, although delayed due to machinery supply issues and unexpected rainfall, is now on track for operations by the end of Q4 2025. This facility will contribute an additional 2.8 million sheets annually.

items.statement: Plywood plant CAPEX of INR 40-42 crores total, company share INR 20-21 crores to be funded internally
items.value: INR 40-42 crores total; INR 20-21 crores company share
items.quote: Second, in terms of ply, the total CAPEX value even next year is around INR 40 to 42 crores, out of which our share would be INR 20 to 21 crores, which we will I think plan internally only.

items.statement: Implemented MDF price hike of 2% to 7% product-to-product last Saturday, average benefit ~3%
items.quote: Yes, in the current quarter, last Saturday, we have already given a price h ike of around 2% to 7% depending on product-to-product

items.statement: Considering second round of MDF price hike, first hike to implement in November, second as early as possible
items.quote: At Rushil, we really want to implement it faster. So, first hike probably will implement in November, and we'll take the second hike as early as possible.

items.statement: Timber prices increased 2-3% in Q2 vs Q1 for South market; expected to remain in this range for next two years
items.quote: Roughly at this point of time if we calculate out in October, it's around 2 to 3% range.

items.statement: MDF industry growing at ~20% CAGR; company H1 volume 1.47 lakh CBM vs 1.19 lakh CBM in H1 FY23
items.quote: So, we see good demand like if we compare our H1 'FY23, it was like 1.19 lakh CBM and this half year we are almost 1.47 lakh. So, we see quite good growth and industry itself is growing at around 20% CAGR.

items.statement: Value-added MDF products accounted for 54% of MDF division revenue in Q2; targeting 50% of AP plant capacity
items.quote: Notably, value added MDF products accounted for 54% of division's revenue, reinforcing our focus on high margin segment.

items.statement: Chikmagalur MDF unit scheduled for 10-12 day maintenance shutdown starting Diwali; no significant revenue loss expected due to inventory buildup
items.quote: So, plant will be typically shut down for 10-12 days and this is a general breakdown in which s ome parts which has to be changed due to which the fiber losses and other losses are not made

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity ratio at 0.44; repaid ~INR 170 crores debt over last 2 years including rights issue; expect further reduction of INR 50-55 crores annually
items.quote: If you see last 2 to 3 years overall figure, w e have two things. One , last year as a part of the rights issue, we have reduced debt of around INR 55 crores which was unsecured loan converted into equity, and on a yearly basis, we have been repaying around INR 50 to 55 crores

items.statement: May establish wholly owned subsidiary in Singapore to serve Southeast Asia market
items.quote: Additionally, we may establish a wholly owned subsidiary in Singapore to better serve the Southeast Asia market, a step we anticipate will strengthen our international footprints and drive revenue growth in the region.

items.statement: Implemented currency hedging strategies from this quarter to mitigate FOREX exposure on export revenue
items.quote: To mitigate FOREX exposure, we have implemented currency hedging strategies from this quarter, focusing on maintaining stability in our export revenue despite market fluctuations.

items.statement: Plan to open 55 restaurants in FY25, reaching 510 total; locations identified and most under construction
items.quote: Our plan remains to open 55 restaurants this year, giving us a total of 510 restaurants. At the end of last quarter, we had opened 9 restaurants. And of the remaining 46, locations have been identified and most of these restaurants are already in construction.

items.statement: Medium-term gross margin target of 69% by FY27 remains intact, driven by delivery pricing and supply chain initiatives
items.quote: our medium-term plan of achieving 69% by FY '27 remains intact, and this would be on the back of pricing, especially on the delivery side that Raj spoke about, as well as some of th e supply chain and distribution initiatives that we are taking

items.statement: Targeting cash breakeven at country level in Indonesia on back of new Spicy Chicken launch, marketing plan and cost containment
items.quote: Going forward on the back of the launch of the new Spicy Chicken, the marketing plan as well as some cost-containment measures, we are targeting to reach cash breakeven at a country level.

items.statement: No new capex in Indonesia; all marketing spend funded from local sales; India expansion continues with 55 store openings planned
items.quote: We are not putting any capex in Indonesia. So you'd appreciate that. All the marketing spend over there comes from within the sales that we generate there.

items.statement: India restaurant EBITDA pre-IND AS 116 at 19.8%, up 7.6% YoY and 19.8% QoQ; company EBITDA up 39.4% QoQ to INR24.4 crore
items.quote: EBITDA restaurant level pre -IND AS 116 was 19.8%. Let me repeat that 19.8% higher than quarter-over-quarter. This is a fantastic job that the entire te am has done over here to deliver 19.8% better profitability over the last quarter, 7.6% over year -over-year over last quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin at 67.5%, flat QoQ and up 0.7% YoY; dip attributed to aggressive trial pricing on new snacking launches
items.quote: Gross margin, 67.5%, which is 0.7% better over last year's same quarter and about flat quarter -over-quarter.

items.statement: Delivery pricing actions taken to improve profitability despite traffic impact; value strategy at 2 for INR79/99 and Puff at 2 for INR59 driving dine-in traffic
items.quote: We have taken some pricing there and we are okay with some of the traffic falling there, but the profitability is improving and increasing in our delivery business.

items.statement: India dine-in traffic growing every month; SSSG -3% due to delivery pricing and new store ramp-up; value demand shift observed
items.quote: Dine-in traffic continues to improve, continues to increase. Every single month, we see the dine-in traffic continue to increase.

items.statement: Veg Pizza Puff launched at 2 for INR59 selling 200-300 units/store/day; Chicken Pizza Puff rolling out nationally; Snacking a key daypart
items.quote: At an invitational price point of 2 for INR59, we saw a tremendous response from our guests. And some of our stores, they're selling upwards of 200, 300 puffs per store per day.

items.statement: Indonesia facing geopolitical headwinds, deflation, middle-class shrink, 22% dine-in sales drop; no new stores until business fixed
items.quote: We haven't build any stores. We don't intend to build a new stores until we fix that business over there.

items.statement: Evaluating liquidity position; may need to raise funds for India expansion from 500 to 700 stores over next couple of years
items.quote: Yes, we do believe there will be some amount of liquidity that we might have to add. We are just kind of still internally finalizing the plan in terms of which part we could take.

items.statement: Digital transformation: 320 stores with SOK/QR/table service; 4 drive-thrus with voice ordering; BK App installs up 33% YoY, user base up 2.3x
items.quote: As we speak, over 300 stores are enabled with Self Ordering Kiosks, Table QR Codes, and all our dine -in stores offer table service.

items.statement: Indonesia marketing spend at ~5% of sales per franchise agreement; 360-degree campaign launched for Spicy Chicken BIC
items.quote: We are supposed to, as per our franchise agreement, spe nd 5% of our sales on marketing. It's required, and we are well within that

name: Home First Finance Company India Ltd

items.statement: Target 30% AUM growth for FY25 and next 2-3 years; disbursement run rate of INR 400 cr/month this year, INR 500 cr next year, INR 600 cr year after
items.quote: Our design has been to get to a 30% AUM growth. The design is not for a 30% disbursal growth. With a 20% to 30% disbursal growth, we should be able to achieve a 30% plus AUM growth. The design is that this year, we will clock a run rate of about INR 400 cr per month. Next year, we'll clock about INR 500 cr and the year after about INR 600 cr per month.

items.statement: Credit cost annual guidance 20-30 bps, conservative
items.quote: Our annual guidance for credit cost is around 20 to 30 bps, being conservative here.

items.statement: Opex ratio expected to remain range bound 2.7%-2.8%
items.quote: We e xpect the ope x ratio to remain range bound within 2.7% to 2.8% as we focus on expansion

items.statement: Plan to add 25-30 branches per year
items.quote: Yes. We continue to operate on that format. So about 25 - 30 branches per year.

items.statement: Spreads excluding co-lending expanded 10 bps to 5.3% after Aug repricing; NIM 5.2%
items.quote: Starting with spreads, after repricing in Aug'24, our Spreads, excluding Co-Lending expanded by 10 bps, and it is at 5.3% right now. Net interest margin was 5.2% owing to the leverage effect.

items.statement: PLR hike of 35 bps in Aug'24; 2/3 reflected in Q2, full impact in Q3 (12-13 bps additional)
items.quote: Fully reflected but you can say 2/3 of it has got reflected in this quarter, Q2FY25 because it got effective only from 1st August. A full impact will come in Q3. If we had a 10-basis points impact in Q2, may be in Q3 it will be 12 - 13 bps.

items.statement: No moderation seen in 30% AUM growth target; expansion in MP, UP, Rajasthan driving higher growth
items.quote: No, we don't see a moderation. We want to grow by 30% and all other activities in terms of employee hiring, branch expansion, new location expansion, etc. have been planned on that basis only.

items.statement: Comfortable increasing leverage to 5x D/E; 12-18 months before capital raise needed
items.quote: We think that we can increase it for a fair bit, perhaps closer to 5 x. We have about 12 – 18 months before we need to look at a capital raise.

items.statement: Q2 disbursals INR 1,177 cr (highest ever); AUM INR 11,229 cr (+34.2% YoY)
items.quote: We continue our track record of q-o-q increase in disbursals with our highest ever disbursal of INR 1,177 cr for Q2. The AUM has grown by 34.2% y-o-y to INR 11,229 cr.

items.statement: Added 9 branches in Q2 (total 142); 351 touchpoints across 138 districts, 13 states
items.quote: In Q2, we added nine new branches, two branches in Gujarat, one branch each in Maharashtra, MP, Chhattisgarh, New Delhi, Uttarakhand, UP and Rajasthan bringing the total to 142 branches. With digital and potential branches, we now operate across 351 touch points in 138 districts spread across 13 states and union territories.

items.statement: Capital adequacy 36.4% (Tier 1 36%); D/E 3.9x; net worth INR 2,289 cr; book value INR 257/share
items.quote: Our total capital adequacy is 36.4% with Tier 1 CRAR at 36%. Our debt-to-equity is 3.9x. As of Sept'24, our net worth is INR 2,289 cr. Our book value per share is INR 257 per share.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton guidance of INR15,000 on blended basis; H1 FY25 at INR14,159 per ton, in line with guidance
items.quote: The guidance which we've given of INR15,000 per ton has been on a blended basis. Considering the position that we are in and based on the existing order book, our EBITDA per ton for H1 was at INR14,159 per ton, which is in line with the guidance which was given.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 seamless pipe dispatches expected at 100,000-110,000 mt; EBITDA per ton guidance of INR15,000 to continue
items.quote: I think we should be able to dispatch around 100,000 to 110,000 mt of seamless pipes. And since our order book remains good, it's a good product mix. I think the guidance of INR15,000 per ton should continue for the next quarter.

items.statement: FY25 volume flat at 400,000-410,000 tons; FY26 slightly higher after Telangana finishing line commissioning in Dec 2025
items.quote: For FY '25, volume will be flat. It should be around INR4 lakh tons to 4,10,000 tons. For FY '26, it will be slightly higher as after December '25, the finishing line in Telangana will become active and we'll be able to utilize the capacity, which we are not able to utilize right now.

items.statement: Telangana debottlenecking capex of INR852 crore; purchase orders issued, work ongoing, commissioning expected by December 2025
items.quote: We expect to commission it by December 2025. That is the date which I've given earlier as well.

items.statement: Cold-drawn pipe equipment ordered, land/shed/water supply ready; solar plant pending Telangana govt open access permission; hot mill upgrade deferred until after Telangana finishing line completion
items.quote: For cold-drawn pipe, the relevant equipment has been ordered. And we have segregated land, shed and water supply for it. Those 3 processes are completed. The only requirement right now is the installation of equipment for which orders have been placed. For the solar plant, which we want to put up in Telangana, we have written to the government of Telangana more than 8 months ago. And we were antic

items.statement: Order book at INR1,700 crore, maintained in INR1,500-2,000 crore range; fluctuation due to timing mismatch, demand environment conducive
items.quote: Our order book, secondly, is at INR1,700 crores, which is in the range of INR1,500 crores to INR2,000 crores and that is the range where we want to maintain our order book at. The fluctuation in the order book is primarily on account of timing mismatch rather than anything e lse. The order book remains good as demand environment is conducive for manufacturing industry and oil and gas sector

items.statement: EBITDA per ton guidance INR15,000; H1 FY25 at INR14,159; Q2 EBITDA increased 83% to INR231 crore on revenue of INR1,291 crore
items.quote: In Q2, our revenue improved by 14% v ersus Q1 FY '25 to INR1,291 crores. EBITDA increased by 83% to INR231 crores. PAT and EPS increased by 65% to INR224 crores and INR16.42 per share, respectively

items.statement: Raw material price risk managed by booking inventory against orders to lock margins; policy followed for many years
items.quote: When we receive an order, we book inventory against that order. The reason we do that is because we want to ensure our margins are locked, and we are not impacted by fluctuating raw material prices. That is the policy that we have followed for many years, and it's a policy which we maintain, which is why we hold the level of inventory that we do because we want to earmark our order book with raw m

items.statement: Seamless pipe demand buoyant driven by capex and spending in oil & gas; order book replenished and maintained at good level
items.quote: Finally, I wish to reiterate that capital goods and infrastructure in general and oil and gas specifically continue to witness strong demand for medium term. items.statement: Climate Technologies Australia introducing B2C products (air conditioners, heaters, fireplaces) to reduce builder-channel dependence; new products well received but need time to scale
items.quote: We are introducing a slew of other products including air conditioners, portable air conditioners, electric heaters, panel heaters, gas heaters, fireplaces, products which don't necessarily have to go into the builder segment, which are more consumer -- more of a B2C kind of a business.

items.statement: China subsidiary improvement driven by combination of outsourcing, domestic business growth, and product development for data centers (still in development stage)
items.quote: Combination of both. It is a combination of both, outsourcing from China to other parts of the world, domestic business. All of it has shown an improvement.

items.statement: Expect to sell 2,700-2,800 printers for the full year, same as previous years but with better quality
items.quote: we would still be at that 2,700-2,800 printer mark at the end of the year, which is normally what is right, that's what we bought too, But of a better quality.

items.quote: the pipeline is good in terms of new printer sales, but they are taking a bit more time to close. Now I don't know if it's because the market is slowing, the customers are not saying that any project is dropped, or factories are there.

items.statement: Strong pipeline and good orders in pipeline for track and trace and packaging businesses
items.quote: We have some good strong orders in the pipeline. Global footprints will be increased by focused management of overseas subsidiaries and the installed base will be increased focusing on increasing our larger market share.

items.statement: Cost of goods sold steady at around 40% of sales in H1; committed to optimize procurement costs to reduce operating costs going forward
items.quote: Regarding the expenses and profitability levels, the cost of goods sold has remained steady at around 40% of sales in H1. Management remains committed to optimize the procurement costs and also look closely into the economy , efficiency and effectiveness operations.

items.statement: Revenue mix for the quarter: printers 13%, consumables 64%, spares 7%, service income 15%
items.quote: for this quarter, the breakup between printers, consumables, spares, and service income is approximately 13%, 64%, 7%, and 15%, respectively.

items.statement: Inventory increased from 88 to 97 crore due to committed component orders and strong pipeline; expect to reduce to 85-88 crore by March
items.quote: as of Q1, it was about 88 and now it is about 97, but we definitely bring down to that Q1 level of 88 or maybe to 85 as well. So, we are monitoring the situation very closely.

items.statement: Track and trace, packaging, and digital printing businesses are in investment phase, incurring losses of a few crore per quarter; expect two-year period before clear picture emerges
items.quote: I would say it would be in the order of few crore. I have the numbers for the last year, b ut obviously, we have a certain number of sales people, employees, costs, and it would be at least a few crore a quarter towards that.

items.statement: Markprint turned profitable in current quarter; Codeology and CP Italy (V-Shapes) still in investment stage
items.quote: Markprint which we had acquired way back in '22, now we are working on with the business plan for them , and we are supporting them with ever y initiative what they are taking and in the current quarter , they have turned positive . In fact, they have shown a good net profit.

items.statement: Employee costs increased due to new incentive program to hire and retain best talent; rewards and recognition aligned
items.quote: So, this is the internal management decision what we have taken to make sure that we hire, we retain the best talent and make sure that the rewards and recognition go hand-in-hand.

items.statement: Coding and marking industry growth 10-12%; acquisitions aimed at increasing long-term organic growth rate beyond current constraints
items.quote: our industry growth is anywhere between 10%, 12%, and that's more for the standalone coding and marking growth. Whatever acquisitions we made, that's obviously to increase the longer-term organic growth of the company.

items.statement: Core coding and marking business market growth rate is about 1.5x GDP, 10% to 12%, and company is confident to grow at market rate or better
items.quote: on the standalone coding and marking business, our core business, the market growth rate is about 1.5x GDP. That's about 10% to 12%. And we said that we are confident that we can work the market rate or better, and that's the only guidance we have given, unfortunately, Rohan.

items.statement: Expect to sell 2,700 to 2,800 printers in FY25, need stronger second half to make up for first half shortfall of 150-200 printers
items.quote: we are still expecting to sell the same amount as what we did in previous years, which means we have to have a stronger second half in the coding and marking business, but again, we did expect maybe that we would sell about at least 150-200 printers more in the first half than what we have, we are expecting to make up in the second half.

items.statement: New printer sales pipeline is good but taking longer to close, no projects dropped, expecting to make up in second half
items.quote: what has happened is that for some reason, the pipeline is good in terms of new printer sales, but they are taking a bit more time to close. Now I don't know if it's because the market is slowing, the customers are not saying that any project is dropped, or factories are there. So, it just seems to be a little bit slower.

items.statement: Consumables business has been sales growth driver in first half, existing printer utilization is fine
items.quote: the consumables business has been the sales growth driver for us so far, this first half of the year. Now again, I don't know if it's because the quality of sale has been better over the last year and a half. And that's why the printer consumables ha s increased, which means people are printing more from each

items.quote: we have about four core patterns around the technology of the packaging machinery. You cannot patent a material theoretically. You cannot patent the structure. That's the way the patent rules work. What we have is that a patent on the machinery and the way the machinery is used. So, what we have done is we have put a RF, like we have locked our machine to the system.

items.statement: Packaging business gross margins on materials lower than coding, machine gross margins similar, net operating margins expected similar or higher at scale
items.quote: the gross margins and packaging materials are definitely lower. The gross margins of the machines are good. They are similar to our existing overall gross margins. But the net margins in that business is pretty good because the cost, so each person ends up or each, the amount of revenue that we drive in terms of the SG&A is significantly lower as a percentage of sales. So, on an overall operating

items.statement: Developing recyclable packaging material locally in India to reduce cost by 40-50% and enter food/cosmetic sectors
items.quote: we have developed a recyclable package in the process of scaling it up. It's also going to be significantly cheaper with a high barrier, and that's something we are also looking at making ourselves locally in India, and that's something which we feel will get the cost down by almost like 40%-50% from where it is right now.

items.statement: Packaging machinery sales cycle involves 6-month aging tests for pharma, accelerated aging for food/cosmetics, delaying revenue recognition
items.quote: each machine, if we sell a machine, it's going to take six months before we can execute it, because I need to do a whole bunch of packaging tests to validate the material, to validate the aging test. And in a pharmaceutical environment, there is a six-month aging that takes place.

items.statement: Capacity utilization for coding and marking is 63-65% for H1 FY25
items.quote: Yes, we are about 65% of the capacity utilization. Rohan Patel: This stands for H1? Jaideep Barve: Yes, for the coding and marking, yes, H1. We are on the same thing, about 63% to 65% is what we look out for

items.quote: on a consolidated basis, it's very difficult to understand or to predict anything b ecause the other three businesses are still relatively young. And like I said, we are expecting the things, we believe things are going relatively

items.statement: Board guideline was 400 crore top line in 2 years by March 2024, company believes it is on path to achieve
items.quote: I think 400 CR was our Board guideline to achieve in terms of top line in 2 years, that is March 24th. So, we are, I think, on the path of achieving that.

items.statement: SEBI MTF target INR2,500 crores by March 2025; LAS target additional INR500 crores by March 2025
items.value: INR2,500 crores MTF, INR500 crores LAS
items.quote: SEBI MTF has almost hit INR2,000 crores. Our plan is to take it to INR2,500 crores by March '25, and our plan is to add another INR500 crores of LAS business by March '25.

items.statement: Real estate book INR4,000 crores to run down over next 3 years; FIFG INR777 crores to fully run down in next 1 year; MSME and Digital to run down over next 6-9 months
items.period: next 3 years / next 1 year / next 6-9 months
items.value: INR4,000 crores RE, INR777 crores FIFG
items.quote: Real estate will keep running down, the balance INR4,000 crores we expect to run down over the next 3 years. FIFG, which is INR777 crores, we expect to fully run down in the next 1 year. And MSME, Digital, we fully expect to run down again over the next 6 months to 9 months.

items.statement: Will invest INR1,500 crores to build back Bespoke, INR1,000 crores for LAS in next 6-12 months, INR500 crores for debt buyback of later maturities
items.value: INR1,500 crores Bespoke, INR1,000 crores LAS, INR500 crores debt buyback
items.quote: You can just assume we will use at least INR1,500 crores to build back Bespoke. We'll probably use another INR1,000 crores to build LAS immediately next 6 months to a year and maybe INR500 crores we will do a debt buyback of later year maturities.

items.statement: DRHP filed for IPOs valued over INR50,000 crores; expect to file another INR50,000 crores in next 6 months
items.value: INR50,000 crores filed, INR50,000 crores expected
items.quote: The estimated value of transactions for which DRHP for IPOs is filed by us already stands at over INR50,000 crores, and we expect to file maybe another INR50,000 crores in the next 6 months.

items.statement: Blended lending yield ~13%; cost of borrowing 8.5%-9%; target 500 bps total spread including origination and sell-down fees
items.quote: You can assume our cost of borrowing is 8.5% - 9%. Yield is 13%. We look to make fees around 1% to 1.5% over and above that. So we try to maintain a 500 basis point total spread on lending including fees on origination and fees on sell-down.

items.statement: Affordable housing yield 13.5%-14%; Bespoke 12.5%-13%; Loan against shares 12%-12.5%; MTF 12%-12.5%
items.quote: Affordable housing is 13.5% to 14% yield. Bespoke is around 12.5% to 13% yield. Loan against shares is around 12% to 12.5% yield and margin trade finance is also 12% to 12.5% yield.

items.statement: Strong traction in focused businesses; cross-selling between wealth and investment banking; leading market shares in pre-IPO placements and alternative products
items.quote: traction through the festival season. In addition, also happy to report that we've seen some tremendous amount of cross - selling between our wealth and our investment banking divisions, taking lead market shares in pre-IPO placements and a lot of alternative products

items.statement: Affordable Home Loans seeing strong traction through festival season; 126th branch opened
items.quote: Happy to report that we've opened our 126th branch for our Affordable Home Loans business, and we're expecti ng strong traction through the festival

items.statement: Pivot from on-balance sheet wholesale lending to off-balance sheet syndication model across real estate, distressed credit, corporate credit, promoter credit
items.quote: the first being a pivot in our wholesale credit businesses moving from on -balance sheet lending to off-balance sheet loan book driven business to focus more on a syndication -driven model. And we will do this across asset classes like real estate, distresse d credit, corporate credit as well as promoter credit

items.statement: Provision coverage on gross NPA increased from 59% to 70.4% conservatively; incremental provision INR109 crores; gross NPA barely moved from INR813 crores to INR835 crores
items.quote: The provision on gross NPA has been conservatively increased to INR588 crores as compared to INR479 crores for quarter ended June 30, 2024. The incremental provision of INR109 crores has resulted in the provision coverage ratio to increase from 59% as of June 30, 2024 to 70.4% as of September 30, 2024.

items.statement: INR1,300 crores needed to purchase Credit Solutions stake; INR6,200-6,300 crores group liquidity available; INR5,000 crores surplus cash after stake purchase
items.value: INR1,300 crores stake purchase, INR5,000 crores surplus
items.quote: We will need INR1,300 crores of that to purchase the stake of Credit Solutions. So, when we remove INR1,300 crores, we are left with roughly INR5,000 crores of cash.

items.statement: Dividend policy from next year: significant portion of earnings from treasury, NBFC, and capital market profits to be paid out; will not pay out capital
items.quote: Going ahead, we will have a proper dividend policy from next year where a significant portion of the earnings from our treasury assets, from our NBFC profitability as well as our capital market profitability will be paid out as dividend. So, as I've mentioned before, we will not pay out our capital. We will pay out the profits that we make from our capital and business as dividend.

items.statement: FY25 R&D spend expected to be 7% to 8% of sales
items.quote: We expect our FY '25 R&D spend to be in the range of 7% to 8% of our sales.

items.statement: R&D spend needs to increase in H2 to meet full-year guidance
items.quote: For us to reach 7% or 8%, it needs to go up by a corresponding number so that the annual number is reaching the guidance.

items.statement: India formulation sales grew 11% YoY in Q2, driven by volumes and new launches
items.quote: For Q2, the sales of formulation in India were at Rs. 42,652 million, recording a growth of 11% over Q2 last year.

items.statement: India volume growth at 5.2% vs industry 0.7% on MAT Sep-24 basis
items.quote: the volume growth for the industry is on MAT September '24 basis is 0.7% and we are 5.2%.

items.statement: U.S. specialty business underlying prescription trends remain strong
items.quote: The underlying business and the prescription trends for the specialty business remain strong.

items.statement: Japan price cuts to pressure Rest of World revenue for next few quarters
items.quote: Japan price cuts, as mentioned in the previous quarter, are an important reason for revenue decline in ROW. We expect this pressure to flow through the next few quarters' performance.

items.statement: Leqselvi launch timing depends on court judgment; ready to launch in a couple of weeks if favorable
items.quote: It will be a couple of weeks, not definitely a couple of months. So, to that extent, we will be ready.

items.statement: Worst-case Leqselvi litigation outcome is launch delay until patent expiry in Dec 2026
items.quote: And up to that is the worst-case situation is that in case if we get an unfavorable judgment and then even on appeal if we lose, then that is the time to which our potential launch gets delayed.

items.statement: ILUMYA psoriatic arthritis approval could address ~30% of market currently missed
items.quote: the split between psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis is somewhere, and you can use this as a ballpark figure, so don't hold me to it, it's like a 70-30. So, the 30% is the market you are roughly kept around with.

items.statement: No material movement expected in staff costs for rest of year
items.quote: As such, we do not expect any material movement in the staff costs.

items.statement: Utreglutide Phase-II moved to first half of next year
items.quote: No, I think if you see our disclosure, what we've said is that it will move to the first half of next year.

items.statement: Fibromun licensing milestone capitalized on balance sheet, not in P&L expenses
items.quote: No, it's not part of other expenses. It is part of a balance sheet item.

items.statement: Emerging markets underlying constant currency growth was 5% YoY in Q2
items.quote: The underlying growth in constant currency terms was 5% year-on-year for Q2.

items.statement: GLP-1 asset GL0034 Phase-II trial delayed but aiming to make up time during conduct
items.quote: There is a certain amount of delay in terms of starting the large Phase-II study. But we hope that we will be able to make up during the conduct of the study.

items.statement: No specific gross margin or EBITDA margin guidance provided for full year
items.quote: So, we are not giving any specific guidance on gross margins.

items.statement: Expect cement demand growth of 4% to 5% for full year FY25, implying 8% to 9% growth in H2 FY25
items.quote: We expect demand during FY 2025 to grow in the range of 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Full year FY25 organic capex expected at INR 7,000-8,000 crores, with INR 3,500 crores spent in H1
items.quote: So closer to INR7,000 – 8000 crores, is what we are expecting for the full year.

items.statement: Targeting 140 million tons cement capacity by FY28, with 118 million tons by end of FY26 and 115 million tons by Q3 FY26
items.quote: As we plan to expand our cement capacity, 140 million tons by FY '28, we are pacing well to achieve the stated target.

items.statement: Acquired 70 million tons of new limestone reserves in Q2 FY25 via two mine wins in Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra
items.quote: To secure our limestone supplies in quarter 2 FY '25, we have won bids for another 2 new mines having reserves of 70 million tons, 1 in Madhya Pradesh and 1 in Maharashtra.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin at 14.8%, EBITDA per ton INR 780; H1 FY25 margin at 15.1%, EBITDA per ton INR 795
items.quote: With the improvements mentioned on the cost front, EBITDA stood at INR 1,111 crores at a margin of 14.8% and EBITDA per ton of INR 780.

items.statement: Operational cost per ton declined 4% YoY to INR 4,497 in Q2 FY25, driven by 10% lower energy costs and 7% lower logistics costs
items.quote: On the operational cost for the quarter, it was INR4,497 per ton, showing a decline of 4%.

items.statement: Targeting INR 90 per ton power cost reduction by FY28 via 1,000 MW renewable energy (60% green power), with 200 MW Khavda solar phase 1 charged
items.quote: This would help in reducing the power cost by INR90 per ton by FY '28.

items.statement: Cost reduction program targeting INR 450-500 per ton savings by March 2028; 25-30% (INR ~150 per ton) achieved so far
items.quote: I would say 25 %-odd has been achieved, 25% to 30%. But -- this is, again, yes as of now our assessment, but safe to assume say INR150-odd has been achieved.

items.statement: Strong infrastructure demand and housing/commercial needs expected to boost cement demand in H2 FY25, supported by PMAY Urban Housing 2 (INR 11 lakh crore allocation)
items.quote: Strong infrastructure demand and ongoing needs from the housing and commercial sectors are anticipated to boost cement demand in H2 FY '25.

items.statement: Blended cement at 84% of sales; premium products share in trade sales up 300 bps YoY to 26% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: blended cement at 84%, increase in premium products as a percentage of trade sales by 300 bps up to 26%.

items.statement: Orient Cement acquisition (46.8% stake) to be funded via internal accruals; post-completion capacity reaches 97.4 million tons
items.quote: Ambuja enters into a binding agreement to acquire 46.8% stake in Orient Cements Limited. The acquisition complements existing cement footprint, reducing overall lead distance and logistics costs and improving market share in core markets.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with INR 10,135 crores cash and equivalents as of Sept 30, 2024; net worth increased to INR 59,916 crores in H1 FY25
items.quote: As of 30th September, the consolidated cash and cash equivalents stood at INR10,135 crores.

items.statement: Waste heat recovery capacity at 196 MW currently, targeting 218 MW by March 2025; AFR share in fuel mix improved to 9.5% from 7%
items.quote: Our wastage recovery capacity at the time of takeover was 40 megawatts, which we are now targeting to increase to 218 megawatts by March '25. Currently, the WH RS capacity is 196 megawatts.

items.statement: Penna Cement integration progressing well: 45 days of operations in Q2, clinker utilization at 70-75%, cement volumes ~1 lakh tons, clinker supporting southern grinding units
items.quote: Cement volume for Penna would be in the range of 1 lakh to 2.5 lakhs.

items.statement: Sanghi plant: one kiln fully refurbished and running, second kiln under maintenance; Mundra project on track for commissioning in 2026-27
items.quote: Mundra, we stay on track, and I think we should be commissioning this pr oject somewhere in '26, '27

items.statement: Government incentives income ~INR 250 crores per quarter (INR 600-650 crores annual run-rate); INR 138 crores accrued in Q2 for West Bengal unit post Supreme Court win
items.quote: Quarterly, my incentives ballpark is around INR250-odd crores. And therefore, if I extrapolate so for a year, we're close to around, I would say, INR600 crores to INR650-odd crores is my incentives which I put in a year.

items.statement: Domestic demand conditions unchanged in Q2; exports impacted by ocean freight volatility
items.quote: There is no material change to the domestic demand conditions in Q2. Exports have continued to remain impacted given the volatility of ocean freights.

items.statement: Monthly run rates moderated to 1,000-1,200 crores versus 1,500-2,000 crores last year
items.quote: The monthly run rates moderated 1,000 to 1,200 crores versus 1,500 to 2,000 crores last year.

items.statement: Expecting increase in tile consumption in H2 with moderating capacity additions and Morbi supply curtailment
items.quote: The changing landscape in the industry, the expected increase in tile consumption in H2 and our own efforts on branding and strengthening of our sales team structure should enable OBL to come back strongly here on.

items.statement: Q2 gross margin 35.7% versus 33% last year, a 2.7% improvement
items.quote: So, for Q2, we were at 35.7% versus 33% same time last year, which is a 2.7% improvement.

items.statement: Cost of production in H1 approximately 5.5% lower versus last year on like-for-like basis
items.quote: cost of production in first half was approximately 5.5% lower versus last year on a like-for-like basis, which is at constant product mix in energy costs.

items.statement: EBITDA on like-for-like basis 6.2% versus 3.7% last year, up 2.5%; reported EBITDA 5% versus 3.8%
items.quote: EBITDA on a like-for-like basis too, which is excluding the impact of these increased investments that we are doing on branding consistently for the quarter was 6.2% again higher by 2.5% versus the last year.

items.statement: GVT salience improved to 40%, increasing by 14% over last year
items.quote: Our product mixes have changed rapidly in the last six months to match customer expectations with GVT salience improving to 40%, increasing by 14% over last year.

items.statement: Added net 19 OBTX in last six months, active count 380, contributing 46% of revenue versus 42% last year
items.quote: Our distribution too continues to expand as we have added a net 19 more OBTX in the last six months, taking the active count to 380. These OBTX now contribute 46% of our revenue versus 42% last year.

items.statement: Proton 5.5 MSM plant stabilization underway, ramp-up expected over next half to one year, largely for exports
items.quote: For all practical purposes, please assume Q3 coming in. So, this is just something which has started. They are in that phase of stabilization. It will take time. And eventually largely this capacity is meant for exports.

items.statement: Older projects now ready for tiling, seeing increasing queries and bigger projects asking for tiles
items.quote: So, Miraj, we have the older projects which are now ready for tiling, we are seeing increasing number of queries which we are not seeing in Q1 and Q2, it has slowly started picking up, and we are seeing bigger and bigger projects which are now asking around for tiles.

items.statement: Branding spend increased to 4.1% of revenue to support TV campaign running for 10 months
items.quote: To drive premiumization and brand recall, we continue to invest on branding. Our spends increasing to 4.1% of our revenue primarily to support the TV campaign that we have been running for last 10-odd months consistently.

items.statement: Advertising campaign to continue in Q3 with possible strategy adjustments, committed to brand building long-term
items.quote: As we speak, we are pretty clear that in Q3, we will keep investing in media, maybe with a slightly different strategy maybe or a different property. So, I think yes, actually we launched this campaign in December '23. So, I guess for 12 months, it is going to be alive at least and we will see for Q4 when we come to that.

items.statement: Launched 51 OBTB in H1, closed 31-32, net adds ~20 (almost one per week)
items.quote: So, we launched 51 in H1. We closed I think 31 or 32. So, net adds will be about 20-odd newer OBTB in H1, which is almost one new OBTB a week is what we have added in H1 broadly speaking.

items.statement: Export markets weak last 3-4 months at 1,000-1,200 crores, need to be watchful for opportunities
items.quote: you would know export markets in general have not done so well. The last three months, four months have been really bad. It's 1,000 to 1,200-odd crores. So, we need to be watchful.

items.statement: FY25 volume growth guided at 5%-6.5% for full year, implying high single-digit to low double-digit growth in H2
items.quote: The guidance for next year for the H2 is that we should be able to do high single digit, low double digit growth, which means that we should be able to conclude the year in the mid single digits between the 5% and 6.5% growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to improve by 1%-1.5% from current levels in FY25, returning to last year's level, assuming stable gas prices and 2.5% brand spend
items.quote: The EBITDA margins obviously from the current levels will go up by 1.5% if we achieve that with the caveat being that there is no surprise on the gas pricing, especially from a geopolitical point of view and the branding remaining at 2.5%.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 operating margin flat at 8.5%, same as Q1, despite price pressure and lower capacity utilization
items.quote: Our sales, however, grew by 2.6% in Q2. The operating margin nevertheless remained the same as 8.5% in Q2, just like it was in Q1.

items.statement: Average realization faced Rs. 4/sq m discounting pressure in Q2, fully offset by improved product mix
items.quote: We have had a pressure of about Rs. 4 square meter in terms of discounting, in terms of average realization. All of that has got mitigated with the product mix.

items.statement: GVT share in tile mix increased to 38% from 34% YoY, ceramic declined to 34% from 36%, PBT to 28% from 30%
items.quote: The Tile segment, the Ceramic went down by 2% from 36%-34%. PBT went down from 30%-28% again by 2%. this was all in favor of GVT, which went up from 34 %-38%.
