items.quote: In fact, all the while we have been saying that our steady state spreads will be about 12%, which will translate to a steady state ROA of about 6% or so.

items.statement: 14% of active loans (59,000 accounts) overleveraged with 3+ other loans; only 1,600 loans (0.4%) show lower collection efficiency
items.quote: Out of our total active loans of 4.3 lakhs, we find that about 14% of our loans which is 59,000 loans are overleveraged, that is, the applicant having three or more loans with other financial institutions.

items.statement: Disbursements slowed consciously to moderate portfolio growth; Q2 disbursements Rs 1,251 cr (4% YoY, -5% QoQ)
items.quote: We had a good disbursement of 1,251 crores versus 1,204 crores last September, registering a growth of 4% YoY and 1,318 crores in June quarter, which shows a negative growth of 5% Q oQ.

items.statement: Opened 113 branches in Q2 (32 new, 77 split); split branches address concentration risk; new branches take 7-9 months to break even at Rs 2.5 cr AUM
items.quote: We have opened 113 branches in the September quarter, out of that, 32 are new branches and 77 are split branches.

items.statement: Borrowing cost stable at 9.65%; incremental borrowing cost 9.52% (+5 bps); non-bank borrowing share reduced from 74% to 70%
items.quote: On the borrowing cost, the borrowing cost for the quarter was at stable at 9.65% versus 9.65% last June. Incremental borrowing cost w as at 9.52% versus 9.47% with an increase of just five bps.

items.statement: AUM at Rs 10,927 cr (6% QoQ, 32% YoY); active loan base 4.3 lakh
items.quote: Our portfolio stands at 10,927 crores versus 10,343 crores in June and 8,264 crores in last September, registering a 6% QoQ growth and 32% YoY growth.

items.statement: Gross Stage-III assets at 1.47% (+6 bps QoQ); collection efficiency 98.4% (vs 98.5%); unique customer collection 97% (vs 97.2%)
items.quote: Our gross Stage-III assets was at 1.47% versus 1.41% which had an increase of 6 bps.

items.statement: Onboarded Nippon MF, Kotak MF, HDFC MF, HSBC MF as PTC investors; liquidity buffer Rs 1,700 cr + Rs 250 cr undrawn lines
items.quote: We have onboarded Nippon Mutual Fund and Kotak Mutual Fund as lenders to us. They have subscribed to our PTC transaction. Incidentally given that this is a public call and today it could be public news, we also had HDFC Mutual Fund and HSBC Mutual Fund subscribing to our PTCs today.

items.statement: ~30% borrowers have active MFI loans; overleveraged loans primarily unsecured (MFI, gold, 2-wheeler, agri); secured overlaps minimal
items.quote: So, what is happening is, people are starting to prioritize and in the order of their priority, we stand almost on top so which means that they are repaying us.

items.statement: FY25 disbursements likely flattish in H2 vs H1; full-year disbursement ~Rs 5,200 cr (10-12% YoY) to achieve 25% AUM growth
items.quote: So, if we do a flattish disbursal, we will probably end up with about 5,200 crores of disbursal for the full year as against about 4,800, 4,900 last year which will mean like a 10%, 12% disbursement growth translating to about 25% AUM growth.

items.statement: Stricter underwriting for overleveraged customers; tightening LTV and DBR norms in stressed pockets; bureau scrub used for underwriting
items.quote: So, for these cases, we will definitely be tightening the underwriting norms both in terms of LTVs and DBR.

items.statement: Cost-to-income (incl. credit cost) guided at 35-36% steady state; OPEX ~5.1% currently, 60-70% fixed; credit cost 3-4%
items.quote: So, including our credit cost, we will be at about 35% of cost-to-income even in a steady state scenario.

items.statement: Branch split program focused on branches >1,500 accounts; expect most pending splits done in 2-3 quarters; organic growth resumes mid-FY26
items.quote: So, I think in about two to three quarters, we should have been done with most of the splits which are already pending at this point of time.

items.statement: Overleverage stress expected short-term (2 quarters); regulators tightening unsecured lending norms; board prioritizing collections over growth
items.quote: My hope is it should be shorter, not more than two quarters from now.

items.statement: Expect to cross INR3,000 crore revenue in FY25 and operational EBITDA margin above 15%
items.quote: We believe that the second half would be showing solid growth so that our company will cross the milestone of INR3,000 crore s in FY25. With the trend in EBITDA margin improvement, we believe we will cross the operational EBITDA of 15% this year

items.statement: Order book increased from INR50,386 million in Q1 FY25 to INR54,228 million in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our order book surged from INR 50,386 million in Q1 FY25 to INR54,228 million in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Smart meter acquisition opens ~40-50 million meter opportunity over several years targeting 15-20% share of awarded orders
items.quote: Kaynes Technology acquisition of Iskraemeco has opened up a sign ificant opportunity worth approximately 40 million to 50 million Smart Meters to be executed ov er several years

items.statement: Expect significant gross margin and EBITDA margin improvement in H2 FY25 due to high-yielding sector mix and operating leverage
items.quote: we think that in the second half, we will get a sig nificant increase in our gross margins and also EBITDA. Gross margins because of the mix and EBI TDA because of the leverage, because we’ll be doing almost twice as much as what we did in the first half

items.statement: Target net working capital of 72-75 days by end of FY25, down from 108 days in Q2
items.quote: Last year, we had delivered about 85 days. This year, probably we’ll go closer to abo ut 75, 72 days net working capital at the end of the year

items.statement: Kavach rail signalling addressable market estimated at INR12,500-15,000 crore targeting 15-20% share over 4-5 years
items.value: INR12,500-15,000 crores addressable; targeting INR2,000 crore
items.quote: So, about INR15,000 crores anywhere between INR12,500-15,000 crores is the kind of addressable market at this point in time. And so, we think that about 15% market share. So, Yes. So, we will get about INR2000 crores.

items.statement: Aerospace & defense ramp-up expected from Q4 FY25 with large US OEM; could become single largest customer in FY26
items.quote: Now, fourth stage is to gear up for serial production, which we expect by end of this year to start off, say, maybe Q4. And maybe it will accelerate in FY26. That's why we are saying that this might be a very large or probably single largest customer in FY26.

items.statement: Target ~7% of sales as operating cash flow (approx INR200 crore) in FY25; aim to self-fund EMS growth at 50%+ rates
items.quote: We were contemplating about INR200-odd crores of OCF by end of the year. Maybe we'll get there. We still have INR2000 crores of business to be done. So, by end of the year, probably should be able to generate.

items.statement: Industrial/EV segment mix roughly three-fourths smart meter & other industrial, one-fourth EV electronics in steady state
items.quote: So, three-fourths of that will be, say, one-fourth of that proba bly will be EV and three-fourths of that will be roughly smart meter and other industrial like instrumentation

items.statement: Smart meter rollout faces state-level political resistance and installation issues but half of 11 crore meters already awarded; program accelerating post-elections
items.quote: Certain states have been ahead of the curve, certain states have been lag ging behind. And of course, the certain some of the states like Maharashtra, etc., they are also undergoing election and so on. So, obviously, there are maybe mixed signals given by different political parties, etc

items.statement: Export revenue target ~20% of total in FY26 driven by OSAT, HDI, instrumentation and US customers; long-term goal ~33%
items.quote: From FY ’26 onwards, you can see some significant increase in expo rts, aided by, of course, some revenues in the fourth quarter from both OSAT revenues as well a s HDI, high-density interconnection. And also, there are areas like instrumentation and there are areas, other areas in the U.S. that we are working with

items.statement: Smart meter factory Phase 1 operational in Telangana; Phase 2 construction started
items.quote: Our Telangana factory phase one for sm art meters is up and running, and construction for phase two has also

items.statement: EV business diversified across 2W, 3W, charging, components; 4W EV limited to two large customers, monitoring hybrid trends
items.quote: So, electric vehicle, if you were to segment that entire electric vehicle business as far as electronics is concerned, we are into four areas. The first area, of course, two-wheeler electric vehicles electronics.

items.statement: Lifetime order visibility of 2-3 years from aerospace, auto, rail; targets 3x revenue by FY29 (approx $1B by FY28 as per IPO commitment)
items.quote: When I say two to three years, I had committed, if you remember, I had committed on the day we got listed that we will be doing a billion dollar by FY'28. And so far, as per plan, we are fully ready for that. And I feel whatever you ask me as three times of my current plus minus, FY '29, we should be there.

items.statement: Order book stood at approximately INR21.5 crores as of 30th September with L1 pipeline of more than INR300 crores
items.quote: Our order book, as of 30th September, stood at approximately INR21.5 crores, with an L1 opportunity pipeline of now more idea than INR300 crores

items.statement: L1 pipeline has increased slightly from Q1 and includes sizable international opportunities
items.quote: It has actually gone up a little bit, but we are just currently retaining the position in terms of numbers.

items.statement: Government capex spending slowed in H1 due to general election; resumption and momentum expected in H2
items.quote: However, we are tracking these opportunities closely, and as we approach the second half of this financial year, we anticipate resumption and momentum in government spending that was slowed in the first half due to events like the general election.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margins of 25-30% as pipeline converts, similar to last year's performance
items.quote: Hardik, the EBITDA that we were tracking was about 25% to 30%.

items.statement: No firm FY25 revenue guidance; awaiting order closures to communicate positioning
items.quote: Hardik, we are awaiting the closures on the order that we are tracking. And depending on when these finally get executed in the timeline that we are left with to overall execute, we will come back to you and the overall market as well to communicate our positioning for this year.

items.statement: Lower gross margin in Q2 due to product mix and BOQ of contract signed a year ago; believed temporary
items.quote: The reason for lower gross profit is because of the product mix and BOQ of the product delivered during this period, for contract that was signed about a year back. However, we believe this is temporary in nature

items.statement: Drone-as-a-Service revenue expected to exceed INR1 crore in FY25; meaningful growth expected next year as franchise model matures
items.quote: We do expect to do more than INR1 crore in revenue this year because these are early days for our POCs as well. But next year onwards, we should start seeing good improvement in revenue from products.

items.statement: H1 FY25 gross profit margin 30.7%; Q2 gross profit margin 24.6%; EBITDA negative due to scale and lower quarterly revenue
items.quote: For H1 FY25, gross profit stood at INR37.8 crores, with a gross profit margin of 30.7%. EBITDA for the quarter was minus INR10 crores and INR minus 1.5 crores for H1 FY25.

items.statement: Increased government scrutiny on technology origin and national security creates barrier to entry, benefiting indigenous developers
items.quote: They have to look at the country of origin of the technology. They have to make sure that the national security interest is also kept into mind when building technology. And therefore, we will see that it will mature the industry quite a bit and it will make it a much safer industry from a national security point of view

items.statement: Proactive steps taken for manufacturing capacity and critical supply chain items to fulfill large orders within timelines
items.quote: Further, we have taken certain proactive steps for building capacity and capability for manufacturing and also have secured several critical items from a supply chain point of view so that we can fulfil even large opportunity within anticipated timelines.

items.statement: Global demand uptick due to geopolitical conflicts; adapting products for international deployment methods and pricing
items.quote: So, in fact, slowdown -- it's the exact opposite of slowdown, Sahil, in terms of the market and the opportunity there because the global wars and several of these geographies are participating in those wars. So overall, there is an uptick and there is a huge uptick in preparing for any eventual conflict that is being seen globally.

items.statement: Middle-mile logistics drone targets 100+ kg payload over 100+ km at high altitude; tactical UAV targets 10 kg payload over 50 km
items.quote: The middle mile logistics drone platform is a platform that's going to be about, 10 times heavier than the tactical platform, where we are looking to load up to about 100 plus kilos to 100 plus kilometers.

items.statement: Board gave in-principle approval to raise up to INR 500 crores for growth capex and working capital for Mundra land development, Farrukhnagar/Jhajjar ICD-MMLP, Kences CFS, and JNPT extension.
items.quote: So, in this board meeting, we took an in-principle approval to raise funds up to INR 500 crores. I think while answering the previous call, we talked about various projects, upcoming projects. Which includes Mundra land development, Farrukhnagar or Jhajjar ICD MMLP plan, then Kences CFS, JNPT extension.

items.statement: Capacity expansion from 8.5 lakh to ~12 lakh TEUs over 2-3 years via Kences CFS (Q1 CY25), Mundra Phase 1 (Q3 FY26), JNPT 25 acres (Mar-Apr 2025), and Jhajjar ICD (Dec 2026/Jan 2027).
items.quote: We expect to have business and volumes coming into ATL from Q1 calendar year, which is January to March time of 2025. Mundra, the land that we have acquired, this is outside the Adani SEZ. We expect to have the first phase of construction to be completed in the next nine months to 12 months and business to start coming in from Q3 of FY26.

items.statement: H2 FY25 volume growth expected similar to H1 (~4% YoY) with market share maintained; EBITDA per TEU expected to remain around INR 2,000-2,100 in near term.
items.quote: We expect similar kind of growth going into H2. And if you were to look at how the market has been between Q1 and Q2, Q1, there was significant growth. Q2, there's been a little bit of a tapering down, which I mentioned in my opening remarks saying in September, the volume seemed to have tapered down a little.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA per TEU crossed INR 2,000; gross margin exceeded 33% and EBITDA margin exceeded 17% driven by better yields and operating efficiencies.
items.quote: In this quarter, we were able to cross the INR 2000 mark per TEU EBITDA. The gross margin exceeded 33% and the EBITDA percentage was in excess of 17%.

items.statement: Global maritime trade projected to grow 2% in 2024 and 2.4% avg 2025-29; India EXIM trade grew with exports $213B and imports $350B in H1 FY25.
items.quote: The United Nations Trade and Development Agency in its annual report has projected that global maritime trade will grow by 2% in 2024 and for the period 2025-29, which is a four, five year period, projected to grow at an average of 2.4%.

items.statement: Strategic shift from CFS-heavy to CFS+ICD player nationally; acquired 7.6% stake in Haryana Orbital Rail Corp (INR 138.7 cr) for rail connectivity to Farrukhnagar ICD-MMLP.
items.quote: Allcargo Terminals has acquired 7.6% stake in Haryana Orbital Rail Corporation from Allcargo Logistics. This stake purchase is in line with the company's growth aspirations of entering into multimodal logistics parks and ICDs.

items.statement: Early signs of consolidation among ~150-155 CFS operators visible, which could stabilize pricing pressure for national footprint players like ATL.
items.quote: We have reliable market information which goes around which says that there are CFS operators who are looking at moving out for various reasons. So we believe that there could be consolidation which will assist serious national footprint operators like us.

items.statement: No specific revenue guidance given; management expects current volume and profitability trends to continue but does not provide quantitative guidance on calls.
items.quote: Apart from that Sanket, we don't give any specific guidance on these calls and we won't have any commentary around that.

items.statement: Strategy remains asset-light plus asset-right: Chennai Kences partnership and JNPT lease are asset-light; Mundra land purchase is asset-right for strategic fit; Farrukhnagar ICD-MMLP will be largely asset-light on leased land.
items.quote: I would like to modify this and say wherever there is a requirement which has a strategic fit, we will have assets of ourselves, which is like in Mundra. And therefore, the asset-light plus an asset-right approach is what we are now embarking on.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guided at approximately Rs. 65 crores
items.quote: But, yes, for FY '25, the approximate revenue will be around Rs. 65 crores.

items.statement: FY25 margins expected to continue at current levels
items.quote: So, whatever the current margin is, we expect to continue with that.

items.statement: New projects expected to start in beginning of next year after land consolidation and approvals
items.quote: So, in the next six months, the picture will be more clearer and we probably will have some of these projects starting in the beginning of next year.

items.statement: Existing projects fully operational with steady monthly run rate; no material revenue changes expected until new projects operational in FY26 or FY27
items.quote: All our existing projects are fully operational, and we have now a monthly run rate of revenues. We do not have any projects getting completed between now and March, so we do not expect any change from our monthly rentals. And it will be at a steady state going forward. Our new projects will be operational mostly in FY '26 or '27 and that is when there will be a significant change in revenue.

items.statement: Blended rental yield on operational properties is 8.5% to 9%
items.quote: Rental yields on the property is different for different locations, but blended yield you can say is close to 8.5% to 9% in the range, puerly rental yield.

items.statement: Evaluating alternative asset classes including data centers, MMLP, plotted development, and residential plots; no concrete plans yet
items.quote: We are evaluating options. The picture will be clearer on the other type of assets probably by the first quarter of next year.

items.statement: Related party transactions for land acquisition followed due process with two independent international valuer reports, audit committee, board and shareholder approvals
items.quote: has followed all the due process of the law, including obtain the valuation from the two registered valuer of the repute. It has obtained, apart from Audit Committee and Board approval, it has also obtained the shareholders' approval for the transaction

items.statement: Cash and liquid investments of Rs. 150 crores on balance sheet as of September 2024
items.quote: I mean, Rs. 150 crores as on the September balance sheet we have got cash.

items.statement: IFM revenue growth guided at 10-15% for FY25, BSS organic growth guided at over 20% for FY25
items.quote: Revenue growth range of between 10% to 15%, or closer to 15%, is something that we have always guided, at least informally, not a formal guidance. And we are confident that we will maintain that as far as the IFM business is concerned.

items.statement: IFM EBITDA margin target upwards of 6% for FY25, BSS margin to stay in 9-11% range with slight improvement
items.quote: This year, we will be aiming more in terms of IFM going upwards of 6%. We are aiming for that, primarily from the operational synergies which are kicking in now and from the unviable contracts which we exited.

items.statement: IFM EBITDA margin improved to 6.1% in H1 FY25 from 4.2% in H1 FY24, a 190 bps improvement
items.quote: EBITDA margins of the IFM segment stood about 6.1% as of H1 ‘25, wh ich was 4.2% last year, an improvement of about 190 bps

items.statement: BSS EBITDA margin stood at 9.5% in H1 FY25, up from 9.7% in FY24
items.quote: EBITDA margins on the BSS segment stood at 9.5% as on H1-FY25.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 7.3% in H1 FY25 from 5.7% in H1 FY24
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 7.3% versus 5.7% in H1 FY24 a 1.6% improvement over last year.

items.statement: Added 48 new logos in IFM and 26 in BSS during H1 FY25, with clients above INR 5 lakh revenue threshold
items.quote: During this H1-25 we added 48 logos in IFM segment and 26 logos in BSS segment.

items.statement: Strong demand outlook driven by GCC growth, manufacturing expansion, infrastructure investment, and outsourcing trend
items.quote: With the government's push to create jobs, the rapi d growth of global capacity centers in India, and rising foreign investments, we are confid ent in maintaining our growth trajectory going forward

items.statement: IFM focusing on hard services and manufacturing for higher margins; BSS expanding into sales intelligence, AI-enabled services, and cross-selling between segments
items.quote: At UDS, we are committed to providing solution-based services with strong focus on hard services that contribute more to our margins.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks and sector-specific risks remain headwinds; Athena facing disruption from BFSI customer changes and AI-led market shifts
items.quote: While headwinds remains because of geopolitical risks as well as in many parts in terms of specific sector-specific risks.

items.statement: Net cash company with net debt-to-equity of -0.1x as of September 2024; acquisition funding from IPO proceeds and internal accruals
items.quote: UDS is a net cash company and our net debt-to-equity stood at negative 0.1x as on September 30.

items.statement: Exiting unviable IFM contracts largely complete; share of non-viable business now in single digits
items.quote: As informed earlier, we are cautiously exiting some non-viable and not very profitable businesses, and that share has come down to sing le digits

items.statement: Global (ground handling) revenue grew from INR 12 crores in Q1 to INR 13 crores in Q2 with 8-10% EBITDA margin
items.quote: We did a INR12 crores revenue in Q1 for Global with a 10% margin. We have done INR13 crores now and we con tinue to do it better than this, quarter on quarter

items.statement: Sales enablement contracts 90% fixed, 7-8% mixed fixed-variable, 2-3% fully variable; 80-85% annual contracts
items.quote: 90% of our contracts are fixed contracts where we have a predefined number and we have a month-on-month fixed payment.

items.statement: ROCE at 23% annualized as of September 2024, marginally below 23.5% in March 2024
items.quote: The ROCE on an annualized basis stood at 23% as of September 24, marginally less compared to 23.5% during March 2024.

items.statement: Cash conversion expected at 85-90% sustainably unless large acquisition requires borrowing
items.quote: That would be a fair assumption. Unless we have another large acquisition which makes us to borrow.

items.statement: Management expects to maintain the same growth pattern achieved over the last 3 years for at least the next 3 years, targeting around 63-68% CAGR.
items.quote: We should continue for at least 3 years. 5 years is too long to talk about at this moment. Yes, three years we should and internal growth will all depend on capex which we are already doing, skill enhancement which we are already doing and the expansion of the manufacturing unit which we have already started.

items.statement: Management aims for a 50/50 revenue split between traditional mould base business and new businesses like aerospace and defence within the next 3 years.
items.quote: Yes you are very right from approximately in the next 3 years it should be a 50/50 number easily that is what we are striving and we are looking at and envisioning

items.statement: Two machines installed in H1 FY25 contributed to growth; four machines arrived mid-September and were not yet impacting results; one machine at JNPT port expected to be commissioned in 3-4 weeks.
items.quote: two machines were installed decently enough to give any addition to the ﬁrst half year numbers and they did give a little bit of growth to our numbers. The other four machines came in maybe around mid September. So they were yet to be commissioned or commissioned but not good enough to be impacting the top line of the the bottom line of the company

items.statement: New land identified for Vasai factory expansion with advance paid; flats booked for employee accommodation visible in other current assets.
items.quote: We have also identiﬁed a plot of land for future expansion of the Vasai factory and paid a little advance for the same while we do the other formalities, due diligence, title search and other things

items.statement: Margins improved by sourcing steel directly from mills like ArcelorMittal and Jindal, avoiding distributor margins of 5-10% and gaining better credit terms via LC.
items.quote: We have stated that we have increased our margins to a certain extent and a reason also is that steel mills like Arcelon Mittal and Jindal thus avoiding a distributor in between and his margins to an extent of 5 to 10% which normally a distributors charge, so that is now a gain for us

items.statement: PAT margins expected to remain stable at healthy 18-23% levels over the next 2-3 years with limited upside from optimization.
items.quote: I think my margins should be constant now it should not be a drop there if not an increase. We will try to optimize a lot of things in our business in our processes and in our costs so that we can add on to the margins but it will add to a limited extent so what I see that we are already at a healthy 18 to 23% PAT levels so I think we should be able to maintain that over the period of next two to

items.statement: Work in progress of ~12 crores as of H1 end expected to convert to sales in coming months; WIP execution cycle is 14-21 days.
items.quote: As I have mentioned in my press release there is already a working capital of 12 odd crores. So you can assume that that is the work in progress that we have and that will culminate into sales in the coming months.

items.statement: Four verticals (mould base, sheet metal, die casting, capex/machine parts) each capped at 25% of sales for risk mitigation; policy in place since 2013.
items.quote: We have a strict policy since 2013 that we have four verticals. So we don't exceed 25% of our total sales in each vertical because we don't want to be forced if there is one industry which is going through a bad turn we also go to a bad turn.

items.statement: Steel price volatility is the biggest current challenge; prices have stabilized but a further decline would be negative while an increase would benefit inventory.
items.quote: The steel prices are the biggest challenge nowadays. it has come to a very good level as of now and it has stabilized for the moment. So now there should be an upward move in the steel prices and with our kind of inventory in stock it should be a blessing in disguise, but if it goes down it will be a little problem a little negativity for us.

items.statement: Company is long-term debt-free since August loan repayment; no immediate capital raise planned unless a very substantial acquisition opportunity arises.
items.quote: we are a long-term debt-free company. The last loan was paid o� in August. So the future numbers will see a reduction in bank interest cost to a major extent

items.statement: Sunita Leo Equip (Ahmedabad) acquisition complete and running smoothly; consolidation from March 2025; one new machine added, another CNC VMC expected by December 2024.
items.quote: Leo equip Ahmedabad acquisition is complete and running very smoothly with Mr. Prashan Gupta director handling the operations very well. We have added one more new machine in that factory and one new CNC VMC should reach that factory by December 2024. And as far as the consolidation of the numbers of Sunita Leo is concerned, it will start with the March 25 statements

items.statement: Sunita Imperial (Coimbatore) acquisition still in process; GST number awaited to start production; target company had ~4 cr sales and ~1 cr PAT pre-acquisition.
items.quote: Sunita Imperial Comibatore, we are still completing the acquisition processes. GST number is applied for and still awaited as we speak , to start production in that unit. It's a very good company. We have a lot of good orders awaited in that company. And before we acquired the company, it used to do a 4 crore sales and a 1cr of proﬁt after tax

items.statement: Combined acquisitions expected to add ~3 crores to H2 FY25 top line and ~1 crore to consolidated PBT by March 2025.
items.quote: As of now both together have a potential of adding approximately 3 crores odd to the second half year 24-25 top line and maybe a cr to the proﬁt before tax of the consolidated numbers of Sunita tools March 25

items.statement: Distributors appointed in Gulf region (Saudi Arabia, UAE); formalities underway with embassies; orders expected from new calendar year 2025.
items.quote: As we informed that we have appointed distributors agent in Gulf region that is primarily Saudi and UAE and they visited us inspected our facilities and the potential that we carry for them for their products they were highly impressed and we assumed to start to get orders from them in the new calendar year 2025 onwards.

items.statement: LOI signed for mould-based manufacturing company acquisition in Chennai to access auto cluster; initial due diligence done for potential US aerospace acquisitions.
items.quote: We have signed an LOI with a small mouldbased manufacturing company in Chennai to acquire the same and increase our manufacturing foothold in the south Indian market and the largest autocluster of the world.

items.statement: Aspiration to reach 25% revenue contribution from new businesses in next two to three years
items.quote: we are looking that in the next two to three years , we want to have a 25 -75 split with new businesses contributing around 25% of our top line

items.statement: Aspiration to reach 25% revenue contribution from new businesses in next two to three years
items.quote: the aspiration of the company is that we will walk towards a 25% and a 75% diversification in the next two to three years.

items.statement: Investing in new lines of business including data stack, open digital ecosystems, international expansion, cloud and infosec
items.quote: we are continuing to invest in these new lines of business. Our primary aim is to mature these businesses in the next three to five years and establish them as core contributors to our overall top line.

items.statement: 13 states integrated with Agri Stack, first phase live
items.quote: Currently, 13 states are already plugged in, and we are building from there.

items.statement: Adjusted operating profit grew 21% QoQ to INR 32 crores with 14.4% operating margin vs 13.3% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Adjusted operating profit, excluding other income and ECL provision for the quarter, grew by 21% quarter-on-quarter to INR32 crores, with operating margin of 14.4% versus 13.3% in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: International RFP bids target operating margins upwards of 20%
items.quote: we go in with a margin which is upwards of 20% in most of these mandates, and we pitch for them.

items.statement: Competitive pricing pressure at foundational eSign layer causing margin compression
items.quote: Additionally, we are facing competitive pricing at the foundational level for the eSign services.

items.statement: PAN penetration under 50% in India, strong headroom for growth driven by government schemes requiring PAN

items.statement: Technical textiles (100% man-made fabric) project first phase of 15 lakh meters/month targeting September-October 2025 start; projected PBDIT-to-sales 25-30%.
items.quote: So, we are dividing it into two phases. The first phase we are aiming for a capacity of 15 lakh meters per month. And our profitability of PBDIT to sales would be in the range of about 25%-30%.

items.statement: Fabric capacity expansion: solid dyed +20%, yarn dyed +20%, digital print added; solid dyed expansion operational in 14 months.
items.quote: So, our major is solid dyed. So, we are expanding solid dyed by 20% and this capacity should also be operational in the next 14 months. So, that is first. In yarn dyed also, we're expanding a bit, say around 20%.

items.statement: Fabric running at 100% capacity utilization; strong export order visibility through January and beyond; domestic demand okay post-festive season.
items.quote: We are running at 100% capacity utilization. So, that is the first indicator. And the second indicator is also that we have visibility of good orders up to Jan, and even further than

items.statement: Cotton yarn spread compressed to ~60 US cents/lb (down from 75-80 US cents in Q1) due to high Indian cotton cost (84-85 US cents/lb) vs global parity (~83-84 US cents/lb).
items.quote: The first quarter, almost the stress was in the range of about 75 -80 US cents, which now has come down to about 60 US cents.

items.statement: Indian cotton at 1,300 basis points over NY Future (~84-85 US cents/lb), equal to US cotton price but inferior quality; 11% import duty blocks cost arbitrage.
items.quote: Indian cotton is also available at 1300 on over New York future as of now. So, the price of Indian cotton and US cotton is almost comparable as of now.

items.statement: Next 1.5-2 months critical for CCI procurement policy and cotton arrivals; CCI holds ~1 million bales old stock, new season arrivals 60k-80k bales/day rising to 100k.
items.quote: And next 1.5-2 months is more critical from that perspective. It is one of the major component s of our cost and it definitely determines the profitability of the business for the next couple of months

items.statement: Recycling trends in West (EU law from 2025 banning landfill) may reduce virgin fiber demand long-term; Vardhman runs 6 tpd recycling line, adding another 6 tpd.
items.quote: Europe has passed a law starting next year 25, which will be landfilling through the garmenting is not possible or will not be allowed. So, it has to be recycled, or it has to be resold.

items.statement: Fabric share of topline growing from current ~35%; garmenting remains small (6,000 to 10,000 shirts/day) with no big expansion plan due to labor cost/availability.
items.quote: If you look at the topline today, it's almost 65-35 in favor of spinning and fabric. And I think in the times to come if the situation on the spinning side doesn't improve, the expansion on the spinning side may be low and we may continue to grow on the fabric side.

items.statement: Garmenting labor cost $230-240/month vs Bangladesh ~$120; attrition 5-6%/month; MGNREGA and other schemes reduce migrant labor willingness.
items.quote: The cost of labor in India is not less than $230 to $240 per person as of now. As the Bangladesh cost is still about 11,000-12,000 Taka which is equivalent to about $120.

items.statement: Net cash ~Rs 2,300 crore; debt ~Rs 1,000 crore.
items.quote: It is almost Rs. 2300 crores. And the debt is about Rs. 1000 crores.

items.statement: Green energy share ~5% of consumption; aggressive plan to reach 25% in 2 years, possibly 40%; targeting 15-20% ROCE on each project.
items.quote: In the next 2 years, we are trying to reach from 4%-5% to at least 25% of the green energy in next 2 years. And maybe there could be a possibility that we will be crossing this 25% to even 40% also.

items.statement: Home textile players running full capacity, especially sheeting; yarn demand from them doing well.
items.quote: Home textile players are doing reasonably well in India. So, if I look at most of them are running full capacity especially on the sheeting side is doing pretty well, even on the yarn side is doing well.

items.statement: Industry estimates >6 million spindles permanently stopped in last 2 years; another 2.5-3 million running on job-work/marginal basis; utilization ~80-85% of ~47-48 million active spindles.
items.quote: As per the industry estimates, it is estimated almost 6 mill ion spindles have stopped permanently, more than 6 million, and maybe another 3 million spindles are running on job or on a marginal basis.

items.statement: No quantitative sales volume guidance for next 12 months; demand increasing daily, capacity additions (mostly complete by June 2025) needed to capture further volume.
items.quote: As of now, we will not be in a position to give as numbers because the demand is coming every day, is increasing every month, every day. So, I think we are only expecting that we require to create that capacity so that further demand could come.

items.statement: Expect 10-11% volume CAGR in carbon black over next 5 years
items.quote: We are very confident that growing at 10%-11% volume CAGR in the next 5 years is not going to be much of a challenge for us, we just need to have capacities.

items.statement: Carbon black capacity expansion of 430,000 tonnes by 2029 with Rs. 2,500-2,600 crore capex
items.quote: So, if we grow at about 10%-11% every year, by 2029 we will require another 430,000 tonnes of capacity, which will involve a CAPEX of about Rs. 2,500-. 2,600 crores, and that's the number that we shared during the last call.

items.statement: Aquapharm capex of Rs. 600-700 crore over next 3-5 years for India and USA
items.quote: We expect to invest roughly around anywhere between Rs. 600-700 crore over the period of next three to five years, between Aquapharm India and USA.

items.statement: Specialty carbon black 20,000 MTPA at Mundra and 30,000 MTPA brownfield at Tamil Nadu commissioning in Q3 FY25
items.quote: PCBL expects to commission the specialty project o f 20,000 MTPA in Mundra and 30,000 MTPA brownfield expansion of carbon black facility in PCBL, Tamil Nadu i n Q3 FY '25

items.statement: Aquapharm expansion of 38,000 MTPA likely to commission by March 2025
items.quote: Aquapharm Chemicals is implementing an expansion project of 38,000 MTPA, which is likely to be commissioned by March 2025.

items.statement: Target 1 million tonnes carbon black capacity by FY27-28, possibly surpassing target
items.quote: We aim to reach 1 million tonnes capacity in carbon black by FY '27 -'28, possibly we will surpass this target as well.

items.statement: Carbon black EBITDA per tonne at Rs. 21,324 sustainable with cushion to improve further
items.quote: We not only believe that these margins are sustainable, but we also believe there is a fair level of cushion for us to go up on margins as our product mix change s, as our operating leverage improves

items.statement: Aquapharm targeting 20% EBITDA margin from next year, improving to 25% by FY29
items.quote: We believe that from next year itself we will have around 20% EBITDA margin, which will gradually improve towards 25% by FY '29.

items.statement: Specialty carbon black volume to double in 4-5 years with 10,000 MT annual additions
items.quote: Specialty will become almost double in the next four to five years' time, but this portfolio will increase by about 60-65%. So, the volume growth is on the entire pie.

items.statement: Export share to Europe increased from 3.5-4% in FY22 to ~21% currently, constrained by capacity
items.quote: In FY '22 it was only about 3.5-4%, currently we are doing close to 21% in those markets and the scope is much, much better, we are constrained by capacity.

items.statement: Nanovace commercial plant of 2,000 tonnes in FY27 targeting Rs. 2,000 crore revenue at $100/kg
items.quote: Even at $100 /kg revenue, this 2,000 tonnes capacity will generate a Rs. 2,000 crore s top line. So, that's kind of, and we believe that once this plant comes up, which should be in FY '27, it will not take us more than couple of years' time to utilize full capacity

items.statement: Nanovace targeting ~50% EBITDA margin on commercial plant with 65% gross margin potential
items.quote: Could be around 50%. Because it's a small capacity, we do not see any kind of elevated fixed overhead structure here. It will be a very lean structure. So, around 50% should flow to EBITDA level.

items.statement: US oil & gas market for Aquapharm in rough patch, demand down substantially, expanding to Europe to derisk
items.quote: The US market from the point of view of oil and gas sectors is going through a very, very rough patch in recent times, and the demand has come down substantially.

items.statement: Aquapharm top line growth of 17-18% from FY26 onwards
items.quote: Growth in terms of top line, we believe that we can grow at around 17-18% from FY '26 onwards.

items.statement: PCBL infusing $44 million in Nanovace over next two years for IP, pilot plant and commercial facility
items.quote: PCBL would infuse $44 million in Nanovace in multiple stages over the next two years for acquiring IPs, setting up pilot plant, and thereafter commercial scale manufacturing facility.

items.statement: Jindal Supreme deployed with ONGC on 15 October 2024 at $88,859 day rate, ahead of November timeline
items.quote: This rig commenced operations on 15 October 2024, which is ahead of the deployment timeline given earlier of November 2024.

items.statement: Jindal Pioneer acquisition in final stage, awaiting statutory approval, expected shortly
items.quote: Further, we are in the final stage of acquisition of rig Jindal Pioneer and are still awaiting approval from statutory authorities.

items.statement: Earnings will improve immediately on acquisition of Jindal Pioneer rig
items.quote: Earnings will improve immediately on acquisition of the said rig.

items.statement: Jindal Supreme new day rate $88,859 vs previous $40,700, incremental rate flows to EBITDA
items.quote: Originally, the rig was deployed at $40,700 in the previous contract, which concluded in March 2024. From 15th October 2024, it has been deployed on the new contract at $88,859.

items.statement: Bulk of incremental day rate on Jindal Supreme will flow down to EBITDA as company-owned rig
items.quote: Should I say bulk of it will flow down to the EBITDA? Kaushal Bengani: Yes

items.statement: Jindal Supreme refurbishment cost over INR130 crores due to MODU standard change, amortized over 3 years
items.quote: For Jindal Supreme, the total refurbishment expenditure is more than INR130 crores. That is because there was a change in the MODU standard as per the safety requirement.

items.statement: Debt at INR173 crores, will reduce to INR132 crores by March 2025, then INR66 crores each next two years
items.quote: Considering the cash flows that we have right now debt position is at INR 173 crores. This will reduce to INR132 crores as on 31st March 2025 and thereafter the repayment schedule is INR 66 crores each in the next two financial years.

items.statement: Jindal Explorer contract ends May 2025, ONGC to issue two tenders before year end, expect to participate
items.quote: Explorer is going to end contracts in May 25. ONGC is in talks for getting two new tenders before the year ends. So, hopefully, we will be participating in both those tenders and expect to gain the contract.

items.statement: Explorer renewal rate benchmark USD 64,000, expect to maintain or get slightly better given improved international market
items.quote: The latest contract was at USD 64000 something. So USD 64000 being the benchmark with ONGC being the last contract.

items.statement: No significant one-off expenses expected in next four quarters for current assets
items.quote: I don't believe there are any significant one-offs expected going forward, but that by nature is the definition of one-off that you cannot predict them.

items.statement: Strong global demand for rigs, especially with war continuing, prices increasing internationally
items.quote: No, we do not see any risk because there is a lot of demand worldwide, especially with the war and everything, the prices are going up again, and hopefully it is a great market to be in.

items.statement: Rig segment contributes almost 90% of total EBITDA, focus area for growth
items.quote: The EBITDA mix has been g iven on slide 10 wherein you will note that the rig segment contributes to almost 90% of total EBITDA and that is the area of focus where we want to grow further

items.statement: Net cash position improved from INR51 crores to INR69 crores, will improve rapidly with cash generation
items.quote: Our net cash position has improved from INR51 crores to INR69 crores.

items.statement: Net debt-free status targeted by end of next quarter (Q3 FY25)
items.quote: As we discussed in our previous update, we remain firmly on track of achieving a net debt -free status by the end of next quarte r, a key strategic objective for Anant Raj Limited

items.statement: Cloud capex estimated at INR 100 crores per megawatt additional to co-location capex of INR 26 crores per megawatt
items.quote: Yes, sir. The co-location is INR26 crores and an additional INR100 crores, sir.

items.statement: 28 MW data center capacity fully tied up with clients by FY25 end
items.quote: Completely tied up, sir, fully tied up, sir. We will divert around 25% of t his towards our cloud business, but then we will catch up very fast because the work will continue and by next year we will be almost 63 megawatts

items.statement: Cloud infrastructure-as-a-service EBITDA estimated at INR 126 crores per MW per year (INR 150 crores revenue minus INR 24 crores operating cost)
items.quote: So we are talking about a running cost of about INR2 crores per month, which is INR24 crores. So your EBITDA is about INR 126 crores. So INR150 crores minus INR24 crores is your EBITDA in this situation.

items.statement: Strong demand for cloud services; 0.5 MW pilot fully subscribed with revenues starting from Oct 7
items.quote: The good part about cloud is that your rentals start from day one. Co-location, you know, things take time because the facilities are made, then you hand it over, then the servers start to come in. But this year, in this case, your revenues start from day one itself. So in this case, the revenues have actually started from 7th of October, sir.

items.statement: Plan to allocate 14 MW out of 63 MW (25%) to cloud by FY26, rest to co-location
items.quote: Out of 63, 14 will go, which is almost about 25%. So we plan to maintain the same ratio.

items.statement: Fundraise of INR 2,100 crores (INR 100 crore promoter, INR 2,000 crore market) primarily for data center cloud expansion
items.quote: As of now, this fundraising is completely focused. It's going to be INR2100 crores out of which promoters are going to put in 100 and we will go to the market for the balance 2000. The main focus of this fundraising is going to be for the data center business.

items.statement: Target 63 MW total data center capacity by March 2026 (FY26) from current 6 MW
items.quote: In the coming year, and we are almost there at 28 now, so in the coming year, we plan to add another 35, taking the toll to 63 megawatts.

items.statement: No license cancelled; only 1,000 sq yards restricted from third-party rights in Gurugram court matter
items.quote: No license whatsoever has been cancelled. Only 1,000 square yards has been said that the company should not create any third-party right, which the company as it is not going to do, sir.

items.statement: Group housing project launch scheduled for January 2025 after election code of conduct lifted
items.quote: Fully on track, we will do it in January. Prateek Singh: In January. Okay. Understood, sir. Thank you, sir. Amit Sarin: There was an election, so there was a code of conduct. So that is all done now. So Haryana, as you know, went in for elections. It is all done. So now things are back on track. So we will do it in

items.statement: Co-location EBITDA margin ~82% (INR 8 crores revenue, 18% operating expenses)
items.quote: In this quarter, we have done INR8 crores revenue and the operational expenses is around 18%. So, it is around 82%.

items.statement: Commercial leasing revenue expected to triple in next two years from current INR 12.5 crores per quarter
items.quote: Coming two years, the commercial revenue will at least, although future numbers we should not be giving like this, but the revenues from here will at least go close to two and a half to three times.

items.statement: 20 acres land acquired in Gurgaon at average INR 20 crores per acre for 3 million sq ft saleable area
items.quote: So we spend about INR20 crores an acre if we translate it in the money terms, average for this.

items.statement: Cloud services launched as infrastructure-as-a-service; platform-as-a-service and software-as-a-service planned next
items.quote: Basically, sir, what we've done is we've started with a private cloud and almost 50% of whatever we've set up right now, and the remaining 50% is for a government community cloud, which actually qualifies as a sovereign cloud.

items.statement: Real estate launches of 1.8 million sq ft on track for FY25
items.quote: If we talk about this year sir, we are going to be launching 1.8 million square feet. We are fully on track for that. So that is all on the decided dates. It will all happen.

items.statement: Management expects 18% year-on-year revenue growth for next three years, targeting ₹350 crores by FY27 with higher margins
items.quote: we'll be growing at a rate of 18% year-on-year for the next three years. That is our estimate, of course. We don't know what happens in future, but that is our estimate, and we will try and see that we reach those targets. Maybe we'll be reaching almost ₹350 crores in '26, '27 with higher margins as compared to the current margins.

items.statement: Current margins above 21%, expected to reach 22% next year and 23% in FY27; 6-7% price hike pending from customers after September
items.quote: Margins as it is, it is more than 20% now. It is almost 21%. And what I feel that next year, it will go up to 22%, and thereafter in '26-'27, it will lead to 23%.

items.statement: Export orders strong from USA, Dubai, African countries; Japan orders reduced substantially; industrial segment (compressors, generators, steel) growing and will continue
items.quote: So far as export growth is concerned, it will continue to be like that in future as well, because what we see for this quarter as well, the export orders are very good. So far as VAC is concerned as well as for African countries to Dubai. Though orders from Japan have reduced substantially, USA that's giving a good growth for us.

items.statement: No additional capex required for German luxury car, airport, or railway business; existing expanded capacity can accommodate
items.quote: There is no additional CapEx required for that business because in the existing capacities, we can accommodate that which has been already under expansion.

items.statement: Revenue target of approximately INR2,500 crores for FY25 with expected EBITDA margin of about 15% to 16%
items.quote: We are opt imistic about achieving our esteemed revenue -- our stated revenue target of approximately INR25 crores (Errata: Actual number to be read as INR2,500 crores ) for financial year '25 with an expected EBITDA margin of about 15% to 16

items.statement: Expect 50% top line growth in FY26 over FY25 with EBITDA margin maintained at 15%-16%
items.quote: So in terms of the guidance, earlier also we said this -- we expect a 50% growth in the top line and we maintain the same EBITDA level of 15% - 16%.

items.statement: Total order book including all SPVs and GIC platform stands at about INR31,776 crores net of taxes for 8-10 year concessions
items.quote: As on 30th September 2024, our total order book, including all SPVs and GIC platform, stands at about INR31,776 c rores net of taxes, and these concessions are for eight to 10

items.statement: Total equity outlay for Genus in GIC platform around $210 million; 40% of remaining to be invested in FY26, 40% in FY27, balance in FY28
items.quote: We have to understand that the total outlay of Genus will be around $210 million and right-now its hardly $2 million or $3 million that has been invested by Genus. So next year, it will be around 40% of the remaining what we have committed will be there and next year, again, a 40% number will be there.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 724 bps to 16.7% in Q2 FY25; anticipate sustaining operating margins at similar levels going forward
items.quote: Our EBITDA for Q2 was INR81 c rore, up by 232% compared to INR25 crore in Q2 '24. The EBITDA margin improved by 724 basis points to 16.7%, driven by the positive impact of operating leverage

items.statement: No live tenders currently; order book not expected to increase for next 6-8 months; new tenders expected from Q1 FY26 as 40% market remains uncovered
items.quote: Currently, there are no live tenders in the market. So I don't see that order book increasing for next six to eight months. I don't see this as a peak because only 60% of the countr y is covered under the smart meters in terms of either tenders have been floated, orders have been decided, few tenders are still running. So 40% of the market is still remaining, which I feel will start -- tenders wil

items.statement: Order book split: 45-50% meter supply and installation, 25-30% O&M, 20-25% remains with platform; 90% of order book from platform
items.quote: So, in the total order book, whatever we are supplying to the platform, that order book can be divided into three parts. So, around 45% - 50% is the meter supply and installation, 25% - 30% is O&M, because different contracts have different pricing, and 20% - 25% remains with the platform.

items.statement: Manufacturing expansion on track; new Guwahati plant almost started, will be in full swing in one month; will comfortably manufacture 1 million meters monthly
items.quote: The new plant in Gu wahati is already started -- almost started and it will be in full swing in next one month. So that the expansion plan is more or less on under the place, and we will be comfortably manufacturing 1 million meters every month

items.statement: Working capital inflated due to project ramp-up; receivables high as projects under FIT/SAT take 90-120 days to go live; expect normalization in 6-9 months
items.quote: These receivables are very high because the arrangement with the platform is, once we install the meters, we have to do the site acceptance test. And once the site acceptance test is done, the project goes on live. And when the project goes live, then you start receiving the ca pex payment from the platform. And all this process takes minimum 90 days to 120 days

items.statement: Long-term debt increased to INR494 crores for Bihar project on Genus balance sheet; company policy to maintain cash buffer for growth
items.quote: So whatever this long term debt that has been in creased is for the Bihar project, which is the company is doing on Genus Power balance sheet. There is only one project which is being done and this is a one and a half year old project with Genus

items.statement: Employee expenses to grow for next 6-8 months then stagnate; interest cost expected around INR135-150 crores for FY26
items.quote: If not INR150 crores, INR140 crores, INR135 crores will be a good number.

items.statement: Export business slow in H1 FY25; good traction with large potential customers; expect significant shape from Q4 FY25 onwards
items.quote: So the export run rate is a bit slow in the first two quarters of this financial year. And in terms of inquiries, we are working on some large potential customers and we see -- and there is a very good trac tion. So we see export business also getting a very good shape from fourth quarter onwards

items.statement: Water meter projects have 3-4 year gestation; expect significant revenue contribution in 3-4 years; gas meter business focused on domestic market, regular supplier for 2-3 years
items.quote: But you will see the significant numbers coming from these projects after three to four years. It is not going to happen something tomorrow. But yes, we are on the right path. We are very confident that water will become a very significant portion of our business in next three to four years.

items.statement: Maintained FY25 volume growth guidance of EXIM 15%, Domestic 25%, Total 18%
items.quote: At this point I would like to maintain the guidance that I gave at the start of the financial year, that is for EXIM 15%, Domestic 25%, and a total of 18%.

items.statement: LLF guidance for FY25 in range of Rs 350-400 crore
items.quote: That will be in the range of 350-400 crores, not more than that.

items.statement: Capex budget of Rs 610 crore for FY25, Rs 276.16 crore achieved in H1, may upgrade budget
items.quote: We had earmarked the CAPEX budget of Rs. 610 crores for this financial year. In the first half, we have already achieved Rs. 276.16 crores, and we may be looking at the CAPEX budget very soon, whether we want to upgrade it, seeing the infrastructure requirements of the company.

items.statement: Rail freight margin grew 80 bps YoY to 27.85% in H1 FY25; operating margin ex-exceptional grew 95 bps YoY
items.quote: Rail freight margin grew by 80 basis points year-on-year. Operating margin excluding exceptional items grew by 95 basis Container Corporation of points year-on-year

items.statement: Confident of maintaining 25% EBITDA margin including other income
items.quote: I am quite confident that 25% EBITDA levels can be maintained by the company.

items.statement: Domestic loading picked up nicely from October, expecting very good growth in Q3
items.quote: But I am happy to announce that from this month, it has picked up very nicely, and we are getting very good growth in domestic in Q3.

items.statement: Rice exports showing strong demand at ICDs Nagpur, Raipur, Sonipat; traction to pick up after Diwali
items.quote: Then we have very good demand for rice exports now, and especially at our ICDs at Nagpur, Raipur, Sonipat, etc. And we hope that in the coming months, already actually rice exports have started. After Diwali the traction is going to pick up.

items.statement: Double-stack trains grew 11.5% YoY to 3,083 in H1 FY25; 70-75% of DFC volume now double-stacked
items.quote: In this first half, we had 3,083 double-stack trains as compared to 2,766 last year.

items.statement: Varnama terminal near Baroda to be commissioned by November-end for double-stack to JNPT via DFC
items.quote: By November end, I am confident that we will be able to start this service, wherein we will give benefit of double-stacking to North India customers for Nhava Sheva traffic.

items.statement: Tank containers for bulk cement movement expected from Braithwaite by December; targeting cement manufacturers
items.quote: I had a meeting recently with CMD of M/s Braithwaite Corporation, which is a sister PSU of CONCOR under Ministry of Railways, and he has assured me that by December he will start giving us tank containers, which will be utilized for bulk cement movement.

items.statement: No price hikes in EXIM; domestic pricing dynamic, tweaked rates positively in some streams from October
items.quote: No, EXIM we have not undertaken any price hikes because railways also not revised the prices, and domestic also we keep on changing. As such we have not done any, not across the board increase and we keep on revisiting because domestic is a dynamic pricing kind of thing.

items.statement: Signed and signing 3-5 year volume-based discount agreements with shipping lines including Maersk
items.quote: We are also, we have signed, and we are still signing agreements of volume-based discounts with shipping lines, long-term agreements, 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: Red Sea disruption causing erratic vessel schedules, congestion at transshipment ports, less slot availability for exports
items.quote: International, as you all know, because of the challenging geopolitical scenario, international supply chains are adversely affected. This has resulted in erratic vessel schedules. There is congestion at transshipment ports, and there is less availability of slots in vessels for exports.

items.statement: JNPT rail coefficient at 16% (CONCOR share 58%); cargo shifting to Mundra due to double-stack benefit and shorter distance
items.quote: JNPT rail coefficient at present is around 16% in which CONCOR'S share is 58% for the first half of this financial year. The main reason is that lot of cargo has, for North India, lot of cargo has shifted to Mundra Port, which is giving a benefit of double-stacks.

items.statement: First LNG pump in North India to be commissioned mid-November at MMLP Kathuwas; 130 LNG trucks deployed, 200 more being procured
items.quote: The first LNG pump in North India of our country is going to be commissioned this month only, sorry, next month in November, mid November at our MMLP Kathuwas.

items.statement: Targeting 50% first-mile-last-mile penetration in FY25 (currently 27-30%), 80% target for next financial year
items.quote: In this financial year FY '25, we are targeting 50% of our business that we are giving should be on first mile, last mile. So, at present on pan-India basis around 27% to 30% we are able to achieve in the first half of this financial year, and we are continuously working to improve it and achieve the target of 50%, and next financial year we will set up a target of 80% of our volume should be firs

items.statement: Target to cross INR30,000 crores AUM by FY27
items.quote: We are well positioned to drive growth and are confident of crossing our target of INR30,000 crores AUM by FY '27.

items.statement: Expect to achieve mid-teen ROE by March 2027
items.quote: And I think by March '27, we should achieve our mid-teen ROE target.

items.statement: Insurance distribution fee income expected to cross INR40 crores in FY25
items.quote: We are looking to generate around INR40 crores in net fee income from insurance distribution in FY '25.

items.statement: Rooftop solar loan book target of INR1,000 crores; INR50 crores by year-end, INR300 crores next year
items.quote: In near term, we should be able to achieve the INR1,000 crore book, the first target is INR1,000 crores book. But by the March, we will be able to give you the clear guidance by when it will be achieved.

items.statement: Plan to add 50-70 gold loan branches in FY25
items.quote: We'll be adding about 50 -70 branches this year.

items.statement: Spread maintained at 7%; NIM may decrease with higher leverage but ROE to improve
items.quote: Currently, NIM margin, you see the decrease because the leverage is going up. If you look at the spread, that is being maintained at 7%.

items.statement: Micro LAP book at INR30 crores; target INR60 crores by March, INR300 crores next year
items.quote: We currently have already received a book of about INR30 crores. And by March, we should be able to cross about INR60 crores. Next year is something which we are likely to cross about INR300 crores.

items.statement: Gold loan monetization at 5%; huge growth potential as most market with pawn brokers and local jewelers
items.quote: We see the data, monetization is still in the range of 5%. And most of the market is still with the pawn brokers and local jewelers and local money lenders. So there's a huge growth possible for everybody in this segment.

items.statement: Launched rooftop solar loans (INR50,000-25 lakh) with Credit Fair; also Micro LAP in MSME
items.quote: in this quarter, we launched rooftop solar loan s, part of green financing in partnership with Credit Fair, a leading renewable energy fintech, with ticket size ranging from about INR50,000 to INR25

items.statement: Board resolution to raise up to INR1,000 crores via NCD issuance
items.quote: As part of our resource diversification strategy, we have taken Board resolution to raise up to INR1,000 crores via NCD issuance.

items.statement: CRF components account for ~13.6% of a wagon's value; full fabrication scope raises this to 20-21%.

items.statement: NCLT process for Amzen acquisition has already taken four years; outcome uncertain but management remains committed.

items.statement: Consolidated financials reflect true performance; management insists on >51% ownership to consolidate subsidiaries.

items.statement: Order book maintained at ~1x annual revenue; management avoids overbooking beyond executable capacity.

items.statement: Management expects 30% year-on-year revenue growth for FY25 and the next three years.
items.quote: So, year-on-year, we can assume that, we can grow at 30% at revenue level.

items.statement: Second half FY25 revenue expected between ₹115 crore and ₹130 crore.
items.quote: Yeah. ₹115 Cr to ₹130 Cr is, I think we are hoping for.

items.statement: Existing installed capacity can achieve ₹400-425 crore annual revenue within two years.

items.statement: Company invested ₹60 crore in building, plant, machinery and solar rooftop over the last 1.5 years.

items.statement: New PEB plant with 1,000 metric ton per month capacity to be built this year.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margin to remain at current levels with potential 1-2% improvement from new plant.

items.statement: Demand for PVC furniture is stable and growing driven by real estate growth and government housing initiatives.

items.statement: No slowdown in demand; equal demand from new housing and renovation segments.
items.quote: There is equal demand for that. But we are also targeting renovation, with existing customers who have installed wood furniture in their house.

items.statement: SPC flooring machinery acquired, production to start in November; uPVC window installation plant started in September.
items.quote: In this period of the first half, we have started uPVC window installation plant, work of PEB that is existing its capacity is 300 metric ton per month, selling off HVLS fans and acquired the machinery of SPC flooring

items.statement: PVC furniture is generally 20-25% cheaper than wood panel alternatives.
items.quote: It depends, but generally, you can say 20% to 25% will be cheaper in PVC.

items.statement: Advertising spend budgeted at 5-6% of sales; currently using shutter painting, hoardings, radio and movie partnerships.
items.quote: Percentage of sales, you can say 5% to 6%.

items.quote: So now our installed capacity has been increased to 54,000 metric ton per annum from 20,500 metric ton per annum at company level. And the actual achievable capacity is increased to 37,500 metric ton per annum.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved 1.1% sequentially to 54.8%
items.quote: EBITDA margins came in at 54.8% , an improvement of 1.1% .

items.statement: Operating free cash flow (EBITDA minus capex) highest ever at Rs.11,000 Crores; capex for quarter was Rs.6,260 Crores

items.quote: So yes the amortization should flatten off, subject to the millimeter growth. Other than that as I said there is no CWIP so whatever you see in Q3 should be the run rate of amortization for Bharti Hexacom going forward.

items.quote: We believe that the industry is still delivering sub 7% ROCE and this needs to substantially increase. Our investments are channelized towards building Airtel into a strong digital services player.

items.quote: The company has incurred a capital expenditure payment of INR62 crores in FY24 and INR27 crores in H1 of FY25.

items.quote: The pending order as on 1st of October 2014 was INR619 crores out of which domestic cable orders was INR427 crores and the export orders were INR192 crores pending.

items.quote: To summarize, content 10%-12%, platform 12%-14%, and then eLearning 14%-15% organic growth.

items.quote: Most of our reinvestment goes into MPS Labs, which is our R&D hub. And that allows us to future-proof ourselves but also allows us to future-proof our customers.
