items.statement: Price drop impact of almost 3% still affecting revenue growth
items.quote: Because of the price drop at the beginning of the year, there's still an impact of almost close to 3%.

items.statement: No price cuts planned due to volatile raw material costs and currency
items.quote: So keeping this in mind, I don't think we are looking at price cuts at this point of time because I think that will be naive because then you will have to take significant price increases next year to cover the cost of any wage inflation and other things t hat you -- NFT or whatever you ask, right

items.statement: EBIT margin guidance maintained with only 0.5% depletion depending on competitive intensity
items.quote: I stick to the EBIT margin guidances that I've always given. We don't want to deplete our profitability other than 0.5% type of stuff depending on competitive intensity.

items.statement: A&P spend to increase from 2.5-3% to 3.5-4% of revenue with initiatives from January and more pronounced by March
items.quote: A&P, we have been hovering around the 2.5% to 3% of revenue. As I said, our stated intent is to go closer to 3.5%, 4%. You will see various initiatives that Rohit and team will deploying starting January, more pronounced towards March next year.

items.statement: B2B growth driven by focused order book work across businesses
items.quote: I think it's also because we've focused and we've been working hard on our order book across our businesses, right? So I think that with a specific focus in certain sectors is giving us better growth.

items.statement: Collections and overdues becoming challenging across industry due to money crunch
items.quote: We believe that in this industry and many of the other peer industries, overdue and collections have become a bit of a challenging because of some money crunch that we observed in the market.

items.statement: Inventory built up to INR 741 crores ahead of festive season, expected to normalize in 30-45 days
items.quote: The inventory buildup is predominantly ahead of the festive season. We beefed up the inventory, and that has resulted in a spike in inventory, as of 30th September, we were at INR741 crores. It will get normalized over a period of 1 month to 45 days period.

items.statement: Distribution expansion targeting 5,700-6,000 towns in next couple of quarters
items.quote: We are on the anvil of getting close to 5,700 to 6,000 towns between -- in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Competitive intensity increased in decorative B2C after new entrant, discounts marginally up
items.quote: So the answer on competitive intensity is, of course, it's increased. I mean, frankly, it has increased over the last 6 months after the new entrant has come in.

items.statement: Management hopes to cross 10% volume growth for FY25
items.quote: I think this year also we hope to cross 10%.

items.statement: Finished good prices dropped 5-6% while raw material prices dropped 3-4%, squeezing margins by about 2 percentage points half-year to half-year
items.quote: So, the finished good prices have dropped a little more than the raw material prices over the period half year to half year. And therefore, the margins have got squeezed by about 2% at points. So, say the finished good prices have dropped by an average of 5%-6% but the raw material prices have dropped 3%-4%.

items.statement: Focus will be on volume over margins in H2, but management tries to expand margins; difficult to predict where margins will land
items.quote: Well, it's difficult to say at this point in time whether we will be able to. We are always optimistic that we will try to improve the margin, but we don't want to sacrifice volume because of it. So, our focus will be more volume than margins, but of course at the same time, we try to expand the margins. But it's difficult to say where we will in the end land up. Hopefully, better margins and bett

items.statement: New CAPEX of 225 crores (now likely higher) for a new import-substitute product at Dahej; first phase in 15 months, potential debottlenecking in 3-4 years
items.quote: No, this is a part of that 225 crores project. The other part we are still on the R&D stage. This is one of the two lines of products which we were looking at that time. And in the meantime, of course, costs of plant and machinery have got up. So, I think that 225 crores was an underestimate. So, whenever it comes up, it will be probably more than that. But of course, it's been delayed a bit.

items.statement: FY25 CAPEX around 80-100 crores; FY26 CAPEX around 100-120 crores
items.quote: This year it will be around 80 to 100 crores, and next year may be a slightly larger, about 100 to 120 crores may be.

items.statement: Pharma inventory issues easing; agrochemicals remain under pressure from Chinese cost competition and inventory overhang
items.quote: I would like to say at a macro level, the issues which we had a couple of years back in terms of the so much of inventory in the pipeline and things like this, within pharma sector we see that this seems to be easing a little bit because the other part of the life science, which is the agro-chemical segment still continue to remain under pressure both from the inventory point of view and also from

items.statement: Monoisopropylamine volumes under pressure from Chinese imports; applied for government protection, decision expected in 9-12 months
items.quote: First question about the Monoisopropylamine, yes, the issues which we pointed out six months ago still continue. We haven't yet received any protection from the government against the Chinese imports. We have applied very recently for protection, and we hope over the next maybe 9 to 12 months, we will get some protection. But till then the pressure on Monoisopropylamine will continue.

items.statement: Life sciences accounts for 65-70% of turnover; domestic-export split ~80-20; pharma share growing over agrochemicals long-term
items.quote: They haven't changed at all from our regular life sciences accounting for 65%-70% of our turnover and the rest all, as you can see from our website or wherever, it doesn't change dramatically. Even the domestic export sectors are more or less the same 80-20.

items.statement: Coal cost stable at Rs 9,000-10,000 per metric ton (+/-10% over two years); ammonia prices may see slight bump due to Middle East crisis but planned month-to-month; ethanol imports cheaper than domestic, covered for 5-6 months
items.quote: Yes, the coal is Rs. 9, Rs. 10 Kg. Yes, we of course look at metric ton. So, Rs. 9,000 to Rs. 10,000 a metric ton.

items.statement: Acetonitrile market ~30,000 tons; company market share ~50-55%; utilization ~60% across two plants
items.quote: So, I think the market share remains in that region. As earlier stated by, I think, Nirav, that the market is in the region of 30,000, and you can see that the imports are coming in from the Chinese. So, we are in that region.

items.statement: Existing capacity utilization 65-70% on average; ethylamine plant has headroom for 3-4 years; new CAPEX will not detract from existing lines
items.quote: The existing capacities on average would be 65% to 70% utilization, but it varies from product to product. Some we have very tight where we will be de-bottlenecking and there is some CAPEX involved with that. But of the major products, as we have known the Ethylamines last year, we commissioned the huge plant. So, there is plenty of headroom in Ethyl. And similarly, the other products, we have som

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty investigation on acetonitrile ongoing; MoC plant investigation and costing records review next, then MoF decision in 3-4 months; total 4-5 months expected
items.quote: So, after oral hearing now they will come for investigation of our plant and as well as costing records, and then MoC will issue their findings. After that, MoF generally takes 3 to 4 months. Next 4 to 5 months we should expect something.

items.statement: Chinese overcapacity and weak global agrochemical demand driving pricing pressure across value chain; normalization timeline uncertain
items.quote: Yes, I think it is more of a capacity expansion issue. There are overcapacities. They have put on more capacities in the last few years, and the demand has really not picked up too so that all those capacities are utilized, and we see such an immense pressure across the value chain.

items.statement: DEK plant utilization not yet improved as expected but management more optimistic; worst period likely over
items.quote: The utilization rate has not improved as much as we expected to, but going forward, we think it will improve even further. And hopefully, the worst period is over, and we are lot more optimistic on the product now than we were before.

items.statement: Ethylamine plant campaign-based operation runs at 100% when running; no meaningful efficiency gain from higher utilization at contribution margin level
items.quote: No, you have to understand how our plants operate. Our plants are campaign based. So, when they run, they run at 100% capacity, and then we shut down and start. So, there is no question of improvement in efficiencies as such. So, utilization occupancy keeps going up.

items.statement: Working capital cycle stabilized; no significant change expected in working capital requirements
items.quote: I think the working capital cycle, number of days of debtors, number of days of creditors and all have, I think, more or less stabilized, maybe an improvement marginally as volumes go, but nothing significant. I don't think there will be any change in working capital.

items.statement: No CAPEX guidance for FY27; too far out
items.quote: No guidance. We are too far off.

items.statement: Expect to reverse slow call-offs before March 2025 as customers remain committed to orders
items.quote: However, we expect to reverse the situat ion before March of 2025 as the customers remain committed to their orders

items.statement: Expect to end FY25 on a higher note than FY24 in sales
items.quote: Basically, our hope is that we are actually going to be ending this year on a higher note than what we did last year.

items.statement: Expect tomato tonnage close to last year or slightly better
items.quote: But in terms of tonnage also, we are trying to expect to do somewhere close to what we did last year or maybe slightly better.

items.statement: Expect Q4 FY25 to be a power play with growth vs Q4 FY24; Q3 may not be great
items.quote: So, by Q4, you can actually expect a growth as compared to what we did in Q4 of last year. Q3 might again not be that great is what our indications are.

items.statement: Tomato processing capacity more than doubled; new capacity going on stream this month
items.quote: We have more than doubled our tomato processing capacity as we also mentioned about this in the previous conference call and that capacity is going on stream this month.

items.statement: Planning to expand pastry line by adding two more lines in immediate future
items.quote: We are planning to expand the pastry line further by adding two more lines in the immediate future.

items.statement: Capex is already over apart from pastry line expansion and replacement capex
items.quote: as far as we are considering now, then the capex is already over. Apart from the pastry line that we have actually guided you for, I don't think there is any further capex that we would be doing apart from the replacement capex and a few here and th ere small investments that we would be doing

items.statement: Order position almost similar to last year or better; no reduction in order booking
items.quote: However, due to the d emand/supply situation in Indian beverage industry as well as across the globe, due to some freight issue, non-availability of the vessels, there is some delay in the shipment, which is a major cause for -- I mean, one of the major cause for the slightly lower sales relation. Otherwise, order position is almost similar like last year or better than last year

items.statement: Larger brands agreed to pay additional inventory carrying cost for delayed call-offs
items.quote: Since there is a delay, one of the major brands who consume hug e products from us, they have agreed to give an additional inventory carrying

items.statement: Expect good movement of stock in domestic market after a couple of flat months
items.quote: We are expecting as per the customer's shipment plan or dispatch plan , it will be a flat for a couple of months more. And after that, we are expecting a good m ovement of the stock in domestic market specifically

items.statement: Expect bumper summer sales in domestic beverage sector; brands bullish on Q4
items.quote: They are very bullish that this summer there will be a bumper sale in this sector.

items.statement: Major growth potential beyond mango from tomato and frozen segments; spice to contribute in couple of years
items.quote: So, major growth potential other than mango may come from the two segments. One is the tomato and other is definitely from the frozen segment. Spice is also in our focus. We have started spice in the retail market in Delhi region and Mumbai region. As you know, penetration is a little slow. But it has its own teething problem, which we are trying to overcome. And we hope that in the near future, m

items.statement: Pectin JV commercial run started; revenue generation expected from Q4 FY25 (January onwards)
items.quote: Good news, is that JV project commercial run has already started. First round of production already we did. Though our team believes that we need to have further tuning on the production process to get the best result and cost-effective product which is o n. So, we are expecting the revenue generation should be from Q4, that is from January onwards, because these are all B2B

items.statement: Banana processing and sampling started; export opportunity due to Ecuador issues
items.quote: are already getting a lot of enquiries. So we have started our banana process ing and sampling has already been submitted. So let us see. There we have defined taste profile as a color profile in India Foods & versus Ecuador, but we see there is an opportunity. We are already doin g export, but this year there may be an opportunity we feel which will be good for us

items.statement: Export shipments dependent on container pricing and availability; FOB contracts create uncertainty
items.quote: It's likely lucid, basically, because a lot of our contracts are based on FOB and the shipments can actually happen based on the pricing of the ships or the contai ner availability in the export markets. So, we are trying to tie up as much as possible, but it still remains to be decided based on the container pricing

items.statement: Domestic stationery volume growth target 15% for FY25; value growth low single digit due to 10-12% price cut
items.quote: So as far as volume growth is concerned, we are still confident of growing it by 15% volume. But in terms of value because of around whatever reduction of pricing that we had to take on our books. So net-net, the now as a value growth will be hardly low single digit.

items.statement: Standalone publication EBITDA margin expected 30-31% in FY25; stationery 12-13%
items.quote: So margin in publication should be around 30%, 31%. And in stationery, it should be around between 12% and 13%.

items.statement: Margins expected to improve in FY26 due to lower cost inventory, curriculum-driven volume growth, and stationery volume growth
items.quote: It will be higher on two counts. One, these margins in the current year also has her cost inventory, which was used during our production, which will not be the case next year.

items.statement: Gujarat curriculum change in 15 subjects across grades 1-4 (50% of titles) expected to drive 10-12% Gujarat publication growth in FY26
items.quote: So Gujarat business, which is almost 50% of our total state board business that we have, that will have seen a growth of at least 10% with this change.

items.statement: Maharashtra likely to change only grade 1 curriculum in FY26, adding ~5% growth
items.quote: Yes, Maharashtra -- as I mentioned earlier, we have a gut feel that they'll be able to change only 1 grade, which is grade 1 that in that additional 5% should come from arrest.

items.statement: CBSE textbook business targeting 11,000 schools in FY25 vs 8,500 last year; orders from 6,000 schools targeted vs 4,700 last year
items.quote: And as far as number of schools are concerned, so I'm saying at the group level, we were almost reaching 8,500 schools, and this year, the target is to reach 11,000 schools. And of 8,500 schools, we had received order from around 4,700 schools. So this year, our target is to at least get in orders from 6,000 schools.

items.statement: Navneet standalone CBSE revenue to grow 25-30% in FY25 from ~Rs.25 crore base
items.quote: But coming to specific to Navneet, the revenue from CBSE schools would grow by around 25%, 26% over last year, which was around -- again, in terms of rupees, it was around Rs.25 crores.

items.statement: Group CBSE textbook revenue ~Rs.85 crore expected to grow 15-17% in FY25
items.quote: So overall, on Rs.85 crores that we had, we should grow around 15% to 17%.

items.statement: FY25 capex Rs.40-42 crore including Rs.40 crore land conveyance and Rs.30 crore Gujarat factory construction
items.quote: So altogether, with land, it will be Rs.40 crores to Rs.42 crores of investment, additional investment in the current year.

items.statement: FY26 capex planned Rs.50-60 crore for manufacturing and storage capacity expansion on new land
items.quote: There we plan to further increase the capacity, both manufacturing and storage, and for that, we may end up spending between Rs.50 crores to Rs.60 crores.

items.statement: Export stationery outlook strong for Q4 FY25 and FY26 with good inquiries, anti-dumping duty reversal on one category, and new product acceptance
items.quote: Overall inquiries are really very good. And thankfully, a couple of products, which were not bought from us because of the anti-dumping duty that also now the same buyers are saying that we don't mind buying from India now.

items.statement: Export stationery new categories (metal office products, plastic folders, molded items) ramping up; first sales in Q4 FY25
items.quote: For metals, we have already got the sales. But for the other 2 items I mentioned that we will see first sale going in from us in the last quarter, and then it should start growing there on.

items.statement: Digital business loss narrowing from ~Rs.30 crore to ~Rs.15 crore in FY25; now integrated with publication segment
items.quote: But generally, I would say that earlier that -- on a yearly basis , last year that we would have lost around Rs.30-odd crores purely on digital business. This year, that loss may come down to around Rs.15 crores.

items.statement: Paper prices expected stable; further significant reduction unlikely as mills facing losses
items.quote: Very difficult now because I think now paper mills will go under losses if they reduce further. And therefore, I foresee, though they do not have orders and they are trying to get orders at any cost but much reduction from here is not seen.

items.statement: Short-term loan of Rs.50 crore given to strong party in H1 FY25; expected repayment by January
items.quote: So it was -- we had an excess money today, and we have given loans for a short period to a very strong party. And therefore, that should come back by January.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 20% plus-minus for FY25-26, tapering to 15% range thereafter
items.quote: '25, '26 you can find, as I have mentioned before also, around 20% plus-minus we should be.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 10% plus going forward
items.quote: Yes. I mean that for convenience purpose if we could reduce this and that, otherwise 10% plus.

items.statement: Order pipeline of around INR30,000 crores in various stages with INR12,000-13,000 crores bids already submitted
items.quote: We have got closely around INR30,000 crores of jobs under pipeline in various stages. Some of the tenders, some tenders is issued, some we have submitted the bid.

items.statement: Expect to secure INR10,000 crores of orders in FY25, with INR5,000-6,000 crores in H2 FY25
items.quote: But as I said that end of the year, total job I think INR10,000 crores will be secured in this year. That we are confident about that.

items.statement: Received INR1,600 crores plus GST order in October, over and above the INR5,000 crores H2 target
items.quote: INR1,600 is not part of that. That is beyond INR1,600 crores.

items.statement: Capex of INR67 crores in Q2 FY25, expected to be under control in FY26 as major investments done in last 2 years
items.quote: so far, our capex is around INR67 crores this quarter. Going forward, next year, we had said that the capex will be under control because whatever we have invested, just we have done the last 2 years, we don't see that much investment coming.

items.statement: Middle East market showing very good promises with infrastructure and township building activity
items.quote: Yes. I think the Middle East market has shown very good promises. A lot of things are happening there. You maybe knowing that infrastructure and the township building, etc.

items.statement: Focus on marine segment, with capability for airports, buildings, industrial structures; exploring data center, green energy, renewable energy, high-speed track laying
items.quote: Well, as a principle, we'd like to stick to the segments what are working and do more jobs going abroad, increase the footprint, etc. But we also can keep at it from the new segments like data center, green energy, renewable energy.

items.statement: Bangladesh transmission line project affected by political situation; work expected to restart from December after mobilization
items.quote: So hopefully, from December onwards we'll be able to start the work. And as a local competition, so far, we are okay. I mean, we don't see much of problem.

items.statement: Q2 margin impacted by Bangladesh political issues and monsoon affecting marine and road projects
items.quote: Marine as I told you that, see, one of the marine job in Bangladesh, which was supposed to be done. We could not do much because of the political issue. So revenue has affected and accordingly margin also.

items.statement: Adani Group ownership expected to positively impact international expansion and domestic growth
items.quote: Definitely, it will impact positively. That's what I can say now.

items.statement: Mobilization advance of INR1,300 crores as of September 2024
items.quote: As of September, we have about INR1,300 crores.

items.statement: Expect growth from Q4 FY25 onwards and at least 10% growth in Q4 FY25 for bimetal volumes
items.quote: In fact, the fourth quarter onwards we are just hoping that we will get at least a 10% growth.

items.statement: Expect shunt business growth from Q4 FY25 and continuing into next financial year from existing and new opportunities
items.quote: we have sort of a brighter view from from the fourth quarter of this year onwards, where we have already received some forecasts of increase in quantity. So we expect to see certain growth coming in this quarter onwards, the last quarter of this year, that is Q4 and then thereafter, the next one year or so, the next financial year or so, we should continue to see growth coming in from those areas

items.statement: Smart meter business expected to grow 70-75% YoY to Rs 70-75 crore in FY25 with continued growth for next 2-3 years
items.quote: we are looking at about 70% to 75% growth in that area. And that is keeping in mind the business that we've done in these two quarters, this current quarter, as well as the next quarter, the Q3 and Q4 we expect to see a further growth of 10% to 15% from these previous two quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to improve to 50% if product mix reaches 50-50 split between shunt and bimetal
items.quote: if the combination of both, the product will be in 50- 50% it will improve, improve further on, further here on. So today, if we are at 47-48% it should go up up to 50%.

items.statement: Target shunt resistor throughput below 20% average; bimetal throughput around 8-11%
items.quote: in shunt register, which is still an evolving application, based on which we try to get it reduced and keep it below 20% as an average.

items.statement: Plans to aggressively add R&D capabilities in CY25-26 including testing equipment, prototype processes, and manpower
items.quote: we have projects and plans in place for 25 calendar year, 25 and 26 where we'll be aggressively adding further capabilities in terms of testing equipment, you know, smaller prototype processes which replicate our production lines, and also, of course, manpower.

items.statement: Indian switchgear customers forecasting 20-25% higher bimetal demand for next calendar year
items.quote: they have been asking us to be prepared to supply 20% to 25% in some cases, higher than this year.

items.statement: H1FY25 gross margin 46.57%, down 272 bps YoY due to strategic product mix shift toward high-demand lower-margin products
items.quote: We recorded a gross margin of 46.57% for H1FY25, marking a reduction of 272 basis points compared to the previous year. This reflects our strategic pivot toward high-demand products that, while slightly lower in margin, align with evolving market needs.

items.statement: Contact business gross margin declined 89 bps to 20.79% in H1FY25
items.quote: Our gross margin has declined a little bit, which was in the last year, 21.68%, it goes down to 20.79% marginality of 89 bps.

items.statement: Shunt segment in India grew 45.27% in H1FY25 driven by industrial expansion
items.quote: In H1FY25, our Shunt segment in India grew by 45.27%.

items.statement: US bimetal market still declining but expected to improve from Q4 FY25
items.quote: Most of this is coming from the decline of the US market, so that is still under decline at this point. We expect that to increase in the fourth quarter.

items.statement: Smart meter business is majority domestic; energy meter share of total sales rose from 8.5% to 13.5% in H1FY25
items.quote: in the last year we have done almost eight and a half percent. And this year, till compared to the six months, is around 13 and half percent.

items.statement: Metalor JV not proceeding in original structure due to high investment relative to returns; evaluating alternate arrangement
items.quote: the investments required were much higher than the kind of business or kind of, you know, the bottom line that it could eventually add so financially, it was not making as much sense, at least in the structure that was originally envisioned.

items.statement: Established wholly-owned subsidiary in Italy to engage European market directly, replacing retiring agent
items.quote: establishing a wholly-owned subsidiary in Italy this year is a significant step forward. This subsidiary will now allow us to engage directly with the market, bypassing intermediaries, and delivering products more efficiently and responsively.

items.statement: R&D spend currently ~1% of sales; targeting increase over next 1-1.5 years
items.quote: currently we are at approximately 1% but we have projects and plans in place for 25 calendar year, 25 and 26 where we'll be aggressively adding further capabilities

items.statement: Volume growth guidance maintained at 10-20% for FY25
items.quote: So considering the market scenario, we have told you that last couple of quarters, around 3,4 quarters, considering that there is so much of volatility in green coffee prices, the contracts have been very, very short term. So we are maintaining that guidance of 10% to 20%.

items.statement: No new capex planned; existing capacity sufficient for 3-4 years
items.quote: So no capex plan. We are already good on capacity for the next 3, 4 years. It's only after that, we will figure out whether we need more capacity expansion.

items.statement: Vietnam freeze-dried line in trial phase; commercialization expected next quarter
items.quote: The Vietnam FD, we are right now in the trial phases. As you know, whenever we put up a line, a lot of trials, certification, blend matching, all that work happens. So hopefully, we're looking to kind of do all of that, complete all of that by this quarter.

items.statement: India plant commercialization expected within a month; certifications underway
items.quote: Coming back to India, the India plant should start operations maybe a month from now because all that trial and most of it is now over the certifications are also on their way.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved due to better value contracts, brand owners, and RoDTEP benefit of INR5-6 crores
items.quote: There is also an element of RoDTEP, which is approximately INR5 crores to INR6 crores of RoDTEP, which is a substitution of MEIS that we used to get. So if you see, if I combine all of them, volume growth, better value contracts, more brand owners seeking -- coming in and this RoDTEP. All of that put together has helped us improve our margin this quarter.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA per kg guidance stable for next 1-2 years; may improve at 50-60% capacity utilization
items.quote: And that's the reason we have given this guidance that it will be a more or less stable for the next 1 to 2 years. And thereafter, probably when we are utilizing our current expanded capacity to almost 50%, 60% levels, that's the time when we start building more efficiencies and getting into more high value contract because these will stabilize and then I will get better margins.

items.statement: Global coffee consumption remains sticky with no significant demand destruction despite high prices
items.quote: But interestingly, it's good news and bad news because the coffee consumption at the end consumer, we haven't seen much of an impact globally. So globally, this -- we all know that this category is pretty sticky. So what it means is that there has been no consumption drop.

items.statement: Coffee prices likely peaked; may soften slightly to $3,800-4,000 levels but not to $2,000-2,500
items.quote: No, sir, right now, none of them. So right now, when I'm -- been talking about softening, we're saying that from $4,500 or $4,400, maybe at around $4,000 levels. It could go to $3,800 levels, it could soften up. But $2,000 levels, I don't see it settling at that price any time in near future or CCL Products ( mid future

items.statement: Order book driven by long-term contracts; spot orders limited; expecting longer contracts post-December price stability
items.quote: So as I told earlier, I think after December, once the picture is clear, I'm hoping that a lot of clients will now revert back to long term because the general consensus that has built around the globe is that there won't be significant softening from here.

items.statement: Freeze-dried capacity ~25% of total; premium value-added coffees ~5-7% of business
items.quote: So we don't do a flavored coffee in B2B segment, yes. Flavored coffee is a very small segment, not only across the globe but in India also. And if I were to take a freeze dried, it will be around 25% of our capacity.

items.statement: EUDR implementation postponed 1 year; working with suppliers and associations for compliance
items.quote: And coming to deforestation issue, so EUDR, we all know that it has been postponed as of now for 1 year because it requires -- it's a -- while the intent is right, the whole implementation has its own challenges because of the certification and all that you have to get.

items.statement: Domestic branded business targeting INR300 crores for FY25; grew ~50% in H1 FY25
items.quote: And for the year, we are looking to -- for the branded business close to INR300 crores. We'll see how this quarter and next quarter goes because the first half momentum was pretty good. We are almost like 50% growth over last year.

items.statement: B2C distribution expanding to 130,000 general trade outlets plus modern trade and quick commerce
items.quote: We will be directly servicing around 130,000 or so number of outlets. You add another 5,000, 6,000 of modern trade. And then, of course, there are these other things like we target, like the tea shops and all that, which we take it as a separate segment.

items.statement: Gross debt INR1,974 crores split: INR1,300 crores working capital, balance capex
items.quote: So around INR1,300 crores will be the working capital and the balance will be capex.

items.statement: Cost of debt stable at current levels; no reduction expected unless RBI cuts rates
items.quote: No. Currently, it's also the same price. As we know that RBI did not change any rate profile in their monetary policy. So unless the rates are being softened from the RBI end, we don't see that any reduction in the in the rate of interests are concerned.

items.statement: Insurance claim for business interruption loss under process; will take more time
items.quote: Relating to the issue, as you know that they will take a good amount of time. And our request towards the business interruption loss has been put forth which we have placed with them, it is under process. Definitely, it will take some more time.

items.quote: For the Ethanol Supply Year 2024-25, which we've just embarked upon and commenced on the 1st of November, the OMCs have invited bids of 916 crore litres and allotted 837 crore litres in the first cycle. It's a huge increase. And this corresponds to at least a nationwide target of 18%.

items.statement: Sir Shadi Lal Enterprises distillery requires capex to operate efficiently; turnaround expected this sugar season
items.quote: The distillery at the Sir Shadi La l Enterprises was in terrible conditions when we took over management control requiring a reasonable amount of capex in order to be able to let it operate at the efficiencies that the Trive ni distilleries operate

items.statement: Water business sees massive opportunities from central/state government funding post-elections; new models like HAM and zero liquid discharge emerging
items.quote: The business anticipates a surge in business opportunities and new funding is expected to flow both from Central and State Governments post the elections, including the state elections as well. I think that is now very, very clear.

items.statement: 0238 sugarcane variety reduced from 75% to 50% of crop; further reduction expected next year
items.quote: Last year, we were around 75%, and we have come to around 50% this year, and we expect a substantial reduction going forward next year.

items.statement: No further capex contemplated beyond ₹20 crore IMIL approval; CBG viability questioned due to press mud prices above ₹50/quintal
items.quote: So the only capex that has been approved by the Board in its board meeting yesterday was ₹20 -odd crore for the IMIL business. Be sides that, we are not contemplating any further capex at this particular point in

items.statement: Expect to maintain run rate of more than INR800 crores per quarter in remaining two quarters of FY25
items.quote: And on the revenue side, I think we should be able to maintain this run rate of more than INR800 crores going forward as well. So...

items.statement: Will announce expansion plans before FY25 ends; evaluating spinning and fabric capacity additions with focus on better margin products
items.quote: Definitely before this financial year ends, definitely we will come with something going forward as well.

items.statement: EBITDA margins running at 14-15% range for last 3 quarters; expect improvement in H2 but depends on cotton prices and demand
items.quote: If you see our last 3 quarters, we are running at near to the similar kind of EBITDA about -- in the range of about 14% to 15% is the EBITDA range, which we have been there.

items.statement: Domestic demand expected to improve in H2 due to winter and marriage season; export demand subdued but maintaining momentum via new markets
items.quote: And we expect that normally in second ha lf always we have better domestic demands due to the seasonal requirements of winter as well as the marriage season which happens

items.statement: Cotton-yarn spread currently INR90/kg; Indian cotton at 14-15% premium to NY futures; landed cost now at parity with imported cotton
items.quote: Yes, cotton to yarn spread is, as of today, is in the range of about, basic cotton to yarn is in the range of about INR90 a kg.

items.statement: Blended yarn reached 17-18% of total production; fabric exports 17-18% direct, rest via domestic exporters; knitted fabric utilization limited by margin threshold
items.quote: Blended has now reached nearly, out of our total production at this point of time, blended yarn has reached about 17%, 18% of our total capacity.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions suppressing global demand; Bangladesh transition smooth but ongoing issues; US tariff risk on China could benefit India
items.quote: But we have been able to maintain our momentum by exploring certain new markets as well as penetrating more with our existing customers.

items.statement: Gross debt INR1,180 crores; expect to repay INR90-100 crores in next two quarters; debt-equity improved to 0.97 from 1.17
items.quote: We have repayments of nearly INR90 crores to INR100 crores going in, in next six months. So, that should be there.

items.statement: Solar capacity at 18.8 MW (8-9% of power needs); grid cost INR7/unit vs solar INR3.50/unit; spent INR12-13 crores in H1 on solar
items.quote: I think last year we did, we had spent -- in the first half itself, again we have spent INR12, INR13 crores.

items.statement: Cotton procurement based on order book; imported cotton 25% of usage in last 6 months; may increase under advance license for exports
items.quote: So in last 6 months our utilization of imported cottons exceeded more than 25%. So this may still continue going forward looking to the prices which is there.

items.statement: Full-year volume growth guidance lowered to double-digit from 15%; EBITDA per kg expected around Rs. 38 for FY25
items.quote: Probably we are still aiming at double digit growth for the full year and probably the EBITDA average which is now currently at 36.73, probably it will land around 38.

items.statement: Paint segment volume growth expected 7-8% for FY25 vs earlier 10% target
items.quote: Paint this year will be we expected around 10% but I think we will end up somewhere at 7% to 8%.

items.statement: FY26 volume growth target 12-15% driven by ABG ramp-up and pharma scale-up
items.quote: Next year onwards we should be in the position to reach somewhere around 12% to 15% volume growth.

items.statement: FY25 capex expected Rs. 85-90 crore including Panipat, Cheyyar, pharma balancing and printing equipment
items.quote: Already Rs. 70 crores has been committed and we have some more printing and other equipment being ordered, which will arrive before March. So, the overall cost of investments could be in the region of Rs. 85 crores to Rs. 90 crores.

items.statement: FY26 capex estimated Rs. 50-60 crore, lower than FY25 as no greenfield projects
items.quote: Next year CAPEX may be limited to 50 crores to 60 crores as of today but we can only comment as we go towards the end of this year.

items.statement: ABG H1 volumes 1,500-1,600 tons; H2 expected 2,000+ tons; targeting 70% utilization of 5,000 ton initial capacity
items.quote: H1, maybe the volumes are around 1500 tons to 1600 tons. Probably in the second half, it may go to 2000 plus. So, we are online. About 70% of the capacity will be utilized.

items.statement: EBITDA per kg currently Rs. 36.73; target Rs. 40 by Q1 FY26 as capacity utilization improves
items.quote: I think we should be able to see that in the first quarter of next year itself. That is the Q1 of next year. It may inch towards 40. And overall, next year, we are aiming definitely for 40 as a minimum number to achieve.

items.statement: Paint realization down to Rs. 180-190/kg from Rs. 215/kg two years ago due to lower raw material prices and mandatory recycled plastic usage
items.quote: At that time, the raw material price went up to 120 -125. Currently the raw material price is around 105. More or less in this year, the price was stagnant there. And also, in the paint segment, like any other segment, RCP, that is recycled plastic usage has become mandatory.

items.statement: Pharma sales accelerating: Rs. 1 crore in Q2, Rs. 75 lakh in October alone; targeting Rs. 1-2 crore/month from January
items.quote: In the month of October , we did close to 75 lakhs sales in pharma alone and going forward the numbers will increase because now Marksans, MSN Labs, Graviti, Pulse. and also, Nutra Life and many other companies have cleared their audit and started taking our commercial line trials and small lot supplies.

items.statement: Pharma revenue target Rs. 30-50 crore for FY26; long-term opportunity Rs. 5,000 crore market
items.quote: At least we will see Rs. 30 crores to Rs. 50 crores. It could be 30 or 50. It all depends upon how products that are being launched we will be taking off.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Paint 47%, Lubes 20%, Food & Qpack 32.4%, Pharma 0.5%; IML share up to 72.57% from 66.7%
items.quote: In terms of revenue, 47% is from pain t, 20% lubes, food and Qpack together is around 32.4%, 0.5% is pharma.

items.statement: Mahad plant delayed due to local pollution approvals; supplying ABG from Satara for 2-3 quarters
items.quote: There are some issues related to local pollution and local approvals. They got delayed and that is why because the plant got delayed, ABG agreed supplies from Satara for next few quarters.

items.statement: Printing capacity constraints limiting IML development; consolidation to Sultanpur delayed to January 2025
items.quote: We have moved 70% of the machines but another 30% we are not in a position to move because of the i ncreasing demand for IML. And this will be able to do only in January once additional machines are received

items.statement: Asset turnover ratio currently below 2x due to high unutilized capex; target to exceed 2.5x as plants ramp up
items.quote: Our asset turnover ratio always used to be around 2-2.5, but currently it is low because of very high investments that have been made which are yet to become completely utilized. So, going forward, we should be able to cross to 2.5 asset turnover ratio.

items.statement: Panipat plant Qpack supplies started Oct-Nov; full IML food packaging from January; ice cream/dairy by March-April
items.quote: Just in the month of October and a little bit in November, we are making some supplies of Qpack from North. But the real quantities would start only by end of December. As I said, the printing consents will be coming out by end of this year, that is December and then we will be in a full-fledged way to provide the IML containers f rom January in the North also.

items.statement: FY2025 revenue target Rs.900 Crores; confident of exceeding it
items.quote: This time we have been cautious and we have set a target of Rs.900 Crores and we hope to cross Rs.900 Crores, but by how much, let us wait and see.

items.statement: Average 50% CAGR over next three years based on FY2025 figure
items.quote: With respect to the F Y2026 projection, we have said that we will have an average CAGR of 50% over the next three years and we are confident, given the huge order pipeline that we have, that we will be able to achieve the 50% average CAGR over the next three years, based on the 2025 figure

items.statement: Order pipeline Rs.3500 Crores; expect Rs.1200 Crores inflow by end of FY2025
items.quote: Even though the order pipeline is almost Rs.3500 Crores, we expect about Rs.1,200 Crores to come in by the end of this financial year, which we will be able to execute in the next year.

items.statement: FY2026 order inflow expected to be very big; order book upwards of Rs.2000 Crores to support 50% CAGR
items.quote: The order book should be upwards of Rs.2000 Crores if you want to achieve that. Again, we think that the order book in FY2026 is going to be really big for orders that we are expecting.

items.statement: US manufacturing setup estimated cost less than $10 million (~Rs.80 Crores) in FY2026
items.quote: We have estimated it should be less than $10 million, maybe about Rs.80 Crores or so. That will be the total expenditure that may happen for our setup and cost over the next it may be for the FY2026.

items.statement: Acquisition and capex budget Rs.400 Crores and less than Rs.100 Crores respectively
items.quote: Our budget has been about Rs.400 Crores for acquisition and capex would be less than Rs.100 Crores that is what the plan is.

items.statement: H1 FY2025 EBITDA margin 36.8% and PAT margin 28%; expect to maintain FY2025 guidance of 35% EBITDA and 25% PAT
items.quote: Despite the lower margin we were able to maintain our operational margin of 37% in H1, though the Q2, it is on a lower side but in H1 this operational EBITDA is around 36.80% which is above our guidance given for 35% and PAT is also 28%.

items.statement: Gross margin 50% in H1 FY2025 lower due to evolving new products, R&D allocation, geography and product mix
items.quote: You are correct that in H12025 our gross margin is 50% which is quite lower however it is partly offset from the benefit of scale of operations and despite the lower margin we were able to maintain our operational margin of 37% in H1.

items.statement: Order book split expected 40-60 between simulators and anti-drone systems
items.quote: We will not be able to exactly predict that at this point in time, but again, we expect a 40 -60 split to be there . Last year it was there and maybe probably that will continue in this year also.

items.statement: Anti-drone systems and remote control weapon stations seeing dramatic demand increase; surveillance systems also strong
items.quote: In terms of short -term pain everybody is feeling the pain of the drone attacks. The drones are becoming very, very severe problem. Drones with the AI -enabled remote control weapon stations and surveillance system is the complete solution that they are looking forward.

items.statement: US market entry expected to yield large orders from FY2027; could be 10-50% of revenue
items.quote: In FY2027, it could be as little as, about 10% to 15%, but it could go as high as 50 %. By the way, we have not factored this into our growth plans and this would be completely additional revenue that we will be getting.

items.statement: No slowdown seen in Indian defense orders; government committed to strengthening defense
items.quote: No, we do not see any slowdown in the defense orders. We expect the orders to come through, but definitely there may be some delay in action, but definitely not any complete elimination of the orders or anything like that.

items.statement: QIP of Rs.1000 Crores subscribed 5x; proceeds for acquisitions (Indian and overseas targets Rs.100-300 Crores typical size)
items.quote: Again, coming back to the fact that we have raised through a QIP Rs.1000 Crores it was subscribed more than five times, part of the proceeds we intend to deploy for acquisitions and we have in view both Indian and overseas targets. A typical size we are looking at is between Rs.100 to 300 Crores.

items.statement: Working capital cycle expected to improve to 160-170 days by end of FY2025 from ~200 days in H1
items.quote: Going forward, we can say that by end of this financial year, it will be again down to 160 to 170 days. This significant realization will happen in the current quarter.

items.statement: Barbarik remote control weapon station tested by Army; orders expected next year
items.quote: With respect to Barbarik the army has seen it, they have tested it and they have found it to be very useful. We expect requirements to come up in the next few months and we will be waiting for that.

items.statement: Management does not provide guidance for FY26 and FY27
items.quote: We are not giving guidances.

items.statement: H2 FY25 domestic business expected to grow high single-digit, better than market in specialty
items.quote: We should do a high single -digit growth at least in H2.

items.statement: U.S. business H2 FY25 will be much stronger than H1 due to back-ended launches and market share ramp-up
items.quote: H2 will be much stronger for us compared to H1.

items.statement: ROW generics expected to grow 15-20% in H2 FY25 with strong order book
items.quote: I expect th at the H2 will remain at these similar levels 15% to 20% growth, at least, for the ROW business

items.statement: U.S. price erosion continues at high single digits to low double digits, no change in intensity
items.value: high single digits to low double digits
items.quote: it could be anywhere between high single digits to low double digits. That's what we're seeing in terms of the market.

items.statement: Gross margin comfortable at 72% ± range, depends on product mix and launches
items.quote: I think 72% ± is a good range to be in.

items.statement: R&D spend for FY25 revised lower to INR 500-520 crores from earlier INR 550 crores
items.quote: It will be a little bit on the lower side, w e would be closer to the INR500 crores, INR520 crores kind of
