items.quote: We have 3 major projects around as of now in hand, one is a new formulation facility for domestic market, which is coming up near Indore. That should be completed by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Targeting semaglutide and tirzepatide for GLP-1 portfolio; semaglutide launch will be late, not in first wave; in-house peptide manufacturing capability being built
items.quote: Yes. we will launch -- we will target semaglutide and tirzepatide both. There's still time of tirzepatide and the launch is still some time off. Sema, we will not be in the first wave, we will be a little late.

items.statement: API business degrew 15% due to price erosion and loss of key accounts; recovery expected by end of FY25 or FY26
items.quote: API business degrew by 15%. This is a trend that we've seen in the last couple of quarters. We've seen some price erosion in the API business and have lost some key accounts.

items.statement: API business loss due to competitors offering lower prices, Chinese aggression, and customers switching vendors for better pricing
items.quote: s just a matter of price erosion and competitors offering lower prices, and we moved some, I think. There are a few key accounts that we lost is built up which occurred, but we're seeing price erosion

items.statement: ROW business has strong order book supporting 15-20% growth in H2 FY25
items.quote: This has a strong order book, and I expect th at the H2 will remain at these similar levels 15% to 20% growth, at least, for the ROW business

items.statement: Filed 1 ANDA, received 9 approvals, launched 8 products in U.S. in Q2 FY25; plan ~10 launches in H2 FY25
items.quote: We filed 1 ANDA. We also received 9 approvals and launched 8 products in the U.S. during the quarter. And as I mentioned, we will launch about 10 products in H2 as well.

items.statement: ANDAs filing lag expected this year due to project push to complex and cost reduction; back to 15+ ANDAs from FY26
items.quote: From next year onwards, we will get back to the higher 15 -odd ANDAs that we've been filing.

items.statement: Working capital and debt elevated in Q2 due to inventory build for launches and dividend outflow; expected to normalize by end FY25 and FY26
items.quote: Probably that will be a close call. But going forward, if we talk of FY '26, I think we should be back to normal level

items.statement: Unexecuted order book of 1.7 GW peak as of 30 September 2024
items.quote: we have an unexecuted order book of 1.7 gigawatts peak

items.statement: Order book value roughly Rs 2,500-2,700 crore
items.quote: This would roughly now translate to around Rs. 2,700-odd crores, between Rs. 2,500 crores to Rs. 2.700-odd crores.

items.statement: Pipeline of 17.8 GW being chased
items.quote: our pipeline which you asked is now 17.8 gigawatts

items.statement: Expect to execute 1.2-1.3 GW from current order book in H2 FY25
items.quote: we are hopeful of around 1.2 gigawatts to 1.3 gigawatts

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin guided at double-digit near 15% for current order book valid next 9-12 months
items.quote: our EBITDA margins at a sustainable level should be double-digit, almost near to 15% levels

items.statement: Government targeting 40-50 GW renewable procurement per annum; tenders coming up significantly
items.quote: government has committed that they will increase the business of renewable energy in terms of procurement of power up to almost 40 gigawatts to 50 gigawatts per annum

items.statement: No significant slowdown observed in sector investments from government or other parties
items.quote: We haven't observed any significant slowdown in this sector in terms of investments from the government or from other parties as well.

items.statement: Order book split 15-20% PSU, rest utility/rooftop/other; bulk is balance-of-system orders
items.quote: our current order book is between 15% to 20% in PSU side, and the rest is towards either utility scale or rooftop or other projects

items.statement: O&M portfolio at 587 MW; expect 2-3x growth next year onwards
items.quote: O&M is at 587 megawatts. Also, what happens is that when we undertake EPC clients, they give us, majority of them, not all of them, give us between three to five years of O&M. So, mostly once the projects gets completed next year we will see an uptick in O&M as well. And the company also keeps actively bidding for O&M customers outside. So, we are hopeful that this should also see a 2x to 3x growt

items.statement: No significant supply chain bottlenecks foreseen; domestic supply geared to meet requirements
items.quote: we are until now not foreseeing any significant bottlenecks towards that end as of now

items.statement: Business model requires only working capital; negative working capital cycle with 21-30 day collection vs 40-45 day payables
items.quote: Technically, our working capital cycle is, actually we have a negative working capital. It means we do not need capital to do this business.

items.statement: Advance payments 5-15% (thumb rule 10%); performance bank guarantees 10-15% (thumb rule 10%)
items.quote: advanced ranges hover between 5% to 15%, but thumb rule is 10%. And performance bank guarantees we have observed has been around 10% to 15%, thumb rule again 10%.

items.statement: Green hydrogen demand not yet scaled up in terms of orders; expecting it to scale up
items.quote: But from a demand perspective, we are expecting it to scale up. But as of now a significant demand on that front has not been scaled up in terms of orders.

items.statement: Hit rate on pipeline historically 25-30%; entire 17.8 GW pipeline up for bidding in H2
items.quote: Our hit rate in the past has been around 25%-odd, but depending upon which is numerator, and which is denominator, 25%, 30% has been our hit rate. The entire one is for the second half anyway

items.statement: Volume growth guidance for FY25 revised to early double-digits (11-12%) from earlier 20% revenue growth target
items.quote: Yes, early double-digits. Like I think 11%, 12% would be a good estimate.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA expected at Rs. 220-230 crores
items.quote: I think it should definitely be much higher than last year, there should be about Rs. 220 crores to Rs. 230 crores in Q4.

items.statement: FY25 capex revised to Rs. 720 crores (H1: Rs. 337 crores, H2: Rs. 377 crores)
items.quote: Yes, you are right, it's at about Rs. 720 crores, yes.

items.statement: FY26 capex estimated at Rs. 450-500 crores (Silchar Rs. 300 crores, Jorhat Rs. 100 crores, operational Rs. 100 crores)
items.quote: So, in total it is about Rs. 480 crores to Rs. 500 crores.

items.statement: Silchar grinding unit commissioning delayed to December 2026 from September-October 2026
items.quote: Now we are expecting it to commission by December '26. So, there is a two, three months delay.

items.statement: Jorhat grinding unit expected commissioning by FY27
items.quote: In Jorhat plant we are expecting by FY '27 and.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 per tonne EBITDA Rs. 995 vs Rs. 1,164 YoY; H1 FY25 Rs. 1,007 vs Rs. 1,176 YoY
items.quote: On per tonne EBITDA front it is Rs. 995 during this quarter, as against Rs. 1,164 per tonne same quarter last year.

items.statement: Northeast EBITDA per tonne Rs. 1,300; Outside Northeast EBITDA per tonne minus Rs. 200 in Q2 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA per tonne for Northeast was about Rs. 1,300 per tonne, and the EBITDA per tonne for outside Northeast was about minus Rs. 200.

items.statement: Northeast cement prices increased Rs. 10/bag QoQ; Outside Northeast (Bihar/Bengal) prices crashed and remain flat QoQ
items.quote: In the Northeast, the prices have increased by about Rs. 10 compared to the quarter too. So, in the Northeast the prices are a bit more stable than outside the Northeast.

items.statement: Current Northeast cement price ~Rs. 460/bag; expect Rs. 15-20/bag increase by December
items.quote: The current price in Northeast is about Rs. 460 per bag. And in November I do not see an increase in the pricing. But I think going ahead, hopefully, I think we should be, I think by December I think normally the prices do increase. So, we do see like a Rs. 15 to Rs. 20 scope of increasing prices.

items.statement: Fuel cost at Rs. 1.5 per GCV in Q2, expected to remain same in Q3/Q4 with possible reduction
items.quote: Yes, I think it probably will remain the same only. So, I think in Q1 also it was Rs. 1.5, right now also it's about Rs. 1.5. And I think it should remain Rs. 1.5 in the coming quarters as well. I think there could be some reduction but no increase.

items.statement: Northeast demand subdued in H1 due to low government spending; expect pickup from Dec-Jan with scheme rollouts
items.quote: So, basically the main problem at least in the North East was that the government expenditure in Northeast in the first half was a bit low, right, and because of that the demand was a bit subdued.

items.statement: New clinker plant (Line-3) stabilization delayed due to electrical panel faults; expect resolution by Nov 22, ramp-up to 7,000-7,500 TPD by end-Nov
items.quote: So, now on the 17th those panels will be received, and on the 22nd we will erect those panels. And I think after that we should have smooth functioning. So, this is broadly what it is.

items.statement: GST incentive booking low in Q2 (Rs. 37 crores) due to clinker plant issues; expect Rs. 50-60 crores/quarter in Q3/Q4
items.quote: But in whatever is left of Q3 and in Q4, we do expect a good generation of GST. The exact numbers I will quantify, and I will let you know. I will probably ask my CFO to get back to you. But I think about Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 60 crores quarterly is what we expect in the coming quarters.

items.statement: AAC block plant in Guwahati to commission by early December 2024; eligible for central and state subsidies
items.quote: AAC block in Guwahati should be commissioned by December, in the first two weeks of December. And with that, we are also launching construction chemicals, right, so we will be getting into motor, waterproofing chemical and all these items.

items.statement: No disbursement targets given for current or next year; clarity expected in January (revised estimate) and February (budget)
items.quote: I will not be giving numbers but going forward I can assure you that our disbursement as well as the project sanction will pick up steadily.

items.statement: NTPC wagon leasing deal signed for Rs 700 crore (first tranche of 20 rakes, 15-year lease)
items.quote: That is 700 crores. This is just the beginning because this is the first time they have done a leasing model with us.

items.statement: Expanding beyond railways to forward/backward linkages in logistics and infra; targeting NTPC, petroleum companies for rolling stock leasing
items.quote: We are entering into arrangement to fund NTPC for purchase of their wagons which they use in the railway system for their coal logistics.

items.statement: Railway lending at 35-40 bps margin; non-railway lending expected at higher spreads (peers at 250-300 bps) to boost PAT
items.quote: Once we go outside this purview, we don't have that restriction. So obviously we will be doing the lending at a very attractive rate and try to be competitive than the

items.statement: Will maintain zero-NPA track record; building robust appraisal team with government and industry talent for prudent underwriting
items.quote: We are a zero-NPA company and would like to maintain that kind of good thing that we have with us that we remain there.

items.statement: Board and shareholders approved Rs 8 lakh crore total borrowing limit; current debt-to-equity at 7.83x, net worth over Rs 50,000 crore
items.quote: Our board and shareholders have already approved 8 lakh crores of total borrowing limit.

items.statement: No equity raise needed; capital adequacy over 700%, net worth growing annually, comfortable for growth
items.quote: there is absolutely no constraint for further growth and plus I will be adding to my net worth . Further, as you know since more than 99% exposure to M oR, m y capital adequacy is more than 700

items.statement: Lease rentals based on WACC plus risk pass-through (interest rate and currency variations); cost-plus model
items.quote: it's a cost-plus model. So, cost plus some of the risks are also p assed on. But you're right if cost is 7, then at 7.4 I will be calculating my lease rentals

items.statement: Railway disbursement paused for 6 quarters to cool debt-to-equity from ~9x to ~7.5x; discussions ongoing with MoR and MoF for renewed lending
items.quote: With very high and steep growth in its assets under management for 5 consecutive FYss, there was no disbursement in the last FY and current FY till now.

items.statement: Tax status: zero tax payment expected for next couple of years due to accumulated depreciation on lease assets including NTPC deal
items.quote: because of the accumulated depreciation and further depreciation on whatever financial leases we do subsequently will get dep reciation on that also. So, we don't see any tax payments coming for the next couple of years

items.statement: Provisioning for non-railway exposure at 0.4% (same as RVNL loan); minimal impact on profitability
items.quote: We are currently doing 0.4% for whatever funding we have done, for RVNL Loan, the same provisioning will do for this exposure also.

items.statement: Project lease structure: 15-year primary lease, 5-year moratorium, secondary lease reduced from 15 to 10 years (total 30 years)
items.quote: The primary lease period would be 15 years and in case of a project asset, secondary lease period will get reduced from 15 to 10.

items.statement: Management hopes muted demand streak ends in Q3 and industry reverts to normal growth rate
items.quote: Finally, we hope that this long streak of muted underlying demand situation comes to an end in Q3, and that the industry does a sharp reversal towards its normal growth rate.

items.statement: Water-based plant at Jodhpur expected to commission in Q2 FY26; solvent-based plant by Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26; putty brownfield expansion by Q4 FY25
items.quote: The water-based new plant is expected to be commissioned sometime in Q2 of the next fiscal, while the solv ent-based plant, we are trying to get it up and running by the Q4 of this fiscal, at most, it may spill over to Q1 of the next fiscal

items.statement: Total capex outlay: water-based plant INR250-275 crores, solvent-based plant ~INR50 crores, putty brownfield expansion below INR15 crores
items.quote: The total capex outlay for the water-based plant that we are setting up is going to be somewhere around INR250 crores to INR275 crores. For the solvent-based plant, I believe, is about INR55 crores or something like that. Sorry, it's closer to INR50 crores. And for the brownfield expansion of the putty plant, it will be around below INR15 crores or so.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin 44.1% in Q2 FY25 vs 45.7% in Q2 FY24; EBITDA margin 14.8% vs 15.2% YoY; PAT margin 8.2% vs 9.6% YoY
items.quote: As usual, we have maintained the pole position in terms of gross margin, which stood at 44.1%. The gross margins were sligh tly muted compared to the corresponding period of the previous year when we had recorded 45.7% in Q2 of last year

items.statement: Price cuts of ~4.5-5% in Q3/Q4 FY24; price hikes of ~1.5% in Q2 FY25; net pricing deficit of 3-3.5% YoY
items.quote: the price cuts that were taken in Q3 and Q4 of last year aggregated to somewhere around 4.5%, almost 5%, depending upon your product mix. And the price hikes that have happened in the quarter just gone by is at best 1.5%. So there is still a clear 3% to 3.5% deficit in pricing.

items.statement: Q2 opened with strong double-digit growth in July but August-September were a drag; low-demand scenario persisted in Q2
items.quote: Though this quarter, Q2, opened with strong double-digit growth for us in July, the months of August and September were a bit of a drag, which resulted in the streak of a low-demand scenario to continue in Q2 as well.

items.statement: Premium emulsion grew significantly faster than economy; waterproofing drove higher value vs volume growth in Primer/Distemper/Misc segment (13.7% value vs 7.1% volume)
items.quote: The Emulsion segment, which is the largest segment, also saw good growth, and premium segment of the emulsions grew at a significantly higher pace than the economy segment.

items.statement: Differentiated products collectively account for 30% of top line; putty >10% of top line; 65% of offerings don't require tinting machine
items.quote: Most of our differentiated products, which account collectively for 30% of our top line, they don't require tinting. Putty accounts for well over 10% of our top line

items.statement: Putty gross margins positive but lowest among segments; competitors cutting putty prices and compromising quality; Indigo maintains quality and pricing
items.quote: For us, Abneesh, putty has never been a negative gross margin. And the reason is that we are perhaps the only paint company that manufactures almost all of its putty in-house.

items.statement: Apple Chemie Q2 margins impacted by adverse mix due to monsoon affecting big projects; margins recovered in October
items.quote: In Q2, due to .., well they have some star products which have high gross margin, and those products deteriorated in volume during Q2, largely due to certain big projects being affected due to excessive monsoon in those parts of India. It has picked up very strongly again in October.

items.statement: Active dealers 18,718; tinting machines 10,555 (55% penetration); target 75% in medium term
items.quote: As on the 30th September of this year, our count of active dealers was 18,718, and our tinting machine population was 10,555.

items.statement: Digital advertising ~15% of media spend in first year; influencer marketing program started last month
items.quote: Now this year, it may comprise of maybe 15% of o ur total media spend, which is a subsection of the total A&P spend. And since this is the first year, we'd like to go a little slow

items.statement: Health insurance for painters expanded to 11 states; >5,000 families enrolled; INR1 lakh coverage per family per year
items.quote: In the beginning of this fiscal, we extended the program to the states of Odisha and Chhattisgarh, and now we have decided to expand the benef it to a much larger community spanning over 11 states. Already more than 5,000 painter families have been enrolled in this program

items.statement: New differentiated product undergoing regulatory clearance; expected approval in 3-4 months
items.quote: Yes, there is one very major product that is on the annual, which is undergoing some regulatory clearance, which is required. I'm hopeful that we will get it in the next 3, 4 months or so

items.statement: No significant capex expected for next 3-4 years after current projects complete; capacity additions will follow demand
items.quote: So basically, with the kind of capex that we are putting in now, which will all come in stream somewhere between February, March to maybe August of next year, we don't envisage any significant capex for the next 3, 4 years, keeping healthy demand growth in mind.

items.statement: Buyback may be considered by Board in ~1.5 years after current capex completes and surplus funds accumulate
items.quote: Maybe 1.5 years from now when all this capex is behind us, I'm sure when we have a lot more surplus funds, the Board will take a decision at the appropriate time for a capex and -- for a buyback, as you suggested.

items.statement: FY25 Capex target of Rs. 110 crores for IPL and SSL combined
items.quote: Looking ahead at FY25, we aim to do Capex of Rs. 110 crores, combining both IPL and SSL.

items.statement: Capex split: Rs. 50 crores for Sandila and Rs. 60 crores for Hamirpur in FY25
items.quote: It was Rs.50 crores for Sandila and Rs.60 crores for Hamirpur projected Capex.

items.statement: Hamirpur two blocks total Capex Rs. 40-42 crores plus Rs. 25-30 crores infrastructure
items.quote: Both the blocks, see, the total Capex for both the blocks would be around Rs.40 crores to Rs.42 crores, and around Rs.25 crores to Rs.30 crores we have spent already on the infrastructure.

items.statement: Hamirpur plant revenue Rs. 50-60 crores in FY26, Rs. 70-80 crores from two blocks at full run-rate
items.quote: From our Hamirpur facility, next year we feel that we should be able to get around Rs.50 crores, Rs.60 crores.

items.statement: Formulation revenue growth target at least 20% per year
items.quote: Formulation growth also would be similar, at least 20% per year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance 18-20% for H2 FY25
items.quote: Sir had given 18% to 20% EBITDA margin for H2, so what gives him the confidence to achieve higher margins in the second half?

items.statement: Gross margin improvement sustainable at current levels if prices stable
items.quote: Yes, this will be in the similar range.

items.statement: Technical prices declined 19-20% YoY on blended basis; raw material prices fell similarly
items.quote: Yes, prices had declined on an average, on blended basis, around 19% to 20%.

items.statement: Key product prices (Captan, Folpet) declined ~15% with corresponding raw material cost reduction
items.quote: They have also decline d almost 15%. But similarly , there has been reduction in the raw metal prices also.

items.statement: Domestic demand strong due to good monsoon and Kharif sowing; export demand subdued with excess supply
items.quote: The Domestic market is in good shape, primarily driven by good sowing of crops in Kharif season.

items.statement: Technical volumes grew ~30% YoY; formulation volumes grew ~40% YoY
items.quote: Volume growth in technical will be around 30%.

items.statement: Pricing pressure from China continues; they dump material at unreasonable prices
items.quote: Pricing pressure from China still continues because they are trying to dump the material as much as possible at unreasonable prices.

items.statement: Hamirpur EC approval received for ~30,000 tonnes per annum; no further EC needed for listed products
items.quote: EC approval of what we have received is almost about 30,000 tonnes per annum.

items.statement: Japanese company tie-up signed; expected revenue ~Rs. 20 crores annually with better than 20% margins
items.quote: Revenue is not very big, sir. I think it is about , overall revenue would be around Rs.20 crores.

items.statement: Inventory days currently ~150, targeting 120-130 days by March 2025
items.quote: They will be in the range of 120 to 130 days by March.

items.statement: Management confident of delivering double-digit organic growth of 15% to 16% for the year
items.quote: But coming to seasonality, it was almost like a similar quarter that we had in the last year. And on the growth guidance, Amey, like we always said, we are confident of delivering double -digit growth of, say, 15% to 16%.

items.statement: Capex guidance of approximately INR200 crores for 10 new hubs across FY25 and FY26 remains unchanged
items.quote: So the capex guidance of approximately like INR200 crores on these new centers remains same.

items.statement: Plan to add at least 10 to 12 hubs across FY25 and FY26; 2 hubs already launched (Ongole, Nizamabad), 1 upgraded in Gurgaon
items.quote: Out of that, 2 hubs are already ready, like 1, we already launched, Ongole, okay and the other 1 is tomorrow at Nizamabad, similar hub centre and a larger area. So another 10 more centers apart from these 2 hubs will get opened in these 2 financial years, FY '25 and FY '26.

items.statement: Expect to maintain 40% EBITDA margin for full financial year despite new center drag
items.quote: But what I look at it is, okay, for a full financial year, I'm fairly confident that 40% EBITDA margins will be maintained.

items.statement: Volume growth of 30% year-on-year and footfall growth of 24% year-on-year in Q2 FY25
items.quote: And this robust revenue growth, just like the previous quarter, was again driven by volume growth of 30% year -on-year and footfall growth of 24% year -on-year.

items.statement: B2C revenue at 93%, radiology at 35% of revenue; wellness at 13-14% of business
items.quote: The B2C revenue stood healthy at 93%, and our radiology business stood at 35%.

items.statement: Kolkata operations impacted by strikes and Bangladesh issue for 20-25 days in Q2, but recovery seen in October-November
items.quote: Because of that, there were multiple strikes. And even because of this Bangladesh issue, for some time, that market has suffered. So that's the only reason why almost for 20, 25 days, the business got hit in this market.

items.statement: AI-powered path transition completed across network to improve radiologist specialization, reporting speed, and quality
items.quote: I'm happy to share that we have successfully transitioned our network to a new AI powered path as part of our digital strategy, and this upgrade will allow us to further leverage the skillset of our specialist radiologists, improving both customer and clinician satisfaction.

items.statement: Medinova integration approvals pending from stock exchanges and SEBI; NCLT process expected to complete by May-June
items.quote: We have received a few points from the stock exchange because both are listed companies, right? So, we need to get the clearance from the stock exchanges and SEBI first, which is supposed to be received last month, but there is some delay from the authority side. So once we get those approvals, then petition will be moved to the NCLT. Then from there, the process will take at least like 5 to 6 mon

items.statement: Nizamabad hub capex approximately INR14-15 crores with 3T MRI, CT scan, automated lab on 8,000-9,000 sq ft
items.quote: So approximately INR14 to INR15 crores there. I don't have the exact number, but it is in this range. Because we are going to invest in good technology, the high-end 3T MRI we're investing. And also high-end CT scan machine, we're investing. And also all the basic radiology modalities will be there. And with a very good infrastructure built on almost close to 8,000 to 9,000 square feet facility.

items.statement: Company is debt-free with surplus cash balance of approximately INR225 crores; expansion funded from internal accruals
items.quote: We don't have any bank borrowings. As of now, we're a debt -free company. And the surplus cash balance is approximately INR225 crores.

items.statement: Expect 6 hubs in FY25 (2 already opened, 3-4 more across regions by Q1 FY26); spoke additions to follow in subsequent years
items.quote: So, we would say we'll open at about 6 at least 6 hubs in this year. We already we have opened 2 hubs, right? And we have upgraded 1 more hub in Gurgaon, right? Other than this, you'll see another 3 to 4 hubs across it can be any region, across these regions coming up in this year. Or maybe early Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to remain in 87-88% range (industry-leading) driven by B2C dominance and integrated model
items.quote: So going forward as well, it will be in the range of 87% to 88% gross margin.

items.statement: New hubs outside core geography typically take 3-4 quarters to break even; Ongole expected to break even ahead of 2-3 quarter timeline
items.quote: typically, these hubs take at least like -- outside geographies that take like 3 quarters to break even.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 remains approximately INR 200 crores
items.quote: Our capex guidance for the year remains at approximately INR 200 crores.

items.statement: INR 95 crores spent in H1 FY25 out of INR 200 crores annual capex plan
items.quote: So, our capex plan for the year, for the current financial year is about INR 200 crores. And out of that, we have spent about INR 95 crores in H1 FY '24-'25.

items.statement: New facility in Kharkhauda expected to come on stream in Q1 FY26
items.quote: In alignment with the customer production requirements, we are setting up a new facility in Kharkhauda, expected to come on stream in financial year 2026, quarter one.

items.statement: EBITDA at INR 250 crores, down 120 bps YoY due to greenfield ramp-up costs
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 250 crores. While absolute profit remained resilient on a year-to-year basis, it is lower by 120 bps.

items.statement: Greenfield ramp-up costs to normalize in 6-9 months after SOP stabilization
items.quote: So as a window, it takes 6 to 9 months' time until the time the SOP and the production gets stabilised.

items.statement: Indian PV industry flat YoY, 6% sequential growth; 2-wheeler industry up 13% YoY, 7% sequential
items.quote: The Indian passenger vehicle industry remained relatively flat year -on-year, registering a 6% growth sequentially. Similarly, 2 -wheelers industry demonstrated 13% growth year -on-year and 7% sequentially.

items.statement: EV revenue share at 4.1% for the period, up from ~4% previously
items.quote: Our EV shares of the revenue for the period is 4.1%.

items.statement: Forex pass-through arrangements with customers at quarterly or half-yearly lag, no net P&L impact over time
items.quote: With some customers, it is at a quarterly lag, and with some customers, it is at a half yearly lag. So there could be impact on the P&L but that's more of a timing gap. Over a period of time, it really doesn't kind of impact our P&L in either way.

items.statement: Second greenfield plant delayed by 6 months by customer, SOP starting Q1 FY26
items.quote: The other plant, which we are talking about has gone delayed. The project has gone delayed by 6 months by a customer.

items.statement: Dividend policy: return 40% to shareholders, reinvest 60% in business
items.quote: We have a stated policy that we will return to the shareholders 40% and the rest will be reinvested in the business.

items.statement: ROCE exceeding 40% in H1 FY25, company remains debt-free
items.quote: We continue to remain debt-free and ROCE exceeding 40% in half one in financial year '25.

items.statement: Significant new model launches in Q2 and planned for H2 FY25, company inundated with customer requests
items.quote: There has been a significant number of new models launched in the quarter and planned for second half financial year '25.'

items.statement: New plant asset turns expected to align with existing plants once fully ramped up
items.quote: So as far as turnover is concerned, it should be more or less in line with what we have with the existing plants once the full ramp-up had taken place.

items.statement: Localization of EV components growing with volumes; cables and charging connectors already localized
items.quote: From our side, as we had mentioned earlier that the group has already started and locali sed the cables, started locali sing and achieved success in the charging connectors completely made here in India.

items.statement: October saw record 47% year-on-year growth; management confident about Q3 festive and wedding season
items.quote: In October we had a record month with a 47% year -on-year growth. Looking ahead we are confident that the festive season and heightened wedding activities in Quarter 3 paired with our continuous efforts in operational excellence and customer engagement will drive robust results.

items.statement: Targeting 13 more store openings before end of FY25; 12 stores opened April to present with Rs 35 crore capex
items.quote: At the beginning of the year, we announced our plan to add 20 new stores by FY25. We are pleased to report that from April 2024 to present time, we have successfully opened 12 stores with a total capital outlay of Rs. 35 crores. Looking ahead we are actively working on adding 13 more stores before the end of FY25.

items.statement: 12 stores opened in H1 FY25 with total capital outlay of Rs 35 crores
items.quote: We are pleased to report that from April 2024 to present time, we have successfully opened 12 stores with a total capital outlay of Rs. 35 crores.

items.statement: Excluding Rs 4.65 crore forex loss, Q2 EBITDA would be Rs 52.9 crore (27.4% YoY growth, 17.5% margin) and H1 EBITDA Rs 102.7 crore (28.1% YoY growth, 17.6% margin)
items.quote: Excluding the FOREX fluctuation our actual EBITDA for Q2 would be Rs 52.9 crores with a growth of 27.4% Y OY and for H1 it would be Rs 102.7 crores with a growth of 28.1% Y OY and margins of 17.5% and 17.6% respectively.

items.statement: If GST increases from 18% to 28%, revenue-neutral price increase would be ~8.5%; brands may absorb part via lower discounts or margin sharing
items.quote: If foreign exchange is stable and the GST increases , the revenue neutral price increase is likely to be 8%. I don't think that brands will take a full 8% increase in price if that comes. I don't think it's required as well. Anyways the consumer offers now in India are much higher than the rest of the world. It can be lowered.

items.statement: Share of luxury and high luxury watches at all-time high in H1 FY25; ASP rose to Rs 2.16 lakh from Rs 1.87 lakh
items.quote: Our ASP for H1 FY25 stood at Rs. 2,15,952 as compared to Rs 1.87 lakhs in H1 FY24. Share of luxury and high luxury watches for H1 FY25 stood at an all-time high.

items.statement: Certified pre-owned (Second Movement) billings grew 33% YoY to Rs 43 crore in H1 FY25; expect 20% growth for full year
items.quote: In our pre-owned segment, the certified pre-owned business, which is Second Movement, it has experienced a 25% year -on-year growth , reaching billings of Rs. 43 crores in H1 FY25.

items.statement: Favre Leuba India launch on 10-11 January 2025; available across 40 boutiques from 12 January with strong digital campaign; pre-orders >100,000 CHF at zero discount
items.quote: The launch in India will be in January. On 10 th of January there will be a launch at the Swiss embassy. On 11th of January is another launch at the Formula One circuit celebrating motor cars and the association of Favre Leuba with it. And we have from 12th of January onwards the Favre Leuba watches will be available across 40 boutiques in India along with a strong digital marketing campaign which

items.statement: Rimowa boutique profitable; targeting 8-10x business growth in 5 years; more luxury luggage brands coming next quarter
items.quote: Rimowa as you know, we're just about celebrating one year of us opening the boutique. It's been a fabulous experience. It's the first time that we did a boutique outside watches. It's one of our most profitable boutiques. We are going to be expanding that business. In my opinion over the next 5 years, we are going to at least target an 8X to 10X increase in the business of just Rimowa itself.

items.statement: Opportunity exists to open 20 stores per year for next 5 years; constrained by manpower and brand tie-ups
items.quote: But is there an opportunity in the next 5 years to open 20 stores a year, yes.

items.statement: Gross margins expected to be maintained at 30% irrespective of GST hike; management confident in ability to protect margins
items.quote: I do believe that. Again, as I mentioned I don't want to go into something that is when and if it happens, I am sure our management will make sure that our 10-year vision doesn't change. I can't comment about what will happen in a quarter or two quarter. Overall, yes, I think we will be able to maintain and grow those margins

items.statement: Same store growth 15.5% in H1 FY25; goal to grow overall business 10x in 10 years via mix of SSG and new stores
items.quote: As I mentioned our SSG has been 15.5% in the last 6 months. Our goal is to increase our overall revenue, and our overall business will be 10times in 10 years. I think it will be a healthy mix of same store growth and new store addition.

items.statement: Three stores combined into one under renovation; store count 72 as of October after 4 openings in October
items.quote: And the 2 that are shut down they're not shut down. They have been combined. Three stores have been combined into one store. So therefore, the store count will come down but the overall revenue will increase in this case. We are combining three different boutiques into one boutique in a location, this is under renovation right now.

items.statement: Expect ethanol supply of about 6.5 crore litres for current ethanol supply year 2024-25
items.quote: We expect this year's ethanol supply to be in the region of about 6 crores litres. I think the total ethanol quantity which we have contracted for the current year is 6.5 crores litres.

items.statement: Grain-based distillery capex of INR48 crore out of INR94 crore CWIP as of Sep 2024; balance is normal sugar capex
items.quote: Against capex of INR60 crores around INR48 crores is of grain. Rest is normal capex. 94, 48, 50 is grain. Rest is normal.

items.statement: No major sugar capacity enhancement planned; only marginal capex for country liquor bottling and value addition
items.quote: We do believe our sugar basically, we don't see any major capexes or capacity enhancement plans for the sugar in the foreseeable future.

items.statement: Contracted 6.5 crore litres ethanol for current supply year including syrup, B-heavy and C-heavy molasses routes
items.quote: We have bid for a certain quantity of syrup based ethanol. We have also bid for B -Heavy ethanol and we have some quantities of C heavy ethanol with the private OMCs, the private oil marketing companies.

items.statement: Expect higher cane crushing than last year in West UP; Asmoli and Meerganj also hopeful of higher crush
items.quote: In West UP, the crop is looking considerably good. We do expect some increase there. In Asmoli and Meerganj area, we could see maybe not the similar level of increase as compared to West UP, but we are definitely hopeful we will crush higher than last year.

items.statement: Targeting 60-70% sugar sales via non-conventional channels (institutional, pharma, packaged) in next couple of years from ~25% in H1 FY25
items.quote: This year in 6 months I think we've sold about close to 25% of our sugar that we've sold. Roughly 25% is on the non -Asian, non -conventional methodology, non -conventional challenges like institutions, industries and we hope over the next - we hope to continue to have this going up to maybe 60%, 70% in the next couple of years

items.statement: Government policy uncertainty on ethanol pricing, sugar MSP, exports; Supreme Court ruling on state control of industrial alcohol may create sporadic impacts
items.quote: We haven't got any favourable decisions last year in industries. We fear that if they don't take any sizable remedial measures, you could find some stresses building up, especially in the inefficient mills

items.statement: Maize availability for ethanol questioned; ~11 million tons maize needed for current tenders, may exceed national supply given poultry demand
items.quote: I think roughly 11 million tons of maize is required, which I don't think the country has the, I mean, if you look at the entire demand that the country has between poultry and ethanol sectors, I don't think this is the kind of numbers which are going to be produced.

items.statement: Pharma-grade sugar capability provides export premium advantage when exports are allowed
items.quote: We have pharma -grade sugar, so we do tend to get a premium for our sugar whenever export comes in. So that is the other advantage that we as a company enjoy.

items.statement: 1 GW TOPCon cell line expansion to be completed by Q4 FY25 with capex of INR670 crores
items.quote: We are executing a 1 GW TOPCon cell line expansion, which will be completed by Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Planning 2 GW wafer manufacturing facility targeted for commissioning in FY26 with capex of INR175 crores
items.quote: Further leveraging the opportunities for backward integration, we are planning an investment into a wafer manufacturing facility of 2 GW, which is targeted to be commissioned by

items.quote: We are also pleased to announce today our foray into aluminium frame manufacturing business by setting up a 36,000 metric ton per annum facility for captive consumption. This project would require a capex of INR230 crores.

items.statement: Aluminium frame manufacturing investment will improve EBITDA margin by 100 to 150 basis points
items.quote: This investment into aluminium frame manufacturing will improve our EBITDA margin by 100 basis points to 150 basis points.

items.statement: Plan to maintain current EBITDA margins for 2-3 years before potential softening as competition increases
items.quote: You know, it's our plan to maintain similar margins than what they are today. And according to us, we will continue to maintain these margins because the industry, the demand is very robust. We are looking at a little bit of softening the margins only after about 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Order book of INR6,233 crores (3.86 GW) executable over 10-12 months
items.quote: Q2 numbers is 3860, that's 3.86 GW, INR6,233 crores.

items.statement: DCR market demand estimated at 10-15 GW annually and growing with government schemes like PM Surya Ghar and Kusum
items.quote: I would estimate it's been 10 GW to 15 GW as of today, but it's growing.

items.statement: Module production mix: 70-80% TOPCon, rest mono PERC; lines are technology neutral
items.quote: At the moment, almost 70% to 80% of our production is TOPCon.

items.statement: US expansion on wait-and-watch due to political uncertainty around IRA; no capex deployed yet
items.quote: On US expansion, we are a little bit of a wait and watch looking at the political developments. We have signed, you know, an MOU and announced that we'll be setting up a gigawatt of facility along with our US partner that's Heliene.

items.statement: 4 GW cell + 4 GW module expansion capex of INR3,300 crores; land acquired, design agreements signed, tool orders not yet placed
items.quote: For the 4 GW plus 4 GW, which is coming from the IPO rate, is INR3,300 crores.

items.statement: Wafer and ingot backward integration will improve margins even without polysilicon manufacturing
items.quote: Yes. Even without getting into polysilicon, wafer and ingot itself will improve our margins.

items.statement: Non-DCR module prices at USD 0.155-0.16/W; DCR module prices at USD 0.23-0.24/W; cell prices at USD 0.13-0.15/W
items.quote: As of now, in India, the TOPCon module prices are around USD 0.155 to USD 0.16 for non-DCR and DCR is around USD0.23 to USD0.24.

items.statement: Net cash positive after IPO; long-term debt INR863 crores, short-term debt INR385 crores, cash INR1,520 crores as of Sep 30
items.quote: As on 30th September, long-term debts are INR 863 crores, short-term debts are INR385 crores. So, 1248 crores is the total debt. Against that, we have cash in hand of about INR1,520 crores, including the IPO proceeds.

items.statement: No formal revenue or margin guidance given; aim to maintain leadership position and grow with industry
items.quote: So, it's not that we cannot give any guidance, but what we can tell you is that, you know, being one of the top companies in the solar manufacturing space in India, we will continue to maintain leadership position and as the industry grows, we will be in the top tier of the growth.

items.statement: Interest cost for FY25 estimated at INR180-200 crores; long-term debt cost 9.25%, working capital 8.5%
items.quote: Full year? Around INR 180 crores-INR 200 crores.

items.statement: Expect double-digit growth in branded apparel in H2 FY25 and healthy EBITDA margins
items.quote: What we are seeing clearly is that with the wedding season spread out over five months now, that we should see a double-digit kind of a growth happening across apparel or a healthy growth happening across apparel.

items.statement: Target 200 additional stores over next 18 months via asset-light franchising, focusing on Ethnix by Raymond
items.quote: Aligned with our growth strategy, we are progressing towards expanding our retail footprint, targeting 200 additional stores over the next 18 months, primarily following an asset-light franchising model.

items.statement: Expect net working capital to normalize by end of March FY25 as festive and wedding season sales materialize
items.quote: Hence, we believe that by the end of March, we will be in a pretty regularized and normalized space of networking capital.

items.statement: Expect debt reduction by year-end FY25 as working capital eases
items.quote: Yes, that would be a fair assumption to make.

items.statement: Garmenting capacity expansion capex of INR 200 crores, 50% under implementation, balance over next 12 months
items.quote: We have invested INR200-odd crores of capex. 50% of that is already under implementation. Balance 50% will come over the next 12 months.

items.statement: Healthy order book in garmenting; added over 20 new clients across US, UK, Europe; early wins from Bangladesh Plus One
items.quote: In the garmenting business, we have a pretty decent and healthy order book. And I see that going forward in the second half, we should be able to deliver strong growth in the garmenting business.

items.statement: Branded apparel EBITDA margin improved to 13% vs 12.1% YoY; focused on intake margin and sourcing efficiencies
items.quote: The branded apparel segment delivered in a beta margin of 13% v ersus 12.1% in the same quarter of the previous year

items.statement: Branded textile EBITDA margin declined to 18.9% from 22.2% YoY due to operating deleverage from 8% revenue decline
items.quote: The segment EBITDA margin was impacted due to lower revenues primarily, and was at 18.9% in Q2 FY25, as compared to 22.2% in Q2 FY24.

items.statement: October retail optics positive across categories; double-digit growth on Diwali-to-Diwali comparison; wedding season from Nov 12 for 45-48 days
items.quote: The month of October has already shown good optics compared to the previous period and we anticipate this momentum to go ahead as we move through peak wedding and winter season.

items.statement: Launched Sleeps by Raymond sleepwear brand targeting unbranded market; 60 distributors, 1000 MBOs, target 8000-10000 stores in 6-8 months
items.quote: We have already appointed over 60 distributors, with product pricing positioned attractively between INR500 and INR999.

items.statement: Ethnix by Raymond at 129 stores (136 as of Oct), targeting 150 by end Q3 and 300 over 2-3 years; mass premium positioning
items.quote: We have reached 129 stores already in Ethnix by Raymond. And we are looking to cross 200 stores over the next 6 months to 8 months.

items.statement: Macro headwinds: geopolitical tensions, economic volatility, food inflation, excessive rainfall impacted Q2 discretionary spending
items.quote: Amidst these positive demand indicators, we remain mindful of a challenging ma croeconomic environment marked by ongoing geopolitical tensions and concerns around economic volatility

items.statement: Red Sea logistics challenges increased lead times by 2-3 weeks, delaying garmenting revenue recognition in H1
items.quote: The part of this garmenting result that you see is also due to certain logistics challenges that we got from due to the Red Sea piece, where the lead times have increased by around two to three weeks.

items.statement: Focused on improving sourcing and intake margins in apparel; intake margin efficiencies playing out strongly despite tough demand

items.quote: Around 18 -- between 18 -- around 18, we can say.

items.quote: Regarding the debt reduction, we are -- from today's level, like it's round about INR34,500, we are planning a reduction of around about another INR4,500 crores to INR5,000 crores in the remaining part of this financial year provided the markets support us.

items.quote: No. Actually, we are basically operating at a very good capacity. So we will be having an annualized crude steel production of around 19.2 million tons. So this is more or less -- I think it will be more than 95% of our capacity.

items.quote: So, we now have an installed biofuels manufacturing capacity of close to 450 KLPD, in Kashipur. And overall, if you see, the all India blending program has been running quite well.

items.quote: And if we get the land alloted in the next 6 months, then we will next 2.5, we should be able to go live on no commercial production on the tractor side. So, I think our original plan of FY '27, '28 remains there.

items.quote: The greenfield project, we're estimating will cost somewhere around INR 4,500 crores, which will obviously spend over the next 4 years' time, it is not upfront.

items.quote: But we expect from Q4, you will see a growth momentum to start on the export so far, exports have not done well for the European market, which is our largest market, has been under pressure. But now from Q4, we expect the numbers to start improving.

items.quote: We had a net profit of Rs. 576 crores on a consolidated basis for Q2, higher than the Q2 of last year, but slightly lower than Q1 of this year.

items.quote: For the first nine months of 2024, we are seeing a drop of 0.9 million barrels a day in crude oil imports into China.

items.quote: The crude tanker fleet is 100% on spot. The product tanker fleet is about 20%, 25% on charter. The gas carrier is fully fixed down. And dry bulk is on the spot market.
