items.statement: 30% more wedding dates in H2 FY25 vs last year, with strong business on books for November-December
items.quote: With 30% higher, wedding dates and increas e in foreign tourist arrivals expected in H2, we remain confident of comfortably delivering double- digit revenue growth, even excluding the positive impact of TajSATS

items.statement: Foreign tourist arrivals yet to reach pre-COVID levels, but expected to reach pre-COVID by end of FY25 and exceed next year
items.quote: And finally, we are benefiting from strong domestic spend on leisure and on business, with the FTA, which is the foreign tourist arrival, yet to reach the pre-COVID level. And ideally, it's pre-COVID plus another 20% after so many years would be the right level. So we have some way to go. And we remain fairly, not cautiously, but fairly optimistic that we are getting there on a month-by-month basi

items.statement: No debt on projects, funding company-owned hotels from internal accruals, net cash of INR2,500 crores on balance sheet
items.quote: There is no debt. And we will continue to do that where it makes sense, that it's a brand-enhancing opportunity. It comes at a compelling price or is with a very good partner. Then we will do that and push especially our new and reimagined businesses forward so that they become significant contributors in the times to come.

items.statement: TajSATS fully consolidated, revenue INR254 crores in Q2, up 19% YoY with 24% EBITDA margin, 59% market share in airline meals
items.quote: TajSATS clocked a revenue of INR254 crores, growing 19% over the previous year, with the EBITDA margin at an industry-leading 24%. TajSATS continues to lead the market with 59% share of meals served in the skies.

items.statement: Expect at least similar revenue in Q3 and Q4 as Q2, with potential for better performance
items.quote: So, we can expect at least to have similar revenue as what we got in Quarter 2 if not better in quarter three and quarter four in our total orders.

items.statement: Target to achieve EBITDA margin of around 12% over a few years
items.quote: There is no reason why we can't get back to our target, which we always internally set, to achieve an EBITDA margin of maybe 12% or something like that or close to that.

items.statement: Invested 90 crores in modernization of spinning, finishing, and garmenting; further term loan increase expected over next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: We have invested, about 90 crores and this has been done to up skill and modernize our entire spinning part, as well as the finishing equipment and even garmenting in different areas we have invested.

items.statement: Increased order book position in domestic and export markets for fabric and garments; yarn has no visibility beyond 30 days
items.quote: we are seeing that we had a first half in which there was subdued demand, and now with the inventory levels of all customers coming to normal, there is an increased order book position that we have both in the domestic and export markets for both fabric

items.statement: Margins expected to return to at least FY24 levels; yarn pricing remains a challenge
items.quote: we are seeing that the margins will come back and be at the leve l at least of what it was in FY 24

items.statement: Good demand revival from Asian markets (Hong Kong, South Korea, Australia) for garments; Europe and UK demand remains strong
items.quote: There is a good demand revival for garment business from the Asian markets such as Hong Kong, South Korea, Australia, that are growing for us as new geographies.

items.statement: Focus on high-value yarn products, worsted yarns, and core articles in uniforms and corporate wear; brand Simone Frederico & Figli expanding to 1200 locations
items.quote: We are continuing to focus on high value yarn products that will lead to better value and utilization.

items.statement: Yarn pricing pressure and subdued demand persist; inventory rose 50+ crores due to slower customer lifting and fiber stocking
items.quote: Our inventories have risen by about, 50 crores plus. And here we are seeing there is an inventory rise of about 15 crores in fiber, which is primarily because fiber prices were going up and we did stock a little extra.

items.statement: Technical textile JV with Tesca did 40 crore revenue and 2.5 crore PAT in H1 FY25; potential to reach 200 crore yearly revenue
items.quote: On a technical textile joint venture in this particular first half, they have done the revenue of 40 crore, and their PAT is 2.5 crore.

items.statement: Pushing for price increases in fabric and garment business; freight costs increased due to Red Sea crisis
items.quote: Moving forward we are pushing for these pricing both in the fabric and garment business where we can push and it is appearing that maybe if we get those price increases which we are asking for, we will be able to get the margin back.

items.statement: Mexico plant capex estimated at INR250 crores over next 2 years; decision within 3-4 months, production start 4-5 months after decision
items.quote: Yes, we have plans to put a plant in Mexico U.S., then it would be around INR250 crores capex.

items.statement: Regular capex in India for machinery upgradation and capacity enhancement ongoing
items.quote: And it's the regular capex here in India, we are doing for the upgradation and -- time to time. Yes, we are doing for the upgradation of the machineries and capacity enhancement.

items.statement: Selected for OEM supplies to new models in export markets; OEM export sales expected to increase this year and coming 2 years
items.quote: As informed earlier, we have been selected and received some good orders from our OEM supplies to new models in export market and based on that, our OEM export sales are expected to increase further in this year and in coming 2 years.

items.statement: Export OEM growth will continue at same speed, can be a little better in coming years
items.quote: The export OEM growth which is running it will run with same speed, but it can be a little better in coming years.

items.statement: BMW full volume supply expected by February-March at 20,000-25,000 yards per month
items.quote: Large volume has started already. By fourth quarter or by February-March, we'll have between 20,000 to 25,000 yards per month.

items.statement: Domestic OEM expected to remain same for next 6 months; footwear domestic not expected to grow much this year
items.quote: Domestic OEMs will be the same, not changed. Whatever we have done this 6 months, coming 6 months also will remain same.

items.statement: Management expects to reach INR1,000 crores revenue in FY26
items.quote: We are expecting. It should happen, okay? We are trying our best to make sure that it should happen.

items.statement: Gross margin increase from 44% to 47% due to both export mix increase and PVC price decline
items.quote: It is because of both reasons. Because of increase in exports. Majorly, it is on account of increase in exports.

items.statement: US-Mexico relations and Chinese competition in Mexico create uncertainty for Mexico plant decision
items.quote: Because how is the relation between U.S.A. and Mexico. Becau se USA is not happy with China a nd in Mexico, a lot of Chinese companies are there with which Americans are not satisfied

items.statement: Focus on higher margin segments; exiting low-price domestic OEM business
items.quote: We are only working on higher segments. Lower segments, we are not working.

items.statement: Ford Motor Company added as new export OEM customer
items.quote: We are doing the models and the Ford Motor company got added to exports, some models got added.

items.statement: Q2 order bookings INR 46.8 billion, up 333% YoY; order backlog INR 98.4 billion as at Sep'24, up 57% from Mar'24
items.quote: Our order book in Q2 saw bookings of INR 46.8 billion, up by 333% YoY, compared to INR 10.8 billion in quarter ended Sep' 23.

items.statement: H1 order bookings INR 57 billion vs INR 20.8 billion last year; export orders 47% of H1 bookings
items.quote: Similarly, on an H1 basis, we booked about INR57 billion of order compared to INR20.8 billion in the last year.

items.statement: Q2 gross margin 41%, EBITDA margin 18.8%, PBT margin 17.5%; H1 gross margin 40.8%, EBITDA margin 19.5%
items.quote: We generated a significant 41% gross margin in the quarter. And as a result, overall EBITDA of INR 2.1 billion approximately at a rate of 18.8%.

items.statement: Management maintains sustainable gross margin range 35-40% quarterly; full year target to beat last year's 35.6%
items.quote: I still maintain that range of 35% to 40% as range on a quarter-to-quarter basis. But on the full year basis, we always said that we want to do better than what we did in the last year.

items.statement: Planned capex $8-10 million over next 12 months for transformer capacity supporting both AC and HVDC
items.quote: Depending upon the need of the plant, it will be somewhere between $5 million to $10 million.

items.statement: Strong domestic pipeline from Power Grid, private TBCB players, data centers, steel; export orders growing from group entities
items.quote: We are seeing a sustainable pipeline, I think we had some slowdown during the last quarter when elections were there. But apart from that, I think now we have seen that there is good traction which is happening in terms of pipeline for TBCB project.

items.statement: No quarterly order run-rate guidance; sustainable yearly run-rate (excl. 2 large orders) INR 55-58 billion; with large orders INR 78-82 billion
items.quote: If we take out these 2 large orders, those are about INR30 billion. Sandeep is trying to say that excluding these 2 large orders on an H1 basis, we have routine orders of INR27-28 billion. If we extrapolate, that becomes like INR55 billion to INR58 billion on a regular run rate other than the large 2 deals.

items.statement: Order backlog: 62% private, 32% central utilities/PSUs, 6% state utilities; export ~40% of backlog
items.quote: In terms of breakup of orders in hand of about INR98 billion, about 62% of the orders in hand we have from the private segment customers, about 32% orders in hand are from the central utilities and PSUs, and about 6% orders in the overall portfolio from the state utilities.

items.statement: HVDC tenders (Fatehpur-Bhadla, Khavda-Nagpur) decision expected within 3 months; addressable portion $1-2 billion
items.quote: I think it should happen within the next 3 months.

items.statement: Domestic pricing improving; export orders margin-accretive; royalty ~1% of revenue
items.quote: Various factors, first, there is also an improvement in the pricing in the domestic market. Export orders are also accretive and some of the business lines have better profitability.

items.statement: Cash & equivalents INR 6.8 billion Sep'24 (incl. cash pool lending); cash pool yield ~7%; forex loss INR 55 million in Q2
items.quote: Cash and Cash Equivalent balance improved and stood at 6.8 BINR as on 30th Sep 2024 vs 2.8 BINR as on 31st March 2024 and net debt of 0.1 BINR as on 30th Sep 2023.

items.statement: Expect reduction of $20-25 per ton in coking coal prices in Q3FY25
items.quote: We expect a reduction of around $20 to $25 per ton in coking coal prices in Q3FY25.

items.statement: Taken price hike of Rs 1,000-2,000 across products in Q3 so far
items.quote: We have taken a price hike of 1,000 to 2,000 across products in Q3 so far.

items.statement: Demand post festive season is good and prices are holding up
items.quote: Demand post season, festive season is good, and prices are holding up.

items.statement: Expect H2 to be better than H1 driven by strong seasonal demand and lower input cost
items.quote: We expect H2 to be better than H1 driven by strong seasonal demand and lower input cost.

items.statement: Capex in Q2 was Rs 2,642 crore; cumulative capex under current expansion program is Rs 20,562 crore
items.quote: Our CAPEX in quarter stood at Rs. 2,642 crore. With this cumulative CAPEX spent under the current expansion program is around Rs. 20,562 crore.

items.statement: Maintenance capex is about Rs 600 crore per quarter (Rs 2,500 crore annually)
items.quote: So, Pallav, our maintenance CAPEX is close to about 600 crores on a quarterly basis.

items.statement: Angul expansion project progressing well as per schedule; blast furnace scheduled for commissioning in Q4FY25
items.quote: In fact, the blast furnace is scheduled to get commissioned in Q4 itself and we are at the advanced stages of commissioning.

items.statement: DRI second plant on track for Q3FY26 (not Q4FY27 as earlier typo suggested)
items.quote: So, DRI is on track for the third quarter of FY '26. I apologize for the goof up over there, but it is 3Q FY '26 only and not 4Q FY '27.

items.statement: Slurry pipeline 80% complete; targeting commissioning in Q4FY25
items.quote: The good part is we have almost completed 80% of the project as of now when we are talking.

items.statement: Utkal B1 coal mine expected to start in Q4FY25; Utkal B2 expected next financial year
items.quote: We are very hopeful of starting our Utkal B1 in quarter 4 of this financial year.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA Rs 2,124 crore; EBITDA per ton Rs 11,467, down 15% sequentially
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA on a consolidated basis for the quarter was Rs. 2,124 crore and EBITDA per ton stood at Rs. 11,467 per ton, down by 15% on a sequential basis.

items.statement: Standalone ASP down 3% sequentially to Rs 61,695; cost flattish sequentially
items.quote: So, if you divide by standalone, then standalone is coming around 61,695, down by 3% around from the last quarter.

items.statement: Iron ore prices increased Rs 500-1,000 per ton by NMDC/OMC; spot spreads compressing as steel prices haven't kept pace
items.quote: Iron ore, right now, they slightly increased by NMDC and OMC in the tune of Rs. 500 to Rs. 1,000 per ton. So, that is there.

items.statement: Net debt increased to Rs 12,464 crore; net debt/EBITDA at 1.21x, below 1.5x red line; expect reduction from peak debt levels
items.quote: Our consolidated net debt is Rs. 12,464 crore at the end of Q2 which has increased from Rs. 10,462 crore reported in last quarter.

items.statement: HSM utilization at ~40%; ramp-up to 80%+ dependent on blast furnace commissioning and metallics availability
items.quote: We are running at almost 40% utilization of HSM.

items.statement: Expect EIR from USFDA in December and positive outcome
items.quote: We are pretty confident that this will get resolved and it all depends on the EIR, which we expect will be coming in December. And we expect a positive outcome of that.

items.statement: Remediation costs up to $2 million for FY25
items.quote: Rashmi, a little bit was already spent and we expect that this could be anywhere up to $2 million for this year.

items.statement: Q3 lost sales impact less than Q2
items.quote: In the sales, the impact of lost sales will be less than quarter 2.

items.statement: Paracetamol demand improving in Q3, normalcy expected by Q4
items.quote: We saw some positivity in Q2 and we think that it will improve in Q3, but definitely not come back to normalcy. Rashmi Shetty: Okay. It will not come back only. Krishna Prasad: In Q3. Q4 could be a normal

items.statement: Capex spend INR1,324 million in Q2, primarily INR794 million in Granules Life Sciences
items.quote: Capex spend during the quarter was INR1,324 million, primarily invested in Granules Life Science amounting to INR794 million.

items.statement: Three approvals pending from Gagillapur in Q4 FY25
items.quote: We have about three approvals pending from Gagillapur in Q4.

items.statement: Q2 gross margin 62%, up 1,036 bps YoY and 307 bps QoQ due to favourable formulation mix
items.quote: Gross margin as a percentage of sales for Q2 FY '25 was 62% as compared to 51.7% in Q2 FY '24. Gross margin as compared to Q2 FY '24 is up by 1,036 basis points achieved by higher favourable mix of FD sales.

items.statement: Q3 gross margin expected moderate, slightly better than Q1 but not as high as Q2
items.quote: So overall, you can look at not as high as Q2. Probably would have to consider a moderate margin in Q3.

items.statement: API/PFI decline due to price erosion and high customer inventory, especially paracetamol
items.quote: The API and PFI segment saw reduced contributions due to price erosion and softer demand in light of the still continuing high customer inventory levels, especially for paracetamol.

items.statement: Growth driven by new launches from GPI (CNS/ADHD) and Europe finished dosage sales
items.quote: Our growth in the near future will be driven by new product launches from our GPI site in the US market, especially the CNS and ADHD segment and finished dosage sales in Europe.

items.statement: GLS Phase 1 commissioned, commercial dispatches of monograph products started; prescription products for Europe targeted Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26
items.quote: Phase 1 with a capacity of 2.5 billion doses ha ve been commissioned and commercial dispatches of monogra ph products have commenced. We are targeting prescription products commercialization for Europe inQ4 '25 and Q1 of '26

items.statement: Voluntary pause at Gagillapur after six Form 483 observations; engaged third-party consultants for remediation
items.quote: Following the inspection, we took a voluntary pause in manufacturing and distribution to assess any possible risk to the already manufactured products and also future production.

items.statement: R&D spend INR524 million in Q2 (5.4% of sales); H1 spend INR1,144 million, up 26% YoY
items.quote: R&D spend of INR524 million in Q2 FY '25, this continues to be a consistent focus for Granules. R&D spend in H1 FY '25 of INR1,144 million is significantly higher, 26% more than that of the same period last year.

items.statement: 17 ANDAs under review in US, 4 in Europe, 8 in rest of world
items.quote: Granules at present has 17 in the US and four applications in Europe and eight applications in rest of the world under review for approval.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations INR2,007 million in Q2
items.quote: Cash flow from operations for the quarter was INR2,007 million as compared to INR329 million in Q2 FY '24 and INR2,161 million in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Net debt INR7,973 million, down from INR8,421 million at March 2024
items.quote: Our net debt was at INR7,973 million as compared to INR7,941 million in Q1 FY '25. Our net debt was INR8,421 million at the end of March '24.

items.statement: Core business EBITDA margin is 4.5-5.5%; current quarter EBITDA 2.5% due to 2-3% revenue investment in growth initiatives
items.quote: Otherwise, our business as usual, we are generating 4.5 to 5.5% of EBITDA, which is our regular performance.

items.statement: No additional CAPEX planned for FY25; expansion CAPEX of ~40 crores completed over last 2 years including 15 crores for SMT line
items.quote: For this year, we are not planning any additional CAPEX as of now. If there is a business requirement, we will take the call as and when it is required.

items.statement: EMS business development ongoing; separate reporting planned in 3-4 quarters; auto electronics certifications targeted by December end
items.quote: We are also having a plan of having a separate reporting in the 3 or 4 quarters as things progress.

items.statement: EMS focus on auto electronics and IT peripherals; first phase for captive consumption then external clients; R&D team grown to 20-25 members
items.quote: So, we are definitely looking at auto electronics, electronics being our backbone. So, definitely auto electronics.

items.statement: CSS segment historically unprofitable due to consumer electronics services; exited that business; now focusing on IT, banking, solar for profitability
items.quote: We used to support consumer electronics repairs, break/fix and repairs which was not, unfortunately, something that we could make much of, and that actually dragged a lot of our productivity and our profits.

items.statement: Short term funding through internal accruals; long term fundraising an option if needed
items.quote: In the short term, we are looking to manage our internal accruals. Long term, if we could, we will look at the option of fundraising.

items.statement: Q1 growth driven by government project revenues; quarterly fluctuations expected; focused on long-term growth
items.quote: Quarter 1, as you might have noticed and we also announced, there were project revenues from the government which added to a substantial increase.

items.statement: SMT line setup cost 15 crores including factory infrastructure; capacity sufficient for expansion; no new CAPEX planned this year
items.quote: Yes, the last year we have set up one SMT line, so for that we have invested, let's say, 15 crores.

items.statement: Investing 2-3% of revenue in EMS, R&D and growth initiatives; employee costs up due to hiring 75-80% complete for current needs
items.quote: I think we are focusing on EMS and R&D initiatives. We have invested on these new people, whom we have added in the last 2-3, quarters.

items.statement: Addressable market: Products & Solutions ~2000 crores (18-20% share); CSS ~5350 crores; EMS targeting box-build and Make-in-India opportunities
items.quote: The overall performance of the company is reviewed under 2 business units, Products and Solutions Group and Customer Support Services.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to remain in 19% to 21% range for FY25 despite IT transformation costs starting Q3/Q4
items.quote: But yes, I mean, we'll be fairly gearing that 19% to 21% range.

items.statement: Odisha composite facility (sewing, elastic plant, distribution center, raw material store) expected to start in Q4 FY25 with minimal pre-operative cost impact
items.quote: So the preoperative costs in Odisha is not going to have a significant impact on the bottom line.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin at 22.6% driven by stable raw material costs, higher selling efficiency, measured employee costs and judicious operating costs
items.quote: Stable raw material costs, sustained higher selling efficiency, measured employee costs and judicious operating costs have contributed to good EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Consumer sentiment remains muted but festive period showed positive signs; secondary sales slightly better than primary in Q2
items.quote: We don't believe that the consumer sentiments are back to where it was or where we would like it to be. It is still pretty muted.

items.statement: Premiumization within categories, outerwear mix shift, and higher e-commerce share drove 4% price-mix growth in Q2 with no price increases
items.quote: There has not been any price increase at all. The differential that we see between the volume growth and the value growth, there are two factors. One is definitely there is premiumization within the categories.

items.statement: Distributor inventory at 40 days, down 3 days from start of year; expect further 2 days reduction in H2 FY25
items.quote: We had about 40 days of inventory at the distributor level today, which is an improvement of about 3 days when compared to the beginning of the year.

items.statement: Competitor retailer payouts at all-time high creating stress on secondary performance; IT transformation costs to impact margins from Q3/Q4
items.quote: It could be because retailer payout seems to be at an all-time high, some competition, which puts a little bit of stress on our secondary performance.

items.statement: EBO expansion target of 150-160 stores for FY25 remains on track
items.quote: We will manage to achieve that number this year as well.

items.statement: $1 billion revenue target delayed by a couple of years due to pandemic disruptions and weak retail; management to provide specifics next call
items.quote: And now we feel it may take a couple of years more than what we thought to achieve this number.

items.statement: Subcontracting charges at ~1% of revenue (down from historical 3-3.5%); expected to remain in 1-2% range
items.quote: As a percentage of top line, it's around a percentage, I mean, 1%, not more than that.

items.statement: E-commerce grew 41% in H1 FY25; growth significantly higher than company average driven by quick commerce and marketplace
items.quote: E-commerce channel had a growth of 41% in H1, which affirms the opportunity in online channels.

items.statement: Working capital days improved to 61 from 75 at end FY24; inventory days at 168 vs 93 at end FY24 but distribution inventory optimized to 68 days
items.quote: Working capital days was 61 days, which was an improvement over 75 days in the end of FY '24.

items.statement: Dividend payout at INR 300/share in Q1 and Q2 FY25 (above 60% PAT policy) due to healthy cash reserves; sustainability depends on results and cash position
items.quote: So as of now, our cash reserves are quite healthy and we are able to give a higher dividend. That's why in the first quarter also, we had a higher dividend of INR 300 per share.

items.statement: Women's business growing at par with company average; independent sales team and expanded portfolio (bras, cotton stretch, synthetics) driving growth
items.quote: Our H1 results for women's are positive. We are not degrowing in those parts of the business.

items.statement: Athleisure secondary/tertiary demand positive but primary sales below par due to distributor inventory normalization; category seen as promising long-term
items.quote: Even for this year, while overall our consumer level tertiary as well as secondary numbers have been very promising for athleisure, there is some level of correction in primary.

items.statement: Odisha facility subsidies include state wage contribution of ~INR 2,500 per head for 5-7 years; expected to add to EBITDA during subsidy period
items.quote: For example, I think in the wages, state government will be contributing to almost INR2,500 per head.

items.statement: Maintaining hospital EBITDA margin expansion guidance of 200 bps for full year FY25, factoring in Manesar losses
items.quote: Yes, yes. So we are maintaining our margin guidelines. And when we had given that guidelines, we have factored in these losses of Manesar, which is obvious because it is a sort of Greenfield project.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR800-900 crores per year for FY25 and FY26 including maintenance and growth capex
items.quote: Yes. So we are expecting around INR800 crores to INR900 crores approximate capex, which includes maintenance as well as growth capex for both the years, each year.

items.statement: Agilus Diagnostics targets 25-26% EBITDA margin by FY27-28 driven by operating leverage and cost optimization
items.quote: So what we are seeing -- what we feel is that by in another 15 to 18 months, we should be able to be in the range of about 25%, 26% kind of margins. In the upcoming quarters, we'll be able to see steady progress on these

items.statement: Fortis Manesar 350-bed hospital commenced operations in September with initial 50 beds, targeting EBITDA breakeven in 15 months
items.quote: Yes. So we have initially started with 50 beds. And as we progress in occupancy metrics, we will open more beds. So we have assumed, we expect around 15 months' time for the breakeven of this facility in terms of EBITDA.

items.statement: Hospital key specialties (oncology, neurosciences, cardiac, orthopedics, gastroenterology, renal) grew 13.6% YoY and contributed 61% of hospital revenue
items.quote: This growth was largely driven by revenue gains in our key specialty areas such as oncology, neurosciences, cardiac sciences, orthopedics, gastroenterology and renal sciences. Collectively, these specialties achieved a 13.6% year-on-year growth and accounted for 61% of total hospital revenue.

items.statement: Hospital occupancy improved to 72% in Q2 FY25 from 69% YoY, occupied beds up 5.8% to 2,939, ARPOB up 7.6% to INR2.37 crores per annum
items.quote: Continuing from Q1, our hospital occupancy further improved to 72% compared to 69% in Q2 of financial year '24. This translates into occupied bed increase by about 5.8% to 2,939 beds compared to 2,779 beds in the Q2 of financial year '24.

items.statement: Acquiring 31.52% stake in Agilus from PE investors at INR1,778 crores enterprise value, funded via INR1,500 crores NCD, deal closure by early December
items.quote: it is in public domain. We have gone for the shareholder approval also for that. I think the number is INR1,778 crores enterprise value. Anand Kuppuswamy: Equity value. Vivek Goyal: Yes, for 31% stake

items.statement: Legal costs higher in FY25 due to increased High Court hearings; expected to decrease from FY26
items.quote: Yes. So this year, Atul, we don't expect the legal cost to be low. In fact, this year, the legal costs have been slightly higher than the last year because more number of hearings, etcetera has happened in the high court compared to last year.

items.statement: Agilus Diagnostics expects double-digit revenue growth trajectory from FY26 onwards as brand transition impact normalizes
items.quote: Yes, definitely, that will happen. So we are seeing that trend happening. So I think after this year, you will see that the basis will change because of whatever changes we have done compared to last year, the brand transition, all those things happening now.

items.statement: Agilus Diagnostics pricing stable on blended basis with differential pricing across segments and regions, similar to industry peers
items.quote: No, it's fairly constant. So we have differential pricing across different segments, across different regions. And it's kind of very similar to how the rest of the industry players move.

items.statement: Hospital EBITDA margin improved 300 bps YoY to 21.4% in Q2 FY25; 11 facilities above 20% margin contributing 75% of hospital revenue vs 8 facilities and 62% in FY24
items.quote: The hospital business reported a n operating EBITDA of INR355 crores, driving a robust 300 basis point improvement in margins from 18.4% in Q2 of financial year '24 to 21.4% in Q2 of financial year '25.

items.statement: Digital revenue grew 30% YoY in Q2 FY25, contributing 29.3% of hospital revenue vs 25.6% in Q2 FY24; EMR implemented across 11 units
items.quote: At the same time, revenues from digital channels via website, mobile application and digital campaigns have witnessed a 30% year-on-year growth in Q2 of financial year '25. Digital revenue contributed 29.3% to overall hospital revenue versus 25.6% in Q2.

items.statement: Evaluating divestment of Sacred Heart hospital in Bangalore (Richmond Road) due to small size and rental cost drag on margins
items.quote: Another hospital in this category is a very small hospital Sacred Heart in Bangalore, which actually we are planning to divest and get rid of this hospital because it is very small hospital.

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA expected below 1.5x by year-end FY25 post Agilus stake acquisition funded by INR1,500 crores NCD
items.quote: So Shyam, balance sheet w ill remain to be very healthy even after post acquisition stake through debt of INR1,500 crores because we are seeing a very steady increase in the EBITDA. And with this run rate, by year -end, our debt to EBITDA will be below 1.5, which is quite healthy from that angle.

items.statement: Expect to open INR8,000 crores of new launch inventory for sale in Q3 and Q4 FY25
items.quote: we'll open about INR8,000 plus crores of inventory for new launch in this quarter and the next quarter, in fact, majority being in the last quarter

items.statement: Target rental income of INR150 crores in FY26 and INR200 crores by October 2026 from commercial portfolio
items.quote: by next year, financial year, March, we should get to INR150 crores. The year after, we should get to about INR200 crores by the end of the year. Or 6 months later, I would say possibly by October 2026

items.statement: Target rental income of INR500 crores over next 4-5 years from commercial office portfolio
items.quote: For the larger portfolio, our -- the target is, of course, to get the rental income over the next 5 years of INR500 crores.

items.statement: Deployed INR417 crores via HDFC platform across 2 projects; expect to deploy another INR300+ crores shortly
items.quote: So far, we have deployed INR417 crores. That has been deployed between 2 projects, and we are expecting to deploy another approximately INR300-plus crores very, very shortly.

items.statement: Launch pipeline GDV of INR13,600 crores; plan to open INR8,000 crores for sale in H2 FY25
items.quote: our expectation is in the current quarter and the next quarter, we will launch - the GDV of the launch pipeline is approximately INR13,600 crores, of which we are expecting to totally open for sale approximately INR8,000 crores.

items.statement: Average embedded EBITDA margin on presales 28-32%; Thane project ~30%, redevelopment projects 22-24%
items.quote: we would land up at about a 30% margin between -- EBITDA margin between 28% and 32% on an average.

items.statement: Sustenance project realizations up 15-17% YoY; sales velocity up 14% despite price hikes
items.quote: we have seen last year to this year, price appreciation in sustenance projects of between 15% to 17% between Purva and Provident. And also, what we have seen is that with the increased prices, our sustenance projects, sales have gone up by about 14%.

items.statement: Robust demand in Tier 1 cities; Tier 2 emerging as investment destination; >90% buyers are end-users, 65-75% using home loans
items.quote: The Indian Real Estate sector continued to experience a robust demand, with Tier 1 cities witnessing the sturdy demand, while Tier 2 cities are emerging as a new investment destination.

items.statement: Focus on 6 core markets (Bangalore, Hyderabad, Chennai, Mumbai, Pune, NCR); 80% focus there, 20% opportunistic in Goa/Kochi/Coimbatore
items.quote: 80% our focus will be on these 4, 5 markets, 20% will be more opportunistic on the markets -- other markets, which we are present.

items.statement: Election-related approval delays caused ~1 quarter deferment of launches across industry
items.quote: most of the -- actually, the delay has happened on account of almost a quarter that got lost off during the election process. So the plan sanction across the country was kind of deferred in that sense.

items.statement: Net debt INR2,430 crores, net D/E 1.29x; target to keep absolute debt stable and bring net D/E under 1x over 3-4 years
items.quote: Our net debt stands at INR2,430 crores as on September 30, 2024, with the net debt-to-equity ratio at 1.29.

items.statement: Acquired Miami Apartments redevelopment at Breach Candy, Mumbai; estimated rates INR125,000-140,000/sq ft carpet
items.quote: This marks our entry into Uber luxury South Mumbai market where rates are estimated in the range of INR125,000 to INR140,000 per square feet of carpet area.

items.statement: Lokhandwala cluster redevelopment GDV INR700 crores; total area 4.3 acres with combined GDV INR2,350 crores
items.quote: Adding a new cluster of societies with the potential of GDV of INR700 crores to its existing redevelopment projects, bringing to the total land area in the region to around 4.3 acres with a combined GDV of INR2,350 crores for the project.

items.statement: Signed JDA for 1.95 acre land in Electronic City, Bangalore; saleable area 2.6 lakh sq ft, GDV INR250 crores
items.quote: The company also signed a JDA for 1.95 acre land parcel at the prime location in Electronic City Market in Bangalore. The land parcel is adjacent to Purva Western project and will be saleable area of 2.6 lakh square feet with a potential GDV of INR250 crores.

items.statement: Commercial portfolio: 3M sq ft plan approved, 2.3M sq ft completion expected in FY26
items.quote: currently, we have about a total of 3 million square foot which is plan approved, of which we are expecting to complete about 2.2 million square foot, 2.3 million square foot in the next financial year.

items.statement: Land bank target: grow from 15M sq ft net to 45M sq ft over 2-3 years to support 22.5M sq ft annual launch capacity
items.quote: That net 15 million square foot, we would like to take it up to 45 million square foot. And the logic behind that is that we should have over the next 3 years' time frame, not today, not tomorrow but over 2, 3 years' time frame.

items.statement: Management maintains sustainable EBITDA margin guidance of around 15%
items.quote: we should be delivering around 15% margins on sustainable basis

items.statement: Management reiterates 15% EBITDA margin guidance to the market
items.quote: 15% is our guidance to the market

items.statement: Capex run rate of INR 70-80 crores per year expected for next 2-3 years
items.quote: we are doing something like INR70 crores, INR80 crores every year from last 2, 3 years. And this is the pace we assume next 2, 3 years also

items.statement: Strong order book in iron, pellet, DRI making with four Blast Furnace Cast House contracts and six new Taphole Clay customers
items.quote: We have a strong order book in the iron, pellet, DRI making business. In iron making, we have seen a good order momentum in Blast Furnace Cast House. We have four contracts and added six new customers in Taphole Clay

items.statement: Advanced discussions with OEMs for long-term coke oven and blast furnace stores associations
items.quote: We are also in advanced discussion for long -term association with OEMs for coke oven and blast furnace stores. We should strengthen our order books in the coming quarters as well

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 16% from 14.9% despite raw material cost pressure
items.quote: The EBITDA for the first half year was at INR279 crores, while EBITDA margins improved to 16%, up from 14.9% in the previous corresponding period

items.statement: Alumina-based raw material cost increases pressuring margins; pass-through to customers takes 2-3 months with zero net impact over time
items.quote: increasing raw material costs, especially for alumina-based materials and chromite sands exerted pressure on margins

items.statement: Raw material price pass-through mechanism has 2-3 month lag; zero net impact over cycle but timing uncertain
items.quote: it will always have a lag. We will negotiate, it will take two, three months, but when that round year price goes down, it also takes two, three months to reduce the prices. So it is zero net impact

items.statement: Steel industry growth estimated at 2.7-2.9% vs market talk of 6-7%; cement capacity additions delayed
items.quote: If you check JSW's announcement, it is 2.7% growth in steel in India. And we have our calculation 2.9% growth

items.statement: Two steel plant expansions commissioning in November-December; one plant with 70-75% share
items.quote: two steel plants are going to commission their expansion, SMS4 or XYZ. And one plant in December is also going to commission where we have almost a 70%, 75% share

items.statement: Chinese refractory dumping at $650-700 CIF impacting commodity ladle business; maintaining margins over volumes
items.quote: they are dumping like anything, they are selling at $650, $700 CIF. So either I reduce my margin and compete in that commodity market, then we will say, okay, the margin has come down. We are maintaining the margin at the cost of a little bit of volumes

items.statement: Iron making, pellet, DRI business growing at 6% but lower realization; cement also lower realization impacting mix
items.quote: we are growing rapidly at a good pace in iron making, pellet, DRI business and it is still a small business if we talk in totality and it is about 6% growth

items.statement: Net debt/EBITDA reduced to 0.3x from 0.6x at start of year through operational efficiencies
items.quote: we managed to reduce our net debt EBITDA ratio to 0.3x from 0.6x in the beginning of the year

items.statement: Local-for-local production increased from 55-60% to 65-70%; target 80% local production
items.quote: maybe two years back, it was 40%, 45% import, now, it has come Sensitivity: Internal down to 30, 35%. And in coming days, it will further come down. And our target is to take it to 80% roughly for local-for-local

items.statement: Volume growth target of 1-2% above steel industry growth maintained despite current challenges
items.quote: I still maintain that statement. We want to grow 1% or 2% more than the industry

items.statement: Management expects growth to continue in coming quarters and is bullish about next two quarters
items.quote: I would say that we see this growth to continue in the coming quarters as well and now with the new government shaping up in the US, the overall business scenario will get better, especially if you look at the outbound from India.

items.statement: Management expects exports from India to US to increase drastically over next 2 years
items.quote: I think we are looking at least for the next 2 years, the exports from India to the US will increase drastically and we are really looking forward to that business growth which will be coming over.

items.statement: No major capex planned; borrowings are purely for working capital
items.quote: We are not looking at any major big investment in this. We want to continue on the same growth path which we have and that is working well for us and we want to focus on reducing the cost and getting more efficiency in the system.

items.statement: Evaluating EV trailer fleet for green logistics but capex is big
items.quote: We are looking at having EV trailers for the movement of export containers. So, we are working on it though the CAPEX is big in that. So, we are still trying to evaluate, look at the profitability, look at how this will work out.

items.statement: Order book and pipeline are good for coming quarters
items.quote: So, coming quarters, they are looking good, the order book is good, the pipeline is good and we feel that the growth in last few quarters will continue.

items.statement: Ocean freight margins are increasing and getting better
items.quote: Margins are increasing, and margins are getting better. I would say that rates are fluctuating still because sometimes, now Indian market on the ocean flight is completely dependent on the Chinese market.

items.statement: Ocean freight rates fluctuate with Chinese market; rates softened in Q2 but picking up in October
items.quote: So, now what we were seeing in the first quarter of this financial year, the freights in China were very good. So, the rates really got very high in India also, but in the second quarter, it was a soft market, so the rate started getting lower.

items.statement: Import logistics growing well with good contracts and renewals in government sector
items.quote: There has been good traction on the import side also. We have been able to get some good contracts and get our old contracts renewed, especially in the government sector contracts.

items.statement: Air freight volumes grew 4.5x YoY after becoming IATA agent
items.quote: So, Tanush, the strategy is, that we were not IATA agents earlier. We were outsourcing this activity through other IATA agents. But as you know that last year, we became IATA agents ourselves and because of that we were able to focus on this business more ourselves.

items.statement: Export contributes ~80% of business; import share rising and expected to grow
items.quote: As we mentioned that export is our major focus always. That is our strength. But I would say that import is picking up. Definitely, imports is rising which is good news for us, because we see imports to rise much better in coming quarters.

items.statement: Geopolitical risks (Ukraine war) may ease, supporting international trade
items.quote: I think there could be some respite on that and the exports to Europe and all will pick up better and even the energy, the overall fuel prices will also ease out.

items.statement: Short-term borrowings increased substantially in H1 FY25 purely for working capital
items.quote: Borrowing is only working capital. There is no CAPEX. There is nothing of any other usage, but it is purely being used for working capital.

items.statement: Planning acquisition in LCL space targeting company with 100+ crore topline
items.quote: We are looking at some acquisition in the LCL space which we have mentioned earlier also because we feel that LCL is one product that we don't have with us and we are willing to acquire a mid-size company which will augment our growth overall.

items.statement: Freight Jar adoption low but opening doors to new customers
items.quote: Freight Jar overall is doing good for us, but I would like to say that surely the acceptance is low. People are very willing to know as to what is the new product, what is the new age business, and what are the new options which are available to them, but the adoption is still low.

items.statement: No plans to report air freight revenue separately; all revenue under one head
items.quote: have a separate revenue available with me. I don't have it with me right now, but I just have the volume numbers with me, but I don't have the revenue numbers with me. But you can send a mail to us and we can share that with you. Because all the revenue goes under one head only, so that is the reason we don't divide it in our numbers

items.statement: Chennai project expected to be operational by end of Q3 FY26
items.quote: Chennai project construction is progressing well and expecting to be operational by end of Q3 FY26.

items.statement: Total CAPEX of roughly Rs. 1,500 crores to Rs. 2,000 crores for future parks over next 7-8 years
items.quote: We have a total CAPEX of roughly Rs. 1,500 crores to Rs. 2,000 crores and we are proposing to raise only Rs. 500 to Rs. 800 out of that through equity.

items.statement: Board approved fundraising via QIP or private placement up to Rs. 800 crores for projects over next 7-8 years
items.quote: Aligned with our expansion plan, our board has approved fundraising through a qualified institution placement or private placement up to Rs. 800 crores supporting our projects for the next 7 to 8 years.

items.statement: QIP expected to be completed before end of current financial year
items.quote: Hopefully before the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Plan to add 3 to 5 new parks excluding Chennai over next five years
items.quote: It could be between 3 and 5, excluding Chennai.

items.statement: Mature parks expected to deliver 3% to 5% footfall growth annually with pricing at inflation rate
items.quote: If the matured park will give anywhere between 3% to 5% of footfall growth and then pricing maybe equal to the inflation rate in the country, so that is what we follow on with respect to the matured park.

items.statement: Bangalore park expected low single-digit footfall growth and ARPU growth of 5% to 8% per annum over next 5 years
items.quote: 5 years is hard to predict, but I think we can expect low single-digit growth in Bangalore in percentage terms and ARPU growth, you can expect between 5% to 8% per annum, kind of thing you can take, conservatively.

items.statement: EBITDA margins to stabilize within historical 40%-45% trend despite temporary dilution from new park launches and corporate team building
items.quote: Historically, if you see our margins, the EBITDA margins for the past 10 years and the trend if you see, before this COVID, pent-up demand, it was about 40% of EBITDA margins were there.

items.statement: Target to shift revenue mix from 75-25 ticket to non-ticket to 60-40 over long term via F&B, merchandise and bundled offerings
items.quote: So, we are at some 75-25 ratio between ticket and non-ticket revenue. So, our aim is to make it about some 60-40 in the long run.

items.statement: Large tier-1 city park costs Rs. 700-800 crores; tier-2 city park under Rs. 200 crores
items.quote: If you have to build a large park, it's going to cost us, one park will cost us between Rs. 700 crores to Rs. 800 crores, especially if you're in a city like Delhi or Bombay.

items.statement: Unpredictable weather events like heavy rainfall, landslides, heat waves affect discretionary spending and footfalls
items.quote: I mean the rain and all that we can't predict. And obviously anything to do with rain, floods and heat wave and all that, obviously will affect any kind of discretionary spending where people have to get out of the house, right?

items.statement: Bhubaneswar park targeting 3-4 lakh footfalls in first full year of operation; ARPU stronger than expected
items.quote: So, we were expecting about 3 to 4 lakhs of footf all in the full year of operation. But we are a new entrant to this particular region. So, we need to wait and see the impact by the end of this

items.statement: All large park designs include space for resorts; resorts to be built after park matures, not at launch
items.quote: In fact, every time we design a park, we always leave space for a resort. So, I think definitely it's part of our plan for most of our projects.

items.statement: Expansion to continue via long-term government leases where possible; not averse to buying land if lease rental and land cost are similar
items.quote: Wherever possible we would like to keep the CAPEX low and do the lease.

items.statement: Company has evaluated and passed on acquisition opportunities in last couple of years as they did not make financial sense
items.quote: Yes, we have already passed on. We have actually said no to most of it.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guided range 12% to 14% for Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our EBITDA has also been in the guided range of 12% to 14%, coming at 12.6% for the quarter after investments, as Ravi was highlighting.

items.statement: Gross margin increased by nearly 100 basis points in Q2 FY25
items.quote: At the same time, we have also been able to deliver good increase in the gross margin by nearly 100 basis points.

items.statement: Core lubricant volume grew 8.8% YoY in Q2 FY25, 2-3x industry growth of 3-4%
items.quote: We have seen that in this quarter, there was some lingering effect of the elections and certain liquidity challenges, but given our strategies, we have posted strong volume numbers.

items.statement: Personal mobility mix increased ~2% to ~22% in Q2 FY25 driven by motorcycle growth
items.quote: In terms of personal mobility, we are higher by around 2%. In terms of industrial and others, we are lower by 2% So more or less in that range.

items.statement: Annual lubricant capex ~INR20-30 crore; no further equity investment planned for Tirex
items.quote: Also considering that our capex requirement for lubricant business also is around INR20 crore, INR25 crore-INR30 crore annually.

items.statement: Tirex revenue INR14 crore in Q2 FY25, INR24-25 crore in H1 FY25; target to double annually for 3-4 years
items.quote: For Q2 FY '25, it was around INR14 crore, and for the H1 FY'25, it is around INR24 crore-INR25 crore, which in the last full year turnover was around INR24 crore-INR25 crore for Tirex.

items.statement: Base oil cost linked to crude; comfortable maintaining gross margins if crude stays $75-80/bbl
items.quote: remains at the current level, which is $75 to $80 range. Of course, it sometimes goes to $85 also during the quarter. It went up to $90 in April; and it went up to $85 in July. It is volatile thing and difficult to comment, but if it remains at the current levels, we are comfortable to maintain our

items.statement: AdBlue volume declined seasonally in Q2 FY25; YTD still double-digit growth; floor ~10,000 kl/month
items.quote: However, this was a seasonally impacte d quarter as Ravi highlighted already. During monsoon season, obviously, the movement of trucks and CVs, which is the large consumption segment is relatively lower

items.statement: Dividend payout increased to 55-60% from 35-40% three years ago; may increase further if cash not deployed
items.quote: We have been currently paying out roughly 55%, 60% as dividend payouts. That we have increased over the last two, three years from 35%, 40% to now 55%, 60%.

items.statement: Export share rose to 6-7% of revenue in Q2 FY25 from 5% earlier
items.quote: Yes, I think we are now at around 6% -7% in terms of our export as a percentage. While earlier it used to be 3%-4% and then we stabilized around 5%. Now it has gone to 6%-7%.

items.statement: A&P spend normalized at 3-4% of revenue; Q2 FY25 elevated by 40-75 bps due to mega campaign
items.quote: We have already guided that our usual advertisement is in the range of 3% to 4%, as Ravi highlighted. In a normalized way, we would be towards the lower end of this band.

items.statement: B2B industrial lubricants growing double-digit; market share <5% but expanding with manufacturing growth
items.quote: This business has been growing double -digit volume for us. Obviously, we have certain strengths which we have in each of the

items.statement: Inventory buildup due to global refinery shutdowns increased borrowings in H1 FY25
items.quote: we have had to store higher inventory because as I was mentioning in one of the earlier questi ons, some of the refineries where we have a term contract, were going for a maintenance shutdown during October, November we had to prebuy some of the

items.statement: Premium portfolio growing at 2x overall volume growth rate
items.quote: We continue to focus on our premium range of products. And again, we are happy to share that this has contributed to the overall kitty by notching up double the growth rate.

items.statement: EV fluids to remain single-digit volume share even at maturity; 9-10 EV OEM partnerships in place
items.quote: I think it's going to be still single-digit volume even if it goes to its maturity.

items.statement: Tirex targets INR500-700 crore revenue in 5 years; EBITDA neutral to marginally positive in FY25
items.quote: We will be obviously aiming to double the top line every year at least for the next three, four years. That's where we believe, and we have announced in the past also that we want to take this company at least to INR500 crore to INR 700 crore top line in the next five years.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 is INR 800-1,000 crores
items.quote: No, we'll be incurring the capex will be around INR 800 crores to INR 1,000 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance revised to 5-6% range going forward
items.quote: I think our EBITDA margins would be in the range of 5% to 6% now going forward.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance maintained at 5-7% YoY for FY25 subject to price volatility
items.quote: I think last time also, we gave a guidance of around 5 to 7 percentage. We stick to that guidance, subject to the price volatility and the demand increase, which is going to happen based on that.

items.statement: H1 FY25 capex was INR 330 crores
items.quote: During the quarter, the company invested close to INR 130 crores into the gas infrastructure, aggregating to INR 330 crores up to the half year of this financial year.

items.statement: Morbi market size estimated at 7.5-8 mmscmd, current consumption ~6.5 mmscmd including propane
items.quote: The market size would be around 7.5 to 8 mmscmd. And right now I think because of various issues in Middle East and all, I think, the consumption would be close to 6.5 mmscmd, including propane consumption.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA per SCM at INR 6.86 vs INR 6.14 in Q2 FY24
items.quote: In terms of EBITDA per SCMD, it stands at close to INR 6.86 against INR 6.14 in the previous quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Industrial prices increased by ~INR 2/SCM in Q2 due to LNG price rise from $9.5 to $13/MMBtu
items.quote: During the quarter, we had to increase the industrial prices by approximately INR 2 per SCM. The increase was mainly on account of significant increase in LNG prices. The spot LNG prices were around $ 9.50 per MMBtu in April 2024 and the current prices is approximately $ 13 per MMBtu.

items.statement: Evaluating CNG price increase to offset higher gas procurement costs from APM cut
items.quote: Yes, we are evaluating options to increase the CNG prices in near future to basically offset the increased cost of gas procurement.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 Morbi volume expected at 3.5-4 mmscmd, up from 2.86 mmscmd in Q2
items.quote: I think in quarter 3, we are looking at a growth of around 3.5 to 4 mmscmd.

items.statement: CNG sales grew 12% YoY in Gujarat and 25% YoY outside Gujarat in Q2 FY25
items.quote: In Q2 FY '25, CNG sales in Gujarat increased by 12% year-over-year, while outside Gujarat sales surged by 25% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: CNG and domestic share in portfolio increased from <20% to >40% over last few years
items.quote: See, I think if you look at the last few years, the growth of CNG and the domestic has increased in our portfolio from close to less than 20%, it is more than now 40 percentage.

items.statement: APM gas allocation cut from 74% to 50% in Q2, being replaced by new well gas and spot LNG
items.quote: So for the quarter ended September '24, we were getting I mean, the shortfall was approximately 26% which was being fulfilled through spot. So -- and after that there has been a further reduction in APM gas. The reduction is now approximately 50%.

items.statement: BG and other long-term LNG contracts expiring mid-2025, replacement discussions ongoing
items.quote: So that LNG contract will expire somewhere in the middle of 2025. And we are right now in discussions for a new LNG contract to replace those volumes.

items.statement: FDODO scheme: 400 LOIs issued, 125 accepted with bank guarantees, construction starting Dec 2024
items.quote: We have issued nearly 400 LOIs, out of which 125 have been accepted by the applicants. And apart from that, they have already submitted the bank guarantee of INR10 lakhs for those LOIs from those 125 locations. The way things are going, I think we will start on the action and will start sometime in the first week or maximum second week of December for the construction of the stations.

items.statement: Delhi High Court stay order obtained against PNGRB common carrier regulations for 20 GAs
items.quote: What we have done as GGL management is we have immediately moved Delhi High Court again and obtained a protection order, a favorable order from Delhi High Court. So this prevents PNGRB from taking any coercive action against GGL.

items.statement: LNG trucking: LCNG at 4 stations, surveying routes to major ports and expressways for LNG dispensing
items.quote: We are already supplying LCNG at 4 of our stations where we are converting LNG into CNG and supplying to the customer. So we are in the process of setting up a dispenser at these 4 stations. So we can start LNG dispensing also at these stations.

items.statement: Matchmaking billing expected to return to growth levels in Q3; both billing and revenue growth expected to move to better levels in Q4
items.quote: On the billing and revenue outlook for Q3, the matchmaking billing expect to come back to the growth levels in Q3. However, there will be revenue decline due to the muted billing growth in Q2. In Q4, we expect both billing and revenue growth to move to a better levels.

items.statement: Marriage services expected to be at similar level as Q2
items.quote: Marriage services, we expect to be at a similar level of Q2.

items.statement: Profit after tax expected to be lower than Q3 of last year due to investments in new areas
items.quote: On the outlook for Q3 margins, we expect the profit after tax to be lower than the levels of Q3 of last year due to the investments in the new areas.

items.statement: Expect volume growth and some marginal increase in ARPU from Q4 onwards
items.quote: We may expect some increase in ARPU possibly from Q4 onwards and volume may also increase. But we are not giving a number at this point in time.

items.statement: Matchmaking EBITDA margin at 22.6% in Q2, same as Q1 and up from 21.3% a year ago
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for the matchmaking business in Q2 is at 22.6% same as in Q1 and increased as compared to 21.3% a year ago.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 15.2% in Q2 vs 16.7% in Q1 and 15.1% a year ago
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, our EBITDA margins in Q2 are at 15.2% compared to 16.7% in Q1 and 15.1% a year ago.

items.statement: Profiles have started bouncing back; increase in fresh payments seen in October and November; renewal payments expected to bounce back from Q4
items.quote: The good thing is that the profiles have bounced back and even in the month of October, there is an increase in fresh payment, even in the month of November as we speak there is an increase in the first-time payment. But the renewal may take one more quarter because since we are two quarters of decline, it may take one more quarter to bounce back.

items.statement: Investing in northern markets with Anil Kapoor as brand ambassador for Community Matrimony and Great Indian Matchmaking Fest campaign
items.quote: We have also taken Anil Kapoor as a brand ambassador exclusively for the northern and western markets. So, we intend to invest in northern market in particular.

items.statement: Fraud and fake profiles remain a challenge though numbers are minuscule; no foolproof mechanism exists yet
items.quote: However, the numbers are minuscule, it's a concern, it's one of the challenges the industry is grappling with. So, not only in online matrimony, the online industry is facing various forms of fraud. So, there are challenges in our categories about these kinds of frauds and all the things. We need to figure it out.

items.statement: Created about 30,600 plus success stories in Q2
items.quote: We create about 30,600 plus success stories.

items.statement: Marketing expenses for matchmaking optimized to 45.2 crores in Q2 from 47.1 crores in Q1 and 46.1 crores a year ago
items.quote: Marketing expenses for matchmaking in Q2 is at 45.2 crores as compared to 47.1 crores in Q1 and 46.1 crores a year ago. So, you would have observed we have optimized the marketing expenses a bit in this quarter.

items.statement: Cash balance at 379 crores, declined slightly from Q1 due to dividend payout
items.quote: Our cash balance is at 379 crores, declined slightly as compared to Q1 due to the dividend payout.

items.statement: ROCE annualized at about 13%
items.quote: ROCE annualized is at about 13%.

items.statement: EliteMatrimony present in eight airports across India; intend to focus and grow this premium segment
items.quote: Today, we have a presence in eight airports across India for EliteMatrimony and we are definitely looking Matrimony.com November 07, 2024 at EliteMatrimony as you rightly said, the premium segment is an opportunity though it's small at this point of time. So, we intend to focus, we intend to grow that business as well

items.statement: Second buyback approved by board at a certain premium as a way to reward shareholders
items.quote: Basically, the board evaluates the various ways to reward the shareholders, and so these are the second buyback and we discussed with the board and we thought it's better to set at certain second premium and it was a board decision on the buy back.

items.statement: Management expects double-digit healthy revenue growth in FY26 versus FY25 driven by export order execution and growth in other streams.
items.quote: I definitely see double digit healthy growth vis-a-vis the current FY in the next FY.

items.statement: Management aims to maintain consolidated EBITDA margins around 20-21% and PAT margins around 15-16% going forward.
items.quote: So, in the range of about 20-21% and this would be the range the range of EBITDA and about 15 to 16% of PAT margin moving forward even on a FY basis.

items.statement: Export order book stands at approximately Rs 1,300 crore, expected to start generating revenue from Q1 FY26.
items.quote: Our order book of export as it stands now is about `1300 odd crore and we expect that this will start fetching revenue by early next FY.

items.statement: Total order book is Rs 6,580 crore with visibility of about 2.5 years; target is to reach 3-year visibility.
items.quote: currently the order book at `6580 crore has a visibility of about 2 and a half o dd years. Our aim would be in the coming quarters and the next FY even with the increased execution to keep on expanding the order book and aiming to have an order book of at least a three -year visibility
