items.quote: Okay, then, in the specialty products, on a global scale, we may be less than 1%.

items.statement: Other expenses fluctuate due to HNG litigation costs; expected to phase out post-adjudication
items.quote: There was a lean period in between. And now I think since the hearing is going on in almost all the courts. In short term, you may see some trend going up. But ultimately, it will phase out once the adjudication is done.

items.statement: HNG acquisition funding details confidential until NCLT approval; will disclose upon court order
items.quote: There are some things which are right now confidential because the entire resolution plan proceedings are confidential in nature until it is approved by the adjudicating authority, which is NCLT.

items.statement: Sustainability focus includes employee well-being and empowerment; received SEEM National Sustainability Award Gold 2023
items.quote: We are proud to receive SEEM National Sustainability Award Gold 2023 for our community contribution towards our manufacturing plant, focusing on climate change, water stewardship, waste minimisation, employee well-being and empowerment.

items.statement: Incorporated Sun Reach Pack (FZE) in UAE in October 2024 to expand global footprint and increase exports
items.quote: In October '24, we incorporated Sun Reach Pack (FZE), a wholly owned subsidiary in the United Arab Emirates to expand our global footprint and increase exports.

items.statement: Green electrical energy has small commercial benefit over normal electrical; sustainability primary driver not cost savings
items.quote: I think normal electrical and green electrical has a very small delta of the benefit, on the commercial benefit. It is more towards the environmental and sustainability commitments.

items.statement: Export onboarding takes time due to customer trials, ethical verification, and history checks; UAE entity enables local presence and service
items.quote: They are going to take a trial. They will also do all sort of confirmation about our company, about our ethical working, our old supplies, our history and everything.

items.statement: Glass packaging gaining share over PET long-term due to sustainability trends; constant interchange between materials in overlapping segments
items.quote: As such, globally, there is a clear signal that things should change to more sustainable packaging, which is a glass packaging. PET has gained a bit of points, but I don't think so on a long-term basis, they have any bright future in the times to come.

items.statement: No specific debt commentary; focus on HNG acquisition funding structure pending court approval
items.quote: We'll be disclosing this upon the order from the court once the NCLT approves it. Then at that time, we'll make the appropriate disclosures as per the requirement of the laws.

items.statement: JLR maintains full-year guidance of GBP30bn revenue, >=8.5% EBIT margin, and net cash positive, though headroom is tighter than desired
items.value: GBP30bn revenue, >=8.5% EBIT, net cash positive
items.quote: We have mentioned Q2 was hurt by factors largely out of our control, and we expect to bounce back strongly in H2. Though the headroom to holding these commitments, which are GBP30 billion worth of revenue, greater than or equal to 8.5% EBIT and net cash positive, they are still our commitments.

items.statement: JLR FY26 EBIT margin target of 10% still possible but getting tighter due to D&A effects from extended ICE lifecycles
items.quote: Yes, FY26 follows a similar thought pattern, to be entirely honest with you. 10% is still possible, particularly as the D&A effects of extending out the end point of our ICE products will still be very relevant in that year. But again, it is getting tighter.

items.statement: JLR Q2 production limited to 86,000 units due to Novelis aluminum flood and 6,000 unit quality hold; expects strong H2 bounce-back as constraints ease
items.quote: So the summary for JLR is that we were held back by outside forces in Q2, particularly the flood at Novelis, which restricted our production to 86,000 units in the quarter.

items.statement: JLR Q2 EBIT margin 5.6% (down 190bps YoY) due to operating deleverage from lower volumes; expects recovery in H2 to hit 8.5% full-year target
items.quote: EBIT at at 5.6%, down 190 bps and profit before tax and exceptional items at ~Rs. 5,800 crores, down about Rs. 400 crores.

items.statement: JLR EBITDA margin only 12% in Q2 (very low); expects majority of EBIT recovery from EBITDA improvement as volumes recover, plus lower D&A
items.quote: EBITDA in the quarter that's just passed was only 12%, which is very low for us. So we expect part of the recovery in EBIT margin for the balance of the year to be lower D&A, but the majority of it to be improvements in EBITDA as well as volume recovers.

items.statement: JLR wholesales 87,000 units in Q2 (down from 97,000); 6,000 unit quality hold to reverse in Q3; expects significantly higher H2 volumes
items.quote: we only wholesaled 87,000 units Tata Motors Limited November 08, 2024 in the quarter. Hit significantly by two effects, which are timing reversing. 6,000 units of wholesale hold , and I mentioned beforehand that we had at least 10,000 units of lower production driven by the issues we had with aluminum

items.statement: JLR H1 investment spending just under GBP1.9bn (GBP400m higher YoY) driven by BEV transition and new product cadence; engineering capitalization stable at ~65%
items.quote: Investment in H1 was just under GBP1.9 billion, about GBP400 million higher than the same period last year. This was driven by our BEV transition and our very forward and very exciting new product cadence over the next few years.

items.statement: JLR FCF guidance reduced from GBP1.8bn to GBP1.3bn due to tougher market and higher investment to extend ICE portfolio while developing three BEV architectures
items.quote: There's a couple of reasons. First of all, the market is a little bit tougher than we had envisaged it to be and also the scale of the investment that's required to keep the ICE portfolio of vehicles going for longer and simultaneously to invest in three architectures worth of BEVs is a little bit higher than we had originally envisaged.

items.statement: JLR Halewood BEV facility ready for EMA architecture production starting early 2026; will reduce industrial CO2e by 40,000 tons
items.quote: This picture is the BEV lines up in Halewood. It's an amazing facility dedicated to BEV production, and it'll eliminate tailpipe emissions, but also you'll see near the bottom of the text on the right, it will also reduce our own emissions. So we're taking maybe 40,000 tons of CO2e out of Halewood's industrial footprint.

items.statement: JLR variable marketing expense (VME) rose to 4% in Q2 from 1.1% YoY; expects VME to flatten at current rates and rise slightly in H2
items.quote: Net pricing was also negative for us. So, variable marketing expense or sales support on an incurred basis was 4% in the quarter versus 1.1% in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: CV business maintained disciplined pricing despite volume decline; focuses on value proposition beyond price including Fleetedge, AMC, cost of ownership
items.quote: We continue to have a very disciplined approach with price being only one part of the value proposition. The many other aspects and attributes which add value to the customer, starting from product, cost of ownership, the entire annual maintenance contract package, the Fleetedge and the kind of benefits that Fleetedge delivers.

items.statement: PV business cut prices instead of heavy discounting to protect brand; EV price cuts driven by cell price reductions and localization to bring EV prices closer to ICE
items.quote: Frankly, the discounting in the first quarter had gone up for all the manufacturers and we took a conscious decision to rather cut the prices rather than keep the discount very heavy because it impacts the brand. That is on the PV side. But as far as EV is concerned, we have taken the price cut because as one of the levers for mainstreaming EVs, it was also needed that the EV prices come closer to

items.statement: JLR strategy shifted from volume to value focus; will not return to old model but focus on Range Rover, Range Rover Sport, Defender, new Jaguar and Discovery
items.quote: It's the result of our new strategy. So many years ago we were very focused on volume and very focused on the car lines that deliver us the volume. Now we're very focused on value and the car lines that deliver the value. So we will not be returning to the old model.

items.statement: PV EV portfolio expansion: Harrier EV by end FY25, Sierra EV and ICE in FY26; targeting 70% SUV salience in 2 years, 80% by FY30
items.quote: What we have announced so far is beyond Curvv. Some of the EV models that we talked about, which is Harrier EV, which is going to come at the end of this financial year. But also Sierra, both in EV as well as ICE version is what is going to be launched. So in the next two financial years, we should start reaching a penetration level of about 70%. And we have said 80% by FY30 is what we have commit

items.statement: PV dealer inventory reduced to 30-31 days median after October festive season; highest ever monthly registrations of 68,500 units in October
items.quote: And we focused on reducing the dealer inventory levels to normal level. And therefore, we moderated our offtake also to do that in October and even in the earlier months. So now it is down to 30, 31 days, as I said.

items.statement: CV Ace EV has 62 anchor corporate customers (added 8 in Q2); working with municipalities for intracity decarbonization; capacity can produce thousands per month
items.quote: We have total 62 anchor customers who are our repeat buyers. So, they are essentially corporates who are deploying electric vehicles for their last mile distribution to meet their decarbonization target. In the last quarter, we have added eight such anchor customers.

items.statement: JLR sees intense NEV (PHEV/EREV/BEV) competition in lower price segments in China; top-end segments (Range Rover, Defender) not yet facing local BEV competition
items.quote: In the lower segments, absolutely, there is very strong competition from the new entry BEVs impacting the available market for ICE vehicles. In the top end, there really isn't yet. So there are no local BEVs competing at the price points. All the performance, all the brand that we have with Range Rover, Range Rover Sport, Defender.

items.statement: PLI applications filed by Sept 30 deadline; government accepted submissions; physical verification underway; disbursement expected within 60 days from Sept 30
items.quote: The government has already looked at all the submissions , that's been accepted. The various agencies will now be visiting our factories to confirm and go through the physical verification. The timelines intended for the government for disbursement of PLI funds are 60 days from 30 th September

items.statement: JLR H1 free cash flow flat due to working capital hit from lower production (payables fell to ~GBP900m vs normal GBP1.2bn); expects reversal in H2 as volumes recover
items.quote: If you look through the balance sheet where we ended up the quarter is with payables of just under GBP900 million, whereas in the normal circumstance, they would be north of GBP 1.2 billion. So that will also reverse.

items.statement: Tata Motors consolidated net debt marginally inched up; expects to reverse and become net cash by year-end as working capital normalizes
items.quote: Net debt marginally inched up, not particularly concerned about it. We should expect to see this reverse and go into net cash by end of the year.

items.statement: JLR RCF term loan refinanced; ratings continue to improve at both domestic and JLR levels
items.quote: From a financing side, of course, both the RCF term refinanced and as well as the ratings continue to keep improving.

items.statement: CV business ROCE at ~37.4% in H1 FY25; double-digit EBITDA sustained with 120bps YoY improvement in H1
items.quote: EBITDA has improved by 120 bps, and this is leading to a strong PBT, resulting in a good ROCE at around 37.4%.

items.statement: PV business CAFE compliance with 25g/km headroom below threshold due to multi-powertrain strategy
items.quote: Our CAFE compliance is very below threshold, and we have a headroom of 25 gram per kilometer, which goes to show the impact of our multi-powertrain strategy.

items.statement: CV Fleetedge platform has 710,000 active vehicles with 78% monthly and 52% weekly active users; Mileage Sarathi delivering 4.8% median fuel efficiency improvement on 340,000+ vehicles
items.quote: Fleetedge now has more than 710,000 active vehicles on the platform and a very healthy daily, weekly and monthly active usage, almost 78% monthly active users and 52% weekly active users. Our machine learning based fuel efficiency solution, the Mileage Sarathi is now live on more than 340,000 vehicles and we continue to deliver a median fuel efficiency improvement of around 4.8%.

items.statement: Key risk to JLR guidance is China deterioration; also watching global demand; inventory levels under control in other markets providing buffer
items.quote: What can get this go off track? I think ensuring that China stays and improves from where it is today, is an important one. If things deteriorate there dramatically, then that could skew the pitch. Other markets that are currently holding on for us in the current levels, we have not dramatically shifted volumes over the last few years and therefore it has been a gradual increase, as long as that t

items.statement: Q2 saw muted demand with volumes at base and value down 6.7%; urban centres stressed, rural recovering; extended monsoon and floods in August-September hurt demand; Diwali season weaker than expected
items.quote: We saw a real muted quarter for us in terms of the overall demand conditions, which were impacted. We looked at achieving base volumes. We were just about the base in terms of the overall volume achievement. But I think the effect was more at the value level where we were negative of about 6.7%.

items.statement: Expect single-digit volume growth for FY25 (H1 at 3.3%); aim to maintain 5-6% realization decline band for the year; target H2 EBITDA margin in 18-20% band
items.quote: Based on that, I think we should really maintain single digit volume growth numbers for the year.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin fell 280 bps YoY in Q2; PBDIT margin dropped 530 bps to 16.4% due to price cuts last year, weaker mix, material inflation, higher employee cost %, and higher discounting; H1 PBDIT at 18.5%
items.quote: If you look at gross margins, there is 280 points decline over Q2 of the last year, given the fact that we had taken a price decrease last year. Also, the product mix this year has been weaker and we have seen material inflation in the current year. Similarly, the PBDIT margins have come down and this is a concern area for us. Come down to 16.4%, almost a dip of about 530 points.

items.statement: Took 1.2% price increase in Q2; full realization expected in Q3; Q2 saw 1.5% material inflation vs 4% deflation in Q2 FY24; anticipating part deflation but depends on crude prices and geopolitics
items.quote: Overall, we have taken a price increase of 1.2% in this quarter. But I think the full realization of this price increase will come in Q3. I think this is something which we are clearly seeing going forward. We are expecting that there should be some deflation. But it all depends on how the crude prices behave given the geopolitical situation which is underway.

items.statement: Industrial business grew ~6% in Q2 (auto OEM/refinishes +6%, protective +6%); contributes 6-7% of total vs 20-45% for peers; PPGAP JV PBT margin 15.7%, protective JV PBT margin fell to 7% from 11.3%
items.quote: If you see from the point of view of PPGAP, which is the auto OEM and the refinishes business which we have, we got almost about 6% overall growth at the quarter level and about 8% at the H1 level. Profitability has also been fairly good. We have maintained stable margins, and the PBT is quite high overall at about 15.7%.

items.statement: Most brownfield expansion capex complete; backward integration projects on track - VAM-VAE at Dahej, Gujarat and white cement at Fujairah, Dubai
items.quote: Most of the capex which we had committed for brownfield expansion projects is now complete. Now we are looking at all our backward integration projects, which seem to be online. Whether it was the VAM-VAE which we are doing at Dahej in Gujarat or the white cement in Fujairah, Dubai. I think these projects are also well on track.

items.statement: Retail touchpoints now ~1.67 lakh; adding 5,000-8,000 retailers annually; tinting machine multiplicity increasing as new competitors give machines free
items.quote: Overall, now 7 | P a g e talking of almost about 1.67 lakh retail touchpoints which is very strong, and we are looking at continuance of this market

items.statement: Mix slightly more inferior in Q2; 12% revenue from new products; launched Advance range (2-3% higher dealer margins) targeting 15-30% of dealer sales; Ultima Protek with graphene/PU serum/nano block launching November; Chroma Cosm colour sy
items.quote: We see that today 12% of the revenue contribution still comes from new products and this is something which we are continuing taking forward in a very strong way.

items.statement: Urban centres stressed, rural/T3-T4 performing better; B2B projects segment better than retail but construction slow and government spending muted post-elections; painter loyalty programs focus on higher business volume not just per-litre r
items.quote: Overall, if you were to dissect the performance of the urban centres, definitely we are seeing more stress in case of our business. We saw that the rural areas to some extent have performed relatively better.

items.statement: Competitive intensity up across segments, especially economy; new entrants giving free tinting machines; existing players discounting more; not expecting intensity to ease in medium term; market share variation of 1-1.5% typical for leader
items.quote: We see it almost across segments. Whether it is the area of waterproofing or it is the area of emulsions, we are seeing it possibly across the economy and the premium set as well. As well as on ancillaries like putty and primers and so on and so forth.

items.statement: Calibrating primary sales to weaker secondary; conscious of dealer ROI - balancing margins and inventory rotation; avoiding inventory push that blocks dealer working capital given market liquidity crunch
items.quote: We balance the primary and the secondary. The secondary has been weaker to that extent. And therefore, we are trying to calibrate the primary according to that.

items.statement: No specific debt commentary; exceptional items: ₹200 cr impairment on White Teak/Weatherseal (₹124 cr goodwill impairment) and ₹56 cr forex loss from Ethiopia currency devaluation
items.quote: Therefore, I think we have taken an impairment, which is totalling up to almost about ₹ 200 crores. And this is also covering the fair valuation loss on the derivative contracts for future stake purchases in White Teak and Weatherseal which are in the offing.

items.statement: Interim dividend ₹4.25/share, lower than last year in line with reduced H1 profits; final dividend to be decided later
items.quote: We have looked at really calibrating the overall dividend for the year. We have got a dividend of about ₹4.25. This is a little bit lower than what we gave as an interim dividend 24 | P a g e last year, but this is in line with the reduced profits in the first half of the year

items.statement: Employee cost up due to frontline hiring for dealer expansion (5,000-8,000 retailers/year); absolute cost flat QoQ but % higher due to depressed top line; expect to normalize when value growth returns
items.quote: As far as employee costs are concerned, as I mentioned in Q1 as well, I think the numbers have gone up because we are looking at possibly, in the front line catering to our dealers very strongly. We are adding almost about 5,000 to 8,000 retailers easily every year.

items.statement: Global business +8.7% constant currency; ₹56 cr forex loss from Ethiopia devaluation; Middle East double-digit growth; Bangladesh turmoil dragged Asia; Nepal improving after 2-year liquidity crunch
items.quote: When you look at the performance here, from constant currency terms, was still quite good. It was almost about 8.7%. However, it got impacted very strongly. Given the fact that we saw a currency devaluation in Ethiopia, which was a big kind of impact which came in a t about ₹ 56 crores in terms of forex loss

items.statement: Home Decor: #1 in lighting, modular kitchens, wall coverings; #2 in fabric/furnishings; Kitchen +9% Q2, +7% H1; Bath +6% H1; newer categories (White Teak, Weatherseal) growing double-digit but below plan; gross margins hit, bottom line loss
items.quote: Kitchen - we are number one as the modular kitchen leaders. We have got almost 9% growth in Q2 and that is something which is very strong and almost about 7% in H1.

items.statement: Demand recovery uncertain - higher base in Q3 (late Diwali last year), October challenging; wedding season from mid-November key; crude price volatility and geopolitical risk to material costs; Bangladesh instability; government capex picku
items.quote: Right now, you know we are sitting on a higher base of Q3 overall, given the fact that last year there was a late Diwali and October was a full month. So October has been also a little bit challenging and therefore we are not seeing too much immediate recovery in Q3, but there is a good wedding season in the offing and we will have to see how the demand really goes up from the third week of Novemb

items.statement: Full-year guidance flattish revenue (~3-4% growth) and margins similar to last year; H2 expected stronger than H1
items.quote: So, the guidance was flattish guidance. So we said at the top line level, maybe 3% - 4% we are in kind of, we are okay on that, margins obviously there will be some margin made up in Q3 and Q4 but, obviously margins are under a bit of pressure. We hope to be at a similar level like last year, but probably there will be some amount of margin that will still have to be made.

items.statement: Agrochemical investments dried up; muted for several more quarters. Pharma picking up in India with large projects. Chemical cycle bottom but no green shoots yet.
items.quote: We have seen a shortfall and where we do see a little bit more stress in the glass lined business, especially when it comes to the chemical. And when I say chemical, mainly the agrochemical sector where the investments have really dried up and it does mean that there is probably a few more quarters of, I would say muted investment, I don't see that turning around very quickly.

items.statement: Mixing ~10% of H1 FY25 revenue; Heavy Engineering, Edlon, Mixing driving growth; glass-lined slowing
items.quote: 10% is the number that we have currently in terms of mixing. And mixing is an area where we want to grow. So there is a big push for us to kind of get into new industry segments, mixing opens up petrochemical, oil and gas, food and beverage, lots of other new industries which are not currently under in a down cycle.

items.statement: Poland facility producing first equipment for Mavag; lower cost than Western Europe; English-speaking engineers and welders available
items.quote: Poland becomes an opportunity we already have India as a low cost sourcing hub. But we also wanted to have something in Europe, because some of the customers in Europe only accept European made equipment. So Poland is a nice option for us, like I mentioned to you, we made the first set of two equipment for Mavag our swiss subsidiary, and the FAT was actually done a couple of days ago, and the resu

items.statement: Unbilled revenue +₹28 cr, inventory +₹32 cr, customer advances +₹30 cr, receivables -₹21 cr vs 31 Mar; H1 FCF 50% of cash generation
items.quote: when we compare 30th September versus 31st March balance sheet, we observe our unbilled revenue and inventory have gone up by ₹ 28 and ₹ 32 crores respectively. This highlights higher activity at the production floor. As a corollary, our customer advance receipts are also up by ₹ 30 crores. On the other hand, our receivables are down by ₹ 21 crores due to correction focus, which directs us to the

items.statement: New hires: head of manufacturing, head of sales, process head in India; mixing head hired 6 months ago; international hires; engineering center in India staffed for global work
items.quote: we made a couple of important hires here in India, head of manufacturing and head of sales, the project that is being run right now has seen a lot of traction because of the new perspective that we brought in. We made some hires internationally as well. So that's ongoing, we are strengthening areas, we recently hired a process head as well. So we are, we are trying to build process as a technology

items.statement: Agrochemical downturn may last several quarters; chemical cycle turn timing uncertain; competitive pricing pressure persists; margin recovery to 17-18% will take time
items.quote: I don't see the green shoots yet, I do see some talk happening in terms of new investment coming in like I said in the pharmaceutical industry, we do see positivity, but chemical and agrochemical in particular seem to be a little bit more time before we see a complete turnaround, if you also, I am sure you follow a lot of the chemical and agrochemical companies, many of them are now also not clear

items.statement: Evaluating M&A for new industries with 3-4 years continuous double-digit growth and good margins; strategic plan review ongoing
items.quote: this would also lead into M&A and stuff and looking at new industries which can give us three, four years of continuous growth, double digit growth with good margins. So that's something that we are thinking about.

items.statement: Wallet share growing in key accounts; cross-selling incentivized within chemical/pharma; brand affinity not quantitatively measured (NPS considered)
items.quote: So, the wallet share in our key accounts has definitely grown. We are also currently working on rebooted key account management process where we will kind of have multiple touch points, but our key customers continue to buy, we continue to discuss, we talk about process, technology, all that kind of stuff so, wallet share in our key customers is growing.

items.statement: Glass-lined competitors offer 25-50% lower prices; GMM retains premium via quality/life argument; procurement departments demand multiple quotes
items.quote: The internal view might be that, GMM Pfaudler is the preferred vendor, but there cannot be a very large price gap, they cannot be at 100 and somebody else is going to be at 75 or 50, the gap should be a little bit smaller. And, so that's something that is part and parcel of the Indian market, generally the global glass line market as well. So there's always going to be competitive pressure, but th

items.statement: Participating in CPI-NCL Living Lab project for chemical industry decarbonization; only equipment provider in collaboration
items.quote: internally, we call it as CPI NCL project, so apologies for not addressing it. Yes, we are involved in that project, NCL of India, of course National Chemical Lab, and CPI as a Center for Process Improvement from the UK. We have a collaboration with them, along with leading innovative companies from the chemical space. And the idea is to set up this lab in NCL with an emphasis on figuring out ways

items.statement: Targets $200 million revenue by calendar year 2027, approximately two financial years from now
items.quote: We are hoping that the economy is going to be opening up. Interest rates will open up and like Srini said taxation will be reduced. That means that there will be quicker acceleration in the initial phases, like Srini was talking about. So, our thing is we have set ourselves certain targets for next year and in line with whatever we are progressing now, we will be on a similar path to get to the 20

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margins to improve significantly by the time $200 million revenue target is reached
items.quote: I don't want to give a specific number, but as you see quarter-on-quarter, we have been improving our margins. Because we did some realignment of our bench, realignment of some of the business offerings that we are doing. We are also targeting this is something that for the financial year, we are looking at and we have given a target to all our CEOs operations, sales related leadership that we wan

items.statement: US election uncertainty delayed 4-5 deal closures from last quarter, now expected to close this quarter
items.quote: Before we go into what Trump's Presidency might look like for Kelton, I want to say that there were about four or five opportunities that we were going to sign last quarter, but due to the uncertainty of the elections and so on, customers have pushed them to the right. So, we expect to close all of them in this quarter and hopefully start some of them before the holiday season in December.

items.statement: Expects initial US economic growth under Trump presidency to drive IT spending acceleration starting calendar 2025
items.quote: And we expect to take advantage of that from an IT perspective from an implementation perspective. So, that is an immediate impact. You might have seen that the S&P has jumped up 2.2% immediately after the declaration of Trump's win. So, obviously all of these are indicators that in the initial phase of Trump's Presidency we will see some growth happening in the US Economy.

items.statement: Europe remains a headwind with flat growth due to Ukraine war impact and shrinking economy
items.quote: So, the only headwinds that we faced with Europe, Europe is still struggling, right, while we're still struggling, we don't know when it's going to come out of it. The baggage of Ukraine, how long it will continue in Europe, we don't know. We've been, for lack of a better word, on a flat line when it comes to Europe.

items.statement: Won 5 new clients including major gaming, contract food services, SAP, and global manufacturing clients
items.quote: Now coming to the operational highlights, we have about 5 clients wins. I'd like Karanjit to talk about the client wins for this quarter, Karanjit.

items.statement: Strategy to reduce number of customers while increasing per-customer revenue to improve margins
items.quote: We are also targeting this is something that for the financial year, we are looking at and we have given a target to all our CEOs operations, sales related leadership that we want to reduce the number of customers while increasing per customer revenue. So, that also reduces some of the overheads.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 12.1%, PAT margin 7.2%, with quarter-on-quarter improvement trend
items.quote: The EBITDA margin of 12.1% and the net profit of 19.6 crores. The PAT margin for this quarter is 7.2% and the EPS for this quarter is of Rs. 2.6.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin 12.2%, PAT margin 7.4%, revenue Rs 533 crores up 8.7% YoY
items.quote: For the six-month numbers, the revenue is 533 crores, which is about 8.7% growth year-on-year. EBITDA is 65 crores which is about an EBITDA margin of 12.2%, net profit of about 39.6 crores and the PAT margin of 7.4%.

items.statement: Promoter stake reduced from 51.68% to 40.82% due to share sales and ESOP dilution
items.quote: We did some selling of our shares last quarter. That's the partial reflection of that and partial reflection is related to some of our reporting requirements we have done. Other than that there's nothing else. To answer your question about 60 to where it is now, that is, we've been reporting that consistently, it's nothing that we have not reported. Everything has been reported. It is just over a

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue declined 5% YoY to INR 679 crore due to weak market demand
items.quote: Revenue from operations in Q2 FY25 was at INR 679 crores as compared to INR 715 crores in Q2 FY24, a decline of 5% year-on-year. This is mainly due to we ak market demand during the quarter

items.statement: EBITDA margin maintained at 12.9% in Q2 FY25 vs 12.8% in Q2 FY24 despite subdued demand
items.quote: The company maintai ned its EBITDA margin at 12.9% during the quarter as compared to 12.8% in Q2 FY24, despite the subdued demand

items.statement: Capex of INR 49 crore incurred till September 2024; full year FY25 capex expected at INR 100 crore plus
items.quote: FY25, already we have spent around INR 50 crores. So, it will b e again in the range of INR 50 crores to INR 60 crores in next half. So, total will be INR 100 crores plus in this full year

items.statement: No capacity addition planned in current capex; spending on regular items, machinery and civil work
items.quote: Can we assume any capacity addition in this? Sushil Batra: No.

items.statement: Channel inventory increased due to subdued demand; retail inventory up slightly, GT and new channel flat
items.quote: Channel inventory, we are maintaining, there is an increase in the inventory as compared to March. So it has increased due to subdued demand. And inventory, we are carrying almost in GT and new channel at the same level, but retail, it has increased a little bit.

items.statement: No price increase taken in Q2 FY25; 6% ASP rise driven by January price hike in Hawaii category and premium product introductions
items.quote: No, no, we have not taken price increase.

items.statement: Unorganized competition intensified due to lower raw material prices, GST change, BIS exemption for small players, and increased China imports
items.quote: Yes, it's actually both. Plus 2 years back, there was a change of GST from 5% to 12%. Since then, like a lot of new players or unorganized competitors have come up. items.statement: Industry making regular representations to government for GST reduction from 12% to 5%; no commitment from government

items.statement: Retail network expanded from 55,000 to 70,000 retailers over 2 years; same run rate expected to continue

items.statement: Full year volume growth expected to be flattish; Sparx category targeting 8-10% growth; overall revenue growth positive but no specific number
items.quote: It would be flattish because it will take time to cover up the 6-month sales and volume loss.

items.statement: Inventory increased by INR 47 crore due to subdued demand and factory operations; receivables down
items.quote: Due to subdued demand, and we have to run the factories and bec ause there is pressure on the demand, that's why inventory has increased

items.statement: Company remains net debt free with positive cash flow from operations
items.quote: Our company continues to be net debt free and supported by positive cash flow from operations.

items.statement: Closed footwear mix unchanged from last year; strategy focuses on distributor appointments and e-commerce reach for Sparx
items.quote: So it's same like what it was th e last year and last quarter. T here's not much of a change happening there

items.statement: Average realization per pair increased 6% to INR 156 in H1 FY25; volume decline of ~5% in H1
items.quote: On the slide in the beginning, I observed that our average real ization per pair has gone up by about 6% to INR 156 and the number of pair sold is lower

items.statement: Reduced advertisement spend from 4% to 3% of revenue in FY25; increased trade schemes instead; ad spend to return to 4% next year
items.quote: Generally, we used to spend around 4%. So this year, we have just thought about 3%, 1% lower than last year.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement driven by January price increase, raw material easing, and inventory accounting effect (INR 47 crore inventory increase includes conversion cost)
items.quote: Growth, definitely, there are 3 reasons for this. We took a pri ce increase in January, so that is the advantage has come in the system. Raw materials has also, I think, eased out. And third is, if you see the percentage, there is an increase of inventory, s o that percentage is, I think, 1% looks better than the last year. So these are the 3 reasons. So one is the price increase; second, raw mate

items.statement: Balanced approach between margin and market share; not sacrificing quality for short-term volume; creating separate e-commerce portfolio to manage channel conflict
items.quote: No, we're taking a balanced approach. It cannot be one way. It cannot be only margin or only sales. We have to take a long-term view and take a balanced approach.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu footwear parks focused on exports for multinationals; not seen as threat to domestic market
items.quote: So in Tamil Nadu, whatever manufacturers, they are coming there from Taiwan. They are making for multinationals. And mostly they are making and then exporting. So that is not going to affect our domestic market in that manner so far.

items.statement: Disney and Marvel licensing tie-up to premiumize children's segment and improve ASP over time
items.quote: Yes. That will help in the premiumization of our articles which are meant for children and others also. So we have done a slow beginning. But in the coming times, this will help us improve the ASP of the company.

items.statement: Credit growth guidance maintained at 12%-14% for FY25 despite 18% growth in H1
items.quote: Our guidance is 12%-14%, right. And if you look at within the credit growth, our RAM growth is always around more than 18%; almost 18%.

items.statement: Slippage guidance maintained at 1-1.25% for FY25 despite elevated Q2 slippages from MTNL
items.quote: We had one account MTNL. Let me tell you honestly and around 245 crores was the exposure. Because of that, for this quarter, our slippages are little elevated but overall we have given a guidance of 1.25pc, 1-1.25pc.

items.statement: Target CD ratio of 75% from current 72% level
items.quote: Our target is to reach to 75% CD ratio.

items.statement: NIM improved to 3.10% from 2.84-2.86% range through portfolio rebalancing toward retail and MSME
items.quote: Overall NIM which used to hover around 2.84 to 2.86 has now touched 3.10. and what we have done to achieve this level is we have rebalanced our credit portfolio.

items.statement: Cost of deposits reduced from 4.91% peak in Dec'23 to 4.86% by reducing bulk deposit reliance
items.quote: Our cost of deposit peaked in December ’23 it was 4.91 now it is 4.86. Our cost of deposit has started coming down because we h ave reduced our reliance on the bulk

items.statement: Advances grew 18% YoY in Q2 FY25 with RAM segment growing >18% for 6 consecutive quarters
items.quote: In advances our retail Agri/MSME put together grew by 20% in this quarter September '24. But when we look at historical trend for last 5-6 quarters it has been trending in the range of 18 to 20%.

items.statement: Vehicle loan growth accelerated to >39% in Q2 FY25 from 33% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Within retail our Page | 4 − home loan growth is also high double digit sometimes more than 20 also in the last 5 quarters and our vehicle loan growth is more than 39% in this quarter, previous quarter it was 33

items.statement: CASA grew 8% YoY with CASA ratio stable at ~38% for 6 quarters while industry saw declines
items.quote: If you look at our CASA ratio, CASA ratio has been consistently in the range of 38%, we have not lost on CASA percentage in the last one year or 6 quarters.

items.statement: Gross NPA improved to 3.38% and Net NPA to 0.73% with PCR >95%
items.quote: Our gross NPA which used to be around more than 4% a year before is now 3.38% and net NPA is 0.73. We have already achieved 95% more than 95% PCR Page | 5 ratio

items.statement: Holding >Rs1,000 crore forward-looking provisions above RBI requirements including on restructured and SMA books
items.quote: So, as we speak in addition to the mandated provision by the Reserve Bank of India on Standard Asset Book may be on account of market mechani sm, may be on account of Covid or restructuring book, in addition to all those provisions we are holding around 1000 crores of provisions over and above the required provision

items.statement: No exposure to RIL; SMA 1&2 book reduced to Rs800 crore from Rs2,000 crore with provisions retained
items.quote: RIL, we do not have any exposure and MTNL, we have already made around 50pc provision in this quarter itself and given the buffer available.

items.statement: IT budget of Rs1,000 crore approved for FY25 with Rs360 crore already spent on digital transformation, cybersecurity, hardware replacement
items.quote: At IT we have kept a target of around ₹1000 crores to spend. Out of that, around ₹360 crores plus we have already spent and there are many projects in pipeline currently which we are working and by, I think, March we plan to consume the entire budget also.

items.statement: Plan to open 130 branches in FY25 with 27 operational by Nov 4 and all targeted by March for full-year benefit in FY26
items.quote: We have planned to open around 130 branches in this financial year. About 100 locations have been approved by our HOPC Committee - HO Premises Committee, of which 27 branches have been made operational as on 4th November.

items.statement: Project Parivartan to launch ~25 digital products by March FY25; Tab Banking deployed at 1,700 branches for quality CASA acquisition
items.quote: We have planned to launch around 25 products by March. We have already launched at the time of launching of this project and others are in pipeline. So, by March, I can say, that most of our asset and liability products will be available on our Mobile Banking.

items.statement: Capital raise of up to Rs2,000 crore approved; kickoff meeting held with BRLMs; launch timing depends on market conditions
items.quote: Capital raising, we have already taken approval, and we have already today we had the kickoff meeting also with our BRLM and statutory auditors and legal counsels and now we are planning for the launch.

items.statement: Liquidated Rs3,500 crore of low-yielding securities in Q2 FY25 to fund loan growth via TREPS and overseas deposits
items.quote: We have already disposed off around 3500 crores of securities in this quarter and we have booked some gain also. That was a small gain because they were very low yielding securities maturing in the next year.

items.statement: ROA improving quarterly from June'23; target of 1% ROA achievable but may take until next year
items.quote: If you look at ROA from June 23, we have been improving ROA every quarter and the way the provisioning requirement is coming down, with net NPA of .73pc and operating p rofit of around 1400 crores, I think it is achievable

items.statement: CRAR at 16.84% (17.5% including H1 profit); Tier-1 at 14.59%
items.quote: CRAR of the Bank is already 16.84% and if I include this half year profit it will be somewhere 17.5% for this year. And tier 1 is already 14.59%.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio improved from ~60% to 56% through cost control and income growth
items.quote: Our cost to income ratio has improved because historically our cost to income ratio used to be around 60% and above and now it is 56%.

items.statement: Fee income grew 15% YoY and 10% QoQ in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our fee-based income has also grown by 15% on Y-o-Y basis and on Q-o-Q basis also 10%.

items.statement: ECL implementation impact estimated at Rs2,000-3,000 crore over 5 years; Rs1,000 crore already provisioned
items.quote: Roughly I take, let us say for our bank size, maybe 2000 or 3000 crores is the hit. Let us say 3000. So, 1000 crores, we have already provided for, I think that is taken care, 1/3rd is already taken care.

items.statement: Project finance exposure ~Rs11,000-12,000 crore; RBI draft guidelines impact estimated <Rs300 crore if implemented as-is
items.quote: Project finance is around 11,000 to 12,000 crores for our bank and out of which there are many projects which are already implemented, and cas h flow is there because HAM projects are there, cash flow is Page | 26 coming

items.statement: NARCL resolution: 4 accounts with bids submitted worth Rs610 crore under Swiss challenge; 1-2 accounts may resolve in Q3/Q4
items.quote: There are already 4 accounts are there where bids are submitted by NARCL and now it is the Swiss challenge, and everything has to happen and 4 accounts where bids are submitted are is 610 crores.

items.statement: HR transformation completed with PMS implementation; monthly performance scoring; training programs with external experts for hub staff
items.quote: Now every employee is given target scientifical ly basis their location, basis the opportunities available and basis what other banks are able to achieve and what we are able to achieve. So, all those parameters are taken and scientifically targets are given to them and then every month the score is pushed to them

items.statement: Mobile banking daily active users grew from 500-600 to 7,000-8,000; daily logins from <1 lakh to >3 lakh; app rating 4.6-4.7
items.quote: On an average, active mobile customer addition in June quarter was 500-600. Now, it is in the range of 7000-8000 on a daily basis. That is what. Our daily login used to be less than a lakhs about a year back, now it is more than 3 lakhs every day on an average.

items.statement: No active ECL discussions with RBI; submitting quarterly data as per format; awaiting final guidelines
items.quote: See, if you ask me, ECL growth, there are no discussions with the RBI. RBI has its own style of working and whenever they feel comfortable, it is to be implemented.

items.statement: Management expects volume growth momentum to continue in Q4 but revenue growth will be dampened by seasonal furloughs and fewer working days.
items.quote: Yes, you are absolutely right. Q4 always has a seasonal impact because of furloughs, because of holidays and also a lower number of working days. So one, we believe that the growth momentum should continue. So, growth momentum in terms of volumes will definitely happen. That volume, translating into revenue, will be dampened by the lower number of working days and furloughs.

items.statement: Management sees good signs of activity across all sectors with customers planning to spend more in 2025 and increased RFQ/RFP activity.
items.quote: We've seen traction begin across all sectors now. As the year is coming to a close and also US elections behind us, there are definite signs that customers are plan ning to spend more in the coming year. And this is the time when they're doing a lot of those RFQs and RFPs

items.statement: Telco and tech sectors showing early signs of spending revival after cost-cutting; healthcare, financial services, and hospitality/education/travel also improving.
items.quote: Tech was the biggest impact or highest impacted, and where we are seeing some of the tech spend come back, telcos following behind. So, the signs of while the discussions have started, some of the deal activity signs will probably start off and start showing up.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin expanded to 17.9% driven by higher billing days, improved utilization, operating efficiencies, and rupee depreciation.
items.quote: We closed at an EBITDA of 17.9%, which totals to INR 796 million or $9.5 million, which is a quarter-on-quarter growth of 11.5% in INR terms and year-on-year of 19.5%.

items.statement: Management targets sustainable annualized EBITDA margins while investing in sales and delivery capacity for growth.
items.quote: We are quite confident that we should be able to, when you look at our annualized margin, this is just a quarter margin, so I wouldn't base it on this when you look at the full year margins. That's where we will try to make sure that we are able to stay sustainable.

items.statement: No billing rate increases achieved; margin improvement driven by utilization, operating efficiency, project cost control, and richer business mix.
items.quote: No, the market environment wasn't going to support the rate increase. In fact, in the last couple of earnings calls, there were questions around whether we have given discounts to our customers. Given the nature of our services in the product implementation and product engineering space, we haven't offered discounts to our cus tomers. But on the contrary, we have not increased or we've not been ab

items.statement: Utilization at 83.5%, considered industry-leading with limited room for further improvement; focus shifting to pyramid rationalization and service mix for margin levers.
items.quote: Well, it is pretty much the best of the industry kind of a utilization level. So I wouldn't say that we can or we will try and push for going beyond this level kind of a thing. So yes, your question is valid. We are pretty much at the top from utilization perspective because, from every calculation we look at beyond this, there isn't too much room for the utilization side.

items.statement: Plans to add employees in data, cloud, AI, security and specialized services over coming quarters.
items.quote: There certainly are and we are willing to add bandwidth and employees in data, cloud, AI. And also a bunch of our specialized areas around security and similar services.

items.statement: Pipeline growing with higher average deal sizes and more large deals; win ratios impacted by delayed customer decisions.
items.quote: Anmol, we are definitely seeing our average deal size go up, quarter-on-quarter. We are also tracking it at pipeline level. And we are seeing that in our pipe, also, we are getting more number of larger deal sizes.

items.statement: Blackstone channel contributed ~15 customers with ~12 active prospects; expected to contribute to growth as spending improves.
items.quote: We have already got close to15 customers from the Blackstone portfolio companies. It is beginning to contribute a reasonable percentage of revenue for us. J ust like all the other marke t activities, prospecting and reaching out to clients, we are constantly working with Blackstone portfolio companies as prospects. We currently have another close to a dozen prospects that we're working within the

items.statement: Launched OptimaAI GenAI suite for internal developers and customers; new offerings include Power BI migration and Chaos Engineering with integrated disaster recovery.
items.quote: We also launched a couple of offerings that are widely applicable and finding a lot of acceptance. One was around migration from any reporting tools to Power BI, and second was around Chaos Engineering with an integrated disaster recovery model to enhance our business continuity and resilience.

items.statement: Early success in product sustenance deals (N-1 product stages) with a few wins in Q3 and active conversations with more clients for portfolio management.
items.quote: Absolutely, Sandeep. Though not v ery big numbers, but we have seen a couple of deals in the last quarter in the product sustenance space. We are currently in active conversations with at least another few customers who are talking, basically, product sustenance, the whole product portfolio management type of approach

items.statement: Top client contribution decreased from 5.2% to 5% due to telecom spend curtailment; expected to reverse as telco spend returns. Top 5 clients improved to 14.8% from 14.1%.
items.quote: From a client concentration perspective, our top client contribution came down from 5.2% to 5%. But this is largely because this is a telecom customer, and large telco companies have been curtailing a lot of spend in the recent quarters. But we expected it to reverse back as the telco spend comes back, and we are already seeing signs of that.

items.statement: Revenue mix from customers >$500M and >$1B continues to increase; consciously signing larger deal sizes.
items.quote: From signing larger ISVs perspective, our overall percentage of revenue or revenue mix from customers that are greater than $500 million or greater than $1 billion has continued to move up and I think like we had said earlier, we had set up a sales motion to open large accounts and larger deals.

items.statement: No single client-centric issue worrying management entering CY25; top clients largely sustained with expected growth return.
items.quote: So is there a singular client-centric issue that we are worried about? The answer is no. Our top clients are largely sustained and, in fact, some of whom we've seen either stagnate or not grow year-on-year. We do believe that growth with the spending will come back even in those clients.

items.statement: Key leadership hires: Satyadeep Mishra as CHRO, Srikara Rao as Technology Officer for Cloud and Security (US), Shardul Sangal as Senior VP Global Delivery.
items.quote: We inducted Satyadeep Mishra as our Chief Human Resources Officer. He is based out of India and is now global ly responsible for HR. Srikara Rao joined as a Technology Officer for Cloud and Security Services based in the US and Shardul Sangal has joined us as Senior VP of Global Delivery

items.statement: Sales headcount ~60 hardcore sales resources on-site plus 55-60 ISR support in Noida; sales resources flat to up 2-3% YoY, ISR down 8-10 in last 2 quarters.
items.quote: Our hardcore sales team excluding the ISR would be close to around 60 resources, Nitesh Ji, excluding the ISRs? Nitesh Bansal: Yes. Mihir: Sorry, how much? Nand Sardana: 60 is the hardcore sales guys who are at o n-site location and additional 55 to 60 ISR support them in the sales lead generation, and they support from NOIDA during the night

items.statement: Opened new delivery centre in Mexico with entity created; operations started in Q3 for nearshore staffing and project delivery for North American clients.
items.quote: One of the major steps that we took in the quarter was to open a new delivery centre in Mexico, for which we've created an entity in Mexico. And we are starting our delivery operations from this quarter, which will serve the purpose of nearshore staffing, resourcing and project delivery for mostly our North American customers who require work to be done in the same time zone from a cost-effective

items.statement: DSO improved to 59 days from 60 days; cash and bank balances net of short-term borrowing increased to INR 260 crores from INR 179 crores.
items.quote: DSO is 59 days as against 60 days last quarter. Our cash and bank balances, net of short-term borrowing as on September was INR 260 crores compared to INR 179 crores at the end of last quarter.

items.statement: SG&A percentage expected to increase slightly over next quarters due to planned sales bandwidth investments, but not a massive move.
items.quote: We will definitely see SG&A increase as a percentage over the next quarter and the next, but those investments are already made. The cost, obviously, gets reflected in the next quarter.

items.statement: Revenue grew 2.8% QoQ and 1.4% YoY in INR terms to INR 4,441 million ($53M); YTD revenue INR 12,928 million ($155M) up 1.9% YoY.
items.quote: We ended Q3 with a revenue of INR 4,441 million. This is approximately $ 53 million. This is a revenue growth in INR terms quarter-on-quarter, 2.8% and year-on-year, 1.4%.

items.statement: US rate cuts and election clarity improving spending intent but not yet translating to increased discretionary spend; budgeting cycles in Oct-Nov prepare for future spending.
items.quote: To increase spending directly, not yet. But intend to spend, definitely. Because I think the impact of the cuts, the last cut gave people the positivity and hope that they will be able to spend more. But then there was the election, which created uncertainty, and people were obviously cautious with the election side of things.

items.statement: Deepening partnerships with hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Salesforce, Boomi, UiPath) and start-up ecosystem; upgraded to Salesforce Crest partner and Microsoft APAC partnership upgrade.
items.quote: We've strengthened our partnership with hyperscalers; Azure, AWS, as well as with all other partners that we work with, including Boomi, Salesforce, UiPath and others. This is giving us more long-term sustainable revenue through business solutions and solving clients' critical business problems.

items.statement: Net profit INR 398M ($4.8M); Basic EPS INR 3.37; Depreciation & amortization INR 16.6 crores (incl. INR 6.3 crores intangible from Velotio/Scaleworx); Interest expense INR 1.6 crores; Tax expense INR 11.8 crores (incl. INR 6.2 crores revers
items.quote: Net profit after tax was INR 39.8 crores or $4.8 million compared to INR 24.8 crores or $3 million last quarter. Basic EPS for the quarter was INR 3.37 compared to INR 2.1 last quarter.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue INR422 cr, up 6.9% QoQ; operational EBITDA 10.2%, up 305 bps QoQ
items.quote: Company has increased its revenue to INR422 crores, which is 6.9% higher than that of last quarter. The growth is largely fuelled by the increase in Aroma products and our sustained growth in Blends. Gross margins have improved to 48.2%, mainly on better performance of Aroma, which unwinds us from catechol issues.

items.statement: Operational EBITDA margin reached 10.2% in Q2 FY25, up 305 bps QoQ and 242 bps YoY
items.quote: This has obviously reflected in our operational EBITDA, which has now crossed double digit and is at 10.2%, up by around 305 basis points quarter -on-quarter and 242 basis points with corresponding quarter.

items.statement: Aroma revenue jumped to INR45 cr from INR13 cr QoQ; Blends sustained growth; Performance Chemicals muted due to pricing headwinds
items.quote: Aroma products have clocked a revenue of around INR45 crores as compared to only INR13 crores in last quarter. And the antidumping action on Chinese manufacturer , war by US and Europe would augur well as Aroma business once it is levied.

items.statement: Diphenol facility at CFS Europe impaired INR116 cr; CFS Wanglong China impaired INR30 cr; total exceptional impact INR151 cr
items.quote: The total net impact there of was of INR116 crores on the consolidated results for this quarter. Similarly, the economic conditions are extremely challenging in China, whereby it seems that the repurposing of our facility in China for manufacturing Heliotropin would also take much more time than what was expected earlier.

items.statement: Vanillin capacity utilization at 40%, targeting 55% run-rate by end FY25, 75% by FY26, 100% thereafter
items.quote: Basically, we are seeing very good traction from both US and Europe. Of course, the capacity utilization, currently, we are at about 40%, which, by end of FY '25, we should be hitting closer to -- on a run rate basis, closer to 55% or so.

items.statement: Vanillin pricing improved by ~$1/kg, now nearing $10/kg; antidumping duties on Chinese imports expected to support prices
items.quote: So we've improved the pricing by about $1 or so per kilo.

items.statement: Blends revenue target ~INR1,000 cr for FY25 vs INR700-750 cr FY24, growing 15-20%
items.quote: So in terms of value progression from -- I think we are growing at about -- like I said, we should be able to grow between 15% to 20% for this -- for FY '25 versus FY '24. So FY '24 was around INR700-odd crores, INR750 crores. And this -- we should probably close around -- closer to INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Gross debt INR741 cr, net debt INR650 cr; short-term borrowing ~INR300 cr, long-term ~INR440 cr; no immediate reduction plan, repaying ~INR35 cr annually
items.quote: We have a debt level of around INR750 crores. On a gross level, it's pretty high, you know that. Obviously, we don't have any immediate plans to reduce this debt level because once we have to stabilize the business, put all the business in line, and then we'll think about it.

items.statement: Rights issue planned in very near future to address liquidity and working capital challenges
items.quote: Liquidity situation of the company remains a challenge and working capital management is very high up on our agenda. As you are aware, the management is working on launching a rights issue in a near -- very near future to address these issues.

items.statement: Working capital management high priority; liquidity remains a challenge
items.quote: Liquidity situation of the company remains a challenge and working capital management is very high up on our agenda.

items.statement: US and Europe antidumping investigations on Chinese vanillin/heliotropin; interim order by Nov-end, final by May-Jun 2025
items.quote: First round is end of November in the U.S., and by April -- by May of next year, US will finalize completely. Right now, they will have interim, and then the final order is by May.

items.statement: Aroma signing only quarterly/half-yearly supply agreements, not long-term contracts, pending antidumping duty finalization
items.quote: No, we're not signing any long-term contracts because of the uncertainty on the antidumping as to what the quantum will be. So typically, we are quoting per quarter or maximum for half a year.

items.statement: Chinese dumping suppressed vanillin prices; antidumping actions expected to remove predatory pricing
items.quote: Chinese are the guys who had reduced this price. They're out of the market. The prices should come back. One cannot say how much. It will be certainly higher than what they are at this stage.

items.statement: Vanillin EBITDA margin at 100% utilization expected 15-20% on sale price; Blends EBITDA margin 14-15% standalone
items.quote: So at the capacity level of 35% to 40%, once we scale up the plant to 100%, we will be having a 15% to 20% EBITDA on the sale price.

items.statement: Europe diphenol shutdown bleed INR15-16 cr/quarter reducing to INR1 cr/quarter over 2 quarters via retrenchment
items.quote: So the cost, which we are incurring of around INR15 crores to INR16 crores on diphenol maintenance and people and other costs will reduce it to INR1 crore per quarter.

items.statement: Heliotropin production shifted from China to India due to antidumping risks; China facility fully impaired
items.quote: So the heliotropin, what we have done is we had a relook at the heliotropin project out of China because of all these antidumping actions being taken by US and Europe. So at the appropriate time, we will be setting up the capacity in India for heliotropin.

items.statement: Mexico-US blending revenue INR63 cr in H1; can shift blending to US if tariffs imposed
items.quote: Our first half business, to answer your second part of your question, from Mexico to U.S., that's just blending, which can always be done in US itself, if there is any action taken on Mexico, is about INR63 crores.

items.statement: Europe diphenol retrenchment planned over 2 quarters via furlough; provisions already made
items.quote: So we have given a furlough. So we have taken care of that earlier. So we don't expect any retrenchment. There are enough provision, we will take care of that in the books.

items.statement: Vitafor integration underway; farm product portfolio complementary to feed focus; registrations ongoing in multiple countries
items.quote: Yes. So Vitafor has a different set of products compared to -- I mean mainly their portfolio is more farm products. So -- whereas we are more focused on the feed side. So it gives us an opportunity to address the farm market with the product portfolio that we have in Vitafor, which is proprietary.

items.statement: Double-digit EBITDA margin (10.2%) achieved in Q2 FY25; management expects sustainability at current prices
items.quote: We have already hit double -digit EBITDA margin in this quarter. And we feel that this should remain and

items.statement: No plans to expand vanillin capacity beyond 6,000 TPA; will optimize current capacity first
items.quote: At present, we will first utilize what the capacity we had of 6,000. We will optimize that and then later on -- at this moment of time, we don't have any plans to enhance the vanillin capacity.

items.statement: Dahej diphenol facility operating at 80% utilization; will increase as vanillin and downstream products grow
items.quote: So basically, we are operating Dahej capacity at 80% because that's the requirement that we have for hydroquinone and catechol in our business. As our vanillin business progresses as well as our other downstream diphenol products increase, we will keep pushing up the capacity utilization.

items.statement: Europe loan ~INR80 cr; restructuring with banks planned; blending revenue ~INR100 cr/year expected to service debt
items.quote: So we do have a loan there to the extent of around INR80 crores. But we have -- we would be going to the bank for restructuring those loans. And we are very confident that the revenues which are generated from Blends, we will be increasing our focus on Blends, which will take care of this outstanding.

items.statement: No further large impairments foreseen; China and Europe diphenol CGUs fully impaired
items.quote: At this moment of time, what the stage of business is there, obviously, no because whatever the impairment to be done has been done. One cannot see -- one doesn't know how the businesses go. We feel that there will be no write-offs in the near future.

items.statement: Performance Chemicals (hydroquinone/catechol) targeting 15-20% growth next financial year; currently ~13% of business
items.quote: Performance Chemicals, also some value -added products on hydroquinone and catechol are in the pipeline, which should also give us about a 15 -20% growth in the next financial year.

items.statement: H2 FY25 revenue expected ~10% above Q2 run-rate; EBITDA margin flat for next 2 quarters due to Europe bleed
items.quote: Generally, Jatin, if you see, traditionally, our first quarter -- and it's around INR45-55 crores -- INR40-60 crores. So looking at the current scenario, I think we will lock in around 10% more than what we are doing at this current -- current prices.

name: Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd

items.statement: Average JV revenue share recognized in topline is 30%
items.quote: On an average you can take 30%. It depends on joint venture to joint venture, but average you can take 30%.

items.statement: Typical bid ticket size Rs.300-1,000 crore+ for bulk water business

items.quote: In Rajasthan, there was an election issue, so the tender was not opened. Now there is a sub-election, there is Achar Sanhita, so again they are not opening the tender. Hopefully we should get the tenders to open this quarter and then, you see the tender opening and tender finalization get delayed.

items.statement: Bank rating process with ICRA underway; BG limit expansion depends on rating outcome
items.quote: We are in the process of discussing with ICRA for doing the rating. Once we get the rating, then we will approach the banks for the BG limit. Approximately how much time can it take? | will pass this for the next conference call, because the rating has to come

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin target of mid-teens reiterated
items.quote: Q2 FY '25 financial performance reaffirms our commitment to move forward towards our medium-term objective of achieving mid -teen EBITDA.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 capex target of INR750-800 crore
items.quote: Our capex, we would like to stick to that INR750 crores of capex, which we have indicated earlier, INR800 crores max, which we'll be sticking to those numbers.

items.statement: H2 FY25 MHCV industry expected to be flat to positive, no degrowth
items.quote: Degrowth for H2, we are not seeing. So we are seeing at a minimum, H2 should be kind of flattish, if not positive, like what ICRA is saying.

items.statement: Switch India expected to achieve EBITDA breakeven in FY25
items.quote: As advised earlier, Switch India is expected to achieve EBITDA breakeven this fiscal.

items.statement: Reverse merger of Hinduja Leyland Finance with NXTDIGITAL likely to conclude before end of Q1 FY26
items.quote: Reverse merger of Hinduja Leyland Finance with NXTDIGITAL is on track and we are in the process of obtaining the necessary approvals from RBI. This is likely to get concluded before end of Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Fleet utilization recovered to 95% country average in October from 60-65% in July-August
items.quote: In July and August, I was in the market and especially in the Central and Eastern India, we ha d a situation because of monsoons and other things, the fleet utilization was as low as 60% to 65%. In some areas, we got to hear that fleet utilization was as low as 30%. So now in October, if you have seen the data, recent data that was published on fleet utilization, it is already up to the level of 9

items.statement: Replacement demand expected to return from November as fleet age at 10-10.5 years vs historical 7-7.5 years
items.quote: And this number has passed even, I think, 10 or 10.5 years now. And historically, this number has been close to 7, 7.5. So as soon as I think the environment becomes more positive, which we hope it will starting November, I think you will see a lot of that replacement demand coming back.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 11.6%, up from 10.6% in Q1 FY25 and 11.2% in Q2 FY24
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Q2 stands at 11.6%, better than 10.6% in Q1 of current year and also better than 11.2% in Q2 of last year.

items.statement: Material cost at 71.2% of revenue in Q2 FY25 vs 73.5% in Q2 FY24 and 72.2% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Material cost as a percentage of revenue was at 71.2 % and 73.5% in Q2 last year and 72.2% in Q1 of current year.

items.statement: Steel price softening of INR2.5/kg contributed 0.5% margin improvement; cost reduction initiatives added another 0.5%
items.quote: There has been a considerable softening which has happened on the prices of steel flat steel, proprietary steel, all these have gone down by about INR2.5 per kg So all these have got translated to 0.5% margin reduction. And similarly, on the cost reduction initiatives, just like what we did in last 2 years, as our MD was indicating, we are not doing anything different. The same levers we have used

items.statement: Export volume grew 14% YoY and 42% QoQ; targeting best-ever export performance in FY25
items.quote: Despite global challenges, our export volume continued to grow in double digits, registering a growth of 14% on Y -o-Y basis and of 42% sequentially. We are intensifying our expansion strategy in our focus markets of SAARC, Middle East, Africa and Asia, aim ed at posting the best performance ever during this fiscal.

items.statement: Long-term export volume aspiration of over 50,000 units
items.quote: So in the long term, I would say that our aspiration is to deliver more than 50,000 units of exports volume from the company.

items.statement: Switch India order book of 2,000 electric buses to be delivered in ~15 months
items.quote: So this order book of 2 ,000 that we have in hand, we hope that we will be able to complete in about 15 months of time.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 capex INR153 crore; H1 FY25 cumulative INR307 crore
items.quote: Capex for the quarter was INR153 crores and INR307 crores cumulatively for the year.

items.statement: H2 FY25 investments of INR200-250 crore in Hinduja Leyland Finance and up to INR500-750 crore in subsidiaries/associates
items.value: INR200 crores to INR250 crores equity inclusion, which may happen. And if need be, we may have to make necessary investments in associate / subsidiaries to the extent of INR500 crores to INR750 crores in the maximum situation.
items.quote: One is on the Hinduja Leyland Finance side, we said that we may have to i nvest INR200 crores, INR250 crores. And if need be, we may have to make necessary investments in associate / subsidiaries to the extent of INR500 crores to INR750 crores in the maximum situation

items.statement: Switch India ramping up production of new 12-meter ultra-low floor electric bus for DTC order of 1,200 buses
items.quote: Switch is active in fulfilling DTC order of 1,200 buses, supplies of which would start later this year. This would be a co mplete, newly developed, low -floor electric bus with very contemporary design and features and is updated with all the recent advancements in technology

items.statement: No structured price circulars issued; net sales realization improved via monthly discount reductions and mix management
items.quote: Although in a structured way, if you as k me whether we have done it by way of price circular, we have not done that. But if you ask me whether there is an attempt which has been done, we keep attempting by way of reduction of the discounts on every month whereby we increase our average selling price or as we call it net sales realization

items.statement: Focus on selling higher-margin MHCV products (19-55 ton range) and maximizing margins on new launches
items.quote: Amit, just to add another element that we are quite focused on is to look at what kind of mix we want to sell because we have a very wide product portfolio starting from -- I'm talking about MHCV -- starting from 19 ton and going up to 55 ton. So we keep a very sharp eye on the mix. Of course, some of it depends on how the industry is movi ng. But as far as possible, we try to sell higher-margin p

items.statement: Defense revenue doubled in H1 FY25 after doubling in FY24; strong order pipeline and visibility
items.quote: On the defense side, you know that last year was a damn good year for us. We had more than doubled our top line on defense. And I'm happy to say, even in H1, we have almost doubled our defense top line. So like we had been saying earlier that we have a very strong pipeline of orders and also our future visibility of orders as far as defense is concerned.

items.statement: Aftermarket growing ~15% YoY in H1 FY25
items.quote: On the aftermarket side, we are continuously growing at about 15%. In H1 also, we have grown, I think, by 14% or so.

items.statement: International business performing well in GCC and Africa despite SAARC weakness; entered Southeast Asia
items.quote: Although the SAARC market is way down and continues to be down, but we have done really well in our other markets, which are GCC, Africa. We have also made an entry into Southeast Asia now, like we told you earlier that this would be our next attempt to expand geographically.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR501 crore at end of Q2 FY25 from INR1,139 crore YoY and INR1,295 crore QoQ; debt-equity 0.05
items.quote: Net debt at the end of the quarter was at INR501 crores, much lower than INR1,139 crores at end of Q2 last year and also lower than INR1,295 crores at end of Q1 of current year. Debt equity ra tio at the end of the quarter was 0.05.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded from AA to AA+ with stable outlook by ICRA and CARE
items.quote: Courtesy improvement in our operating performance, cost structure and debt metrics, credit rating agencies like ICRA and CARE have upgraded Ashok Leyland rating from AA to AA+ with a stable outlook, reflecting their expectation of a healthy profile going forward.

items.statement: OHM capitalized with INR300 crore equity enabling INR900-1,000 crore debt raise; total capital INR1,200-1,300 crore
items.quote: In last year, we had put in an equity of INR300 crores and basis that, we have a potential to raise, let us say, about INR900 crores to INR1,000 crores of debt in that company. So that makes it about INR1,200 crores to INR1,300 crores in terms of capital available to invest in E-MaaS business.

items.statement: H1 FY25 MHCV industry volume down only 2% YoY vs earlier expectation of 15% drop
items.quote: When we started the year, we were all saying, and most of the people were saying that H1 would be 15% drop. And eventually, we are at close of H1 now, where we have seen only 2% drop in MHCV industry.

items.statement: Management plans 4-5% price increase over next two quarters to cover commodity inflation
items.quote: So there will be about 4% to 5% price increase in the next 2 quarters. So that we'll have to take, and we will do it strategically in SKUs where we haven't taken a price for some time.

items.statement: Expect to maintain stable margin profile rather than expand margins due to high commodity inflation
items.quote: So we expect to maintain margins rather than increase margins, balance inflation and make sure that we are able to keep a stable margin profile.

items.statement: Urban metros facing demand slowdown due to high housing costs and non-salaried wage stress
items.quote: The housing cost in urban and especially in metro areas is about 22% of the total CPI basket weight. And we know that Real Estate is -- the prices have gone up, the rentals have gone up, and that's creating stress for most consumers in large cities and metros.

items.statement: Rural growth at mid-to-high single digits, urban growth slower, rural growing at 2x urban pace
items.quote: The rural growths are reasonable, I would say, slightly high single-digit kind of growth. They're not the kind of growth that we've seen in the past, but there will be high single digits --Vipin Vipin Kataria: Yes. So it's -- so the rural growth at 2x of urban

items.statement: Will balance price increases and volumes carefully over next 6-9 months given inflation volatility
items.quote: In the next 6 months, 9 months, we are going to be very careful about how we treat price increases, how we route for volumes, et cetera. So we will balance it well, and we will make sure that we do the best from a volume standpoint as well.

items.statement: Three new factories operational in UP, Bihar, Tirunelveli plus Ranjangaon expansion; capacity adequate
items.quote: We've got 3 new factories, which are already in play. But UP, in the north we've never had a factory which is large and it provides us all that is required. So we had 1 plant in Uttarakhand, which was done about 12, 13 years ago. Now we've got a UP factory. We've got a new factory in Bihar in Bihta and we've got a brand-new factory in Tirunelveli. We've also expanded our factory in Ranjangaon.

items.statement: Innovation contributing ~2% of revenue from products launched in last 24 months
items.quote: Yes. So innovation, as we read the innovation, we -- any product which is launched in the last 24 months is considered as innovation, and we are running at about 2% of revenue on that.

items.statement: Palm oil inflation ~45% in Q2 FY25 due to 40% import duty and supply shortage; strategic covers mitigating impact
items.quote: just to give you an idea on palm oil, you are seeing a slight inflation in palm oil in Q2 '25. Actually, the inflation is about 45% over Q1and the reason for that is import duty of 40% and also a demand and supply situation, which is creating some kind of shortage in the countries of origin, which is Malaysia and Indonesia

items.statement: Salary cost up 45% YoY due to phantom stock revaluation from share price appreciation (INR50 cr impact in Q2)
items.quote: That's about INR50 crores.

items.statement: Route-to-Market 2.0 pilot in 25 cities covering 44 distributors and 50,000+ outlets showing encouraging results; full embedding in 12-15 months
