items.quote: We have currently pilots in Q2 covering 25 cities, which is 44 distributors and more than 50,000 outlets, which are showing very encouraging results, and we plan to scale up implementation in the long term to maximize extraction.

items.statement: Direct reach expanded to 28.5 lakh outlets; rural distributors over 30,000; focus states performing 1.9x rest of India
items.quote: We are expanding direct reach. We are now at 28.5 lakh outlets that we cover directly. There is an uptick in rural distribution where we've -- our number of distributors is now over 30,000, the rural distributors. O ur focus states are performing better. They're about 1.9x what rest of India is

items.statement: Volume growth 8% in Q2 FY25; 12-month revenue growth 4.5%; operating profit INR707 cr (12% below YoY, 7% above 24-month)
items.quote: We've achieved INR4,566 crores, which is a volume -- the volume growth is almost 18%. It's -- sorry, 8%, sorry, what am I talking about? So volume growth is 8%. The 12-month growth on revenue is about 4.5% and the 24 months is also similar at 5%.

items.statement: Operating profit margin 15.5%, PBT margin 15.7%, PAT margin 11.6% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: And if you were to look at the ratios at the bottom, profit from operations is still 15.5%, profit before tax is 15.7% and profit after t ax is a very healthy 11.6

items.statement: Wheat inflation structural due to lower crop and government stocks; expecting improvement next year with better acreage and yields
items.quote: Wheat, it's a fundamental issue as far as wheat is concerned because the crop has been lower, the government is holding less stocks. And hence, the release of stocks has been lower. But it's 1 year. Now we are moving into the next year soon. And hopefully, the crops will be better because as the prices go up, more farmers start to look at that crop.

items.statement: Adjacent businesses (wafers, rusk, croissant, drinks, international) showing momentum despite base business slowdown
items.quote: Our wafer business has been doing quite well. Even our rusk business has been seeing the uptick. Croissant has been doing extremely well. Our drinks have been showing resurgence, both in our PET format as well as the Lassi, which is in the tetra pack format. And our international business, especially the Middle East, has been doing extremely well as well.

items.statement: Quick commerce and e-commerce growing well with share gains; modern trade reasonable; traditional trade slower but rural recovering
items.quote: We've been seeing very good growth as far as quick commerce and e-commerce is concerned. Even modern trade has been doing reasonably well. Although the competitive scenario there is pretty tough, but we've been doing well, and we've been gaining share in both quick commerce, e-commerce as well as modern trade. It's the traditional trade, the GT part of the business, which is growing slower current

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR17,000-18,000 crores with 2.5% EBITDA margin
items.quote: we maintain our guidance of INR17,000 crores-INR18,000 crores of revenue by FY27 with 2.5% EBITDA margin

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance INR6,500 crores
items.quote: I guess for full year, we are sticking to our guidance of INR6,500 crores kind of revenue

items.statement: Full year FY25 EBITDA margin 2% plus
items.quote: For the full year yes we never give guidance quarter-on-quarter it is always for the full year

items.statement: Volume guidance FY25 1.2 million tons plus, FY26 2 million tons plus
items.quote: Full year we should do 1.2 million tons plus. Dharmil: And for FY26? Anubhav Gupta: For next year it should be 2 million tons plus

items.statement: H2 FY25 capex INR100 crores, FY26 capex INR300-400 crores for 10 service centers
items.quote: This year, we may spend another INR100 crores in the second half and for the next year, the budget is to spend INR300 crores-INR400 crores to set up 10 service centers

items.statement: Monthly volume target 160,000 tons in FY26, 250,000 tons in FY27
items.quote: next year we will take it up to 160,000 tons per month, which is FY26. And eventually we shall move towards 250,000 tons per month in FY27

items.statement: Construction activity weak due to elections, delayed budget, extended monsoon
items.quote: construction activity, which was weak across the country because of elections, delayed budget and also the extended monsoon

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 1% due to INR17-18 crores inventory loss from 15% steel price crash
items.quote: The margins, if you look at, were a bit soft, mainly because of highly volatilized steel prices, which crashed by like 15% from July to September quarter

items.statement: Margin to recover to 2-2.5% in coming quarters as steel prices stabilize
items.quote: except Q2 which saw some softness in margin due to inventory right now, the margin will recover to 2-2.5% in the coming quarters

items.statement: Steel prices crashed 15% (INR7,500/ton) July-September, now stable and reversing
items.quote: Steel prices came down by INR7,500 per ton from July to September, which is almost 15% crash

items.statement: Q2 volume 350,000+ tons (120,000 tons/month), B2B trading 65%, service centers 20%, distribution 15%
items.quote: if you look at Q2 for INR1,800 crores revenue, we did more than 350,000 ton of sales volume. So that means we are doing 120,000 ton per month easily now

items.statement: Adding solar profile structures (40,000 tons/month market) and PEB construction products (purlins, deck sheeting) in service centers
items.quote: We shall start this product in December or January, over the next 1 to 2 months. The other user industry, what we are planning to service is the PEB construction industry

items.statement: Launched light structure, angles, channels under private label in distribution
items.quote: we introduced light structure, angles and channels into our private label and that distribution started to the existing distribution network

items.statement: Net working capital negative currently, guiding 15-20 days negative until 7-8 service centers operational
items.quote: The net working capital for us remained negative because the warehouses, cum service centers are still ramping up. So, unless until we have like 7, 8 service centers fully operational, we don't expect working capital to bloat

items.statement: Cash on books INR1,100-1,200 crores, to fund service center capex and inventory
items.quote: we are sitting on approximately INR1,100 crores to INR1,200 crores of cash on the books. So this gets deployed as and when service centers get commissioned

items.statement: Tied up with India's largest steel supplier, booking imported steel, domestic mill tie-ups
items.quote: tying up with India's largest steel supplier. And also, there were opportunities for imported steel. So, we knew that there was a lot of imports coming in India and we booked some of them

items.statement: Inventory loss risk from sharp steel price falls (once in a decade event), mitigated by 8-day inventory churn
items.quote: This kind of scenario comes once in a decade. You don't see that very often. You see this once in a decade. Last such fall we saw was in like 2007-2008

items.statement: Inventory days 8 days, 30,000-35,000 tons inventory at 100,000+ tons monthly volume
items.quote: Inventory days were only eight, right. So, the inventory what we hold in our system is like 30,000-35,000 tons. When monthly volume is like 100,000 tons plus

items.statement: Targeting 25-30% ROC on 2-2.5% EBITDA margin with high asset turns
items.quote: these 2% to 2.5% EBITDA margin will generate 25%, 30% ROC, which we are chasing

items.statement: Zinc business started last quarter, emerged as India's largest distributor, revenue guidance clarity by Q3
items.quote: Zinc business we started just to test the waters last quarter. And despite being very like despite doing very low volume, we erupted, we emerged as India's largest distributor

items.statement: No related party deals with SG Transport or SG Finserve, logistics fully outsourced, cash discount model
items.quote: No, there is no deal as such. So, the logistics are completely outsourced, nothing is in the group for S.G. Mart and as far as SG. Finserve is concerned the supply chain funding company. We give the option of cash discount to our customers

items.statement: Business model connects manufacturer to distributor, not retail/Tier 2-3, high volume low margin high ROC
items.quote: Our business model revolves around connecting between the manufacturer and its distributor, right? So, that's where we have identified our space, and that's where we are building our business model, which is high volume, high churn, low margin, but high ROC

items.statement: Regulator halted lending at major NBFCs DMI and Navi due to aggressive pricing and excessive borrower leveraging; RBI enforcing FOIR checks to prevent over-leveraging.
items.quote: Specifically, in recent developments, the regulator has halted lending at three or four major NBFCs, including DMI and Navi, which are prominent in the digital lending space.

items.statement: GNPA ratio at 0.7%, among top 5% in industry, well below internal target of 2%.
items.quote: We target a GNPA ratio below 2%, but right now, it's significantly below that, at 0.7%, which is among the top 5% in the industry.

items.statement: Average loan tenure 6.5 months and ticket size ₹44,000 last quarter; expect both to nearly double to ~12 months and ~₹100,000.
items.quote: Our average loan tenure for the last quarter was 6.5 months, and the ticket size was around ₹44,000. Moving forward, we expect both these numbers to nearly double, with tenures closer to 12 months and ticket sizes around ₹100,000.

items.statement: Secured ₹66 crore in sanctions from lenders (ICICI, RBL, AU Small Finance, others) vs prior target of ₹50 crore; figure may increase further.
items.quote: However, we've been fortunate enough to secure about ₹70 crores in sanctions—₹66 crores, to be precise—and we are optimistic that this figure will increase further.

items.statement: Internal goal to hit ₹100 crore AUM; pushing for more but ₹100 crore definitely achievable.
items.quote: In terms of growth expectations, I would conservatively say our goal is to hit ₹100 crore internally. We're pushing for more, but ₹100 crore is definitely achievable.

items.statement: Average ROI charged to retail customers is 33%; industry benchmarks 60-70%; unofficial cap ~36%; comfortable with current rates per RBI feedback.
items.quote: 33% is the ROI that we end up charging —the average ROI charged to the retail customers who borrow from us.

items.statement: Co-lending revenue includes API revenue plus 17-18% ROI on capital; co-lending revenue potential significantly higher than term loans.
items.quote: From a revenue perspective, co-lending offers multiple streams. One is the API revenue we earn, and the other is the ROI on the capital we provide, which can range between 17% to 18%.

items.statement: 30-40% of book with lenders focusing on audiences with detailed insights rather than standard personal lending; picking top 10% of partner books via data-driven algorithm.
items.quote: Even today, around 30% to 40% of our book is with lenders focusing on audiences for whom they have detailed insights, rather than just engaging in standard personal lending.

items.statement: Moved into new office reflecting growth ambitions; revamped website to modern custom-made platform.
items.quote: We recently moved into a new office! Our previous office was small and cozy but served us well. With our growth, we wanted a space that reflected our ambitions.

items.statement: Team of 28-30 people; hiring high-quality talent for growth over next 12-24 months.
items.quote: Finally, we're hiring! We have around 28 to 30 people on our team, but we're looking for high-quality talent to help us grow over the next 12-24 months.

items.statement: Launched AI tool Senti for sentiment analysis on call recordings to proactively address customer interaction issues.
items.quote: From a tech perspective, we've launched an exciting AI tool, Senti, for sentiment analysis on call recordings.

items.statement: Model robustness requires 10-15 years; 8 years not enough to fully prove; conservative scaling to avoid subpar book.
items.quote: I would say that, like I mentioned, it will take around 15 years for anyone to fully understand all the cycles and nuances of this space.

items.statement: Differentiation via niche use-case platforms (e.g., payment gateway lending, Zomato restaurant lending) rather than generic loan apps; banks unlikely to build such niche platforms.
items.quote: You need to develop an app, websi te, or platform that solves a particular problem for the customer, attracting that specific customer to use your service

items.statement: Q2 capital already deployed; expect minimal negative carry of ₹3-5 crore; borrowings typically 1-3 year tenure.
items.quote: this quarter’s capital has already been deployed. When the results come ou t, you’ll see that we don’t expect much negative carry, if any —maybe ₹3-4-5 crore, but nothing major

items.statement: Borrowings at competitive rates; rates adjustable at partner/lender level; comfortable with lender names; not borrowing under stress.
items.quote: Regarding interest rates, if anything changes, the rates can automatically be adjusted at the partner or lender level, so we don't foresee any major issues there.

items.statement: Projecting highest ever sales and profitability in FY25 with strong Q3 and Q4
items.quote: we a re confident and are projecting a very strong Q3 and Q4, allowing us to record our highest ever sales and the highest ever profitability and cash generation in this financial year

items.statement: Targeting 7% PBT margin over 2-3 year timeframe as higher margin revenue scales
items.quote: So, over a 2-3 year timeframe, I think internally we have a more aggressive target, I think the 7% PBT is what our plan calls for

items.statement: Expecting 200-300 basis point margin improvement over next few years
items.quote: I think at least a 200 basis point, 300 basis point improvement over the next few years is definitely what we are targeting

items.statement: Adding green plant capacity in India and US for PEB with timeline of about a year
items.quote: In pre-engineered buildings, in India and the US , we are adding green plant capacity. We will be looking at another plant in the West of India

items.statement: Strong order books across PEB India, PEB US, process equipment, engineering services, tubes and hydraulics
items.quote: Our growth drivers continue to be PEB India, Ascent, which is US PEB business, process equipment, engineering services, tubes, and hydraulics

items.statement: Exiting 7-8 low margin revenue streams worth ~Rs. 1,000 crores, low margin business now ~30% of revenue
items.quote: So, there is almost, I would say, 7-8 revenue streams which have been removed. So, the impact of that is a reduction in an overall revenue of the company

items.statement: US metal buildings operating margins 28-32%, insulated from raw material price movements
items.quote: We get upwards of 28%, close to 32% on our US order books in metal buildings. What is there right now is quite strong

items.statement: Targeting interest cost at 3.75% of revenue for next year
items.quote: Yes, 3.75% is the next year is what we would like to tell you too

items.statement: Raebareli plant operational, adding 25-30% PEB capacity (~Rs. 300 crores revenue potential)
items.quote: So, the commissioning of the Raebareli plant effectively increases the production capacity by about 25%-30%. Due to a combination of factors, our actual revenue growth in PEB for this quarter is projected to be higher than that

items.statement: Expecting sustained double digit revenue growth driven by market share gains in large addressable markets
items.quote: Our plan is obviously sustained double digit growth. Even this year you would have seen a little less muted growth is because of the exit of the old revenue streams

items.statement: EBITDA already above 10% sustainably for last 2-3 quarters, expect further expansion from operating leverage
items.quote: So, we are already above 10% EBITDA, not 8, 9, we are about 10. And that has sustainably been the case for the last 2-3 quarters

items.statement: Debt-equity at 0.76, not expected to exceed 0.8, over 80% debt is working capital non-cash
items.quote: I think we are right now at 0.7, debt equity 0.76. So, we don't anticipate it ever growing above 0.8 for example

items.statement: Engineering services revenue at Rs. 60-70 crores with high margins, targeting quick scaling
items.quote: Currently that's at about Rs. 60, Rs. 70 crores, we expect that to grow quite well. It is one of the verticals we intend to grow quite quickly

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA guided at ₹1,000-1,050 crore
items.quote: this year is expected to remain broadly similar to last year, roughly ₹1,000 crores to ₹1,050 crores kind of EBITDA given the challenges that we are going through.

items.statement: FY28 EBITDA target ₹1,800-2,200 crore
items.quote: from FY '28 timeframe, I think we are targeting somewhere in the range of ₹1,800 crores to ₹2,200 crores kind of EBITDA, predominantly driven by consistent volume growth over three years because of our increased capacities.

items.statement: Debt-to-EBITDA target <2.5x and ROCE >15% by FY28
items.quote: We're saying that we target less than 2.5x of debt-to-EBITDA, ROCE of greater than 15% and EBITDA in the range of ₹1,800-2,200 crores, which we feel is a realistic with a stretch kind of aspiration and feel very confident of delivering on it.

items.statement: FY25 capex ₹1,300-1,500 crore; FY26 capex ~₹1,000 crore
items.quote: I think the Capex plan has been optimised and moderated. So this year is expected to be in the range of ₹1,300 crores to ₹1,500 crores versus earlier estimate of ₹1,500 crores to ₹1,800 crores. So that has gone down and the Capex for FY '26 is also estimated to be around ₹1,000 crores.

items.statement: MMA capacity expanded to ~200 KTPA with ability to expand further with minor investment
items.quote: For us, the highlight is we've completed our expansion, our capacity is now roughly in the range of 200KTPA and we can expand it even further with a very minor investment.

items.statement: Zone 4 multipurpose plant commissioning by mid next year; commercialisation over 18 months
items.quote: The MPP, the Multipurpose Plant that we are setting up in zone 4 is likely to get commissioned by the middle of next year, it will also give us ramp up abilities to do molecules depending on margin profile happening at that particular point in time because multipurpose, our ability to switch the product portfolio is quite significant over there.

items.statement: Contract 3 expected to ramp to peak by FY27; Contract 4 peak in next 18 months
items.quote: Contract – three, which was a 10-year supply contract again for a Specialty Chemical Intermediates is operating as per contract terms. This is expected to ramp up to peak levels in FY '27 timeframe.

items.statement: Cost optimisation initiatives target ₹150-200 crore EBITDA uplift in near term
items.quote: On cost optimisation, we're doing broadly three buckets – steam, power, fixed cost and then a little bit of yield improv ements. On steam several initiatives are already in the play. We've installed back pressure turbines in one of our zones. We continue to expand that to other zones. It's expected to deliver significant savings in terms of steam unlock potential

items.statement: Volume and margin ramp-up in expanded chains could add ₹350-550 crore EBITDA over 2-3 years
items.quote: The second bucket of volume and margin ramp up. Especially in the areas where we have expanded capacity there's almost upside potential possible of ₹350 crores to ₹550 crores on EBITDA terms.

items.statement: Capex-led growth from Zone 4 and UPL JV to add ₹300-450 crore EBITDA by FY28
items.quote: And then there is a Capex-led growth, part of which, we had sort of announced in the previous calls, which will start delivering ₹300 crores to ₹450 crores, in the kind of timeframe that we're talking about FY '25 to FY '28.

items.statement: Non-energy volumes grew 22% YoY in Q2; agrochemicals soft but showing green shoots
items.quote: On non-energy business, both on Y-o-Y basis and Q-o-Q basis, there is healthy volume growth. We're talking about almost 22% volume growth on a Y-o-Y basis. And that uptick is visible across end applications, dyes, pigments, polymer additives. Agrochemicals continue to remain soft, but still there are some green shoots of recovery as we mentioned in the last call.

items.statement: MMA volumes dropped 36% QoQ in Q2 due to refining margin collapse; October uptick seen
items.quote: The energy business is where the second quarter became tough. So we had a very good Q1 for the energy business. In Q2, on a Q-o-Q basis, there was a 36% drop on the volumes for the energy business, specifically MMA. And that was linked to a steep drop in refining margins.

items.statement: MMA customer diversification: targeting US, Europe, Singapore refineries; bulk shipment capability established
items.quote: We continue to push our efforts to diversify customers and geography base across. We were Middle East heavy for exports. Now we are targeting customers in U.S., Europe, Singapore and as well as other refineries globally. We've had initial success in U.S. We have done already a couple of bulk shipments, one actually went in October and we are hoping to scale up that business quite significantly ove

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on Sulphur Black from China and ADD investigation on PNT could benefit dyes segment
items.quote: There was a recent announcement of ADD on Sulphur Black from China. We supply one of the key intermediate going into that particular molecule. So we expect demand there to grow. On PNT as well, I think there is an announcement of initiation of ADD investigation. We will see how it concludes, but that could potentially also have a positive impact on this end market, particularly for us.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA ₹512 crore, up 18% YoY; Q2 EBITDA ₹202 crore vs ₹311 crore in Q1
items.quote: On an H1 basis, H1 to H1, Y-o-Y comparison, we are still 18% up ₹512 crore EBITDA against ₹434 crores. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, there was a compression in margins. If you sort of disaggregate this perfor mance on the volumes and margins front, I think on volumes, all of you are aware that the Energy business became a significant part of our portfolio and hence we're trying to give details of

items.statement: Contract 6 (nitric acid sourcing) savings to kick in from H2 FY26
items.quote: And contract – six is slightly different. It's a 20-year sourcing contract for purchase of Nitric Acid, which mitigated a risk for Aarti Industries from a key raw material purchase point of view. Again, it is operating as per contract terms and it will also give us supply security for one of the key raw material. Also some of the major savings from this contract will actually kicking in the second

items.statement: Energy segment revenue share fell to 32% in Q2 from 41% in Q1; non-energy mix improving
items.quote: If you look at the FY'22 split versus what you're seeing on FY '25 Q1 and Q2, you will see one obvious trend is of course Energy has become a significant part of the portfolio, it used to be relatively small in the range of 15%. Today, this quarter it came down to 32%, but was as high as 41% in the Q1.

items.statement: Five-plus strategic alliance projects in active discussions; aim to conclude in 6-12 months
items.quote: Strategic alliances have always remained a priority for Aarti Industries and will remain a priority. I think as we speak there are five plus projects where there are active conversations happening for different chemistries. There are different phases, these include the likes of backward integration for a Polymer where we are already in a long-term tie up or intermediate for end use in personal car

items.statement: Early bets on circularity, electronic chemicals, battery materials; battery chemistries may commercialise in 3-5 years
items.quote: And then early bets on new sectors, right. I think we mentioned this, but there are three themes we are focusing on where potentially we could grow with partnerships as well as joint ventures. The models could look very different. I think on Circularity and Chemical Recycling, we see a huge upside, both linked on our strengths as well as based on domestic market potential that's area we continue t

items.statement: Suyog Kotecha onboarded as CEO and Executive Director; three new independent directors added
items.quote: In our 40th year, I think, as a milestone step, we have onboarded Suyog Kotecha as Executive Director and CEO. That's a major milestone in the company's journey in professionalising and taking forward the company from this 40th to 50th year in 2034. He has a strong background of McKinsey and then Reliance and others. We are sure that we will be able to drive the company very well in the future and

items.statement: MMA demand volatile, linked to gasoline-naphtha crack; margin pressure from Chinese overcapacity may persist
items.quote: The market here is linked to what is happening in the refinery market. So it is fair to say that October or Q3 numbers for MMA will look better than the Q2. But using the term bottoming out, I think is sort of stretching it, because ultimately it depends on how the refinery cracks both gasoline-naphtha delta as well as the gasoline-crude crack evolve over the course of next two, three sort of six,

items.statement: Interest costs flat; rate cut benefits expected from next quarter
items.quote: Interest costs broadly have remained constant. I think the original anticipation was that the softening of interest rates will start benefiting from now, but that cycle has obviously got delayed. We expect that the benefits from that will accrue from the next quarter onwards.

items.statement: Management expects 5% annual sales growth for Dhanuka business, with EBITDA margins remaining in single digits.
items.quote: I think on a 6-monthly basis, there is a growth. But last year, I think we will did INR550 crores. So if you see on an annual basis, we are expecting maybe 5% growth, not significant.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 sales declined 8.9% sequentially; management says quarter-on-quarter numbers are not relevant due to shipment timing and seasonality.
items.quote: So Q-on-Q number is never relevant for Orchid because its seasonal, markets are different. So I will -- there is not going to be any pattern or I will not be able to share any data how it is worse or bad, not.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA was INR78.6 crores, up from INR54.7 crores in H1 FY24; operating EBITDA grew 39% year-on-year.
items.quote: Our overall EBITDA for the first half of '25 was INR78.6 crores, making a significant increase from INR54.7 crores in the first half of last year.

items.statement: Enmetazobactam sales have started in EU market; initial numbers are insignificant as sales began recently.
items.quote: I'm pleased to report that our Enmetazobactam sales have officially begun in the EU market. While the initial numbers are insignificant as the sales started just recently, we are encouraged by this initial progress.

items.statement: 7ACA project capex estimated at INR700 crores total; INR35 crores spent so far; commissioning target April 2026.
items.quote: In August, we had talked about commissioning of April '26. So it's early to say, the construction is fully going to begin now

items.statement: Small capacity enhancement project commissioned ahead of schedule; validation batches completed; will contribute to sales in coming months.
items.quote: I'm pleased to share that our small-capacity enhancement project has been commissioned ahead of schedule. We have already completed validation batches, and this additional capacity will start contributing to sales in the coming months.

items.statement: Top 3 molecules continue to dominate revenue; no other product expected to dethrone them in near foreseeable future.
items.quote: These 3 products are the largest. And in the near future, I don't think any other product is going to dethrone them of the top 3 positions. These 3 will continue to be the largest product for Orchid in the near foreseeable future as well.

items.statement: Ceftazidime/Avibactam US FDA filing received observations; deficiencies not serious; working to refile within current quarter.
items.quote: This filing has received some observations from the U.S. FDA. As per our consultant, the cited deficiencies were not of the serious nature and we are no w generating data to address these points promptly. We are currently working to remove the noted efficiencies and expect to be refile within this quarter

items.statement: China launch for Enmetazobactam delayed; no clear timeline; discussions ongoing with partner Allecra.
items.quote: I agree with you, we've had a couple of these discussions with Allecra. They are as confused as we are. Very difficult to get information from China, I agree, so we are discussing with the partners, but no development that we would like to disclose at this time.

items.statement: US commercial launch timing for Enmetazobactam uncertain; partner Allecra evaluating confidentiality agreements; no visibility on launch timeline.
items.quote: So all I can say is that they have shared some confidentiality agreement with the partners evaluating the project. And we are keeping our fingers crossed. I don't have any information beyond that.

items.statement: Lifetime sales estimate for Enmetazobactam (Exblifeb) remains $2-3 billion globally (US, Europe, China combined), unchanged from 3 years ago.
items.quote: Our long-term estimate both for the lifetime sales for this product is $2 billion to $3 billion, which has U.S. and Europe and China combined. This is the same estimate which I said 3 years ago.

items.statement: Enmetazobactam priced 10-15% higher than standard therapies in India; EU per-patient price unknown.
items.quote: Similar to other molecules, we maybe 10%, 15% higher than other standard products that are used for similar kind of therapies.

items.statement: Management avoids flooding market with excess production to prevent pricing pressure; production ramped based on actual demand.
items.quote: And if you produce too much, there is selling pressure, which brings the pressure on the pricing and profitability. And we have always maintained, Orchid is never the company to do that first. So we would only like to sell in the market, what is the demand rather than flooding the market with material and resulting in a price drop.

items.statement: Ceftazidime/Avibactam non-infringing polymorph and process developed; targeting Europe, Brazil markets where patents valid until early 2030s.
items.quote: We have developed a molecule, which is a non-infringing polymorph and non-infringing process. So besides the U.S., there are opportunities that lie in other regulated markets like Europe, Brazil, etcetera, where the patent for the patented [mark 0:14:10] is still existent, until the early 2030s.

items.statement: AMS (antimicrobial solutions) division launched in India last week of September; partnered with Cipla for pan-India distribution; both companies sell in same markets without geographical division.
items.quote: On the reach numbers, I won't be able to share anything with you. But both Orchid and Cipla will be selling in the same market, there is no geographical division between the companies as to Orchid can sell to certain hospitals and they can sell to certain hospitals. Both companies can go and sell.

items.statement: Management welcomes competing drugs for antimicrobial resistance; believes market large enough (5M deaths in 2019, rising to 10M by 2030) for multiple products.
items.quote: this problem is so large, like I said, 5 million people died in 2019, and it's expected by 2030, this number is expected to rise to 10 million; we need more and more drugs to tackle this men ace of antimicrobial resistance. So I welcome any development in that area

items.statement: ORBLICEF (Enmetazobactam-Cefepime) launched in India last week of September; marketing partnership with Cipla; initial doctor feedback encouraging.
items.quote: I'm pleased to report that ORBLICEF, our drug product for Enmetazobactam -Cefepime, was successfully launched in the Indian market during the last week of September.

items.statement: New oral block fully ready for production; ramp-up depends on sales generation and customer vendor approval process.
items.quote: So the block is fully up and ready for the production, but it will depend on how we are able to generate sales. So there's nothing to do with respect to the manufacturing part. We will keep on increasing production as we can generate sales.

items.statement: Last FDA inspection was July 2019; expecting next inspection anytime; facility ready.
items.quote: So last FDA infection was in July 2019. We are expecting them anytime, and we are ready for them to come, although we don't have any information from them as yet when are they going to come.

items.statement: Ceftaroline seeking US partner; Cefovecin engineering batches planned soon.
items.quote: Yes. So we would be taking some engineering methods of our Cefovecin soon. Ceftaroline, we are still looking for a partner for the US market.

items.statement: Cefiderocol theoretical potential 100 million doses (1.6M of 5M AMR deaths treatable); treatment cost INR1M per patient; actual market conversion uncertain.
items.quote: With respect to the potential, what we believe is 100 million doses potential is there for this particular product as about 1.6 million people out of the 5 million people who died due to AMR in 2019 can be cured by Cefiderocol. So that's a very, very large number. What does it translate to value is questionable, as I stated before, because the cost of treatment is very high, currently standing at

items.statement: Phase IV study mandated by SEC for Enmetazobactam in India; clinical data sharing restricted until study completion.
items.quote: We've been asked by the SEC to do a Phase IV. I don't think we will be able to share data before those studies are complete as such. But I can share the clinical trial data, which is globally accepted, based on which we have received the Phase IV.

items.statement: R&D focus on fermentation-based development; 7ACA project expected to create platform for further fermentation molecules; few Indian companies have this capability.
items.quote: At the same time, I feel that by setting up the 7ACA projects, we would have gained a significant insight into the fermentation technology. And that will probably create a launch platform for us to develop further molecules because not too many companies in India have t he capabilities to develop products on fermentation

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY25 is Rs 450-500 Crores and at least 15-20% growth next year
items.quote: The revenue front -- the current financial year, we are expecting something between Rs 450 Crores to Rs 500 Crores. In the next year, we expect at least an increase of another 15% -- 15%, 20%.

items.statement: Current order book stands at Rs 827 Crores, 3x FY24 revenue, with defense at Rs 727 Crores (88%)
items.quote: Our current order book stands at Rs 827 Crores forming 3x of FY 2024 revenue. During the quarter, some of the old orders have been executed and this will enable the company to bid and secure larger and more significant orders from the Ministry of Defense, the Indian defense industry and international defense entities.

items.statement: Order book expected to be maintained between Rs 800-900 Crores for coming 2 years
items.quote: Yes, between Rs 800 Crores to Rs 900 Crores, it will be there.

items.statement: Operating margin 18% in Q2 FY25 and 18.1% in H1 FY25, down from 28% and 27.4% YoY
items.quote: Our operating profit for Q2 FY25 stands at Rs 16.6 Crores as compared to Rs 21.9 Crores in Q2 FY24. The operating margin for the quarter stands at 18%.

items.statement: Full-year margins expected to remain at same percentages as product mix stays similar
items.quote: Same percentages will continue because the product mix will remain same unless there is a -- there will be a shift in quarter-to-quarter. But if you take the full year, the product mix almost will remain same. So we can expect the same percentage of that.

items.statement: Rs 5 Crores provision made for liquidated damages on chaffs and flares order
items.quote: The LD value for the quarter is not yet accounted exactly. Like I mentioned to you, the LD itself is, whether we'll be paying or not paying, is there. So we have made a provision of Rs 5 Crores towards that.

items.statement: Construction started on new RDX/HMX plant at Katepally, trial production expected by end of FY25
items.quote: the construction of the new larger plant for RDX and HMX at Katepally has started and we expect installation and direction of the project to be completed in the first quarter of next financial year.

items.statement: Odisha defense explosives plant got in-principle approval, land finalization by end of month
items.quote: company has received the letter from the Industrial Promotion & Investment Corporation of Odisha Limited, IPICOL, informing the state -level single- window clearance authority through an in -principal approval for setting up defense explosives, raw materials and ammunition plant in 3 phases at Rayagada district

items.statement: Enhanced RDX/HMX capacity expected to contribute at least Rs 100 Crores per annum
items.quote: Yes, with the enhanced capacity and all those at least Rs 100 Crores per annum should be the contribution from this.

items.statement: Expecting orders from BrahMos, Pralay, NGRAM, MRSAM and continuous RFPs for chaffs/flares
items.quote: When it comes to rocket motors and propellants, the new missiles which are being added, BrahMos, we are expecting a good order from BrahMos, we are expecting from other projects, with Pralay and NGRAM, MRSAM and all those.

items.statement: Nipun mines order execution ongoing, further orders expected from MoD
items.quote: And in addition to that, the mines also we started, that is Nipun mines, where the first order we are executing and then we are expecting a further requirement of inflow of new orders to MoD.

items.statement: Export orders constitute around 25% of current order book
items.quote: Yes. around 25% of the current orders are export. That is what we are exporting to.

items.statement: Flares 100% indigenous, chaffs payloads 50% imported due to capacity constraints
items.quote: Flares 100% we are producing within the country and in -house, and chaffs we are procuring the payloads from OEMs ; foreign OEMs.

items.statement: Chaffs and flares emergency order at old prices reducing margins, future orders at negotiated prices
items.quote: The margins will be reduced compared to the previous supplies because this has an emergency procurement order. There was no chance for any increase. We had to accept the -- at the old prices, that is the old prices we have accepted.

items.statement: Chaffs and flares order execution ~Rs 150 Crores delivered in H1, targeting Rs 200 Crores by end November
items.quote: Approximately Rs150 Crores has been executed in the first two quarters. That is deliveries are made. And we have a stock which is being offered in the month of November for inspection. And including that, we should be doing Rs 200 Crores by the end of November.

items.statement: Chaffs and flares order completion expected by July 2025
items.quote: I think the deliveries we are expecting to complete by July of 2025.

items.statement: Defense Acquisition Council approvals expected to benefit company, especially ammunition for guns
items.quote: See, there are so many products in the list and all those. So yes, some of them definitely we are going to get benefited out of that. One area is the ammunition for the guns.

items.statement: Currently only qualified supplier for chaffs/flares, but Economic Industries and others may enter
items.quote: As on date, we are the only supplier. Other participants may come, because we are hearing from the market that economic industries also have developed.

items.statement: Imported components for chaffs payloads causing delays, now met by domestic production
items.quote: logistics have affected some of the imported components and payloads coming. So there were delays in that. So we have accounted -- provided for the delays and the late delivery charges.

items.statement: Singareni order value lower due to reverse tendering and lower Coal India prices
items.quote: Prices also have gone down, the supply prices because these commercial explosives business, it is on the reverse tendering process. So yes, the prices -- current prices are lower based on the Coal India prices.

items.statement: R&D expenditure around 1-2% of revenue, conducted at plant/pilot scale
items.quote: But around the -- between 1% - 2% goes towards R&D expenditure, which appears in the R&D expenditure. the plant level operations and developments which we involve, they go in the normal production expenses.

items.statement: Hoping for LD waiver on chaffs/flares order based on force majeure, revised schedules accepted
items.quote: we are quite hopeful that the LDs will be waived off or they'll be reduced.

items.statement: Collaborating with drone/UAV startups for explosive delivery systems, not making full drones
items.quote: We are working together with the drones and UAV electronic manufacturing people, the people who make the birds and the start-ups. See the Army and our defense forces need delivery of the explosives through UAVs and then drones. So this part is ours.

items.statement: Urban demand under pressure; rural demand recovering gradually; organized trade outperforming with e-commerce and modern trade momentum
items.quote: While urban demand has been under pressure, the rural demand continues its gradual recovery. The organized trade continues to outperform expectations with both e-commerce and Modern trade channels experiencing sustained upward momentum.

items.statement: Sequential rise in commodity prices for key imports increased costs; managed via operational efficiencies, strategic sourcing, and calibrated price increases
items.quote: On the input cost side, the sequential rise in commodity prices for certain key imports led to increased costs. This was actively managed through operational efficiencies and strategic sourcing as well as calibrated price increases.

items.statement: Consolidated net sales grew 12.1% YoY with 8.4% volume growth
items.quote: As a result, the company registered consolidated net sales growth of 12.1% year-on-year basis, of which 8.4% is due to strong volume growth.

items.statement: Personal Care segment grew 26% YoY
items.quote: The Personal Care segment registered strong consumer demand driving a double-digit growth of 26% for the quarter and continuing its upward trajectory over the last few quarters.

items.statement: Food & Nutrition segment grew 9.7% YoY
items.quote: At the same time, Food & Nutrition segment also posted a growth of 9.7% for the quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 261 bps YoY due to operating efficiencies and portfolio strengthening
items.quote: Amidst the headwind of rising commodity prices, the gross margin has remained resilient, showing its upward move of 261 basis points on a year-on-year basis, which outlines operating efficiencies and strengthening of product portfolio to absorb input prices inflation.

items.statement: Net sales INR 4,907 million; EBITDA INR 196 million (+16.7% YoY); Net PAT INR 209 million (+254.2% YoY); Adjusted PAT +154.2% YoY
items.quote: Our net sales grew by 12.1% to INR 4,907 million. EBITDA grew by 16.7% year-on-year to INR 196 million. Net profit after tax grew by 254.2% to INR 209 million, adjusted PAT grew by 154.2% on a year-on-year basis after eliminating exceptional items from current quarter.

items.statement: Complan added 9 lakh households YoY; category +2.8% MAT; Complan share 4.1% MAT
items.quote: Complan has added 9 lakh households over last year as per MAT August 24 reports of Kantar Panel. The category has grown by 2.8% at MAT level. Complan market share stood at 4.1% at MAT level.

items.statement: Medium-to-long term HFD category growth expected at 5-6%; company aims to grow faster if initiatives play out
items.quote: At an overall level, our view is over a medium to long term, 5% to 6% growth is a fair for this category, which is close to a billion as we understand. But our view is that we can grow much faster than that if all the initiatives play out.

items.statement: Launched Complan VieMax (adult nutrition) at INR 900/400g; focused on top states via HCP route; no advertising planned; revenue targets modest initially
items.quote: INR900 for 1 jar of 400 grams, which is in sync with a similar high-quality products that adult nutrition has. We will focus in the top states, which are on adult nutrition and Complan, which is largely around East, South and part of North where we will use the HCP route, healthcare professionals route to promote our products. We are not planning to launch any advertising. That's a broad play that

items.statement: International business targeting doubling every 3 years; Sugar Free D'lite accepted across geographies (Middle East, Hong Kong, Singapore); Complan traction in Nigeria; focus on local populations beyond diaspora
items.quote: We are looking at doubling every 3 years kind of growth and we are looking at being -- doing innovations, which are relevant to each of the focus markets. On Bangladesh, which we are building, we believe the local population will be relevant. So being local, focused around those specific markets, especially around 2 lead brands, the sweeteners and nutrition, but also within tactically other brands

items.statement: PAT margin expanded from 1.3% to 4.2% YoY; EBITDA margin expansion muted due to higher ad spend and consultant fees; gross margin still has room to expand over next 1-2 quarters
items.quote: So in terms of PAT expansion we have actually last year we were at 1.3%. Now we are at 4.2%. So there is a margin expansion. So there is an impact of the exceptional item. But if we take that out, still there is a margin expansion that has happened. Secondly, margin expansion is more than the expected because of the high investment that we made in the advertisement and some other expenses, includi

items.statement: Gross margin expansion levers remain for next 1-2 quarters; longer term visibility limited
items.quote: So one year is a little hard to predict at this stage. But in, I would say, next 1 or 2 quarters, we still believe there is room for us to keep pushing it, and that's really what we are working here.

items.statement: Palm oil price surge a concern for Nutralite and food service; harder to pass on in price-sensitive segment
items.quote: And the other impact I'm a little worried about for future is the palm oil substantial increase because for Nutralite and food service becomes harder to pass on. It may give us growth, but it just becomes that much harder to deal with the market because it's quite price sensitive.

items.statement: Nutralite fat spread business efficient; management confident of competing with Amul; will reassess if effort exceeds value
items.quote: built some of the segments or categories that it existing, so namely the fat spread. It's an extremely efficient business. It has -- it needs a certain kind of management because the consumer or the customers involved are price sensitive. But I think we have demonstrated that we have made the so-called big elephants to dance for what actions we have taken in the past. So I think we know reasonably

items.statement: Naturell acquisition: top 10 cities contribute 70-80% of sales; 80-90% via traditional trade and e-commerce (quick commerce); Zydus to deploy focused distribution, not just broad infrastructure
items.quote: So from a geographical mix, where top cities contribute top 10 cities will be, I guess, 70%, 80% of the business. So it's a very high top urban-centric brand. They are largely traditional trade and e-commerce focused. These 2 contribute to about 80%, 90% of the business substantially, e-commerce and that too specifically quick-commerce and traditional trade in these markets. For us, the leverage i

items.statement: Naturell portfolio includes bars, chips, cookies, granola bars; sufficient SKUs to grow; 1-2 new products possible but focus on availability
items.quote: So they already have -- they already have bars, which is the mainstay, they've launched chips. They also have cookies, protein cookies, so protein chips, protein cookies that itself and granula bars. So they already have enough on the portfolio. We can launch 1 or 2 more products, but I think enough to grow on this and some of the products in the pipeline which we are working with them and figure

items.statement: Naturell EBITDA positive at small scale (INR 119 cr); disciplined operations; Zydus aims to drive growth and achieve EPS accretion by next financial year
items.quote: From a business scale point of view, like we mentioned, it has done about INR119 crores in the last financial year as per the Ind AS. It has got a small EBITDA positive, which for a scale of this size, I think is a great thing because most of the companies we have evaluated at this level typically tend to be substantially negative, and that's what we really liked about this that the current owners

items.statement: Naturell growth target: high double digits; Zydus track record even better; aim to sustain for next couple of years
items.quote: We are hopeful to do more than that. We have a track record is even better than that. So we intend to in the next couple of years, at least say on that.

items.statement: Personal Care 26% growth sustained over 6 quarters; no one-off; broad-based across brands
items.quote: If you look at last 6 quarters since we've been reporting segment wise Food and Nutrition and Personal Care separately, you will see that consistently over 6 quarters that we have reported, we are showing a good double-digit growth. It's not an exception, but more of a trend for us, and both our brands have consistently demonstrated that.

items.statement: Urban slowdown real and challenging across staples and discretionary; Zydus overcoming better due to rural momentum in Sugar Free, Complan, Glucon-D, Nycil
items.quote: Yes. So I think the reality is it's quite challenging in urban. And if you look at multiple segments, not just beyond us, both staples and discretionary, you'll find that everyone is struggling. So we believe it's real. It's just that we've been able to overcome this better. We've been lucky around that.

items.statement: Rural momentum driven by execution of product architecture suited to specific markets; no specific numeric expansion projects
items.quote: Not really. It's just that we've been executing. We've had a set of products, which we have focused on rural, we have a product architecture, which caters to specific markets. But just -- I think the team has executed better, and we're getting better traction on those.

items.statement: Volume growth 8% well-rounded across rural, e-commerce, modern trade, and traditional trade (traditional trade better than urban market)
items.quote: So we've seen very good growth, both from rural and e-commerce and modern trade. But traditional trade is also not like been -- has done better than urban trade, traditional trade has also done reasonably well versus the market. So I would find that our growth is -- for especially the last quarter has been well rounded.

items.statement: Food & Nutrition growth driven by sweeteners, nutrition, Nutralite; Glucon-D slightly pressured by heavy rains
items.quote: So we had a very good traction, both with the sweeteners and nutrition spaces last quarter, even Nutralite has had us a reasonable growth, Glucon-D is small and was a little bit under pressure because of the heavy rains, but otherwise, it's been rounded off growth.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY25 revenue growth target of 14% to 17% with operating leverage and projected mid-teen revenue growth in coming years
items.quote: We reaffirm our FY '25 revenue growth target of 14% to 17%, with operating leverage and project mid-teen revenue growth in the coming years with decent operating leverage.

items.statement: Guided content & broadcasting expenses to reach 18% of revenue for full financial year
items.quote: Sequentially, content & broadcasting expenses as a share of revenue fell to 19.4% in Q2 from 20.6% in Q1 and we expect this to reach 18% of revenue for full financial year.

items.statement: Maintained gross margin at 63.5% in Q2 FY25 supported by strategic pricing and favourable product mix
items.quote: Consistent with our guidance, we maintained strong gross margins at 63.5%, supported by strategic pricing and favourable product mix.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined to 8.7% in Q2 FY25 from 9.5% YoY due to planned investments in digital marketing and airtime costs
items.quote: EBITDA margins came in at 8.7% of revenue compared to 9.5% for the same period last year.

items.statement: No major capex foreseen in coming times; balance sheet to continue getting lighter
items.quote: And we don't foresee much capex in coming times. So, balance sheet will continue to be lighter than we had in the past few years.

items.statement: TV networks now reach 130 million households; unique customer base grew 51% YoY to 682,000
items.quote: Our TV networks now reach 130 million households and our unique customer base has increased by 51% year-over-year approximately to 6,82,000.

items.statement: US revenue declined 1.6% YoY in Q2 due to election and Olympics; expect demand pickup in holiday season
items.quote: The US revenue declined 1.6% year-over-year in the September quarter affected by increased attention on the election activities and Olympics. With consumer confidence improving and the elections now behind us, we expect demand to pick up in the upcoming holiday season.

items.statement: UK revenue grew 15% YoY; expect recovery in consumer demand with improving consumer confidence, lower inflation and interest rates
items.quote: In the UK, revenue grew by 15% year-over-year, majorly contributed by Ideal World. With signs of improvement in UK economy like the consumer confidence index inching up, inflation and interest rates going down, we expect a recovery in consumer demand in the coming months.

items.statement: Germany revenue grew 15.3% YoY; Q-on-Q revenue grew 25% while operating losses declined 41%; confident of operating breakeven by H2 FY25
items.quote: Germany continues to perform well, recording 15.3% Y-o-Y revenue growth in Q2 FY '25. Q-on-Q revenue grew by 25%, while operating losses declined substantially by 41%. We are confident of achieving breakeven at the operating level by second half of FY '25.

items.statement: Ideal World achieved GBP17 million sales in first year; expect full cost profitability from Q3 FY25 onwards
items.quote: Ideal World operates 24/7, reaching 27 million UK households. We recently upgraded our Sky broadcast to HD network. The business is currently profitable on a direct cost basis, achieving GBP17 million in sales over the past one year. We expect Ideal World to reach full cost profitability from current quarter onwards, Q3 onwards.

items.statement: Mindful Souls achieved 10% PBT margin on trailing 12-month basis with over 100,000 unique customers
items.quote: Mindful Souls continue to perform well with PBT margin of 10% on a trailing 12-month basis. Mindful Souls now has a solid base of over 1,00,000 unique customers, which we aim to grow further.

items.statement: Digital marketing spend ramped up based on ROAS productivity; one-year customer lifetime margin exceeds acquisition cost across all six brands
items.quote: We started ramping up digital advertising about a year ago and where you see the content broadcasting costs go up noticeably because of that. And we are seeing benefit of that in terms of new customer acquisition. And that customer lifetime time value is -- one year lifetime value of that customer is higher than the customer acquisition cost for us at all the six brands that we have within VGL por

items.statement: Inventory days increased to 86 from 72 due to festive season build-up; expect normalization after December and March clearances; cash conversion cycle maintained around 170 days
items.quote: we expect the after season, that is at the end of December as well as end of March, the inventory comes down because we run two clearances. We run December clearance and we run March clearance and inventory strategically comes down. So, from the base point of view, you should look at the last year's days as a guidance for your future position. Nitin Panwad: Yes. And even if you refer the cash conv

items.statement: Balance sheet remains strong with net cash positive position of INR100 crores
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains strong with net cash positive position of INR100 crores.

items.statement: Board declared second interim dividend of INR1.5 per share for Q2 FY25 representing 89% payout
items.quote: The Board of Directors has declared an interim dividend of INR1.5 per share for the quarter, representing 89% of payou t and implying a firm belief in our business model and strong growth prospects

items.statement: Sunil Agrawal spends majority of time on team development, meeting direct reports, skip levels and external stakeholders
items.quote: So, initial years, I spent quite a bit of time in product development and strategy. But last many years, a majority of my time goes in team development. So, I meet the team regularly- direct reportee and my skip levels and from outside stakeholders as well.

items.statement: US market share grew to ~4% from <2% few years ago; current run rate ~$3.5 revenue per household vs competitors at $7 and leader at $60
items.quote: Yes. So, we have gained market share over last many quarters, maybe last four, five years, we continue to gain market share. So, our current run rate is around $3.5 or around 3. Our current market share is about 4% compared to Qurate and Shop HQ that we calculate internally, and that grew from less than 2% a few years ago.

items.statement: No adverse impact expected from potential Trump tariffs; believe lowest cost producer status and 62%+ gross margins provide advantage if tariffs applied across board
items.quote: We believe that we are the lowest cost producer and the tariffs would impact equally everybody. So, we don't foresee us getting impacted any adverse. In fact, with our gross margin of 62% plus our cost will be lower than other competitors because their gross margins are lower. So, it will be a t advantage if at all the tariff across the board comes into picture.

items.statement: Budget Pay bad debt rate ~1% of cost to sales; H1 FY25 bad debt INR13.55 crores vs INR15.52 crores H1 FY24 across US, UK, Germany
items.quote: So, I see in my financials for H1 FY '24 the bad debt was $1.65 million for H1 FY '24. So, the velocity of the bad debt is approximately $3 million a year -- sorry it was $2 million in H1 FY '24. It was INR15.52 crores of H1 FY '24. And for H1 FY '25, it was INR13.55 crores for H1 bad debt.

items.statement: Digital revenue grew 11.8% YoY to INR294 crores, contributing 39% of total B2C sales; Budget Pay contributed 38% of B2C revenue
items.quote: Q2, TV revenue reached INR456 crores, while digital revenue totalling INR294 crores. TV revenue grew by 12.3% year-over-year. And digital revenue increased by 11.8% year-over-year with digital contributing 39% of total B2C sales. This growth reflects our continued investment in digital marketing and related infrastructure. Additionally, our budget pay EMI option contributed 38% of total B2C revenu

items.statement: No acquisition plans currently; focus on scaling Mindful Souls and achieving meaningful positive EBITDA from Ideal World first
items.quote: So, not anything on the horizon. Our aim is to get Mindful Soul starting scaling up and Ideal World, giving us meaningful positive EBITDA before we go for a new one.

items.statement: Generated 1.1 million kWh solar energy in Q2 meeting ~100% power needs for two manufacturing units; target carbon neutrality for Scope 1&2 by 2031
items.quote: On sustainability front, we generated 1.1 million kilowatt hours of solar energy this quarter, meeting nearly 100% of power needs for two of our manufacturing units in India. This aligns with our goal to achieve carbon neutrality for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emission by 2031.

items.statement: Reached 93 million meals served under 'Your Purchase Feeds' initiative; currently donating 54,000 meals daily; long-term goal 1 million meals daily by FY40
items.quote: We recently reached a milestone of 93 million meals being served to school children under our 'Your Purchase Feeds...' initiative. We are currently donating 54,000 meals every school day. Our long-term goal is to reach 1 million meals every school day by FY '40.

items.statement: Express gross margin improved 305 bps YoY to 26.4% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Corresponding gross margin has improved by over 305 bps and stands at 26.4% for Q2 FY '25 as compared to 23.3% for the quarter ended September 2023.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 4% in Q2 FY25 vs 3% in Q2 FY24
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Q2 FY '25 stood at 4% as against 3% duri ng Q2 FY '24

items.statement: Targeting 30% gross margin in a couple of quarters based on business mix
items.quote: I would say directionally, we have always been that as a benchmark. Not in next quarter, but I think a couple of quarters, we should be achieving that 30% be nchmark gross margin based on the mix and composition of businesses which we have put in place

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 5.3% vs 4.4% in H1 FY24; plan to maintain and build up 1% more
items.quote: So last year, if you see 4.4% was the EBITDA margin half yearly. I'm talking of half yearly numbers, we were at that level, which are now at 5.3%. So the last run rate for the month, if you take it 5.3% for the current half year, it gives us good confidence that to -- and the plan is to maintain this level for this year, quarter-on-quarter, built up by 1% more from here on.

items.statement: Strong traction in automotive, pharmaceuticals and consumer durables verticals
items.quote: Some strong traction we saw in some verticals, which you wanted to know is in automotive, in pharmaceuticals and in consumer durables. These are some of the sectors that we saw some -- very strong traction.

items.statement: General price increase announced from 1st January; retail new price cards from 20th October and 1st December; key accounts accepting single-digit hikes
items.quote: We've already rolled out the price increase to certain customer sets. And some of our larger customers have taken a price increase of single digit, which will, of course, apply in the coming few months. Retail business, we have already introduced new price cards, in fact, from as early as 20th of October. So we kind of preponed that, And on the 1st of December, we also go out for the retail busine

items.statement: Price hike expected to flow into yield from Q4 FY25 and contribute positively to EBITDA
items.quote: So as Ketan mentioned, the price hike would be a single-digit factor of our entire yield. It will actually flow in from next Q4, which will be Jan onwards. And we are positive about it to have a positive contribution on our EBITDA.

items.statement: Hub modernization budget INR 27-30 crores over 2 years; roughly INR 10-15 crores per year on opex model
items.quote: But if you see on the number front, on the QIB also, we had taken, for hub modernization, budget allocation of INR27 crores to INR30 crores over a period of 2 years. So if we spread that evenly, we should be spendin g roughly INR10 crores to INR15 crores in a year from here on, on hub modernization, which will include both existing and new hubs facility enhancement

items.statement: Phase 2 hub upgrades at 13 locations to be completed in next 1 year; includes Ahmedabad, Hyderabad, Lucknow, Ranchi, Dadri, Guwahati, Jaipur, Patna
items.quote: We have finalized locations, which we want to upgrade in the second phase. These locations will play a vital role in further strengthening our operations. These locations should come up in the next 1 year.

items.statement: Farukhnagar hub already showing visible operational efficiency results
items.quote: So the development of hubs are -- would add a lot of operational efficiency as we see the one which is there on the Farukhnagar has already -- the results are visible.

items.statement: Customer loyalty ratio improved to 1.38 in Q2 FY25 from 0.82 in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Any ratio above 1 is considered good. Today, we are at 1.38 percentage points ratio compared to 0.82 during Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Client mix for Q2 FY25: key accounts 68%, SME 14%, retail 18%
items.quote: Client mix for the quarter ended September 2024, for key accounts, SME and retail stood at 68%, 14% and 18%, respectively.

items.statement: Company is debt-free as of September 2024 with positive cash position of INR 170 crores
items.quote: I'd like to highlight that the company is debt-free as of September '24, with a positive cash position of INR170 crores.

items.statement: Express tonnage handled: 317,000 MT in Q2 FY25 vs 333,000 MT in Q2 FY24 and 300,000 MT in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The total tonnage handled for Q2 FY '25 stood at 3,17,000 metric tons as compared to 3,33,000 metric tons for Q2 FY '24. And correspondingly 3 lakh metric tons for Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Service level at upward of blended 90% across all parameters in September 2024
items.quote: For September 2024, our service level was an upward of blended 90% across all parameters, which are industry leading.

items.statement: Volume growth target: 10-12% above industry growth rate; if industry grows 12%, company targets ~13% absolute growth
items.quote: So if the industry grows at 12%, let's say, that's the study or report we would -- we are -- we have set ourselves to grow 10% more than the industry benchmark. So that's what I can say on the volume front. And it could be around the -- in the absolute term numbers, it would be -- from the market, it would be around 13%, if you see on a totality basis.

items.statement: Corporate restructuring amalgamation expected to complete by end of FY25
items.quote: So let's say, even if you take out a date of, let's say, it ta kes -- the process could take 3 to 4 months. By this end of financial year, positively, we'll be done with this entire amalgamation exercise, which is planned so

items.statement: Market share maintained over last 2-3 quarters; swing from unorganized to organized sector due to e-way bill and GST regulations
items.quote: So we've recently come out of various syndicated research data. And you also must be aware that we have recently also come out of a QIP. So when we kind of looked at the market through that lens of independent data analysis, we're seeing a lot of swing that's happening from the unorganized sector to the organized sector. And that is essentially happening because of a lot of strong regulation that

items.statement: ECL provision of INR 4 crores was in Q1 FY25, not Q2 FY25
items.quote: It was in last quarter, not in this quarter.

items.statement: Line-haul cost impact due to focus on long-haul carriers; reverse load inefficiency from production concentration in particular regions
items.quote: That's the main reason because the focus on long-haul carriers has led to some cost impact, which actually going ahead, if you see, we see growth in that part of our business in next quarter. So we are not that much worried on this account as we see for this quarter, it looks to be a very temporary impact.

items.statement: Cost optimization through data science algorithms on OD pairs, truck types, touch points, load flow repatterning; outsourced delivery model via Gati Associate being revisited
items.quote: So all those algorithms are kind of allowing us to chip away a few, say, cost from the line haul. On the last mile, we have outsourced delivery model through the Gati Associate. That model, we are revisiting and I have already kind of put in a framework, which will further bring down costs.

items.statement: Phil (Pirojshaw Sarkari) announced superannuation; thanked for his service
items.quote: Thanks to Pirojshaw Sarkari, who we all know as Phil, Phil has announced his superannuation. We at Allcargo Gati would like to thank him.

items.statement: Gross margin blip in Q2 due to temporary line-haul cost inefficiency; mitigated in October volumes
items.quote: Yes, yes. We have -- we are -- I think it's a learning process, and we have mitigated that in the current month to a large extent.

items.statement: GESCPL EBIT grew 18% YoY to INR 39 crores in H1 FY25
items.quote: GESCPL has reported an EBIT of INR39 crores during H1 FY '25, representing a growth of 18% as compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Technology: GATE (Gati Associate Tracking Engine) first module launched; further modules being implemented for better visibility, utilization and cost rationalization
items.quote: We launched the first module of our new technology Gati Associate Tracking Engine, GATE. We are in the process of implementing further modules, which will help in better visibility of operations, better utilization percentages and cost rationalization.

items.statement: Capex for FY25 expected around ₹1,000 crore additional, total ~₹1,600 crore including Kakinada
items.quote: I would say including Kakinada and everything put together, another ₹1,000 crores is what we are assuming.

items.statement: Unit-III Greenfield (200-acre) phase-wise production start December 2024, full phase-I utilization in 6-7 months
items.quote: With phase-wise production activity expected to begin in December 2024, this facility will provide us with added capacity needed to support our growth and further extend our production capabilities.

items.statement: Operating multiple 500-litre reactors for Solid Phase Peptide Synthesis, expanding SPPS facilities further
items.quote: We have established infrastructure dedicated to Solid Phase Peptide Synthesis (SPPS) and currently operating multiple 500-litre reactors. With the demand continuing to rise, we are now expanding our Solid Phase Peptide Synthesis facilities further.

items.statement: Custom synthesis RFPs and onsite visits from existing and potential customers steadily rising
items.quote: The number of RFPs and onsite visits from our existing customers and potential customers has been steadily rising.

items.statement: Contrast media volumes expected to grow 20-30% year-on-year under long-term contracts
items.quote: I would say about year-on-year, we would have a 20% to 30% increase in volume would be a fair statement.

items.statement: Material consumption stable at ~41% of sales revenue for H1 FY25, down from rising trend last year
items.quote: Material consumption remains at about 41% of the sales revenue for the first half of the current financial year.

items.statement: Generic pricing pressure across the board (Naproxen, Gabapentin, Carbidopa, Levodopa), volumes growing double-digit but sales impacted
items.quote: we are seeing pricing pressure across the board. It's not related to one segment or one therapy. We are seeing an overall pricing pressure and though volume wise, we have not lost any Divi’s volume. We have seen a volume-based growth on these products

items.statement: Raw material prices stable past six months, but cautious due to Middle East and crude oil sensitivity
items.quote: On procurement front, we have observed stability in raw material prices over the past six months. While the stability has been favorable, we are approaching it with caution as the market remain sensitive to developments in the Middle East and fluctuations in crude oil prices.

items.statement: H1 FY25 product mix: Generics 49%, Custom Synthesis 51%
items.quote: Product mix for generics to custom synthesis for the half year is 49% and 51% respectively.

items.statement: Future generic pipeline robust, products advancing to customer qualifications and regulatory approvals in US/Europe, revenue contribution from 2026 onwards
items.quote: We anticipate these products to start contributing to our revenues from 2026 onwards.

items.statement: Contrast media: Iodine-based products partly commercialized with long-term contracts, Gadolinium compounds in qualification, commercialization in 1-2 years
items.quote: On the contrast media, on the Iodine-based products, few of the molecules we are in qualification stages, and few of them we have already commercialized with our customers where we have even long-term contracts with them.

items.statement: USFDA inspection at Unit-II Visakhapatnam successfully concluded in Q2
items.quote: In Q2, we have successfully concluded a USFDA inspection at our Unit-II facility in Visakhapatnam.

items.statement: Exports 87% of total sales revenue H1 FY25; Europe + US combined 71%
items.quote: Exports for the half year is about 87% of the total sales revenue. Exports to Europe and United States combined are about 71% of the total sales revenue.

items.statement: Advancing shipments by 3-4 weeks, maintaining extended safety stock, diversifying supply base to mitigate Red Sea logistics disruption (transit 45→70 days)
items.quote: To mitigate the risks related to inventory management, we have adopted a proactive approach, by advancing shipments by three to four weeks, maintaining extended safety stock levels and diversifying our supply base, wherever feasible.

items.statement: Cash on books ₹3,602 crore as of Sep 30, 2024; receivables ₹2,181 crore; inventories ₹3,145 crore
items.quote: As of 30th September 2024, we have cash on book of ₹ 3,602 crores, receivables of ₹2,181 crores and inventories of ₹3,145 crores.

items.statement: Constant currency growth 21% for H1 FY25
items.quote: Our constant currency growth for the half year has been at 21%.

items.statement: Nutraceutical business ₹406 crore for H1 FY25
items.quote: Our Nutraceutical business amounted to ₹406 crores for this half year.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis extending transit times to ~70 days and raising logistics costs; mitigated by advance shipment planning
items.quote: continued disruptions in red sea have impacted global shipping lanes, with increased attack on commercial vessels prompting the routing of shipments via South Africa. This change has extended our transit times from around 45 days to approximately 70 days and raised associated logistics costs.

items.statement: Generic pricing pressure expected to stabilize in next 6-12 months
items.quote: It is very hard to answer that particular question, but that is the hope that in the next six months to a year, we should see at least some stability with respect to the pricing pressure.

items.statement: Continuous flow chemistry successfully applied in labs and pilot scale, commercial scale production in next 1-2 years
items.quote: Divi's is set to expand its use into commercial scale production in the next one to two years.

items.statement: Peptide fragments (SPPS and LPPS) for GLP-1s supplied to several innovators across Phase II, III and commercialized projects
items.quote: We are working with customers who have projects already commercialized, we are working with customers who are in phase-III, phase-II. So, we have a pipeline which is working right now.

items.statement: Market share gains in both large and small generic APIs despite pricing pressure
items.quote: I would say not just the larger molecules, but also the smaller molecules, all put together. I would say that this half year for the generic business, we have seen a good volume-based growth and it is 49% for the similar reason that in spite of having pricing pressures, we were able to sustain the generic business to that particular percentage.

items.statement: Other expenses flat/slightly down YoY due to green chemistry, efficiency improvements, backward integration
items.quote: What you have seen is mainly because we implemented a lot of green chemistry and we have improvised a lot on the efficiency front and also the backward integration that we went into.

items.statement: Reiterated FY25 revenue growth guidance of 15%+ with stable EBITDA margins at current levels; agri segment growth 10-15%
items.quote: Going forward, we would like to reiterate our earlier guidance of 15% -plus growth in cranes, material handling and construction equ ipment segments for the current year and expect agri segment to g row 10% to 15% during the year.

items.statement: Management expects FY25 revenue growth could reach up to 20% but guiding conservatively at 15%+ due to election and monsoon headwinds
items.quote: We are very hopeful of doing 15% -plus. And there is an easy chance it can reach up to 20%. But to be on the conservative side, we are saying 15%-plus.

items.statement: Expecting largest ever single defense order of INR400-420 crores from Ministry of Defense within November, executable over 3 years but targeting FY26-27
items.quote: Further, we are on track to receive our largest ever single order valued at over INR400 crores from the Ministry of Defense.

items.statement: Defense segment revenue contribution expected to exceed 5% in FY26 and FY27, aligning with medium-term goal of 5-10% share
items.quote: This milestone will drive Defense segment's revenue contribution beyond 5% for the years FY '26 and '27, aligning with our medium to long-term goal of achieving 5% to 10% share of overall revenue from the defense sector.

items.statement: Revenue capacity to increase from INR4,500 crores to over INR5,100 crores by Q4 FY25 through ongoing expansion; further INR600 crores possible with nominal capex
items.quote: The company currently has a revenue capacity of around INR4,500 crores, which is set to increase by an additional INR600 crores through the ongoing capacity expansion, bringing the total to over INR5,100 crores by quarter 4 of current financial year.

items.statement: Additional 82 acres land acquired (21 acres registered, 61 acres possession by Q4) plus 48 acres applied for in another state for future growth beyond INR6,500 crores capacity
items.quote: We have already done agreements for about 82 acres of land. These are 2 different chunks. One is about, I think, 21 acres, other is about 61 acres. So the 21 acres has already been registered in the company's name and we have possession of that land. The balance 61 acres chunk, hopefully, we should be in a position to bring it on to the books of the company and take physical possession in quarter

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin expanded 268 bps YoY to 18.04%; PBT margin 16%, PAT margin 11.97%; H1 FY25 EBITDA margin 17.94% (highest ever)
items.quote: The operational revenues grew by 12.2% on a year -on-year basis to INR754.34 crores with an EBITDA margin of 18.04%.
