items.statement: Margin expansion driven equally by favorable product mix (higher tonnage cranes, NX-series) and commodity benefit (lower steel prices); steel prices strengthening post-Diwali
items.quote: Yes. First part of your question regarding -- definitely, there is an angle of product mix, which has added to our EBITDA margins in the last quarter. And going forward, this product mix benefit will be there because higher tonnages crane, even in the pick-and-carry segment, within this segment, are gaining more traction.

items.statement: Management to decide in next 2-3 quarters whether to pass operating leverage benefits to customers via price cuts or maintain margins
items.quote: But then I think as a company, we have to make a choice whether to remain competitive or cost effective in the market or continue to keep on increasing prices. So that call we will be taking over the next, I would say, 2, 3 quarters that maybe we will -- whatever is the operating leverage benefit, we start passing it out to our customers and not increase our prices further.

items.statement: Price increase of 5-6% for BS IV to BS V engines and 11-15% (avg 12%) for BS III to BS V engines effective 1st January 2025; 60% of machines affected by higher increase
items.quote: The machines which are going from BS IV to BS V, there'll be a cost impact of 5% to 6%. So from 1st January onwards, like I'll just repeat again, engines going fro m BS III to BS V, there will be a cost impact of around 12%, average. Machines going from BS IV to BS V from 1st January onwards, there will be 5% to 6% increase.

items.statement: Pre-buying started post-Diwali ahead of Jan 1 price hike; expecting 15-20% additional sales from pre-buying; 55% of annual revenue typically comes in H2
items.quote: So we are hopeful that we can expect a 15%, 20% additional sales on this account; balance, time will tell. Man pro poses, God disposes. We are ready with our inventory. We are ready with our planning.

items.statement: Higher tonnage cranes (20T+) and multi-activity NX-series cranes (patented) driving product mix improvement; NX-series adoption accelerating after COVID hesitation
items.quote: No. Again, see it is a mix. It is not only the higher tonnage crane, but some of our NX -series Cranes, which we had introduced 3, 4 years back. But obviously, they were priced a little higher. They were multi-activity cranes. And after corona around the time, people were a little hesitant in adopting technology at a higher cost, which has started happening now.

items.statement: Targeting market share increase of 1-1.5% in pick-and-carry cranes (currently 62-64%, targeting 70%) and tower cranes in FY25; backhoe loader share ~2-2.5%
items.quote: And we are very hopeful to grow our market share in the current year by at least 1%, 1.5%, if not more. And going forward, we target to reach even Cranes segment up to 70% market share with pick -and-carry, and I'm sure we'll do it.

items.statement: Kato Works 50-50 JV for bigger cranes (crawler, truck, rough terrain) definitive agreements by early Q4 FY25, production start within 6-8 months, revenue in FY26, full steam FY27
items.quote: So definitive agreements are being negotiated currently, and we are hopeful that by early quarter 4, all this process would be finished. And we would be setting up a joint venture, maybe within quarter 4 itself or early next financial year in quarter 1 FY '26. And we intend to start producing machines within 6 to 8 months of that.

items.statement: Overseas acquisition put on hold due to better opportunity emerging; may announce in Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26; separate from Kato JV
items.quote: So as of now, that acquisition outside India has been put on hold, and we are working on even a better opportunity. So hopefully, if everything goes well, maybe in quarter 4 or quarter 1 next year, we might be able to announce this -- even a better opportunity, like I said.

items.statement: CFO/EBITDA ratio low at 8% in H1 due to preponed MSME vendor payments (creditors reduced 5-7 days); expected to normalize by March 2025
items.quote: Basically -- typically, the liability is basically the payments to MSME vendors. So we have been preponing our payments to MSME vendor, which has reduced the liabilities which is part of the current liabilities. Going forward, we expect that probably by the year -end probably the numbers will be as similar to what we did for March '24.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR610 crores (INR785 crores investments vs INR140 crores debt); short-term borrowings increased temporarily for MSME payments and land advances, to be repaid by March 2025

items.statement: Additional ₹80 crore capex needed to complete Bangalore hotel (₹60 crore capex + ₹20 crore other)
items.quote: About 80 crores is what we are estimating; about ₹ 60 crores of CAPEX and ₹ 20 crores more of additional expenditures of different nature , operator fees and stuff like that.

items.statement: 70-80% of Bangalore completion capex to be spent in FY25, balance in early FY26
items.quote: So, in this current fiscal, we would spend roughly anticipating and I don't want to give too much of a detail onto it, but between 70% to 80% of this will be done in this fiscal and the balance flowing in into the early part of next year.

items.statement: Bangalore hotel adds 220 rooms initially; site has potential for 300 additional rooms
items.quote: We have completed the acquisition of a 220 - room luxury hotel in Bangalore. It is built on 6.5 acres of freehold land and the development has a potential of adding 300 a dditional rooms to supplement the extraordinarily large banqueting facility

items.statement: Grand Hyatt Mumbai refurbishment complete: 420 of 547 rooms fully refurbished, suites in phased manner
items.quote: So, we have 547 rooms and 120 apartments, all of them have been refurbished. And in terms of the rooms out of the 547 rooms, 420 -odd rooms are fully refurbished, the suites will also be done in a phased manner going forward.

items.statement: Grand Showroom at Grand Hyatt Mumbai completed adding 49,000 sq ft MICE space
items.quote: As you are aware, we have recently completed the Grand Showroom at Grand Hyatt Mumbai, adding 49,000 square feet of additional MICE facility at Grand Hyatt, Mumbai.

items.statement: Strong demand tailwinds continue; ARR growth outperforming city and compset across all major markets
items.quote: I see a continued and robust increase in demand leading to greater ARR across all properties, especially Mumbai and Delhi.

items.statement: Grand Hyatt Mumbai ARR grew 10% vs city 8% and compset 6%; Andaz ARR grew 16% vs city 4% and compset -1%; Lucknow ARR grew 12% vs compset 5%
items.quote: At Grand Hyatt, we have grown ARR at 10%, which is above 8% which city has seen and 6% vis-à-vis the compset. Andaz ARR has grown 16% vis-à-vis 4% of the city and (-1%) of the compset and same with Lucknow where we saw 12% ARR growth against the compset growth of 5%.

items.statement: Foreign tourist arrivals in Mumbai at ~20% vs pre-COVID 40%; Delhi Andaz at ~50% vs pre-COVID 42%; expect Mumbai to reach ~35% in H2
items.quote: In the Mumbai market foreign traveler has not come back to the pre -pandemic level, which was starting at 39% to 40%. At present we are at half about 20%. But if I was to give you an example, what has happened in Delhi, in Delhi, pre -pandemic, we were sitting at 42% in our Andaz hotel were foreign travelers, now we are sitting closer to 50%.

items.statement: H1 FY25 adjusted EBITDA margin 37.1% (excl. one-time items); expect margin expansion in H2 towards 40%+ sustainable
items.quote: As I said, in the first half adjusted for the one -time we are at 37% EBITDA margin and we anticipate th e second half to have a margin expansion

items.statement: Target sustainable 40%+ EBITDA margin on blended basis
items.quote: We strongly believe that Juniper can achieve , on a sustainable basis, 40%+ EBITDA margin, and we should see that trajectory coming along.

items.statement: Grand Showroom expected to generate ~₹50 crore annual revenue; strong business on books for Q3/Q4 high season
items.quote: So, we expect this new banqueting space to generate approximately ₹ 50 crores of revenue on an annual basis. These are for high-end events, this is not your typical banquet where you accommodate 1,000 people at slightly lower rates, this would be a market leader in terms of average pricing and we have very strong demand in terms of business on books.

items.statement: Grand Hyatt Mumbai Q3/Q4 occupancy expected upwards of 80% with ARR ₹13,000-15,000; business on books solid
items.quote: With the full inventory back, we are expecting occupancies upwards of 80% and rates which are competitive in the market. As far as I can recall, Tarun, you can confirm. I think the rates are 13,000 to 15,000 range and given that that this is high season, I think the traction will be even stronger and business on books is solid.

items.statement: Heat, light and power costs flat despite revenue growth; green power expansion to improve further
items.quote: On the heat, light and power, which is another major contributor of cost, it has remained flat despite the growth in revenue. So, that's a big positive contributor. And as we increase our green power across assets going forward, this will only become much more better.

items.statement: Employee cost run rate tracking ₹40 crore per quarter; no material increase expected
items.quote: But what is more important is that we are tracking the 40 crores per quarter run rate that we had actually mentioned last time that we don't believe that the employee cost is going to increase materially from there on and we are well on track of that run rate.

items.statement: Net bank debt-to-EBITDA at 1.5-1.55x after Bangalore acquisition; significant headroom for growth capital
items.quote: But despite taking on that ₹ 280 crores debt, we are at around 1.5 to 1.55x net bank debt-to-prospective EBITDA, which leaves a significant headroom for us to get growth capital.

items.statement: Target not to breach 2.5x net bank debt-to-EBITDA on sustainable basis for expansion
items.quote: But on a sustainable basis, our target is not to breach 2.5 net bank debt-to-EBITDA. So, I just want to add, in the past we have shared is that the mechanics in which these assets would come in at least from a ROFO standpoint would be done in a non-cash share swap transaction.

items.statement: No immediate fundraise planned; well funded post-IPO (₹1,800 crore) with strong operating cash flows and debt headroom
items.quote: We are well funded right now. We have just come out of an IPO, raised ₹ 1,800 crores. We do have significant operating cash flows being generated right now. And as I said, our net bank debt-to-EBITDA is only 1.5x. So, we do have significant headroom to take on more capital if required to fund growth. So, we don't foresee any immediate fundraise to fund our growth.

items.statement: Target to add 1,000 keys in next year including 220 Bangalore; ~500 from ROFO assets (Saraf group listed cos); ~250 from new acquisitions
items.quote: Our management and Company and the development team of Juniper has set a target of 1,000 additional keys over the next one year's period . We have now brought in 220 rooms out of Bangalore and the remaining actually there is a certain amount of these keys are already sitting into the Saraf assets which are outside Juniper, and they are also listed companies. So, I am not at any liberty to give you

items.statement: Working on Kaziranga asset leased by Assam government; details expected next quarter
items.quote: I would like to share that we are working on an asset in Kaziranga which is being leased by the Assam government and that is going to come into our fold and once we have much more clear visibility, I think by this quarter, I will be very happy to share the full details of that project in the coming quarter.

items.statement: Grand Hyatt Mumbai expansion of 293 rooms + 24 service apartments approved by BMC; start targeted FY27, 18-month build
items.quote: Our target to start that was in Financial Year '26-27. We are not at this point in rush moment to start that project because we feel that the market is so strong and the demand is so strong, so we do not want to at this moment disturb the Grand Hyatt Mumbai's revenue potential. So, this is something that we are sitting on it and this is in the future. '26-27 would be the start and would be taking

items.statement: No new luxury/upper-upscale supply in Mumbai suburban BKC-airport zone for 30-36 months; only Fairmont recently opened
items.quote: I think if you look at Mumbai micro market that we are operating in, the supply that has come into the market was the new hotel that is just now opened, the Fairmont at the international terminal next to JW Sahar. Besides this, in our luxury segment, ther e is no other additional capacity being added over the next 30 months to 36

items.statement: H1 FY25 like-for-like revenue growth 10% YoY; adjusted EBITDA growth 15% YoY
items.quote: As I was saying earlier in the call, if you look at the first half the revenues would have grown 10% YoY and the EBITDA adjusted for the one-time cost has grown 15% YoY like-to-like.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue up 32% YoY (14% like-for-like); EBITDA up 21% YoY; PBT ₹20 crore vs loss ₹27 crore YoY
items.quote: This quarter has been a very healthy quarter with a revenue growth of 32% year-on-year despite having 25% of the Grand Hyatt Mumbai room inventory under renovation. We have achieved the EBITDA of ₹ 73 crores which is 21% YoY growth. We achieved the PBT of ₹ 20 crores in the quarter compared to a loss of ₹ 27 crores over comparable period last year.

items.statement: Cash balance ₹247 crore; strong net free cash flow generation; ₹64 crore used post-Sept for Bangalore plus ₹280 crore debt
items.quote: On the balance sheet side, we had a cash balance of ₹ 247 crores. We are generating very strong net-free cash flows, and we have utilized ₹ 64 crores of cash post the September 30th to acquire Bengaluru in addition to ₹ 280 crores of debt that we have onboarded.

items.statement: One-time tax charge of ₹49 crore in H1 FY25 from Finance Bill 2024 capital gains amendments; remeasured deferred tax liabilities
items.quote: And as Mr. Saraf was saying that there is a charge that we have taken which is notional of 49 crores in the first half, which basically reflects the amendments that were made in the Finance Bill 2024 relating to the capital gains. JHL has remeasured its deferred tax liabilities on items which were subject to capital gains, and this is a cumulat ive one-time charge that has been taken on

items.statement: Bangalore hotel ramp-up expected fast: operational in 9 months, healthy occupancy/ARR within 3-6 months post opening
items.quote: So, for our Bangalore asset, we expect it to be operational in about nine months. Post that, the ramp up would actually be quite fast according to us. The market is already there and we would assume that within the next three to six months we would be able to actually achieve a good healthy occupancy and ARR.

items.statement: Expects better growth in Q3 and Q4 FY25 vs H1 due to Dadri ramp-up and consolidation of Balaji and Bansal High Carbon
items.quote: So, we are expecting a little better growth as compared to the first 2 quarters in the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: Targets 80% EBITDA growth in FY25 driven by full consolidation of BSPL, Balaji, Bansal High Carbon and Dadri ramp-up to 6 lakh tons
items.quote: Therefore, all of these three factors combined, we are looking at a good growth.

items.statement: Strong demand across automotive, construction and general engineering drove highest ever quarterly revenue in Q2 FY25
items.quote: In the 2nd Quarter of FY'25 also, we have achieved our highest ever quarterly revenue driven by strong demand across all our key segments like automotive, construction and general engineering.

items.statement: Two-wheeler industry growth and market share gains driving automotive demand
items.quote: Other than that, the two-wheeler industry has been doing well. Therefore, we see a good growth, in which the growth has also come from acquiring market share.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin expanded 192 bps YoY and net profit margin expanded 183 bps YoY
items.quote: We are happy to report that EBITDA and net profit margins for Quarter 2 has expanded by 192 basis points and 183 basis points on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin up 224 bps and net profit margin up 127 bps YoY
items.quote: For the first half too, our margins have risen by 224 basis points for EBITDA and 127 basis points for the net profit.

items.statement: High carbon EBITDA ~Rs 10/kg; mild steel Rs 4-7/kg; stainless steel Rs 7-8/kg
items.quote: Sir, in general, we look at high carbon to be about Rs. 10 per kg EBITDA business. Mild steel and stainless-steel to range between Rs. 4-7 per kg EBITDA.

items.statement: Specialty wire (steel cord, lead wire) to improve margin mix from Q4 FY25
items.quote: So, as and when we are able to ramp up the Speciality Wire vertical, our mix of margin will completely change.

items.statement: Consolidation of Balaji and Bansal High Carbon volumes to be 100% in Bansal Wire from Q3 FY25
items.quote: Therefore, in Quarter 3, we are looking at almost all volumes and revenue from Balaji and Bansal High Carbon to come into Bansal Wire.

items.statement: Dadri capex Rs 500-550 crore; funded partly from internal accruals
items.quote: Sir, the total CAPEX that we are doing in Dadri was about Rs. 500-550 crores.

items.statement: Dadri facility 3.5 lakh tons; at ~20% utilization end Q2; targeting 100% capacity operational by end FY25
items.quote: Sir, Dadri as a whole is 3.5 lakh tons, out of which till about last month of last quarter, we were already at close to 20% capacity utilization and we are looking at bringing this whole capacity or at least being able to operationalize this whole capacity within this financial year.

items.statement: Total capacity to reach 6 lakh tons by end FY25 from 2.5 lakh tons at start
items.quote: So, the starting of this year we started with 2.5 lakh tons and we will end with 6 lakh tons.

items.statement: Bead wire 30,000 tons annual capacity to be operationalized this month
items.quote: Bead wire we are adding about 30,000 tons annual capacity which will be completely operationalized within this month.

items.statement: Steel prices fell ~10% in Q2 FY25 boosting margins despite flat revenue
items.quote: From a very basic number, if you see, our volume has grown by about 10% whereas our revenue is flat. So, there is definitely a difference of at least 10% that has come there.

items.statement: Raw materials sourced domestically; natural hedge via simultaneous order booking and raw material procurement
items.quote: So, sir, we have what we would like to call a kind of a natural hedge in our business model. Because whatever orders or whatever raw material we buy, we also book orders with that simultaneously.

items.statement: Specialty wire vertical (steel cord, lead wire, hose wire) to start production in Q4 FY25; steel cord approvals take 1-1.5 years
items.quote: From the last quarter of this year, we should be seeing some production and some sales happening there and for the future also, we are depending on this segment very aggressively and we want to grow with this product, steel cord.

items.statement: Over 5,000 customers; diversified across sectors; B2C model in Gujarat for agriculture wires
items.quote: Our commitment to quality and customization has helped us build a diverse and loyal customer base of over 5,000 customers.

items.statement: Exports ~10% of revenue in H1 FY25; geopolitical issues slowed growth but momentum improving
items.quote: During the first half, export accounted for about 10% of our total revenue.

items.statement: Vendor financing and bill discounting limits tied up; will be utilized from Q3 FY25 as consolidated revenues increase
items.quote: we have already tied up some limits for discounting and other various tools. We are only waiting for the revenue, which will come in the third quarter of this year to increase from Balaji 7 and Bansal High Carbon, and then we will start utilizing those limits as well

items.statement: Debt-equity ratio 0.21x as of September 30, 2024
items.quote: As on September 30, 2024, we had a comfortable debt-equity ratio at 0.21 times.

items.statement: 100% acquisition of Bansal Steel and Power completed; Balaji and Bansal High Carbon consolidation ~100% by end Q2
items.quote: In the last quarter, we have done 100% acquisition of Bansal Steel and Power and by the end of last quarter itself, we have done almost 100% consolidation of Bansal High Carbon and Balaji.

items.statement: Formed subsidiary Bansal BWI Steels for stainless steel rod backward integration; land parcels identified in Rajasthan and Ahmedabad; targeting finalization Nov-Dec 2024
items.quote: So, sir, in the last quarter, we have formed a new subsidiary, a volume subsidiary for this particular project that is Bansal BWI Steels and we are actively looking for land parcels in the area of Rajasthan as well as Ahmedabad.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 volume 80,000 tons (high carbon 30,000, mild steel 27,000, stainless 21,000-22,000)
items.quote: On the volume front, we did about 80,000 tons this quarter, in which high carbon was about 30,000 tons, low carbon was 27,000 tons and stainless-steel was around 21,000 tons.

items.statement: H1 FY25 volume 1.56 lakh tons including ~8,000 tons from Dadri
items.quote: Sir, even in the first quarter, we had a little bit of volume coming from Dadri, which was 2,000 tons. In this quarter also, we had about 6-7,000 tons coming from Dadri.

items.statement: Steel cord approvals take 1-1.5 years; hose wire approvals faster (1 month or less)
items.quote: After that, we will start inviting customers for the approval process, which will take another one, one and a half years to get us an approval in steel cord. But the by-product of steel cord, which is hose wire, is what we will start off with in the last quarter of this year.

items.statement: Management expects H2 FY25 demand trends to be largely similar to H1, with potential upside if API prices improve and industry volumes pick up.
items.quote: Looking ahead we expect demand trends in the second half to be largely similar to the first half. There could be some upside potential if we see some improvement in API prices and uptake in industry volumes, but that remains to be seen.

items.statement: Management expects API prices to average or normalize in Q3 or Q4 FY25, which would positively impact revenue.
items.quote: An update on to it is while we saw the API prices softening in Q3, most of the intermediates of the KSM have started showing some solidification. So, either in Q3 or Q4, I expect the API prices will at least average or normalize.

items.statement: Management does not expect API business to turn EBITDA positive in Q4 FY25; timeline shifted by 6 months with review starting April.
items.quote: I don't think that in the Q4 this will turn around, or it would not be EBITDA positive. I think we will have to give it 6 months from here and we will revisit our business plans starting April.

items.statement: CDMO volume declined roughly 11% in Q2 FY25; management attributes this to industry cycle and advance ordering patterns.
items.quote: Yes, we did not experience the volume growth. We had a volume decline of roughly 11% this quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin was 12.9% in Q2 FY25 vs 15.8% a year ago; CDMO margin 15.4%, branded/generic 10.3%, API margin negative Rs 14 crore.
items.quote: All these impacted our adjusted EBITDA margin which is down to 12.9% versus 15.8% in the prior year.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 42.3% in Q2 FY25 from 40.6% a year ago.
items.quote: Gross margins on consolidated basis in Q2 were at 42.3% similar to Q1, but higher than Q2 last year which was 40.6%.

items.statement: Received 10 DCGI and 86 FSSAI approvals in H1 FY25; total export dossiers filed at 367 with 350 in pipeline.
items.quote: We received 10 DCGI and 86 FSSAI approvals in H1 of the current fiscal.

items.statement: Spent Rs 150 crore on capex in H1 FY25; new injectable facility at Haridwar started commercial production in Q2.
items.quote: In H1 we spent around Rs. 150 crore in CAPEX. In Q2 we started commercial production at our new injectable facility in Haridwar.

items.statement: Falling API prices (Amoxicillin, Cephalosporins, Paracetamol, Telmisartan) caused revenue deflation in cost-plus CDMO model and delayed customer inventory build-up.
items.quote: Prices of several key API's including Amoxicillin, Cephalosporins, Paracetamol, Telmisartan etc., continues to fall. As you are aware, our CDMO business is a cost-plus model, so when input costs fall, we experience revenue deflation as well.

items.statement: CDMO revenue share 79% in Q2; branded/generic 16%; API 5%. Branded portfolio reshaping driving higher profitability in branded/generic segment.
items.quote: If we were to break the segment-wise revenue, CDMO remains our driving force with almost 79% of the revenue share in Q2, followed by branded and generic with a 16% and API business adding to 5% of the revenue.

items.statement: Caters to over 1,500 clients including 26 of top 30 Indian pharma companies; long-standing relationships with Indian and MNC pharma.
items.quote: Our company caters to over 1,500 clients both Indian and MNC Pharma companies with whom we have long-standing relations. Today 26 out of top 30 Pharma companies in India are our partners.

items.statement: Cash flow from operations H1 FY25 was Rs 71 crore positive; free cash flow post investments was negative Rs 65 crore; net cash surplus Rs 341 crore including IPO proceeds.
items.quote: Cash flow from operations for H1 September 24 was Rs. 71 crore positive and the free cash flow post investment activities was Rs. (-) 65 crore. The company's long-term rating sort of improved, we got AA Stable from ICRA on long-term basis and the short-term rating continues to be A1+ as in that is from our side.

items.statement: Long-term rating upgraded to AA Stable by ICRA; short-term rating A1+ maintained.
items.quote: The company's long-term rating sort of improved, we got AA Stable from ICRA on long-term basis and the short-term rating continues to be A1+ as in that is from our side.

items.statement: Government MSME compliance deadline 8th January; uncertainty on enforcement; management supports compliance but sees no immediate commercial impact.
items.quote: See in the Indian scenario although the date is till 8 th January, but the government has not confirmed yet how it will behave, so our wish is each and every company of our country should follow the system which is under Indian law and grow

items.statement: Continued API price volatility and muted industry volumes pose risk to revenue and margins; API business EBITDA loss may persist beyond Q4 FY25.
items.quote: Muted demand resulting in lower volume growth. Prices of several key API's including Amoxicillin, Cephalosporins, Paracetamol, Telmisartan etc., continues to fall. As you are aware, our CDMO business is a cost-plus model, so when input costs fall, we experience revenue deflation as well.

items.statement: Ethanol production target for ethanol year Nov 2024-Oct 2025 is around 25 crore litres from cane and maize plus 3 crore litres ENA
items.quote: For the ethanol year, which has begun from 1st of November and will run up to 31st October, we are expecting on the basis of current cane availability estimate around 25-odd crore liter, including the maize, we would be in a position to do. In addition to this, it is around 3 crore liter on account of ENA.

items.statement: PLA project commissioning targeted for October 2026
items.quote: And this plant is on track for commissioning in October 2026. Vivek Saraogi: Yes, October 2026

items.statement: PLA plant expected to reach full capacity utilization within 6 months of commercial production
items.quote: We feel that the goods will be sold the day you start your commercial production. So, capacity utilization sales, our best guess today is 6 months.

items.statement: UP Government announced 50% capex subsidy over seven years, 5% interest subvention, and SGST net reimbursement for PLA project
items.quote: The UP Government has announced a policy for bioplastics for this project, which is a 50% capex subsidy over seven years, a 5% interest subvention, and then SGST net reimbursement.

items.statement: Central Government Cabinet approved Bio E3 policy to promote biomanufacturing including biopolymers
items.quote: In August of 2024 the Central Government Cabinet approved a policy called the Bio E3 policy. The policy is meant to give impetus to biomanufacturing, including biopolymers, in which our project also falls.

items.statement: Net sugar production estimated at 28.3 million tonnes for upcoming season after 3.7 million tonnes diversion; domestic consumption forecast at 29 million tonnes
items.quote: Gross production forecasted for the upcoming season is in the range of 32 million tonnes in our mind, ISMA's view is 33 million tonnes. After accounting for diversion of 3.7 million tonnes, the net sugar production is expected to be 28.3 million tonnes as compared to 32 million tonnes last year.

items.statement: Industry estimates scope for nearly 2 million tonnes sugar exports given current inventory and production estimates
items.quote: So, even if the Government is looking at a 60 lakhs tonnes inventory, there is scope of almost 2 million tonnes exports, which can be announced.

items.statement: Sugar prices at Rs 38.5/kg considered low after Rs 20/quintal cane price increase; industry seeks MSP revision, ethanol price revision, and export permission
items.quote: So, first of all, Rs. 38.50 per kg is not a price after Rs. 20 per quintal increase in cane price. The pricing should be a little higher to our mind.

items.statement: Government lifted all restrictions on sugar diversion for ethanol production; ethanol price revision expected soon
items.quote: Following a brief policy shift in the previous year, that is the election year, the Government has lifted all restrictions on sugar diversion for ethanol production. The industry is also awaiting the announcement of revision of ethanol prices which is expected in the coming days.

items.statement: Received full juice allocation and ~6 crore litres B-Heavy molasses allocation for Q1 of ethanol year
items.value: full juice allocation, ~6 crore litres B-Heavy
items.quote: Entire juice we have received. Vivek Saraogi: B-Heavy we have received almost 6-odd crore liter

items.statement: Distillation capacity can handle 11.5-12 crore quintals cane; current cane availability ~10 crore quintals
items.value: 11.5-12 crore quintals capacity, ~10 crore quintals current
items.quote: Our existing distillation capacity can handle cane of around. 11.5 crore to 12 crore quintal of cane. Currently we are in the region of around 10 crore quintal of cane.

items.statement: No further capex planned for co-generation; current capacity 175 MW
items.quote: So, we have no further capex expansion program in this segment.

items.statement: Power export realization to UP grid at Rs 3.46/unit; average annual realization including open access at Rs 5.82/unit
items.quote: Power which we are exporting to grid, the Uttar Pradesh grid, we are getting realization of around Rs. 3.46 per unit. Plus, open access, so average realization should be on an annual basis Rs. 5.82 per unit.

items.statement: Board announced interim dividend of Rs 3 per share
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that the Board of Directors has announced an interim dividend of Rs. 3 per share.

items.statement: UP Government made electricity free for irrigation in March 2024, benefiting farmers in East UP where company has eight factories
items.quote: The benefits it was very heartening to see that the farmers were able to irrigate without having to think of cost, especially our East UP farmers, where we have eight of our factories.

items.statement: Ethanol production mix for ethanol year: ~9 crore litres from juice, 10-11 crore litres from B-Heavy, 1-1.5 crore litres from C-Heavy, rest from maize
items.value: ~9 crore litres juice, 10-11 crore litres B-Heavy, 1-1.5 crore litres C-Heavy, rest maize
items.quote: Within this 25 crore liter, maybe around 9 crore liter on account of juice and around 10-11 crore liter on B-Heavy, may be 1 -1.5 crore liter C-Heavy and the rest is maize.

items.statement: Cane yield uncertainty due to late planting in 2-3 factories and dependence on winter rains; new varieties still acclimatizing
items.quote: Due to some late planting in 2-3 factories, we might have slightly lower cane availability due to yields having a month less to grow. But having said that, there is a tailwind on the fact that the diversion should be much lower than last year.

items.statement: Sugar Control Act draft has zero impact per management; Government already had powers under Essential Commodities Act
items.quote: So, first of all, the Government always has all powers under the act regarding essential commodities. So, there was just zero impact of that in my mind on anything at all.

items.statement: Management asserts Balrampur's distillation capacity is properly sized for 320-day utilization; competitor's higher ethanol output attributed to lower asset sweating
items.quote: We build our capacity on 320 days capacity utilization. Hence that is the ratio for 320. So, if you want to sweat your assets less that is your options.

items.statement: India ethanol blending reached ~15% in 2024, on track for 20% by 2025; current bid for 18%
items.quote: Ethanol production from cane has played a pivotal role in supporting the Government's blending target. This diversion remains essential as India has reached ~15% in 2024 and is on track to meet 20% by 2025. Right now, the bid is for 18%.

items.statement: UP sugar production expected stable at ~10.8 million tonnes; Maharashtra and Karnataka may see a dip
items.quote: Regionally, UP is expected to remain stable at a production of about 10.8 million tonnes, similar to last year's level. Maharashtra and Karnataka, however, may see a bit of a dip.

items.statement: PLA project subsidies (capital and interest) payable after commercial production commencement; land portion accrues earlier
items.quote: So, you are saying, and I am clarifying that to the best of our understanding anything which is payable will be payable after commercial production except the land portion of the subsidy. It will accrue.

items.statement: PLA offtake depends on enforcement of existing single-use plastic ban; 19 items already banned but enforcement is grey
items.quote: I think the only lacuna here is that the single use plastic ban needs to be enforced properly because though the regulation exists, the enforcement is sometimes grey this is what we want from the Government.

items.statement: Full marketing team already working on PLA product sales ahead of commissioning
items.quote: There is a full team working on marketing already. So, we would not go into more detail. One would hope to sell the day you produce and stabilize also very quickly.

items.statement: No raw sugar produced or sold; raw sugar cannot be sold to customers in India
items.quote: We have not produced any raw sugar. Vivek Saraogi: And by the way, raw sugar cannot be sold to the

items.statement: UP Government encouraging more cane diversion to sugar sector; no levy molasses requirement for Gur/Khandsari units yet
items.quote: The effect I am telling you and they are encouraging more diversion towards the sugar sector. So, the Government of UP is interested that sugar industry crushes more cane. And they are working indirectly towards it. On Gur and Khandsari molasses, there is no restriction till now.

items.statement: Next investor call will provide better visibility on cane crushing estimates after plant yield assessment in February
items.quote: Definitely, the next investor call for sure.

items.statement: Automotive replacement demand strong for 4W and 2W; auto OEM demand modest in Q2; Home UPS soft due to early/heavy rains; industrial UPS and solar trade steady; private/public capex keeps industrial infra order booking healthy; telecom tepi
items.quote: While the automotive replacement demand was strong for both 4 -wheeler and 2 -wheeler, the demand from auto OEMs was quite modest in quarter 2. On the Reserve Power segment, both industrial UPS and solar trade markets are seeing steady increase in business. Home UPS market was soft, because of early arrival of rains in many parts of the country , and the overall heavy rains during the quarter. Pri

items.quote: Write offs for Q2 and H1 were higher, primarily due to Suvidha loan book. We have written off all accounts 90 days past due. A total of 3.2 crores has been written off out of the cumulative disbursement of 15.84 crores in the Suvidha book. We do expect decent recovery from these write offs over the next 12 months, as we have demonstrated in the past.

items.statement: Historical NPA recovery: 91% of FY21 write-offs, 63% of FY22 write-offs recovered; 50-60% SARFAESI cases resolved within 6 months
items.quote: And in terms of our ability to resolve, as I told that whatever we have, whatever the cases which have become NPA or was written off in 2021 has been recovered to the extent of 91% and whatever the cases which were written off in 21-22 has been recovered 63% as on date. So, and in terms of SARFAESI is a very, very strong, I would say, legal tool with us, with arbitration, losing it, I would say th

items.statement: SME disbursements hit by severe weather, heat waves, heavy monsoons, flooding, election disturbances, and internal productivity issues in H1 FY25
items.quote: Lower disbursements were observed due to severe weather and heat wave conditions in Northern India, heavy monsoons and partial flooding in some Western markets. Apart from weather related changes which affected both disbursements and collections, there were some election related disturbances and internal productivity issues which also contributed to tepid AUM growth.

items.statement: Adapted to new RBI policy requiring fund credit to borrower account before booking disbursement; transition caused 1.5-2 month delay but reduces cancellations
items.quote: In our last quarters communication, we highlighted the latest change in RBI policy on booking disbursement, which requires fund to be credited to borrowers account before booking disbursement, while originally disbursements were booked on check issue date, the prevalent industry practice at that time. While this adjustment took longer than we originally anticipated, we believe it will yield long t

items.statement: Tightened credit policies and systems due to RBI concerns on unsecured lending; new LOS scheduled to go live in November
items.quote: In the light of the macro environment and RBIs concerned about unsecured lending, we have also tightened our credit policies and systems. A new LOS for lab is scheduled to go live in November, which we will also support this initiative.

items.statement: Suvidha unsecured pilot product completely written off and launch of pilot 2.0 put on hold due to regulatory caution and practical challenges
items.quote: Following our earlier communication, we have created a new platform based on learning from the first pilot launch. However, the given current industry scenario and regulatory caution or unsecured lending just temporarily put the launch of pilot 2.0 on hold. Also, given the feedback we have received from a team and the practical challenges associated with the product, we would like to re-launch it

items.statement: Co-lending/DA relationships: SBI (Rs 100 cr DA line), IOB, Tata Capital, DSCI, Kotak, HDFC Finserv, Rajasthan Global; prefer co-lending 2.0 (80:20) model
items.quote: The co-lending we have built a lot of relationship with the SME side with PSU belt, namely with IOB and Tata Capital. It is a DA, we have a line of DA from SME, from State Bank of India. And there was another DA, (Inaudible) 10:27. So we have already built four relationships, so either we are doing DA or co-lending, I would say, the same thing for as a lender, and on the wholesale side, we have bu

items.statement: Liquidity position strong at Rs 53.6 crore supplemented by Rs 100 crore DA line from SBI
items.quote: Our liquidity position remains strong at 53.6 crores, supplemented by 100 crores DA line from SBI.

items.statement: No major funding challenges seen in next 3-6 months; bond/ECB fundraising costlier than current credit lines
items.quote: As of now and still, we have a lot of other lenders which we still not onboarded and as a company, being a total secured book, we don't foresee a largely we have two challenge in the coming next three to six months in raising funds. But, definitely we have to look for other sources, but being a raising funds through bonds and other borrowings at this time will be more costlier than the lines of cr

items.statement: Industry stress in micro-SME (<10 lakh) due to over-leveraging from aggressive target-based lending; bottom 40-50% population not participating in GDP growth
items.quote: And that has been the primary reason, I would say, now with this consolidation and some kind of small stress, it is helpful for the industry, and consolidation will definitely happen. And we as a company are far better placed in terms of strong, I would say, capital adequacy and profitability, and our SME blessing in disguise you can say maybe only 30% to 31% of our total portfolio, and that too b

items.statement: 93% of collections digital via e-NACH; e-NACH activation mandatory before disbursement; 15-20 third-party integrations for KYC, credit, fraud checks
items.quote: 93% of our collections is digital only 7% of our total collection is happening in cash. Rachita Gupta: Yes, and all of our collections are happening via e-NACH platforms and e-NACH are in, we don't disperse an account till the time in e-NACH is not activated in today's date, and e-NACH gets activated on real time basis. So a lot of strict monitoring at our end is there in order to go about it

name: Shri Keshav Cements And Infra Ltd

items.statement: If cement prices stay at Rs 3,300, FY26 EBITDA estimated around 60-65 crore, ~50 crore lower than guidance
items.quote: So, 3,300, then you are talking about EBITDA level of around maybe just a rough calculation taking off around Rs. 700 out of your pricing would mean at 50% or 60% capacity, maybe the guidance will be around 60 crores.

items.statement: Cement demand sluggish in H1 FY25 due to elections and monsoon; 7-8% growth expected for FY25 driven by infrastructure spending and PMAY
items.quote: The top industry analysts and cement market leaders expect about 7% to 8% growth this financial year of FY '25. Considering the first two sluggish quarters on account of election and monsoon, the next quarters are expected to deliver significant cement demand due to stabilizing of Central government and try and focus to spend on infrastructure.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 12.44% vs ~32% in FY24 due to ~11% price drop; solar EBITDA stable at ~7 crore/quarter
items.quote: in Q2, we achieved a solar EBITDA of around 7 crores. However, cement gave a negative EBITDA because of a significant drop in the pricing

items.statement: H1 FY25 solar EBITDA ~14 crore, cement EBITDA negative, consolidated EBITDA 11.11 crore
items.quote: The solar EBITDA is around 14 crores, and the cement EBITDA is negative, which is why we have seen 11.11 crores.

items.statement: Net cement realization Q2 FY25 Rs 3,290 vs Rs 3,710 in Q2 FY24 (~11% drop); prices plateaued at ~Rs 3,300 since Sept
items.quote: So, in Q2 of FY '24, we have net cement realization of around Rs. 3,710, but right now it is Rs. 3,290. This is a net realization excluding everything, ex-plant, excluding, of course, taxes and any kind of logistics.

items.statement: Petcoke prices reduced slightly in Oct; other input costs rising with inflation
items.quote: Petco pricing have reduced little bit last month in October. Otherwise, in Q2, the Petco pricing will be pretty stable, but if we compared to previous years, of course it has come down not very significantly, maybe a little bit, but overall if you look at all the other raw materials, the increase in the cost of other things have grown up with the inflation.

items.statement: New 1 mtpa cement plant mechanically complete as of Oct 3; awaiting 110 kV power line (expected Dec/Jan) for commissioning
items.quote: As of October 3rd, we have completed the entire plant. In fact, technically, we have completed all the civil and mechanical work . So, this new plant will require a higher power connection which is right now we are on a 33 kilovolt line. We will need a 110 kilo volt line which is supposed to be supplied by the government infrastructure which is supposed to come up 2 to 3 kilometers from our plant.

items.statement: Full ramp-up of new capacity expected FY26; 60-70% utilization targeted in 1.5-2 years
items.quote: Yeah, we are hoping to start from Q4, but realistically, FY '26 will be full first year with the entire year dedicated to the new capacity.

items.statement: 3 MW solar plant commissioned at Bisarahalli, total solar capacity now ~40 MW
items.quote: One of the significant milestones this half year is the commission of an additional 3 Megawatts Shri Keshav Cements & solar plant at Bisarahalli in Karnataka, which brings our total solar capacity to around 40 Megawatt.

items.statement: Cement dispatches up 10-11% YoY in H1 FY25 despite weak market; Q2 volume ~52,000 tons vs 49,300 tons YoY
items.quote: If you look at half yearly, around 115,000 tons compared to 105,000 tons in the H1 of FY '24. Now, the biggest issue is that compared to H1 of FY '24 to H1 of FY '25, the price has reduced drastically by around 11 %-12%, even though dispatches increased by around 10%.

items.statement: Hired additional sales/marketing staff from Q2; expanding dealer network and engaging institutional buyers; quality clearances received for govt projects
items.quote: In fact, we have already hired additional sales and marketing people . In fact, we have begun to hire it from beginning of Q2 itself, which you can see the employee benefits and everything has taken uptick.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced from 235 crore to 223 crore by Sep; CAPEX debt repayment starts Oct 2025; older debts maturing in 6-7 months
items.quote: Which has reduced to around 223 crores as of September. And as such, first couple of years, we will continue to service the debt as per our repayment schedule. But once we have enough profits generating and cash generating, management will look forward to cutting down on debt and prepayment so that the debt burden will start coming down.

items.statement: Quarterly debt service ~6 crore; carry-forward tax depreciation ~90-95 crore implies MAT tax (15%) for 4-5 years
items.quote: Yes, we have the regular debt payment around I think month, quarterly debt payment is around 6 crores which we have continued to service it on time.

items.statement: Solar tariff reduced from Rs 6.36 to Rs 6.09/unit in Q2 FY25 due to Karnataka policy; expected to rise in Apr 2025
items.quote: So, in Q2 FY '24, we sold average selling price around Rs. 6.36. Now, it has come down to 6.09 because in Karnataka, the price of power has been reduced by 50 paise because of the sudden election promise.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded to IVR BBB- stable on 223 crore facilities
items.quote: In addition, we also secured a good credit rating upgrade from current to IVR BBB minus stable outlook on facilities operating a total of 223 crores.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization Q1 FY25 69%, Q2 57% (vs 62% and 54% YoY); 15-day shutdown needed for kiln hook-up
items.quote: So, for example, compared to H1 of early and compared to H1 of now, there is an increase. But I can give, in Q1 the capacity utilization was 69% and Q2 capacity utilization was 57%.

items.statement: Solar provides stable EBITDA (~7 crore/quarter) cushioning cement volatility; 95% solar power to be consumed internally at full cement capacity
items.quote: No, maybe around 95% . About 35 -36 Megawatt we will utilize. Still 4 to 5 megawatt will continue to remain spare.

items.statement: Large players cutting prices to Rs 300/bag in Goa (net ~Rs 2,800) vs SKCIL's lower freight advantage (Rs 800-850 vs Rs 1,900)
items.quote: So, they are selling cement almost at the naked cement price in the range of Rs. 2,800 to reach the Rs. 300 pricing per bag in a place like Goa, where we are getting much higher naked cement price because again we are closer to the Goa market . Our transportation cost is like around maybe Rs. 800 to Rs. 850 compared to theirs about Rs. 1,900.

items.statement: Company runs 100% on green solar power since 2018, reducing power cost >75%; BIS award for 3 years zero product failures
items.quote: Since 2018, the company has been meeting 100% of its energy requirements through renewable solar energy. The cement plants of SKCIL are likely the only ones in the country to run on 100% green pow er or at least we were the first company to do so, resulting in a significant reduction in the power cost, which is over 75%.

items.statement: H2 FY25 guidance: plywood 12%+ sales growth, EBITDA margin 12-14%; laminate 10%+ growth; MDF 40%+ value growth; Particle Board flat
items.quote: While we have revised our guidelines for H2 at 12% plus sales growth and EBITDA margins between 12% and 14%.

items.statement: MDF EBITDA margin guidance: 15%+ standalone, 10%+ consolidated for H2 FY25
items.quote: In MDF, we would say that margins for consol basis would be 10% plus. The sales growth numbers are on consol, but the EBITDA margins are on stand-alone because it is difficult for us to put EBITDA margins till those reali zations and that operating leverage comes in.

items.statement: MDF demand growing at 15-20% annually; plywood market share target 13-14% from current 8%+
items.quote: Again, we don't have any authenticated numbers, but I would say that MDF demand would be growing at anywhere between 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Plywood EBITDA margin 15% in Q2 FY25, guided 12-14% for H2 FY25 due to raw material cost uncertainty
items.quote: The plywood division reported an impressive year -on-year growth of 21.1% with EBITDA margins of 15%.

items.statement: Laminate EBITDA margin 7% in Q2 FY25 due to higher marketing spend; guided to recover in H2
items.quote: EBITDA margin reduced to 7%, mainly due to higher marketing spend in Q2.

items.statement: MDF South unit EBITDA positive by Q3 FY25; double-digit EBITDA by Q4 FY25; consolidated 10%+ H2 FY25
items.quote: We anticipate it to become EBITDA positive by Q3. While we foresee substantial growth, supply pressures in the MDF market will limit average realization, but we expect over 40% value growth with some margin improvement in EBITDA.

items.statement: Particle Board continuous process facility to start operations by end of FY25; capacity from 250 to 800 CBM/day
items.quote: We are establishing a continuous process facility to enhance quality and reduce costs slated to start operations by the end of this fiscal year.

items.statement: MDF South plant extension to complete in next 2 quarters; capacity to reach 24,000-24,500 CBM/month
items.quote: The extension will take another, say, 2 quarters. Post that, the capacity will increase further.

items.statement: Formaldehyde resin plant approved at Hoshiarpur for backward integration; phased implementation for 100% requirement
items.quote: So we are taking -- the capex is planned for 100%, but we are still deciding how much we will start off with.

items.statement: MDF South plant utilization at 55-60% currently; targeting 80%+ utilization in FY26
items.quote: AP, we will -- I would say we will comfortably be at 80% plus utilization for the whole of next year.

items.statement: Laminate Andhra plant targeting 50%+ utilization in H2 FY25; 2/3+ utilization in FY26
items.quote: We would be looking at clocking in 50% plus utilization towards the second half of the year.

items.statement: Particle Board new plant to start in Q4 FY25; existing 250 CBM/day to shut down; effective capacity 800 CBM/day
items.quote: So we'l l be looking at an effective capacity of 800 cubic meters per day for Particle Board

items.statement: Plywood 2% price increase implemented from August 1; further increases under consideration but deferred due to market conditions
items.quote: From 1st of August, we have taken 2% which we have implemented fully and further price rise is there in our mind, but we are yet to decide.

items.statement: Timber prices rising for MDF/Particle Board (3-4 year plantation cycle); plywood timber stable due to import capability (6-7 year cycle)
items.quote: The timber issue is not -- is likely to continue for 12 to 18 months, as you said. The new plantations that are hitting also, the demand is growing at a faster pace.

items.statement: Plywood margin improvement driven by favorable product mix and volume growth despite raw material cost pressure
items.quote: Despite experiencing cost pressures from rising raw material prices, the EBITDA margin in the plywood segment has improved due to a favorable product mix a nd increased volumes.

items.statement: Laminate: increased feet on street, new catalog launched, 3 new RDCs opened to regain market share lost in domestic and export
items.quote: Firstly, we have increased our feet on street substantially. We have added a much larger team, and that enables us to reach out to more customers, to more influencers, to more dealers.

items.statement: No new MDF capacity additions expected industry-wide due to corrected ROCEs; Particle Board capacity additions may substitute low-end imported MDF but not branded players
items.quote: Currently, we are not expecting any capacity additions, any further capacity additions, I mean. And now it is a question of demand catching up to supply, which will play out, say, over the course of next 12 months.

items.statement: BIS implementation likely by February 2025 for all products; industry taking steps to prevent further deferral
items.quote: February, BIS is likely to be implemented. And we, as an industry, are taking all the necessary steps to ensure that BIS implementation does not get deferred again.

items.statement: Laminate exports to grow faster than domestic due to Andhra export-oriented unit; MDF Andhra unit designed for domestic market
items.quote: Regarding laminates, going forward, we are going to see good traction in exports. So the growth rate in exports is likely to be higher than growth rate in domestic.

items.statement: Forex loss of INR1 crore standalone and INR13 crore consolidated in Q2 FY25; euro correction to show profit in current quarter
items.quote: On a stand -alone basis, it was INR1 crore approx. And on a consol basis, it was INR13 crores approx.

items.statement: Plywood market share increased from 4-4.5% to 8%+; target 13-14% market share
items.quote: With the launch of Semi and with progress in our Club Prime, today, we are at about 8% of the market or 8-plus percentage. Our actual target is to reach much, much higher and become – within in our minds and hearts, we feel that yes, now we are a successful, really good brand in the market. So anything below 13%, 14% is not digestible by us.

items.statement: Raw material timber shortage acute in South for 9+ months; North stabilizing sooner; prices rising for 12-18 months
items.quote: In South, I think the situation will continue for at least another 9 months.

items.statement: PVC board facility in Andhra Pradesh ramping up, expected to contribute nearly INR100 crores revenue over time
items.quote: Our PVC board facility in Andhra Pradesh is ramping up quickly, expected to contribute nearly INR100 crores in revenue over time.

items.statement: Radio industry faced mild slowdown in Q2 FY25 due to volume challenges across FMCG and auto sectors; FCT revenue flat at INR73 crores YoY.
items.quote: the radio industry faced a mild slowdown this quarter due to volume challenges that impacted our FCT revenues. Nevertheless, we retained our leadership position in FCT with revenue holding steady at INR73 crores compared to INR73.3 crores in Q2 of last year.

items.statement: Radio pricing remained stable in Q2 FY25; management expects stable or slight price change in Q3 FY25.
items.quote: Importantly, pricing remained stable this quarter, and we anticipate a recovery in volumes in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Non-FCT revenue grew 3.1% YoY to INR24.2 crores driven by IP events like Spell Bee and Mirchi Freshers; IP business grew 59% YoY.
items.quote: Our non -FCT segment showed a 3.1% year -on-year growth, generating revenue of INR24.2 crores. Despite limited industry events, we achieved this growth through our own successful IP events such as Spell Bee and Mirchi Freshers, which received a strong response.

items.statement: Radio volume declined 3.3% YoY in Q2 FY25; inventory utilization at 74% vs 77% last year.
items.quote: So, volume this quarter has declined, as I was talking about with the way the overall economy and all the industries have performed, we have seen a little bit of downward traction on the volume growth. So, it's about a mild 3.3% degrowth on the business on the volume side.

items.statement: Inventory utilization at 74% in Q2 FY25 compared to 77% in Q2 FY24.
items.quote: We are at about 74% against last year of 77%.

items.statement: Management expects radio volume recovery in upcoming quarters; festive season decent with 48 lakh weddings supporting year-end business; cautious on Q4 government spend.
items.quote: the festive season has been quite good. With the strong 48 lakh wedding s happening this year, we believe with the wedding s the year-end business should do well. That's what we're hearing from guidance.

items.statement: Gaana digital revenue INR15.4 crores in Q2 FY25 (21.4% of radio revenue); subscription price doubled from INR299 to INR599 effective 1 July 2024; upgrades and renewals stable.
items.quote: On the digital side, we discussed in our last earnings call, Gaana's annual subscription price was revised from INR299 to INR599, effective 1st July 2024. Despite this increase, Gaana has maintained a solid traction, contributing a robust digital revenue of INR15.4 crores this quarter.

items.statement: Gaana full-year revenue expected around INR60 crores; breakeven expected in 5-6 quarters as blended price moves to INR599.
items.quote: the way we are trending around, it should be around INR60-odd crores type of revenue on a yearly basis.

items.statement: EBITDA excluding digital at INR22.5 crores with 23.2% margin in Q2 FY25; overall EBITDA margin expected similar to last year depending on radio growth.
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter, excluding digital, came in at INR22.5 crores with a margin of 23.2%.

items.statement: Digital spending reduced to INR12.8 crores in Q2 FY25 from INR15 crores in Q1 FY25; further efficiencies expected.
items.quote: Digital spending reduced to INR12.8 crores in Q2 from INR15 crores in Q1 of this year, and we expect further efficiencies in the quarters ahead.

items.statement: Gaana paid subscriber market share estimated at 15-20%; industry shifting to subscription model with Wynk closure and Spotify/Saavn restrictions on free tier.
items.quote: Just to give you a ballpark on paid subscriber numbers, we will be around a market share of about 15% to 20% on the paid subscription basis.

items.statement: Government considered TRAI recommendation of 0.4% revenue share license fee for new auctions in 234 cities; existing stations await similar treatment; news and smartphone radio inclusion under review.
items.quote: if you have recently seen the announcement by government on new auctions coming up in 234 cities, where they have considered one of the TRAI recommendation s of decoupling the license fee from the onetime license fee to just 0.4% of revenue.

items.statement: Multimedia solutions degrowth led by one large client not repeating; overall industry muted advertising growth impacted segment.
items.quote: Largely, the degrowth, if you see has been led by one client, which we had last year, and it didn't come in this year. But having said that, the overall industry muted advertising growth has led to a degrowth of the multimedia solutions.

items.statement: Cautious on urban growth commentary and potential reduction in Q4 government ad spend compared to election year.
items.quote: we are worried with the commentary on the urban growth. Having said that, I think the wedding season should keep us in state for a growth in the radio business. Though we need to be cautious about heavy government spend, which happened in the last quarter leading to the election, if that could be a deterrent on the growth, it could be if the government spend doesn't come in on the same levels.

items.statement: International markets EBITDA positive contributing INR1.4 crores in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: Our international markets continue to be EBITDA positive, contributing INR1.4 crores this quarter.

items.statement: Cash reserve of INR391 crores as of 30 September 2024.
items.quote: As of 30th September 2024, our balance sheet remains strong with a cash reserve of INR391 crores.

items.statement: Radio market share maintained at 24%+ despite industry volume decline.
items.quote: we have held our market share very strongly. So , we continue to lead our market share at 24% upwards.

items.statement: Target INR1,000 crore paint revenue in 4 years with ~15% EBITDA margin
items.quote: In fact, we have made a road plan for next 4 years. And we are targeting to achieve the turnover of INR1,000 crores from the present level with a margin of around 15% EBITDA.

items.statement: Expect 15% volume growth in steel business for FY25
items.quote: We are expecting 15% growth in the FY '25 in terms of 1 year.

items.statement: Target 10-15% paint revenue growth this year to surpass INR350 crore
items.quote: We have achieved a turnover of INR350 crores in the state. And this year we are trying to surpass that and achieve 10%-15% growth.

items.statement: Franchisee steel volume target 34-35 lakh metric tons for FY25
items.quote: See franchise also, what you can see nearby 34 lakh metric ton, 35 lakh metric ton TMT bar and other steel products is our target for this year.

items.statement: Steel demand recovery in Q2 driven by construction despite flooding
items.quote: After a challenging Q1, we are pleased to report a recovery of revenue growth for Q2 primarily driven by increased construction activities, despite some regional flooding challenges.

items.statement: Paint demand impacted by Shradh shift, heavy monsoon, and new entrants in Q2
items.quote: For example, there has been flooding, this time it rained a lot. And the festive season has also shifted from Q2 to Q3. And the second is that the new entrants in the market also created pressure which has been a factor in the sale.

items.statement: Steel PBT margin improved to 11% in Q2 FY25 from 7.3%
items.quote: We also achieved significant improvement in PBT margins, which rose to 11% from 7.3% last year.

items.statement: Paint EBITDA margin 6.7% in H1 FY25 vs 7% in H1 FY24
items.quote: EBITDA de-grew to INR7 crores from INR9 crores in half H1 of '24 with EBITDA margin of 6.7%.

items.statement: TMT price decline due to international prices, iron ore costs, and seasonal demand pressure
items.quote: First, prices in the international market are decreasing. Second, the prices of iron have also decreased. So, demand supply is also temporarily facing challenges in Q2.

items.statement: Paint ASP grew 37% from INR58 in FY15 to INR79 in H1 FY25
items.quote: Our commitment to premiumization continued to fuel performance as reflected in the increase of our average selling price per kg or per litter from INR58 in the financial year '15 to INR79 in H1 of financial year '25, a growth of 37% over the year.

items.statement: Paint premiumization strategy driving higher ASP and margin improvement
items.quote: Expanding our portfolio with premium and differentiated product allow us to meet evolving consumer preference, particularly the demand for quality and ecofriendly options. The strategy is not only strengthened revenue, but also enhance margin performance.

items.statement: Paint dealer network stable at ~4,360 with onboarding and deboarding ongoing
items.quote: No, sir, we are not facing any challenges. In fact, we are increasing the numbers of dealers. But the dealers who are not performing well, we are also deboarding them. So, both the onboarding and deboarding processes are going on.

items.statement: Target 5,000 paint dealers by end of financial year
items.quote: We are going to take it till the financial year of 5000.

items.statement: 80% of paint sales from Tier 2 cities leveraging steel dealer network
items.quote: Mostly, our presence is in Tier 2. If you have seen in the investor presentation, then most of the sale, around 80% sale is coming from Tier 2 cities.

items.statement: New paint market entrants causing temporary disruption and pressure
items.quote: Two or three new companies have entered the paint business. I understand that there is a disruption in the market. So this is a temporary phase.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free as of 30 September 2024
items.quote: We continue to remain debt-free as on 30 September 2024.

items.statement: Steel franchisee volume grew 11% YoY to 8.3 lakh metric tons in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Our steel volume from franchise route had stood at 8.3 lakh metrics ton in Q2 FY '25 compared to 7.5 lakh metric ton in Q2 FY '24, the year-on-year growth of 11%.

items.statement: Steel royalty income grew 11% YoY to INR33 crore in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Royalty income from franchisee stood at INR33 crores in Q2 FY '25, as compared to INR30 crores in Q2 FY '24, a growth of 11% year-on-year.

items.statement: Paint revenue declined 14% YoY to INR109 crore in H1 FY25
items.quote: Revenue for the H1 '25 stood at INR109 crores as compared to INR128 crores H1 FY '24, a degrowth of 14% year-on-year.

items.statement: Share price decline attributed to market forces, not company performance
items.quote: The market pricing factor has no role of the company. These are market forces, international forces, economic forces, and companies as well as the sensex. There is no role of the company in this that the price has decreased or the share has increased.

items.statement: Steel revenue model based on royalty per ton, insulated from TMT price fluctuations
items.quote: Our revenue model is that we take the royalty per ton basis. Whether the prices of TMT are less or more, it is our quantity base.

items.statement: FY25 scaffolding revenue target INR1,250 crores
items.quote: We are on track to do about INR1,250 crores in revenue this year FY25.

items.statement: FY26 scaffolding margins expected at 20% level
items.quote: So, in FY '26, once the Aurangabad Plant is fully operational, we do expect the margins to be at the 20% level.

items.statement: FY26 PBT expected around INR500 crores
items.quote: So, I think I would say overall, we should expect an increase of about INR100 crores in the total PBT of the company. So, that should put us at close, I think this year our PBT is tending to be around INR400 crores. So, I think that should put us at about INR500 crores in FY '26.

items.statement: No major capex planned for scaffolding beyond de-bottlenecking and routine
items.quote: No, I don't think there are any capex that are being planned apart from de-bottlenecking and routine kind of capex. There are no major capex that are planned.

items.statement: Aurangabad extrusion plant started production, ramping up
items.quote: The extrusion plant has started. We are currently in de-bottleneck mode, and getting that streamlined.

items.statement: Full capacity utilization of Aurangabad extrusion plant expected by end of FY25
items.quote: We expect to reach full capacity utilization of the extrusion plant by the end of this fiscal year.

items.statement: Full capacity utilization of Aurangabad plant expected in FY26
items.quote: And we expect to see full capacity utilization next year in FY26.

items.statement: Freight cost impact roughly 7% on scaffolding margins in Q2
items.quote: The freight rates almost doubled in this particular quarter from where it used to be around $4,000 a container, it went as high as $8,300. So, I think the impact of that was roughly about 7% on the margins.

items.statement: Textile division EBITDA target 12%-15%

items.statement: US scaffolding demand mixed, pickup expected Q1 next year post-election

items.statement: Drum closure demand steady globally except Europe, China growing

items.quote: The second idea is to move more towards the garmenting side of business, where the value addition is higher. items.statement: Engineering division expanded US and Europe sales team, new large accounts opened

So while some new large accounts have been opened up, currently

items.statement: Aurangabad plant potential revenue INR450 crores, profit INR80 crores at full capacity
items.quote: About INR450 crores in revenue and about INR80 crores in profit.

items.quote: The second half of the year, I don't think freight will impact because the freight prices have now cooled down. And so that that pressure will go away. So I think second half of the year should be better than the first half of the year in Scaffolding.

items.statement: Conservative FY26 PBT estimate accounts for potential commodity and freight headwinds
items.quote: But one should also take into account there could be some unforeseen negatives as well. items.statement: Raised INR 905.44 crores via preferential issue of equity shares and warrants

items.statement: About INR 260 crores of raised funds to be invested in facilities

items.statement: Expect robust growth in ash handling and EV fleet for next two years due to government push and corporate ESG compliance

items.statement: Ash handling margins to improve by deploying own vehicles; power trading margins to remain stable
items.quote: But the ash handling, we've been trying to deploy a lot of our own vehicles also going forward to improve the margins there. So the margins will be similar and we don't see any large growth in the percentage of margins in our power trading business, sir.

items.statement: Coal business is back-to-back with no price risk; ash handling risks include forex exposure and tender-based L1 pricing
items.quote: We do not have any risk in that coal business. Like we always keep saying that all our coal businesses are purely back to back. We do not have any price risk in that. And apart from that, we are not having any kind of commodity which we are trading into. The other business risk from the ash handling such as – ash, here risk is about foreign currency which we t ry and hedge whenever possible.

items.statement: Refrigerant gas segment seen as limited growth potential; focus remains on ash & coal handling, power trading, green mobility
items.quote: The company's total going forward will be ash and coal handling. There is a gap it's been contributing the same time over the years. And the market for this is very limited. So we don't see a large growth in this sector in the topic -- in this business in the future.

items.statement: Green Mobility targets ~2,000 vehicles by year-end; current ARR ~INR 34 crores

items.statement: INR 60 crores of raised capital earmarked for debt repayment; debt reduction is highest priority
items.quote: The recent capital raise is almost INR60 crores is towards repayment. And debt reduction is the highest priority.

items.statement: Power trading growth driven by ash & coal handling; considered sustainable
items.quote: The majority of the growth is from Ash And Coal Handling business and this growth is sustainable sir.

items.quote: The prices are very different for every company. Every company has a different pricing based on the number of kilometers we have to dispose the ash. Some have fixed prices and the fixed distance. Some have variable distance to the project.

items.statement: No new revenue streams targeted; focusing on existing diversified portfolio

items.statement: Export opportunities under evaluation; no specific timeline
items.quote: And we are planning to start the export for that one. But which is currently under evaluation. And there is no specific timeline.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY25 revised to 22-24% from previous 25-26% expectation
items.quote: Performance for the H2 is largely going to remain muted because of these kinds of headwinds of imports and lower priced imports coming in. items.statement: Mill expansion project financial closure completed, major equipment orders placed, on track for March 2026 completion

items.statement: Capacity expansion from 450 to 675 tons per day (50% increase) over next 18 months
items.quote: So, we are currently operating at 450 tons per day and we are planning to increase it by 50% and go up to 675 tons per day.

items.statement: NSR dropped INR 6,000 per ton YoY in Q2, wheat straw prices declining helping cost control

items.quote: I think wood is not really seeing a declining trend in pricing. In fact, it's either stable or showing an increasing trend. It's the agro raw material primarily wheat straw which is showing a declining trend and helping and aiding in reduced cost of operation.

items.quote: Sure, so writing and printing the normal grades are growing at a consistent CAGR of about 6 -7% which based on the current volumes is not a small volume it's a decently large volume and it's giving a good opportunity for the industry players to grow. items.statement: Specialty paper currently 18-20% of production, targeting 30%+ in coming years driven by single-use plastic ban opportunity
items.quote: Currently our specialty paper which is about 18-20% of our entire production, we are targeting that it will increase to 30% and beyond in the coming years.

items.statement: Imports increasing above 5-year average, continuing into Q3, primarily from Southeast Asia (Indonesia, China) at lower prices
items.quote: I think last five-year average if you see , the imports in the current year are more than that. Imports are showing an increasing trend over the years and the increasing trend continues for the Q3.

items.statement: Social forestry program: 20 lakh saplings planted, targeting 40 lakh by next year, 1 crore in 3 years to secure wood supply
items.quote: We've started our own social forestry program and we have already reached a level of 20 lakhs saplings and by next year we will reach 40 lakh saplings and it's only going to grow . We have targeted reaching 1 crore saplings in the next three years

items.statement: Industry 4.0 integration: Online sensors and control logic installed for wood bleach section under Project Nirman
items.quote: As par t of our project Nirman initiative focused on industry 4.O integration, we successfully installed online sensors and control logic for the wood bleach section marking a significant step forward in terms of automation, AI and efficiency.

items.statement: Specialty segment EBITDA margin 5-8% higher than writing & printing segment
items.quote: I reckon that the specialty segment will give a better margin EBITDA margin of between 5-8% as compared to writing and printing data.

items.statement: Operating at 100% capacity utilization in both Q1 and Q2, volumes maintained despite price pressure
items.quote: Yes, you are right there our volumes are the same we are already running to our one 100% capacities which was there in both Q1 and Q2.

items.quote: by FY’27 after full commissioning of Subansiri and Pakal Dul (1,000 MW), the resultant Regulated Equity will be Rs. 25,365 Crore.

items.quote: This gross margin is all a play of the product mix. So, as you would see that our economic segment grew higher than the company's volume growth that's why the gross margins were low. So but this will even out in the next quarter, I think.

items.quote: We expect that the modern trade to continues to contribute around 12% to 15%.

items.quote: For FY25 our revised operating revenue guidance is at least Rs.4250 crore in PG Electroplast and another Rs.600 crore in our JV company, Goodworth Electronics implying Rs.4850 crore of operating revenue as a growth, which is a growth of around 77% growth on F Y24 numbers.

items.quote: We are also revising our guidance for net profit to at least Rs.250 crore which is a growth of around 83% over FY24 net profit of Rs.137 crore.

items.quote: The growth in product businesses that is washing machine, room air conditioners and air coolers is expected to be around 78% from Rs.1668 crore to around Rs.2,975 crore.

items.quote: CAPEX guidance stands at around Rs.370 to Rs.380 crore and the progress on all infra and capacity expansion is going on as planned.

items.quote: So, out of 37 0, 380 crore CAPEX we are putting up about close to 165 crores in the product business for expanding the capacities and this will be for the plant and machinery in the product side of the business. items.quote: We have increased the capacity even this year by almost 50% on a base of last year. And we think in the season given the kind of order book that we have, we will be probably out of capacity even on the increased capacity this year.

items.quote: Order, book and visibility for product business remains very robust and the company is on the track to accelerate product business growth significantly in FY25.

items.statement: Margins expected to remain in similar range as today; focus on absolute per-unit margin rather than percentage margin as commodities are pass-through
items.quote: Margin should be in the similar range as they are today. And as I have been explaining actually, for us the percentage margin is not the key driver. Typically, it is the per unit margin in absolute amount that we actually get.

items.statement: Electronics business (ex-TV) EBITDA margins typically low at 2-4%
items.quote: No, the electronics business margins are typically very low in the range at the EBITDA about 2% to 4% at best.

items.statement: ASPs in RAC, washing machine and coolers down due to lower commodity prices; commodity prices are pass-through with price revisions monthly/quarterly
items.quote: The ASPs in RAC, washing machine and coolers were down due to lower commodity price during the period and availability of critical component was also a challenge due to import supply chain becoming more onerous.

items.statement: Strong momentum continuing at least till March; order book very strong giving good visibility for H2 FY25
items.quote: We see a strong momentum continuing at least till March and after that actually, how the monsoon season pans out and how things happen will decide the course of growth.
