items.statement: H1 FY25: Room AC revenue Rs.1,118 crore (+143% YoY), washing machine +41% YoY, air cooler +267% YoY; product business 54% of operating revenue in Q2
items.quote: The room AC business contributed Rs.1118 crore which is a 143% growth on Y-o-Y basis. The washing machine business also has grown by 41% on a Y-o-Y basis and air cooler business has also grown by 267% on Y-o-Y basis.

items.quote: We continue to add clients and we have seen some good client addition. But we don't make announcements on the client-addition during the quarter.

items.statement: Competitive intensity high in RAC and washing machine; new players entering washing machine; supply chain management to determine growth rates in AC business
items.quote: Competitive intensity has always been high, and we continue to see the high competitive intensity. In fact, some new players are entering the washing machine business. In AC business competitive intensity is high but because of the problems of the supply chain this year, the situation is getting a little bit more complicated.

items.statement: Government imposing BIS certification mandatory for component factories; some key factories' certifications not renewed easily, aggravating supply chain challenges likely into next year
items.quote: The government of India of late has been actually putting quality control orders, basically making the BI S certification mandatory for component factories also , which supply the components to India. And some of the key component factories have been had their BIS certification getting over and they are not getting renewed easily.

items.statement: Export planning underway with dedicated team for Middle East and Africa AC markets; expect start in 1-2 years
items.quote: We have started developing products for the Middle East and African market on the AC side and we are working towards it. So, we hope that in next one, two year we should see some start or beginning in the export side as well.

items.statement: Net debt Rs.238 crore at end H1 FY25 due to inventory stocking for upcoming AC season; no plan to repay debt as growth phase financed by debt is acceptable if ratios within limits
items.quote: On the balance sheet side, the net debt stands at 238 crores at the end of first half due to inventory stocking up for upcoming AC season.

items.statement: No plan to repay debt currently; comfortable with debt/EBITDA and debt/equity within internal limits during strong growth phase
items.quote: We don't actually have a plan to repay debt as of today. And given the strong growth phase that company is in, if some part of that growth journey is kind of financed by debt, it's not a problem for us.

items.statement: QIP up to Rs.1,500 crore approved for organic growth opportunities (capex and working capital); no inorganic acquisitions planned
items.quote: We are seeing some very significant growth opportunities coming our way. And if as and when they kind of material ize, we will be utilizing that money for CAPEX and working capital.

items.statement: Not looking at inorganic initiatives; focusing only on organic growth opportunities
items.quote: No, we are actually looking at largely only organic growth opportunities, we are not looking at any inorganic initiative.

items.statement: Target net fixed asset turnover of 4.5x-5x despite capex capitalization increasing asset base
items.quote: Overall, a similar number as it is today, which is about 4.5x to 5x on the net asset side. That should be the range which we should be able to maintain for the net fixed asset turn in our company.

items.quote: So, that will be just 30 crores.

items.statement: TV business confident of maintaining strong momentum into FY26; working on new platforms and acquiring more clients; competitive but maintaining lean cost structure
items.quote: We are confident of maintaining that momentum going forward as well in FY26 as well. And we are already working on certain new platforms in television and we are in process of acquiring more clients.

items.statement: Evaluating 1-2 new consumer durable categories for backward integration; any new project must meet internal ROCE targets significantly above cost of capital

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue mix: Mechanical INR229 cr (+10%), Civil INR395 cr (-20%), O&M INR391 cr (+44%), Mining INR12 cr (new), Electrical INR9 cr (-47%)
items.quote: Mechanical business has contributed INR229 crores against INR148 crores in Q2 FY '24, showing an increase of 10% growth. Civil business, including railway, water distribution contributed to INR395 crores against INR496 crores in Q2 FY '24, a decrease of 20%. O&M revenues are INR391 crores against INR272 crores in corresponding period last year, registering a growth of 44%.

items.statement: Domestic 95%, International 5% in Q2; Power sector 66%, Non-power 34%; Adani ordered 10,920 MW, NTPC 11,580 MW in last year
items.quote: During the quarter 2 FY '25, the distribution between domestic business and international business is 95% and 5%, respectively. Contribution from the power sector remained at 66% and non-power contributed 34%.

items.statement: Power Mech among peers in power sector with 15,000-16,000 labor deployed; BHEL capacity 15,000 MW but annual run-rate 3,200 MW, ramping to 8,000-10,000 MW
items.quote: Perhaps very few organizations have got that capabilities. Therefore, that drives us into the front compared to the others, particularly with the private customers like Adani.

items.statement: FGD orders slow due to Supreme Court ambiguity; NTPC committed to 58,000 MW FGD implementation; Udupi project INR963 cr ongoing
items.quote: It is to some extent, yes, it is slow moving because of the ambiguity attached with the Supreme Court judgment waiting and also some of the recommendations made by some of the government agencies.

items.statement: Project delays from land access, statutory clearances, forest clearance, right-of-way issues; supply chain and working capital management critical
items.quote: We are seeing many of the projects are delayed due to access issues because the land is not fully available. There are other statutory clearances are not taken. Forest clearances are not there. Right of the way is not there.

items.statement: Organization strength up ~10% to meet new business; enhancing civil engineering capability, leadership teams, O&M skill enhancement
items.quote: In fact, the present organization strength both direct and indirect labor has gone up by about 10% to meet the new businesses, which has come not only in the power sector, but also in the O&M and other areas.

items.statement: Overseas O&M revenue INR200 cr FY24, targeting INR235-240 cr FY25; 30-35% CAGR expected over 7-8 years in Middle East, West Africa
items.quote: Last year, we did overseas O&M of around INR200 crores. And this year, we anticipate to do INR235 crores to INR240 crores. So we -- you can expect to see the same trend over the next 7 to 8 years, overseas O&M growing at a rate of 30%, 35% CAGR.

items.statement: Green hydrogen partnerships with electrolyzer manufacturers in advanced stages; targeting SECI tenders for green hydrogen derivatives
items.quote: And apart from this, we are also actively exploring a few opportunities in the green hydrogen space, especially the SECI tenders that have come up for the green h ydrogen derivatives. So this again, we have tied up with a few electrolyzer manufacturers and then we are in advanced stages of forming partnerships with them

items.statement: Steel sector opportunities: ISCO Burnpur INR30,000 cr (4.5 MT), JSPL Oman INR30,000 cr (5 MT), SAIL doubling to 50 MT; INR4,000-5,000 cr construction opportunities
items.quote: And there can be opportunities about nearly INR4,000 crores to INR5,000 crores.

items.statement: H2 FY25 revenue growth ~40% driven by FGD execution, new Mahan/Athena projects, O&M projects from Q1
items.quote: The FGD, we have done around INR52 crores during the Q2 and the remaining are the new orders we received from Mahan and Athena new projects. O&M, we received new projects during the Q1 last year, new orders we received from the various projects.

items.statement: Targets Rs 1,000 crore revenue in 2-3 years with 60-40 domestic-export mix shifting toward 50-50 long term
items.quote: in terms of market and in terms of our business, as we mentioned, I think out of that, 400 to 500 should be from domestic and 500 to 600 should be from the export market which is also private label versus branded. That should be the mix

items.statement: Expects 4-5 crore revenue from Sanand facility in current year, 100 crore peak within 3 years
items.quote: Yes, I think for the current year, we will see probably 4-5 crores coming from this facility and the 100 CR target should be hit. Hopefully, we are expecting it to hit within 3 years' time.

items.statement: Invested 75 crore of 90 crore planned for Sanand Phase 1; 20 crore Phase 2 at Ghatakpukur progressing for completion within FY25
items.quote: On the CAPEX front, the first phase of Sanand-II, Gujarat project being set-up for manufacturing of Protec is nearing completion as per the schedule and the trial run for manufacturing of Dipped Gloves is likely to commence in November 2024. The Company has already invested 75 crores against projected investment of 90 crores.

items.statement: FY26 capex limited to routine 10 crore; no major expansion planned
items.quote: Yes, so as I mentioned, this year itself we are investing around 75 Cr by March 25. And for the next year, as of now, there would be only normal capacity addition we should keep doing. So, normal CAPEX in the range of 10 Cr, which is routine CAPEX we are doing. No specific further expansion is planned as of now.

items.statement: Sanand and Ghatakpukur expansions to add 200-225 crore incremental turnover capacity
items.quote: So it should be, both the units should be giving us around additional turnover of up to 200 to 225 crore turnover in excess of what we are doing now.

items.statement: Sanand trial runs for NBR gloves underway; commercial production expected by end of month; PU gloves line in 1-2 months; helmets by December
items.quote: So, yes, the trials have commenced. So, we within like right now, as we speak, I think this week, next week is when we are doing all this trials. And so hopefully, by the end of the month, we should have successfully set up the infrastructure for the trials and the trials would have been completed and we would be ready for commercial production of NBR gloves.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 12.24% down from prior year due to branding, consultancy, operating expenses; targets 15% EBITDA margin at scale
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was around 16 crores representing a growth of 3% year-on-year with EBITDA margin at 12.24%. The decline in EBITDA margin was mainly due to higher branding and self-promotion expenses, consultancy and other operating expenses.

items.statement: New Sanand products (gloves, helmets, eyewear) targeted at 10-15% EBITDA margin
items.quote: So, we expect it to be in the range of, see, these are all basically the synthetic glass, which we are planning and helmet we are planning initially. So, we have currently margin in the range of 10% to 15%. So, we target that. So, up to 15%, it should be, Yes.

items.statement: Export demand good except Turkey, Argentina; Europe recovering; US inquiries rising on China+1 shift
items.quote: So, the demand from the export market has been good. Barring some countries like Turkey and Argentina, where they had their own internal issues and not being very importer friendly in those countries, rest of the countries have been good.

items.statement: Domestic demand healthy; growth driven by stricter safety compliance, rising labor costs, MNC standards
items.quote: So, definitely we are seeing most of the sectors in India, in terms of compliances, they are getting better, also because the statutory norms are getting stricter. And I think, in general, because when the wages increases, the cost of labor is higher, you want to ensure that you are keeping your Mallcom ( labors

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue mix: shoes 42%, hand safety 27-28%, garments 27-28%, helmets ~2% but growing fast
items.quote: So, as of now for the current half year, the shoe remains the leading contributor around 42%, then we have hand safety and garment equally 27%-28%, and rest coming from other products like helmets. Helmets may be 2% as of now, but it is growing fast.

items.statement: Sanand facility revenue mostly hand protection; helmets 10-20% of facility turnover
items.quote: Mostly it would be hand protection. Helmet would be on the, you know, maybe up to 10% to 20% of turnover will come from helmet. But mostly it would be hand protection.

items.statement: Added 15-20 distributors in last 4-5 years; selective criteria include cash-basis terms; targeting underserved markets
items.quote: So, that number specifically, Rishabh, I don't have it ready with me, but if I am not wrong, I think definitely we would have added anywhere between 15 to 20 or maybe more in the last four to five years.

items.statement: Branded vs private label split 40:60 currently; targeting 50:50 in 3-5 years
items.quote: So, the split is very much similar as the export versus domestic because largely, in domestic we are only doing branded and some parts of Southeast Asia and Middle East where we are doing branded. So, I think the ratio is largely 60% of private label and 40% of branded that we are doing.

items.statement: Inventory at 90-110 days range; slightly elevated due to growth and supply chain buffers; expected to normalize
items.quote: In our type of business, we are supposed to keep the inventory in the range of up to 100 days. So, this quarter and half, the inventory is basically in line with the growth also. So, we had 14% growth and there is an increase in inventory.

items.statement: ICRA reaffirmed long-term credit rating at ICRA (A) with stable outlook
items.quote: ICRA, the rating agency has once again reaffirmed the long-term credit rating of the company as ICRA (A) with a stable outlook.

items.statement: Capex funded entirely through internal cash accruals
items.quote: As stated earlier, the entire CAPEX plan to be sourced through internal cash accruals of the company.

items.statement: Open to acquisitions if opportunity arises; no active discussions currently
items.quote: Yes, definitely we are always on the lookout if an opportunity presents, we would definitely like to take a look into it. We are not discussing with anyone actively right now, but Yes, if there is a possibility, we are open to it.

items.statement: Government and BIS actively enforcing certification standards; implementation strengthening for footwear, helmets; new standards for hand protection, hi-vis clothing in progress
items.quote: And in the last four, five years, the government and BIS has been very active in ensuring that certifications are followed and ensuring the cheap, low quality uncertified products are not imported or not manufactured, or the fake and spurious products are taken out of the market or the market study is being done properly.

items.statement: Logistics challenges (Red Sea, container shortages) extend lead times and revenue cycle; sold mostly on FOB basis
items.quote: Yes, so this is almost like regular business for us. There are something or the other which is happening. Earlier it was COVID and then this Red Sea crisis, and there are container shortages in between. Also, because there are very few shipping lines who are servicing worldwide, so it's a very oligopoly kind of market and they control the prices, they control the availability.

items.statement: Advertising, sales promotion, consultancy costs ~2% of sales in H1; percentage expected to decline with revenue growth
items.quote: So, it is for the period, it is in the range of 2% almost. So, how it is happening that there is a consultant cost also in the range of 1%, and apart from that we have, as Rohit mentioned in his address, we are attending a lot of fairs and seminars, both in India, outside India.

items.statement: Launched own D2C e-commerce website; early orders received without marketing; targeting small buyers and direct consumers
items.quote: We have launched our own e-commerce website and this is in a very initial stage. The idea is to, because we saw that there was demand from direct consumers for our product as well, so we thought, okay, why not reach out to them directly? So, that's why this is primarily to cater to the D2C audience.

items.statement: Land in Kolkata: received 27 crore advance from JDA; considering outright sale instead of partnership; deal not finalized
items.quote: So, just look at the notes which we have in the account. So, this year, we have received around 27 Cr as advance from the JDA. And so, what has happened that they have approached us with the proposal for outright sale, which we are still considering and the deal is yet to be finalized.

items.statement: H1 FY25 consolidated revenue Rs 232 crore (+14% YoY), EBITDA Rs 30 crore (+2% YoY), PAT Rs 19 crore (+5% YoY)
items.value: Revenue 232 crore, EBITDA 30 crore, PAT 19 crore
items.quote: For the first half of the Financial Year 2025, the operating revenue grew by around 14% to Rs. 232 crores. EBITDA grew by 2% year-on-year to Rs. 30 crores. EBITDA margin for this period was 13%. The net profit for the period grew by 5% year-on-year to Rs. 19 crores with PAT margin reported at 8.03%.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guided at mid-single-digit; EBITDA margin improvement of ~100 bps to 18.5-19%
items.quote: on the top line, we would be mid-sin gle-digit kind of growth as far as the overall top line is concerned. But when it comes to the overall margin, we are bullish about at least 100 basis point kind of improvement somewhere between 18.5% to 19%, I mean, a kind of EBITDA, that's the outlook that I would maintain

items.statement: Domestic India growth guidance maintained at 8-9% for FY25
items.quote: On an annualized basis, I foresee -- still I will maintain our overall expectation of close to 8% to 9% kind of growth. So that is something that we are very bull ish about. And H2 will be a lot better than H1

items.statement: US business expects H2 improvement after H1 volume degrowth of 18.7% and 6% price erosion
items.quote: But going forward, we expect that to improve -- so in the second half, we are expecting much better performance as far as the U.S. business is concerned. So that's -- and on the new launches, I think I've already answered.

items.statement: US business annual outlook: flattish to mid-single-digit erosion; H1 saw 15% degrowth
items.quote: annually, we may land at a flattish to a mid-single-digit kind of erosion in the U.S. business.

items.statement: US profitability improved in H1 vs prior year; expects further improvement in H2
items.quote: our profitability is better as compared to last year from the U.S. business, and we expect this trend to even get better in the H2.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement driven by lower API prices, lower US mix, and better product mix in ROW and domestic
items.quote: First is definitely the API prices, as you must have seen all the other pharma companies also. So we also got a benefit of lower API prices that helped us to improve our gross margin.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target: improve by at least 100 bps annually
items.quote: I have always maintained that we will work on improving our EBITDA every year by at least 100 basis points and which is what I'm giving the guidance even for the current financial year.

items.statement: Enzene US CDMO plant order book started; production expected Q4 FY25 to Q1 FY26
items.quote: We've started getting a lot of queries. We've started getting some orders. Of course, furth er details, we'll give you at an appropriate time. But that's how I'll put forward

items.statement: Enzene US plant capex ~INR 450 crore; not capitalizing pre-op expenses
items.quote: So there is a capex layout that we had specified even in the previous call, close to the tune of INR450 crores, and which I think that is what we are maintaining even from -- for now.

items.statement: MedTech and Enzene pre-op expenses revised down to INR 60-70 crore from INR 100 crore
items.quote: So as of now, we don't think we will cross at max INR 60 crores to INR70 crores for both the MedTech and the Enzene U.S. plant.

items.statement: Enzene US CDMO biologics plant production start targeted Q4 FY25 to Q1 FY26
items.quote: We maintain with our expected time lines of Q4 to -- at the most Q1 of next financial year. And we expect -- so our order book has already started. It's already started getting orders basis the progress of the plant.

items.statement: Domestic chronic portfolio outperforming in diabetes and 3 other segments; chronic to grow faster than acute
items.quote: Chronic, our focus has been in diabetes -- in actually 4 such segments. We are actually outperforming in IQVIA. Now I haven't done the calculation of the percentage to chronic, but I can clearly tell you that chronic is growing -- will grow much faster than our grow th in acute owing to 2 reasons: one, the chronic market is growing faster; second, our base is lesser, so we will outperform the mark

items.statement: Trade generic business ~20% of domestic; margins improving on better mix and pricing
items.quote: So it's around 80-20. It's around 20% of our business is trade generic, yes. But even on the trade generic business, we are seeing good improvement in the overall margins. So I think that's a point that I would like to highlight.

items.statement: US back orders reduced from 38% to 2%; inventory rebuilt to win back customers
items.quote: In fact, when we started this year, we were at 38% back orders. Our back orders are now down to 2% in U.S. So what we have done is we have improved the inventory over there, but there were certain contracts where we had lost because we were not able to supply.

items.statement: US market sees 6-7% price erosion for vanilla generics; not chasing unviable pricing
items.quote: U.S. is one perennially price erosion market for vanilla generics kind of portfolio. Like I had said and we are seeing that trend as well, we have seen 6% to 7% kind of price erosion from the U.S. market in terms of pricing.

items.statement: Sacubitril-valsartan approved in US; launch timing dependent on Novartis litigation outcome
items.quote: So we got the approval for sacubitril-valsartan. But as you know that there is a litigation going on with one of the players with Novartis. So we will -- we are just waiting and we will watch how that proceeds. And then accordingly, we will take a call on going ahead with the launch for that particular product.

items.statement: Mirabegron (generic Myrbetriq) launch only post FY26 due to settlement with innovator
items.quote: We are bound by the settlement that we have with the innovator. So others who have launched it has been -- it has been an at-risk launch for them. So we will be launching it only post '26. So that is how -- because we are already bound by the agreement that we have signed with the innovator.

items.statement: US inventory increased deliberately to avoid failure-to-supply penalties (INR 140 crore in FY24)
items.quote: And we see a lot of failure-to-supply penalties in FY '24, which was around INR140 crores. And also, we lost a few of the customers in the U.S. on account of not having adequate inventory.

items.statement: Net cash ~INR 4,250 crore as of Sep 30; cash doubled in last 18 months
items.quote: just to share that we have increased our cash by INR400 crores in this quarter. And the overall cash is around -- net cash is around INR4,250 crores as on 30th September. And in fact, just to add, if you look at last 1, 1.5 years, we've almost doubled our cash position.

items.statement: Non-current investments shifted to NCDs/mutual funds for M&A readiness; all AAA/A+ rated
items.quote: Now since we are looking for a fe w of the M&A opportunities, so we want to have investments which are marketable or tradable, and which we can encash without paying any penalties. So we have started parking a few of our investment in NCDs and mutual fund and not in bank deposits, and that is why you see increase in noncurrent investments

items.statement: M&A strategy: strategic fit, synergy, value creation; IRR hurdle 14-15% vs 12% cost of capital
items.quote: Okay. And our cost of capital is around 12%, so -- and so definitely, we'll not go anything which is lower than the 14% to 15% of IRR. As Vikas said, that all depends upon how strategic it is in terms of our portfolio and also the growth drivers...

items.statement: Domestic volume growth 1.1% in Q2 vs industry 0%; PAN brand growth 12.8% vs market 7.3% MAT
items.quote: According to IQVIA data, our company registered a positive volume growth of 1.1% in a challenging market that witnessed a 0% volume growth in Q2. PAN is growing at 12.8% compared to the market growth of 7.3% on a MAT basis.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA INR 13,615 mn, margin 21.1% vs 17.7% YoY; Net profit INR 12,338 mn, up 36%
items.quote: Key highlights for H1. The total revenue from operations saw a modest growth of 0.6%, but earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization were INR 13,615 million, resulting in an EBITDA margin of 21.1% versus 17.7% in H1 FY '24.

items.statement: Acute market weakness due to COVID base normalization, channel inventory, and zero NLEM price increase
items.quote: One, the COVID base that we have spoken about, when the -- when you see this kind of growth that happens in 1 or 1.5 years, and that happened in the acute side, it takes a while for it to really come back because there is a lot of channel buying that happens during that phase. And that channel buying takes a period of time for it to get normalized.

items.statement: Anti-infectives injectable portfolio low-margin; rationalizing unviable growth opportunities
items.quote: So what I mentioned was that the injectable piece, anyways, if you see the injectable anti-infectives market is a low margin as compared to whether your overall portfolio or whether you compare it to -- even amongst the anti-infectives that's the lowest margin portfolio. So you need a very different cost structure, and there are certain growth opportunities that you have to walk away with, right?

items.statement: Enzene biosimilars: 7 commercialized in India; 5 in global development; denosumab clinical trial completed
items.quote: So far, we have got 7 products to the market, 7 biosimilars, okay? And we are actually -- if you look at for the global markets, we are working on 5 products. But our sense is that at least 2 products to 3 products is something that we will be very clear to -- yes, and that's a long-term play.

items.statement: ROW ex-US/Chile grew ~30% in Q2; focusing on filings, partnerships, out-licensing
items.quote: Other than the U.S. and Chile, if I look at the other ROW markets, we have grown by almost 30% as far as seco nd quarter is concerned. So our -- all other markets where we have improved focus, we are going to do more filings

items.statement: Second half of FY25 expected to be far superior to first half with significant volume and revenue growth
items.quote: we do expect a significant volume as well as revenue growth in the second half of the current financial year

items.statement: Targeting to double revenues over the next couple of years with two new AAC block facilities planned
items.quote: Yes, we are targeting to double our revenues over the next couple of years

items.statement: EBITDA margins targeted at 18-20% as JV facility ramps up, running facilities at 20-24%
items.quote: our EBITDA margins should go up to 18% to 20% at least. That's what we are targeting

items.statement: Plan to install two additional AAC block manufacturing facilities in next 2 years
items.quote: we are also lo oking at installing two other AAC block manufacturing facilities in the next 2 years

items.statement: ZMARTBUILD WALL by NXTBLOC launched - ready-made wall up to 6m height, unique in market
items.quote: this is a ready-made wall, which can be from a height of almost 2.5 meters going up to 6 meters at a stretch

items.statement: Demand picked up after monsoon subsided mid-October, government projects restarting post-elections
items.quote: since October, once the monsoon subsided after 10th to 15th October, the demand has picked up somewhat better

items.statement: Selling prices down 7-10% YoY but raw material costs declined similarly, minimal margin impact
items.value: 7 to 8 percent, maybe up to 10 percent
items.quote: as compared to the last year, the selling prices have gone down by almost 7 to 8 percent, maybe up to 10 percent

items.statement: Siam Cement JV plant capacity to increase from 1 MW to 3.5 MW consolidated by end of FY25
items.quote: by the end of the current financial year, we plan to increase it to around 3.5 MW on a consolidated group level

items.statement: Certification delays (4-5 month lab wait) and customer audits caused Q2 volume shortfall for new wall product
items.quote: certifications, etc from laboratories/IIT there's a waiting period of almost 4 months to 5 months

items.statement: Umargaon plant upgrade completed 16 Oct 2024, operations commenced, scaling up gradually
items.quote: the Umargaon plant upgradation has been completed as on 16th October 2024 and has commenced operations since which shall be scaled up gradually

items.statement: Siam JV plant utilization at 16%, expected to reach 65-70% in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: we expect it to keep on gradually improving over the next two to three quarters. And it might take about three quarters to reach optimum utilization of almost 65%-70% plus

items.statement: Construction chemicals manufacturing to start next quarter, currently outsourced, targeting tile adhesive etc
items.quote: hopefully in the next quarter, we will start manufacturing of construction chemicals also on our own name

items.statement: Company commands 3-5% premium over other AAC block manufacturers due to brand and service
items.quote: we are able to command a premium of almost 3% to 5% as compared to the other AAC block manufacturers

items.statement: Management aims to maintain the margins achieved in the first half of FY25 and expects revenue growth to continue at 22-23% with existing business and acquisitions.
items.quote: We want to maintain the numbers that we've achieved in the first few quarters.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded to 33.1% in Q2 FY25, up 1,186 bps YoY, driven by self-run model transition, iDATA acquisition, and higher service fees.
items.quote: Our EBITDA margins expanded to 33.1% in Q2 FY '25, an expansion of 1,186 basis points from 21.3% in the corresponding quarter.

items.statement: Management's objective is to maintain current EBITDA margin levels around 33% rather than target further expansion.
items.quote: Our main objective is first to maintain the margins that we've achieved. So as of now, our objective is just to maintain the margins that we have achieved.

items.statement: Visa applications processed grew 41% YoY to 10.1 lakh in Q2 FY25, including 1.6 lakh from iDATA; organic volume growth was 18%.
items.quote: During quarter Q2 FY '25, the number of Visa application processed has increased from 7.2 lakh applications in Q2 FY '24 to 10.1 lakhs in Q2 FY '25, which have grown by a robust 41% year-on-year.

items.statement: Won multiple new contracts in the last year including Slovakia Global, Hungary, Italy government, Poland, Portugal; actively bidding for more in Europe and North America.
items.quote: We have won multiple contracts and also we are bidding for newer contracts and as and when we win more contracts we'll definitely announce.

items.statement: Bidding pipeline for visa contracts estimated at $1.1-1.5 billion opportunity over next 2 years across Europe and North America.
items.quote: Opportunity is much bigger. It's definitely upwards of $1.1 billion, $1.5 billion. In Europe, there are multiple countries that are coming in for renewals, in North America also.

items.statement: Transitioning from partner-run to self-run centers in select geographies; 9 iDATA centers to be integrated in 9 months, 4 completed so far.
items.quote: We are evaluating that in certain geographies of the world. So that is what it means.

items.statement: Revenue per application increased from INR 1,988 to INR 2,883 YoY in Q2 FY25 due to higher value-added services and self-run model.
items.quote: Furthermore, our net revenue per application has also increased from INR1,988 in Q2 FY '24 to INR2,883 in Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: Sequential revenue dip in visa business (ex-iDATA) due to higher mix of lower-revenue consular/passport renewal services.
items.quote: This has been mainly on account of consular numbers being much higher, where the revenue per application is much lower.

items.statement: QIP enabling resolution passed but no current requirement; will announce if large acquisition opportunity arises.
items.quote: Right now, there is no requirement but that was just enabling resolution. As and when there is a requirement where we have a big acquisition opportunity or requirement of funds, we will be announcing that.

items.statement: Paid EUR 50 million upfront for iDATA; remaining EUR 4 million to be paid over next year.
items.quote: So we have paid the entire amount, except a small, I think, EUR 4 million, which is to be paid over the next 1 year or so.

items.statement: Completed acquisition of Citizenship Invest for $31 million in October 2024; Aadifidelis Solutions (57% stake) acquisition expected to close soon.
items.quote: We just closed another one, which is a Citizenship Invest about $31 million acquisition, which got finalized in the first week of October.

items.statement: iDATA contributed INR 60 crore revenue and INR 23 crore EBITDA (38% margin) in Q2 FY25; expected to grow 10-15% annually.
items.quote: As we said, this quarter, they did about INR 60 crores of revenue and INR 23 crores was the EBITDA, about 40%.

items.statement: Geopolitical issues like Russia outbound traffic remain suppressed but overall global volumes have increased since 2019.
items.quote: Definitely, after COVID certain countries, for example, Russia outbound traffic still has not come up. So once probably the situation stabilizes, we will definitely see numbers coming back from there.

items.statement: Digital business revenue expected to grow in coming quarters after contract completion in Punjab last year; Aadifidelis acquisition to add scale.
items.quote: We do expect growth coming in digital business in the coming quarters and years.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 15% for the full year
items.quote: I can say that our overall guidance of 15% EBITDA for the whole, this also will be -- after this project implementation also will be in the same level and there won't be any up or down.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin guidance not explicitly stated; standalone guidance reaffirmed at 15%
items.quote: At guidance level, we'll maintain the same guidance.

items.statement: Global steel demand expected to decline 0.9% in 2024, rebound 1.2% in 2025; India steel demand projected to grow 8% over 2024-25
items.quote: According to the World Steel Association, global steel demand is expected to decline by 0.9% in 2024. However, after 3 consecutive years of decline, a broad-based recovery excluding China is anticipated in 2025. Global steel demand is forecast to rebound by 1.2% in 2025, and it's anticipated that there will be moderate demand recovery in the second half of this financial year.

items.statement: Overseas businesses face economic pressure and geopolitical uncertainties; moderate revival expected in H2 from EU and US
items.quote: This quarter proved to be particularly challenging for us as our overseas businesses faced economic pressure, slowdown and geopolitical uncertainties. However, we anticipate some moderation in these challenges during the second half of the year with a moderate revival in demand from EU and the U.S.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 13% in Q2 FY25, 15% in H1 FY25; consolidated EBITDA margin 9% in Q2 FY25, 11% in H1 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 13% in Q2 FY '25 and for H1 FY '25, it was 15%.

items.statement: Net realization reduced 7-9% from steel customers; alumina price more than doubled from INR 350-360 to over INR 600; magnesia price also increased

items.statement: Domestic business grew 15% YoY in Q2 FY25 despite client shutdowns; standalone domestic revenue share increased to 69% from 61% YoY
items.quote: I'm pleased to share that our domestic business has demonstrated strong growth with a 15% increase in Q2 FY '25 despite facing challenges such as shutdown at some major client facilities.

items.statement: JV greenfield facility with Marvels International at ~INR 300 crores; trial and commercial production by March 2026; IFGL holds 51% stake
items.quote: The estimated project cost is INR 300 crores, with plans to begin trial and commercial production by March 2026. We are committed to maintaining balanced debt -to-equity ratio for the JV, which will not exceed 1:1.

items.statement: Odisha land payment completed; possession expected shortly; commercial production in latter part of FY27

items.statement: US subsidiary EI Ceramics acquired building in Ohio for ISO plant; 40% capacity uplift when complete

items.statement: Inaugurated casting flux granules unit in Visakhapatnam with 18,000 MT annual capacity; launched magnesia carbon production line under Phase 3 expansion

items.statement: Combined ISO capacity of 80,000 pieces/year sufficient for next 5 years; Kandla plant has 50,000 capacity
items.quote: We have a combined capacity of 80,000 pieces a year, roughly, okay? And we do see that this will be sufficient until next coming 5 years, when we are going to utilize for both domestic and export put together.

items.statement: Magnesia bricks and mould flux products together expected to reach INR 300-350 crores revenue at maturity
items.quote: And we are reaching say, 90%, 95%, both bricks and casting flux, it should be anywhere between INR 300 crores to INR 350 crores, both put together.

items.statement: Casting flux and magnesia carbon bricks volume supplies expected from Q4 FY25; currently in entry stabilization phase
items.quote: No, this quarter is primarily on entry stabilization. I know all those. So actual supplies volume will take place in Q4.

items.statement: Alumina price increased from INR 350-360 to over INR 600 (more than double); magnesia price also increased; LME-linked pricing
items.quote: Now it is already crossed INR 600 and going towards INR 650, more than double. So they have a formula of markup price over this.

items.statement: Pass-through of raw material cost increases to customers takes 5-6 months in refractory industry; relief expected mid-Q4 or next year
items.quote: And conventionally, in refractory, passing on takes place after 4 to 5 months or even 2 quarters constant effort to customers. And that has not happened. We are only hoping and we are fighting with various customers to do that. We hope that some relief may come in the middle of Q4 or next year only when the passing -- the lag period of passing on to customer is almost 5 to 6 months, and that's unf

items.statement: Liberty Ostrava restructuring caused revenue loss of ~INR 30-35 crores this year; no business done with them currently
items.quote: I think, if you go to our December '23 res ults, we have mentioned around INR 38 crores, INR 39 crores of provision we have taken. So something about INR 30 crores, INR 35 crores of revenue we have lost this year. We have not done any business with Liberty

items.statement: TRM (Total Refractory Management) currently contributes 35-40% of steel business; expected to exceed 65-70% in future
items.quote: That's, but -- like in the total year, maybe I can put a ballpark figure of 35% to 40%.

items.statement: Strengthened approach towards Tata Steel; reorganized structure to leverage Tata Steel growth
items.quote: As far as Tata Steel business is concerned, yes, we have a great potential. And then we have even reorganized our structure in such a manner that we also leverage Tata Steel growth for our business.

items.statement: Chinese competition exists (1-2 players) but customers prefer supplier partners offering longer value chain services; price pressure present but manageable
items.quote: Yes. See, there are some players, particularly China, 1 or 2. But more and more now customers are looking into supplier partner, refractory partner, who can provide service over a little longer value chain throughout so that it becomes seamless in producing and managing the refractory.

items.statement: Acquisition under review in India; details not disclosed; open to both organic and inorganic growth
items.quote: Yes, we do have an acquisition that is currently under review, and it is in India. But with regard to details, I wouldn't like to share any of the details at the moment.

items.statement: North American steel market down 3.9% YoY; European business flat; subsidiary Sheffield maintaining sales but profit dipped due to geopolitical/economic scenario
items.quote: The North American market, for example, is about 3.9% down. And so far this year from last year, we have seen the European business with no growth.

items.statement: Expect at least one more quarter of depressed subsidiary figures; hope for improvement from Q4 FY25 onwards
items.quote: And so subsidiary-wise, we still feel that we have another quarter at least of, let's say, depressed figures, but then we hope to see some changes from there.

items.statement: Freight costs increased substantially in H1 FY25 vs H1 FY24; Deloitte HR transformation cost reflecting in other expenses for full FY25
items.quote: See, I could only tell that it has increased from last year H1 substantially.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt free; cash and equivalents INR 193.3 crores as of Sep 30; JV debt-to-equity not to exceed 1:1
items.quote: With respect to the liquidity position, we remain net debt free with a strong balance sheet. Cash and cash equivalents stood at INR 193.3 crores on a consolidated basis as on September 30.

items.statement: Annualized ROCE 9.3%, annualized ROE 6.7% on consolidated basis
items.quote: Our annualized ROCE stood at 9.3%, and our annualized ROE stood at 6.7%.

items.statement: Nonferrous contribution currently 15-17% of top line; expected to increase over 3-5 years as market matures
items.quote: So this will have a share in top line of close to 15% to 17% as of now, but it may change and increase.

items.statement: No recovery yet from provisioned client (Liberty Ostrava); 100% provided, any recovery will be updated
items.quote: As of now no amount of recoveries that we mentioned. Because -- and it has no impact on our books also as we provided 100%. If we get something, we'll update.

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY25 is INR4,000-4,100 crores and for FY26 is INR4,500-4,600 crores at close to 11% EBITDA margin
items.quote: This year, we'll be closing something in between INR4,000 crores to INR4,100 crores. And therefore, for the next year, we have a guidance of around INR4,500 crores to INR4,600 crores of revenues that we'll be generating at a margin of close to 11%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY25 is 50 bps improvement from 9.95% to 10.45%, with further 50 bps improvement in FY26 targeting 11-11.5%
items.quote: Last year, like we closed at a margin of 9.95%. This year, we have given a guidance that we'll be improving in between a 50-point basis followed by 50-point basis in the coming FY '25, '26. So we expect the margins to be hovering around 11%, 11.5%.

items.statement: Capex for FY25 is around INR250 crores including INR100 crores carry forward; annual maintenance capex policy is INR150-155 crores equal to depreciation
items.quote: While this year, it might be around INR250 crores because we have INR100 crores of carry forward commitments, which we need to settle in this year for the expansions that we took in the past.

items.statement: Sheet metal capacity utilization at 55-82% with orders in hand; new product lines to start production in H2 FY25 and FY26
items.quote: In terms of sheet metal, the new business that we had generated, our capacity utilization at this point stands at somewhere in the region of 55% to 82%. So that gives us a leg room to be able to grow this. And the orders are in place.

items.statement: Commodity prices are pass-through with quarterly price settlement; customers have bulk contracts with suppliers and set prices reimbursed to Sandhar
items.quote: When you say bulk contracts, this is a routine process in the industry that every quarter, our prices are banked up so that for us, commodity prices are a pass-through.

items.statement: Gross debt INR620 crores, net debt INR581 crores as of September; peak debt not expected to exceed INR700 crores; cash generation INR142 crores in H1; no accelerated debt prepayment planned
items.quote: As of September, we have a gross debt of INR620 crores and a net debt of INR581 crores. And we expect that we will not be reaching a level of INR700 crores. As of now, we are operating at a working capital of around INR30 crores.

items.statement: Pune expansion for cabins, fabrication and die casting expected to commence commercial production by end of January 2025
items.quote: The company's expansion projects in Pune for cabins and fabrication and die casting are expected to commence commercial production by the end of January 2025.

items.statement: Suzuki smart lock order delayed from November to January; will start adding revenue in Q4 FY25 and FY26
items.quote: In terms of locks, our -- the Suzuki order, which was the order to do smart locks was delayed -- has been delayed from November to January now. Again, in the next quarter, you will see that, that will start adding along with some other componentry.

items.statement: Hyundai 4-wheeler order delayed; pilot production now expected in March 2025, revenue impact in FY26
items.quote: It's a very good product, which was supposed to launch off in November and December. That was the initial target. We've now been told to start pilots in the month of March, which means the effect of that revenue will come in the next financial year.

items.statement: Sandhar Engineering subsidiary revenue doubled to INR192 crores in H1 FY25 from INR87 crores; at breakout EBITDA level of 7%, targeting double-digit margins as volumes ramp up
items.quote: For this half year, it has registered an income of INR192 crores versus INR87 crores of the corresponding. So it's just -- you can see the growth is more or less a double growth. And as far as the EBITDA is concerned, they are well at the, I would say, breakout level. They have already achieved EBITDA of 7%.

items.statement: Domestic order book of ₹347 Crore to be executed over 2-3 years; bids submitted totaling ₹700 Crore with results expected soon; plan to submit bids worth ₹1,500 Crore targeting financial order book of ₹800-1,000 Crore including internationa

items.statement: Target executed order book of ₹1,000 Crore by end of March 2025 (up from ₹650 Crore currently); unexecuted order book of ₹400+ Crore expected by March 2025
items.quote: Today is a 650 crores total order book. That should reach to 1,000 crores by end of March. So, you can say April-May is our declaration date. So up to May, I'm calculating so 1,000 crores shall be the executed order book.

items.statement: Targeting EBITDA margin much higher than FY24's 17-18%; international Mozambique project expected ~75% EBIT; private assignments typically 50% profitability
items.quote: Definitely we have a target of much more, much higher EBIT than even FY23-24, that was 17%-18%. We are targeting much higher EBIT than March FY24.

items.statement: Preferential allotment proceeds of ₹33.24 Crore deployed: ₹8-9 Crore for equipment orders (FWD machine, German/Danish/Swiss equipment), ₹5 Crore for bank guarantee margins, ₹2-3 Crore for new office, remainder for high-interest debt repayme
items.quote: We had now already expenditure is done. So, we had a plan to buy equipments to the tune of 8 to 9 Crores. We have already ordered part payment has been released and this equipment will give a good revenue to the Company private sector, mainly the testing part.

items.statement: High-interest unsecured loans being repaid from preferential allotment proceeds; cash credit (CC) utilization to be minimized; working capital requirements to be fulfilled from equity funds
items.quote: Secondly, we have started repaying the debt which was high interest rate coupons and of course the CC of the bank which is to be utilized now in a minimum way, so working capital requirements shall be fulfilled from equity side fundraise only.

items.quote: And definitely higher can be the profit margins and EBIT because roughly the one mark carries weightage of about Rs. 50 lakh. So, if I score 2 marks more than my competitors so I can bid even 1 crore more than my competitors with safe win.

I should not say but NHAI and MORTH nowadays are very hard and strict. And in last 6 months four of the top consultants in India are debarred or blacklisted for poor service on the site. items.quote: The recent preferential allotment of 3077800 equity shares at ₹108 per share totaling ₹33.24 Crore, will further strengthen our financial position to support these growth plans.

items.quote: See, revenue, our stated position is definitely our effort is that we want to be at least 6% to 8% more than the market growth.

items.quote: So we have given a guideline of INR200 crores. But I think seeing this that we are investing now and including on the land also, so this could go up to this year INR260 crores, INR270 crores.

items.quote: And next year also, I think definitely, we would try to see that it is around INR200 crores, but it could also, depending on the growth and we are quite aggressive now on new sales wins, so there, again, it could go up to INR260 crores, INR270 crores next year also.

items.statement: H1 FY25 net new business wins with annualized peak revenue of INR6,046 million, 37% from EV models
items.quote: In H1 FY '25, we have achieved net new business wins with annualized peak revenues of INR6,046 million. The order book from EV models constitutes more than 37% of these wins.

items.statement: Cost reduction initiatives to fully reflect by Q4 FY25, operating leverage to improve margins
items.quote: Some of these measures have already started showing impact on our bottom line, but most of them will fully get reflected by Q4 of FY '25.

items.statement: Normalized effective tax rate expected at 25-27% going forward
items.quote: Going forward, the stable effective tax rate could be in the range of around 25-27%.

items.statement: EV 2-wheeler volumes grew 74% quarter-on-quarter in Q2 FY25
items.quote: EV 2-wheeler volumes on quarter-over-quarter grew by almost 74%.

items.quote: In 2-wheelers, if you look at -- if I compare the EV models with 125 cc vehicle, so the content on an average with our incumbent customer -- incumbent customer in 2-wheeler ICE for 125 cc, it will be around INR4,000 to INR5,000 per vehicle, whereas for EV, it will be around INR25,000 to INR30,000 content per vehicle.

items.statement: China arbitration verdict expected by end of November or December 2024

items.statement: Net debt target of INR700-750 crores by end of FY25 through internal cash generation
items.quote: Yes. I mean, internally, we have aggressive targets, but I think we should end this year with maybe around INR700 crores to INR750 crores is what is possible.

items.statement: Capex preponed by 6 months for EV motors and electronics capacity expansion
items.quote: So we are now preponing a lot of the capex in this regard now to at least 6 months earlier.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to improve from current levels due to operating leverage and cost reductions
items.quote: Well, we don't give that kind of guidance, but definitely, the operating leverage should definitely help us as we continue to grow our business, particularly in the EV segment. items.quote: And there are also some resin-related lags in our RM pricing or in resin-related RM pass-through lag.

items.statement: Overseas operations losses not recognizing deferred tax assets until turnaround confirmed
items.quote: On some of these overseas businesses where we are actually incurring some losses, we haven't recognized the deferred tax asset as of now because we need to see the turnaround to actually get that confidence and give that confidence to the auditors.

items.statement: Management guided for 20%+ revenue growth in FY2025 with higher EBITDA and PAT growth
items.quote: we are confidently on track to deliver 20%+ revenue growth in FY2025 and even higher growth in terms of EBITDA and PAT this year.

items.statement: Management expects strong Q3 and robust Q4 in FY2025 similar to last year's seasonality
items.quote: October, November, December is typically the best quarter of the financial year for us. Last year, we were able to beat our Q3 performance in Q4 and this year again, we are keeping similar outlook that we will have a strong Q3 as well as a robust Q4.

items.statement: Q2 FY2025 EBITDA margin expanded 65 bps y-o-y and 76 bps q-o-q to 20.9%
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin was 20.9%, with an expansion of 65 basis points y-o-y and 76 basis points on a sequential basis.

items.statement: Management expects inventory & data cost efficiency improvements in next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: Also, we believe that in the next 2-3 quarters onwards, you might see some efficiency in inventory & data cost also.

items.statement: Intangible assets increased over 10% y-o-y due to GenAI technology development investments
items.quote: You can say that there is an increase of over 10% on a y-o-y basis on the intangible assets.

items.statement: Capital allocation trend from H1 FY2025 to continue for next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: For the next 2-3 quarters, this is the go-to trend. What you have seen in H1 is going to be a trend for next 2-3 quarters.

items.statement: India and Global Emerging Markets contributed 73.4% of Q2 revenue growing 25.3% y-o-y
items.quote: India and Global Emerging Markets, together contributed 73.4% to our revenue in Q2 FY2025, and grew by 25.3% y-o-y.

items.statement: Developed Markets grew 27.5% y-o-y contributing 26.6% of Q2 revenue
items.quote: In Q2 FY2025, we saw a robust growth of 27.5% y-o-y in Developed Markets, which contributed 26.6% to our quarterly revenues.

items.statement: October showed strong momentum heading into festive quarter
items.quote: With respect to the ongoing festive quarter, the month of October has already gone by where we saw a strong momentum.

items.statement: CPCU revenue grew 35.2% y-o-y to Rs. 5,416 million with 95 million conversions at Rs. 57.1 CPCU rate
items.quote: Our CPCU business delivered about 95 million conversions during the Affle (India) Limited November 11, 2024 3 quarter, at a CPCU rate of Rs. 57.1 that helped us achieve a CPCU revenue of Rs. 5,416 million, an increase of 35.2% y-o-y and 4.6% q-o

items.statement: Non-CPCU business has graduated to CPCU model as part of strategic focus
items.quote: Even when we had the non-CPCU business, I had always provided such guidance that we expect this business to graduate to becoming the CPCU business.

items.statement: CPCU pricing expected to keep inching upwards through competitive bidding and premium inventory
items.quote: We are looking at this in a balanced way, and we believe that the CPCU pricing will continue to move in the right direction. It will keep inching upwards as we have already done over the last many years.

items.statement: At least 10-15% of inventory cost is forward-looking for predicting non-shopper conversion potential
items.quote: I would not quantify it today, but I would say at least 10% to 15% of the cost is forward-looking.

items.statement: Competitive advantage in emerging markets from best local teams vs global competitors' one-off country directors
items.quote: We bring in our best people on the ground in all the emerging markets, whereas most of these other, global companies listed in US or in Europe are focused on developed markets and their best people are fighting the battles in developed markets.

items.statement: Antitrust and data privacy regulations strengthening non-walled garden platforms like Affle
items.quote: A lot of these antitrust or data privacy related regulations are strengthening the non-walled gardens. Platforms like Affle would actually benefit much more.

items.statement: Future acquisitions will target full integration within first year and 20% EBITDA margin
items.quote: We feel confident that we can absolutely achieve full integration within 1st year of any acquisition, make sure that we bring the acquired business to similar levels of profitability of about 20% EBITDA or so within the first year.

items.statement: Appointed one new Independent Director with phased transition plan for three directors completing tenure next year
items.quote: We have also appointed one new Independent Director to the Company's Board in India. With 3 of our 5 Independent Directors completing their tenure next year, we have ensured a phased transition plan to further strengthen our governance.

items.statement: Operating cash flow to PAT ratio of 81.7% in H1 FY2025
items.quote: Our Operating cashflows for H1 was Rs. 1,459 million, with an OCF-to-PAT ratio of 81.7%.

items.statement: No material changes in collection risk with continued focus on efficient working capital management
items.quote: We continue to prioritize efficient working capital management and as such there were no material changes in the collection risk.

items.statement: RMG segment evolved with calibrated growth path after regulatory shake-up
items.quote: Sometimes you need a bit of shake up to settle things back, and then have a more robust foundation to build upon and I think that is what has happened in the RMG segment.

items.statement: Granted two US patents for live stream interactions and user identification optimization
items.quote: During the quarter, we were granted two additional patents in the US related to 1) Enabling user interactions with live streams such as a podcast via machine learning; and 2) Optimizing user identification through IDs, thus enabling high-quality consumer engagements.

items.statement: Filed 15 GenAI-related patent applications for long-term roadmap
items.quote: We have then distilled that into 15 unique intellectual property patent applications related to GenAI which we have already filed.

items.statement: Subsidiaries achieved ISO 27001:2022 certification for information security management
items.quote: Affle's subsidiaries have achieved ISO 27001:2022 certification underpinning our proactive implementation of robust data security controls and excellence in our Information Security Management System.

items.statement: E-commerce, fintech, and gaming are strongest verticals across geographies with case studies in India, Brazil, Indonesia, and US
items.quote: In categories E, we see e-commerce as the leading vertical; in category F, we see fintech; in category G, we see gaming. So these are the three verticals. items.statement: Over 70% of business is direct-to-customers/advertisers with agencies as strategic partners
items.quote: If you look at our direct -to-customers business, over 70% business is direct to the customer s / advertisers. Agencies are important strategic partners & channels and we have a good balance

items.statement: GenAI implementation optimizing operating costs and improving employee productivity for margin expansion
items.quote: We are also seeing a lot of GenAI implementation and optimization of our operating cost. As our revenue grows, we will see some efficiencies of GenAI on our operating expenses as we don't have to increase our operating cost in line to the revenue growth.

items.statement: Aiming for around Rs 1,400 crore revenue in FY25
items.quote: This financial year, it is difficult to touch 1,500 crores, we are aiming around 1,400 crores this year.

items.statement: Expect 25-30% top-line growth in FY26
items.quote: The top line, we can expect around 25% to 30% growth for the next financial year.

items.statement: Target to maintain current EBITDA margin in FY26
items.quote: Yes, we'll try our best to maintain current EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Total capex of Rs 400-450 crore by end of FY25 for Sarigam and Saykha

items.statement: Additional Rs 50-60 crore capex planned for FY26, then only maintenance capex
items.quote: For the next year, I think as it was already mentioned, there's around 50 to 60 crores worth of CAPEX will be done in the next financial year, that is FY'26. After that there will be no CAPEX, only maintenance related CAPEX.

items.statement: Sarigam Phase-I (6,000-7,000 tons) started in Q2 FY25; Phase-II (3,000-4,000 tons) by Q4 FY25; Saykha Phase-I (4,000-5,000 tons) expected in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Sarigam phase-I will be around 6,000 to 7,000 tons and Sarigam-II will be around 3,000 to 4,000 tons. Almost total capacity for Sarigam will be around 9,000 to 10,000 tons. Saykha first phase will be having a capacity around 4,000 to 5,000 tons.

items.statement: Order book of 1-2 months for majority of products
items.quote: Yes, it is picking up and we have almost booked for one or two months order booking is there for majority of our products.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 14% vs 7% in H1 FY24; margins normalized to historical 15-18% range

items.statement: Rating agency upgrade discussions in process; will update when finalized

items.statement: Q3 expected to be strong with festive and wedding season demand across all segments

So if I talk about last year Q2 to last year Q3, you can easily see that Q3 had produced more revenue than Q2, but margins were higher in Q2.

items.statement: No significant inventory loss from duty cut due to weighted average accounting; book value supported prices

So, in general, you know, our book, there was a sudden decrease in, you know, custom duty, but that has not impacted the books to the greater extent.

items.statement: Revenue split 50% sale of goods (retail+wholesale), 50% sale of services; volume mix 70-75% B2B, 25-30% retail
items.quote: So, jewellery sales of retail, when you talk about sale of goods, jewellery sales of retail and wholesale is 50%. And when you talk about volumes, we are 70% to 75% driven into B2B market. And 25% to 30% driven for retail market.

items.statement: Organized retailers' Q1 weakness deferred demand to Q2-Q3; now seeing strong walk-ins and wholesale demand
items.quote: We have got good load in job work that is sale of services right now in hand. Walk -ins in retail stores are very promising. We have strong walk -ins. There is a good demand in wholesale.

We have not done that kilos because 30%, 25% price of gold went up. So, we will be doing perhaps 1300 kilos or so. So, I mean, we do have a capacity in hand. We should be very, the timing of the expansion has to be very right. I think after this, I think in th

items.statement: Adding 3,000 sq ft retail floor space in Q3 FY25; flagship store capacity supports INR500-600 crore revenue
items.quote: Right now we have expanded, like in the Q3 we will be expanding one more floor in retail of 3000 square feet. Retail is growing at the right pace. Around 35% -40% or plus is the retail growth right now.

items.statement: No fundraising planned this year; focus on delivering committed performance

We are seeing a very strong transformation happening in the industry. And we have got

items.statement: Heavy investment in HR resources and team building; added SAP for financial integrity
items.quote: Apart from this, the company has invested heavily in HR resources and team building and we are moving on a much stronger path ahead. The fundamentals of the company are intact and we are building brick by brick, be it team, be it resources, be it infrastructure.

items.statement: H1 volume 542 kg vs ~580 kg last year; retail+wholesale volume up 25-30% YoY
items.quote: I think this year, I think sale of services volumes has got impacted. Retail and wholesale volumes are positive in numbers. On an environment basis, we have done around 542 kg this year versus around, I think, around 580 plus kgs last year. And I think tha t is just because of impact of sale of services. Otherwise, retail volumes and wholesale volumes, both are heavily positive to the tune of 25%

items.statement: Gold price volatility and geopolitical uncertainty may confuse customers; wedding demand is need-based
items.quote: We are in a volatile market. I agree that being an occasion jewellery player, what you are quoting is the bang on opportunity for us. We are not into daily wear. We are more into occasion wear. An d this is a big opportunity for us. But still, the market is very volatile. Because of external geopolitical environment, sometimes the gold prices rises up and it comes down and it confuses the customer

items.statement: Revenue grew 57% YoY in Q2 (INR74 cr to INR116 cr); H1 revenue growth positive
items.quote: We have just concluded our quarter two results and we are happy to announce that the revenue growth of the company on Y -o-Y basis is around 57% from last year's INR74 crores to this year's INR116 crores and then Q1 41% from INR82 crores to INR116 crores. Half yearly growth has also shown positive in terms of revenue.

items.statement: Telecom infrastructure is a 10% long-term growth industry; EV charging expected to grow 30-40% CAGR over next five years
items.quote: telecom on a longer-term basis is a 10% growth rate business. That is for telecom towers and infrastructure, and roughly, we may be a little bit higher. But generally speaking, on a longer-term basis, everybody would converge to that growth rate. And on EV charging, the growth rate is about 30% to 40% on a CAGR basis for the next five years.

items.statement: BharatNet and other government projects expected to provide multi-year order book for Critical Power
items.quote: BharatNet is a telecom infrastructure opportunity, which is a program by government through BSNL to connect 160,000 panchayats through fiber and yes, through fiber by for giving broadband. While there are Tier 1 system integrators who are bidding this project but this project requires very – a lot of power solutions as well as batteries to make this infrastructure live. items.statement: IPO proceeds of INR400 crore being used for integrated Hyderabad plant; INR174 crore utilized, INR225 crore remaining
items.quote: During the IPO which we had in March of '24, which was a very successful IPO, we raised about INR400 crore as primary capital for the company. CARE has been monitoring the use of IPO funds and we are absolutely on target. Total amount utilized till the period is about INR174 crores and unutilized amount is INR225 crores. Most of this amount has been utilized in our upcoming integrated manufacturin

items.statement: New 18-acre Hyderabad plant will manufacture Critical Power, EV chargers, and lithium-ion batteries for stationary applications
items.quote: This is about 18 acre complex, where we are building production facilities to manufacture both our critical power and EV charging product line, as well as lithium-ion batteries for stationary applications.

items.statement: EV industry saw 13% QoQ decline in H1 due to wait for new models; recovered in October with Tata Curvv and MG Windsor launches
items.quote: So, this was the primary reason for H1 slowdown that saw 13% reduction in quarter-over-quarter sales of electric cars while buses still remain steady based on the government, based on the government subsidies which are being provided. In quarter three, since now the market has picked up again, we see a lot of momentum beginning earlier this quarter itself for all components in the electric vehicle

items.statement: INR425 crore debt taken in H1 solely for Tritium acquisition
items.quote: I see that we have took, a considerable amount of debt around INR425 crores in the past half year. Was it for the acquisition or was it for some other reason? Anant Nahata: No, only for acquisition.

items.statement: Critical Power diversifying into cooling solutions, 2W EV charger building blocks, and data center batteries with successful pilots
items.quote: There are also diversification strategies which are beginning to manifest in Critical Power. They range from providing cooling system solutions for use in telecom to providing building blocks for two wheeler EV chargers to providing data center batteries. Pilot in all these areas have been successfully demonstrated and our teams are working hard to build pipeline and to build sales in these areas

items.statement: Lithium-ion battery conversion from lead-acid now default for tower companies; Exicom has high market share
items.quote: One year ago -- two years ago, we had to convince people to buy lithium-ion. One year ago, people were convinced and started to make the switch. Today, by default, the procurement is of lithium-ion batteries only, with the price point and the economic life cycle that it has. So that's again an area where we are seeing very good market share with leading tower companies.

items.statement: Continuous price erosion in EV charging industry; protected margins through indigenous design and technology ownership
items.quote: And even with continuous price erosion, which happens in the Indian market, it's happening in the EV charging industry at quite a striking rate. We have been able to protect the margins, which is a very good thing. It shows our capability to put indigenous design and ownership of technology at work to protect our margins compared to our peers.

items.statement: Finance costs increased due to Tritium acquisition funding; previous year had CCD conversion to equity before IPO
items.quote: And some of the finance expenses have gone up as compared to previous quarter. But if you see from previous year, previous year we decreased because we had converted the CCD into equity, before the public issue that had come in. This quarter we had to raise funds to acquire or invest into Tritium, and that's why there has been a little bit of finance cost that has come in.

items.statement: Continued investment in talent with new hires and increments increasing manpower costs
items.quote: We've continued to invest in our employee and talent and we've hired new talent along with giving increments. So there is an increase in the cost on the manpower that you have seen.

items.statement: Tritium integration will take about a year; acquired from insolvency requiring supplier/customer trust rebuilding
items.quote: It will take about a year's time to fully get this company integrated and let's say, up back again to be able to compete in the global market. But we see a huge value accretion in revenue, in profitability over course of 5-6 years, as we take our ambitions forward not only in India, but on a global scale.

items.statement: Monthly transacting buyers grew 6% YoY to over 28,400 in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: Overall, we saw a YoY growth of 6% on our monthly transacting buyers and we had more than 28,400 buyers, travel agents buying from us on the platform in this quarter.

items.statement: GTV grew 24% YoY to nearly Rs. 8,000 Cr in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: GTV grew very strongly by 24% YoY to hit almost Rs. 8,000 Cr.

items.statement: Revenue grew 28% YoY in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: Revenue grew by 28% and G P grew by 35%.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 24% YoY in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: On the whole, compared to Q2 of last year, our EBITDA has grown by 24% and t here is similar growth for H1 as well.

items.statement: Hotels drove 59% of GTV, 79% of revenue, and 84% of gross profit in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: The big highlight for this quarter has been the increasing saliency of the hotels business. 59% of GTV was driven by hotels. This corresponded to 79% of revenue being driven by the hotels and non- air business and 84% of our gross profit is now driven by the hotels and non-air business.

items.statement: Active agents grew 6% YoY and active bookers grew 9% YoY in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: Our active agent base grew by 6% compared to the same quarter last year. Our active bookers grew by 9% , which is a promising metric, and we talked about it in the past as well.

items.statement: Hotel monthly transacting buyers grew 13% YoY; international hotel buyers grew 26% YoY in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: So, this number is up by 13% on a YoY basis. If you look at the growth in the international market, which is source markets other than India, this growth is actually quite steep at 26%.

items.statement: Hotel GTV grew 56% YoY (India 9%, international 64%) in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: Similarly, the GTV growth in hotels is at an enterprise level is 56% , 9% growth in India as a source market and 64% growth in the international source markets which includes Jumbonline as well.

items.statement: Hotel revenue grew 36% YoY; hotel gross profit grew 48% YoY in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: The revenue grew by 36% and again you would see a very sharp growth of almost 40% in revenue in the international source markets and a 48% increase in hotels' gross profit.

items.statement: H-Next platform coverage expanded from 3% to 13% of international users with better engagement and conversion.
items.quote: We expanded coverage to now 13% of our users and overall, we are seeing better engagement metrics and better conversion metrics on this platform.

items.statement: AI-driven dynamic pricing rolled out to 25% of international wholesale customers showing promising take-rate improvement.
items.quote: Right now , it is rolled out for 25% of our wholesale customers or enterprise customers in the international source markets and we've seen promising results. Also, we've seen some improvement in our take rate for this cohort.

items.statement: LLM voice bots handled 7,000 calls with 60% success rate matching or exceeding human outcomes.
items.quote: So, we've done about 7,000 calls in the last couple of weeks since this rollout, and what we've seen is a 60% success rate, which essentially means that in 60% of these 7,000 calls, the outcome was similar or better to what would be the outcome if a human being was making that call.

items.statement: Jumbonline integration fast-tracked by one year; completed November 1, 2024 instead of November 1, 2025.
items.quote: Now, given the promise that the project is showing, we have fast-tracked this integration by a full year. So, the integration that was supposed to be completed by 1st November 2025 has been fast -tracked and completed by 1st November of this year.

items.statement: Jumbonline contributes 8.5% of enterprise GTV and 7.6% of enterprise revenue in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: The business has shown meaningful growth in the last 12 months and now contributes almost 8.5% of our enterprise GTV and 7.6% of our revenue.

items.statement: Revenue from operations reached Rs. 450.7 Cr, up 27.9% YoY in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: Our revenue from operations reached Rs. 450.7 Cr, up 27.9% YoY.

items.statement: Enterprise take rate improved from 5.51% to 5.68% YoY in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: Our enterprise take rate improved from 5.51% to 5.68% YoY.

items.statement: Airline take rate rose from 2.46% to 2.6% YoY; hotel take rate declined from 8.67% to 7.59% YoY due to Jumbonline consolidation.
items.quote: Breaking this down further, the airline business take rate rose from 2.46% to 2.6% while the take rate for the hotels and ancillary services saw a decline from 8.67% to 7.59% YoY, primarily due to the consolidation of Jumbo numbers.

items.statement: Gross profit as percentage of GTV improved from 3.54% to 3.86% YoY in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: Gross profit as a percentage of GTV for the quarter improved from 3.54% to 3.86% on a YoY basis.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA reached Rs. 89.6 Cr, up 24.5% YoY; EBITDA margin 19.89% in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: On the profitability front, adjusted EBITDA reached Rs. 89.6 Cr representing a 24.5% YoY growth while Profit after Tax came in at Rs. 60.1 Cr showing a 7.1% increase over the previous year. For the quarter, our adjusted EBITDA margin stood at 19.89% and PAT margins as 13.33%.

items.statement: H1 FY25 adjusted EBITDA Rs. 174.7 Cr, up 23.9% YoY; EBITDA margin 20.1%.
items.quote: For the first half of the year, adjusted EBITDA reached 174.7 Cr up 23.9% YoY and PAT totaled at Rs. 121 Cr reflecting a 17% increase. Our adjusted EBITDA margin for H1 stood at 20.1% and PAT margin at 13.92%.

items.statement: Working capital remains negative; cash and bank balances Rs. 1,372.8 Cr as of September 30, 2024.
items.quote: Notably, our working capital continues to remain negative. Our cash and bank balances are also strong, standing at Rs. 1,372.8 Cr as of September 30th, 2024.

items.statement: International GTV growth secular; Europe now largest source market; expect growth momentum to continue into Q3 FY25.
items.quote: We've seen the commentary from other players on some headwinds in the market. I think while the macroeconomic picture is clear, there is geopolitical stress in certain markets, some of our source markets as well. Here we just want to reiterate what we said last time as wel l, ultimately, our business is aggregating existing demand. So, we are hoping that we will be able to continue to grow until u

items.statement: Management aims to maintain take rates; EBITDA growth via operating leverage not take-rate expansion.

We are a platform business so any significant increase in take rate is often at the expense of our travel age nt partners. So, generally, the view remains that we try and maintain our take rates where they are. The whole thesis is that EBITDA should grow via operating leverage not from take rate expansi
