items.quote: I think at the moment, we've already put in money into both the derivatives as well as the Oren Hydrocarbons acquisition and our main plant in Rann of Kutch. I think we don't anticipate too much capex in these businesses even after March '25.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 standalone EBITDA margin at 36% with EBITDA of INR 898 million
items.quote: EBITDA for the company stood at around INR898 million for this quarter, Q2, with a margin of 36% and net profit stood at around INR219 million.

items.statement: H1 FY25 standalone EBITDA margin at 37% with EBITDA of INR 1,747 million
items.quote: EBITDA for the company stood at around INR1,747 million for the 6 months period with a margin at 37%.

items.statement: Bromine demand recovering in domestic market while export market remains soft; China stimulus expected to gradually improve demand
items.quote: It has been somewhat of a mixed quarter for the company as we have seen some broad recovery on the demand side, primarily from the domestic market, whereas demand from export market remains a bit soft. We expect steady demand in the bromine business with end-use applications either stable or recovering. With the recent stimulus in the Chinese market, we foresee China economy to pick up gradually a

items.statement: Two Oren Hydrocarbons plants expected to be fully operational within next few weeks with meaningful contributions from Q4 FY25
items.quote: We expect two plants to be fully operational within the next few weeks with meaningful business contributions than anticipated from the Q4 of this financial year.

items.statement: SOP trials encouraging with second grade production underway; expect meaningful contributions next year
items.quote: On the SOP side, we continue to see encouraging results in our trials, and we have also taken steps to produce a second grade of Sulphate of Potash, which we're seeing encouraging inquiries from both global and domestic markets. At present, there's a work-in-progress, and we expect meaningful contributions in the next year.

items.statement: New domestic bromine capacity expansions expected in 2-3 years; company differentiating through value-enhanced chemistries and derivatives
items.quote: While the local other players expand, I think part of our derisking and diversification into further value-enhanced chemistries and products, I think this was envisaged a couple of years ago, which is what we have implemented. So I think I credit the management team and also our on-the-ground site team for implementing these projects. And I think this will probably add to our strength and distingu

items.statement: SiC wafer fab project plan submitted to government for incentives; return ratios dependent on approval outcome
items.quote: We have submitted it to government and waiting for the necessary approvals. So a lot of that will depend on what quantum of the government incentives, et cetera, we get, which will have an impact on the return ratios. So we will definitely answer the return ratios once we get the clarity on the approval process.

items.statement: Investing GBP 15 million (GBP 10 million primary, GBP 5 million secondary) for 21.33% stake in Clas-SIC Wafer Fab Limited UK
items.quote: Our company will be investing to the tune of GBP 15 million for a 21.33% equity share capital with a primary subscription of GBP 10 million and secondary purchase of GBP 5 million.

items.statement: Investing nearly USD 12 million in Series A for 21% stake in Offgrid Energy Labs Inc. Delaware US
items.quote: We will invest nearly USD12 million in series A fund for the subscription of 21% stake.

items.statement: Oren Hydrocarbons acquisition completed with NCLT order in July 2024; refurbishing plants for specialty mud chemicals and CBF products
items.quote: After receiving the NCLT order in the month of July '24, our team has been actively working on refurbishments and renovations at various production sites of the company. We expect two plants to be fully operational within the next few weeks with meaningful business contributions than anticipated from the Q4 of this financial year.

items.statement: Mr. Kannan joined as Executive Director responsible for all initiatives including parent company and subsidiaries
items.quote: Mr. Kannan has joined as Executive Director in Archean Chemical Industries, which is a parent company for all the subsidiaries that we talked about today. So the broad mandate for him is leading and being responsible for all these initiatives, including the primary company, Archean Chemical Industries.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 salt sales volume 792,000 tons vs 976,000 tons previous year; bromine sales ~4,800 tons; SOP sales ~27 tons
items.quote: For this quarter, Q2, the sale of salt is around 792,000 versus 976 in the previous year's quarter. And with respect to bromine, it's on 4,800 plus. Krishan Parwani: 4,800. Okay. SOP is nil? Raghunathan: SOP is at around

items.statement: Salt logistics mix: 92% FOB, 5-8% CIF basis
items.quote: CIF is 5% to 8%, and almost 92% really on FOB basis.

items.statement: Cyclone Asna caused loss of 472,000 metric tons of industrial salt worth INR 40.18 crores; insurance claim initiated
items.quote: We reported an exceptional item due to the impact of Asna cyclone in Gujarat that occurred in the month of August and in the beginning of September. So almost it prevailed for more than a week or so, which resulted in a loss of 472,000 metric tons of Industrial Salt, which amounts to around INR40.18 crores. We have initiated a necessary claim process with respective insurance companies.

items.statement: Flame retardant project delayed but not derailed; measured approach prioritizing return on capital for current initiatives first
items.quote: I think it's a commercial call. It's not derailed for sure. I think it's delayed, as I mentioned, I think on the previous calls as well. It's easy to always put capital, but I think we want to take a measured approach. As someone else asked earlier on the call, it's about return on capital invested. So we already have a couple of initiatives going on. We would like to first deliver on these.

items.statement: Urban discretionary demand slowdown due to inflation and cost of living; temporary disruptions in Karnataka and Delhi impacted Q2 revenues
items.quote: we are witnessing a temporary slowdown in consumer demand across discretionary categories including alcoholic beverages, particularly within urban India, which does represent more than 90% of Sula's customer base.

items.statement: Karnataka excise policy changes caused retailer hesitancy; situation mostly stabilized with sales recovery underway
items.quote: in Karnataka, retailers were initially hesitant to stock up due to recent changes in the exercise policy, which introduced pricing uncertainty. This situation has since mostly stabilized after clarity came in from the state authorities, and we have started seeing already a recovery in sales there.

items.statement: Delhi excise portal offline for most of second half of September during migration to in-house management, impacting shipments
items.quote: In Delhi, the excise portal was offline for much of the second half of September as they migrated from external management to in-house management of the portal, and which impacted sales during this transition. We were, in fact, unable to ship goods for most of the second half of September in this very important market.

items.statement: Elite and premium portfolio grew 7% YoY with double-digit gains in iconic brands; economy and popular down 18%
items.quote: Our elite and premium portfolio performed well given the current market backdrop, recording 7% growth , with double-digit gains across some of our iconic elite brands such as The Source, which I would like to say has been a particular success for us, RASA and Dindori.

items.statement: Share of elite and premium in own brands improved 500 bps to all-time high of 78.5% in Q2
items.quote: Share of elite and premium in our own brands improved 500 basis points, reaching an all-time high of 78.5% in quarter two.

items.statement: Revenue excluding Maharashtra and Karnataka grew 6% YoY, powered by Telangana with 59% growth and high double-digit growth in Himachal, MP, Chandigarh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal
items.quote: Revenue excluding our top two states of Maharashtra and Karnataka grew 6% Y-o-Y. This growth was powered chiefly by Telangana, with Himachal, MP, Chandigarh, Uttarakhand, and West Bengal, among others, also seeing high double -digit growth.

items.statement: Telangana, the third-largest market, grew more than 50% in Q2
items.quote: Telangana, our third -largest market, particularly stood out as a bright spot with more than 50% growth in Q2.

items.statement: Shifted to third-party sales model for economy and popular brands in Maharashtra starting Mumbai and Pune in Q1; rolling out to rest of Maharashtra with plan to move entire popular and economy to third party by Q1 FY26
items.quote: we decided to shift to a third -party sales model for our economy and popular brands in Maharashtra, starting with Mumbai and Pune in Q1. The early results of this have been extremely encouraging, and we have started rolling out this strategy in the rest of Maharashtra, with a plan to move our entire popular and economy to the third party by Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Wine tourism faced challenges from road infrastructure deterioration and surge in outbound travel to Thailand and Vietnam; inbound travel not keeping pace
items.quote: Our wine tourism business also faced challenges during the quarter due to deterioration in road infrastructure and also a surge in outbound travel. A lot of our people have been traveling to foreign countries, particularly I would highlight Thailand and Vietnam with their very easy travel policies, and with extremely easy and cheap flights available today from almost every Indian city.

items.statement: Wine tourism occupancy improved to 74% vs 66% last year; spend per head up 9% YoY offsetting lower footfalls
items.quote: On the wine tourism front, we saw moderate growth in quarter two, supported by improved occupancy of 74% versus 66% last year, and increase in spend per head by 9% Y-o-Y, which helped to offset the impact of lower footfalls.

items.statement: Pan-India tastings up 6% in Q2 to over 50,000, an all-time high for Q2
items.quote: And pan-India tastings are up 6% in Q2 to over 50,000, so an all-time high for Q2.

items.statement: New expanded Dindori Tasting Room and Bottle Shop at erstwhile ND Wines now open; strategically located <50 km from Gujarat border
items.quote: our new expanded Dindori Tasting Room and Bottle Shop is now open to visitors at the erstwhile ND Wines. This facility, as some of you might be aware, is strategically located less than 50 kilometers from the Gujarat border.

items.statement: Expansion of wine tourism facilities at Domaine Sula near Bangalore slated to complete in Q3 with new tasting room and vineyard view
items.quote: the ongoing expansion of our wine tourism facilities at Domaine Sula near Bangalore is slated to complete in Q3. So, we have a beautiful new tasting room there with a beautiful vineyard view, a bit akin to our facility in Nashik, which was a bit lacking until now.

items.statement: 30-key resort coming up near York Winery in Nashik in FY26, expanding total room capacity by 30% from 104 to 134 keys with convention facilities
items.quote: next year in FY '26 we have the 30 -key resort coming up near our York Winery in Nashik, which will expand our total room capacity by 30% from 104 keys to 134 keys. And as I have mentioned previously, this will also have convention facilities for the first time on a much larger scale than what we have been able to offer so far.

items.statement: Expect wine tourism expansions and SulaFest to boost H2 performance; targeting return to healthy growth from Q4, from December onwards
items.quote: we expect these expansions, along with the upcoming SulaFest, to provide a boost to our wine tourism business and contribute positively to H2 performance. And in particular, we are looking to return to healthy growth from Q4, in fact, from December onwards.

items.statement: Reopening Andhra Pradesh after 5-year hiatus with progressive excise policy; targeting first shipment in Q3
items.quote: We are really concentrating hard on getting it out there within Q3 itself. So, at least it will give us a nice little boost in Q3 itself, because we will be going into a totally empty state in terms of wine.

items.statement: Introducing four new brands in CSD (Canteen Stores Department) including Dindori Reserve Shiraz, Source Grenache Rose, Sula Vineyards Riesling, RASA Syrah; almost doubling brands in CSD
items.quote: We will be seeing the introduction of four more brands in CSD. CSD, I should point out, has shown very strong growth over the last 18 months or so. And we will be introducing four new brands, including our Dindori Reserve Shiraz and also our Source Grenach e Rose, our Sula Vineyards Riesling, and our RASA Syrah.

items.statement: Resuming shipments to BSF after eight months; BSF performed well in H1 FY24
items.quote: We are also resuming shipments to BSF after eight months. And BSF did incredibly well for us in the first half of FY '24. So, it was a shame that due to some administrative issues we were not able to be present. We are now getting back in there, and we will get the benefit of that in H2.

items.statement: Gross margins at 74%, up 78 bps YoY supported by higher elite and premium share; gross profit flat at Rs 104 crores
items.quote: Our gross margins stood at 74%, 78 basis points better versus last year, supported by higher share of elite and premium. Gross profit stood flat at Rs. 104 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA decreased 24% to Rs 34 crores due to increased market spending impacting profitability amid muted sales growth
items.quote: Continuing on, our EBITDA for quarter two decreased by 24% to Rs. 34 crores as increased market spending impacted profitability in a period of muted sales growth.

items.statement: Total borrowings grew from Rs 260 crores to Rs 330 crores YoY due to higher receivables; Telangana's higher DSO primary factor but collections improved 2.5x QoQ
items.quote: Total borrowings grew from Rs. 260 crores in September '23 to Rs. 330 crores as of September 2024. The higher utilization of working capital was driven by an increase in receivables. A significant rise in revenue contribution from Telangana, which has a relatively higher DSO, was the primary factor behind the increase in receivables. However, the collection situation in Telangana has significantly

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA comfortable at 1.8x, well below internal benchmark of 2x
items.quote: While borrowing has increased, our net debt -to-EBITDA continues to be comfortable at 1.8x, well below our own benchmark of 2x.

items.statement: WIPS receivable was Rs 73 crores as of 1 April 2024; Rs 20 crores accrued in H1, Rs 10 crores from unwinding; received Rs 10 crores in July and Rs 22 crores in October, bringing balance to Rs 73 crores; expect to realize balance in FY25
items.quote: Our outstanding WIPS balance, which is the Wine Industry Promotion Scheme, as of 1 April, '24, was Rs. 73 crores, with Rs. 20 crores being accrued during H1 and Rs. 10 crores led by the unwinding of the previous accumulated WIPS. We subsequently received Rs. 10 crores in July 2024, taking the WIPS receivable in our balance sheet to Rs. 94 crores. We are happy to report that we received a further p

items.statement: COO Karan Vasani resigned for personal reasons, moving on in December after 11 years; smooth handover underway
items.quote: Karan Vasani, our COO, has resigned for personal reasons and will be moving on in December. I would like to take this opportunity to express my sincere thanks to Karan. We greatly appreciate all his contributions to the success of the company over the last 11 years, first as Chief Winemaker, and then for the past year as COO.

items.statement: Anant Iyer joins Board as Independent Director; currently Director General of CIABC with 40 years alcobev experience
items.quote: I would like to warmly welcome Anant Iyer who joins our Board as an Independent Director. Anant is currently the Director General of CIABC or the Confederation of Indian Alcoholic Beverage Companies . And he comes with a vast experience of 40 years working in senior roles in alcobev companies and will definitely be adding a lot of value to the Sula Board.

items.statement: FTA with Australia signed with reductions on wines above certain price threshold; negotiations ongoing; government cognizant of wine as sunrise agro-based farmer-friendly industry
items.quote: an early FTA was signed with Australia in which there was some reduction on wines above a certain price threshold. FTA negotiations are still going on. I mean, Australia is probably the most likely to have the second comprehensive FTA signed fairly soon. We very much have a seat at the table, and we are watching it closely.

items.statement: On wines above $15 CIF, tax may come down to 25%; above $5 CIF to 50%; below $5 CIF remains at 150%
items.quote: On wines now above $15, I think tax is going to come down as low as 25%. On wines above $5, please note, these are CIF p rices, tax is going to come down as low as 50%. But for wines below that right now, below $5 CIF, it's 150%. It remains at the 150% threshold.

items.statement: Unsustainable discounting by competitors in Maharashtra impacting net sales; market lacks depth to withstand; hope for return to normalcy
items.quote: there have also been, I would say, some kind of unsustainable discounting by some of our competitors. Unfortunately, the market does not have the kind of depth to allow it to easily withstand this. So, there is a fair amount of wine that has been produced, which is unfortunately being discounted in the market. That has very much impacted, because you see the sales in Maharashtra, we report them ne

items.statement: Successfully transitioned from SAP ECC6 to cloud-based S/4 HANA via brownfield implementation in 5 months, well below standard time; transaction processing nearly 40% faster with real-time analytics
items.quote: We successfully transitioned from SAP ECC6 to cloud-based S/4 HANA through a brownfield implementation, which was completed in a d five months well lower than standard implementation time. This upgrade will enhance operational efficiency, enabling transaction processing to be nearly 40% faster and improving access to real -time analytics, positioning us to make more data-driven decisions with grea

items.statement: SulaFest returning in February 2025 after 5 years as wine and beer festival (no spirits); likely biennial event
items.quote: We come back after five long years due to overwhelming popular demand. This was a festival that was much loved and had grown into being one of India's iconic festivals. We had to shut down due to COVID. And for various reasons, after that, we decided not to restart. But now we do believe the time is right. It will be coming back in a slightly different avatar. I should point out that SulaFest 2020

items.statement: Target revenue less service cost margin of ~20% by summer next year (next three quarters)
items.quote: So by summer of next year, we should be looking at this number getting to about 20%.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin on revenue less service cost is ~15% this quarter
items.quote: This INR13.6 crores of adjusted EBITDA margin is on INR93 crores of revenue less service cost, which is almost a 15% margin.

items.statement: Long-term hotel & packages gross margin expected to settle at 9-10%
items.quote: Over the next three years, given that the business would be largely focused on corporate and mice, I would expect this number to be range bound between nin e and 10

items.statement: Onboarded 29 new corporate clients with INR1.2B annual billing potential
items.quote: In the second quarter of FY25, we onboarded 29 new corporate clients, collectively adding an annual billing potential of INR1.2 billion.

items.statement: Acquired Globe Travels for INR1.28B cash; adds 360 corporate clients and INR470M adjusted revenue at >30% EBITDA margin
items.quote: On September 11th, 2024, we completed the acquisition of Globe for INR1.28 billion in cash.

items.statement: Identified INR60M annual synergies from Globe acquisition; expect to realize slightly ahead of target
items.quote: As part of the combination of Yatra and Globe, we had identified synergies of approximately INR60 million per year. And as we move forward, we expect that we should be able to realize synergies slightly ahead of this initial target.

items.statement: Corporate air volumes growing healthy double-digits; B2C air volumes stabilized and gradually increasing
items.quote: We continue to see healthy double-digit plus kind of volume growth on the air ticketing side on the corporate front. On the B2C front as well, as I mentioned, we've reached a point where we've been able to stabilize the volumes and the last couple of months we've started seeing a

items.statement: B2B now ~60% of gross bookings; hotels & packages B2B ~65%; air ticketing B2B ~50%
items.quote: So in terms of gross bookings, now almost 60% of our gross bookings are coming from the corporate travel business, from the B2B business.

items.statement: Investing in talent for mid-market, MICE, Visa, expense management; annual appraisal cycle partially impacted Q2
items.quote: Our personal expenses, excluding share-based payment, increased by 20% Y-o-Y as we continue to invest in talent to build out our mid-market, MICE, Visa, expense management, and other businesses. This also includes a partial impact of our annual appraisal cycle.

items.statement: Integrated NDC (New Distribution Capability) for richer booking experience and special fares
items.quote: We've become one of the first travel management companies in India to integrate the new distribution capabilities that the airlines are offering.

items.statement: Globe adds 360 non-overlapping mid-market corporate clients (INR2-5Cr spend) vs Yatra's large corporates (INR25Cr+ avg)
items.quote: Globe's customers will typically be between the INR2 crores to the INR5 crores kind of annual corporate travel spend space, whereas Yatra's customers will be much more closer to like on average about INR25-plus crores.

items.statement: Other current assets up INR57Cr due to vendor advances for MICE business; dissolve as trips complete
items.quote: These are advances given to vendors for our MICE business. So they're recorded as other current assets. They get dissolved as the trip comes to an end and the billing is completed.

items.statement: Cash & equivalents INR2.1B; gross debt INR277M as of Sep 30, 2024
items.quote: Lastly, as of 30th September 2024, we had a cash and cash equivalent term deposits equivalent of about INR2.1 billion on our balance sheet. And we were carrying gross debt of approximately INR277 million.

items.statement: Evaluating Holdco restructuring options; restructuring committee formed in July; announcements due
items.quote: We continue to evaluate options. There was a restructuring committee which was formed in the month of July. And the committee has evaluated certain options. We do, we are working with our consultants, lawyers, e tc. To come up with a structure which is the most optimal structure for the organization and the shareholders. We will make some announcements on that in due course of time

items.statement: ESOP cost INR2.5Cr this quarter (down from INR9.7Cr); expect range-bound going forward
items.quote: The ESOP cost for this quarter is about INR2.5 crores.

items.statement: MICE seasonality: ~30% in Q2 & Q4, ~25% in Q1, ~15% in Q3 due to inventory tightness
items.quote: You would see approximately about 30% happening in Q2 and Q4, and about 25% happening in Q1 and 15% happening in Q3. Because Q3 has the tightest availability in terms of inventory.

items.statement: Q3 earnings expected range-bound; full operating leverage flow-through in Q4
items.quote: As of now, the trending seems to indicate that they shouldn't come off. They should remain range bound to what we had just reported.

items.statement: Legal/professional costs ~INR1.4Cr from Globe acquisition and EasyGo matter; non-recurring
items.quote: The combined effect of all of this would be approximately about INR1.4-odd crores. So that would not be there on an ongoing basis.

items.statement: Revenue less service cost (net revenue) grew 15% YoY organic; Q2 INR93Cr vs Q1 INR80Cr
items.quote: Revenue less service cost grew 15% year-over-year, excluding Globe.

items.statement: Payment gateway cost reduced 15bps to 0.55% of gross bookings
items.quote: Our payment gateway cost as a percentage to gross bookings has reduced by 15 basis points, from 0.7% in year-ago quarter to 0.55% in the current quarter.

items.statement: B2C air faces direct competition from airline websites/apps; stabilized via tech improvements and partnerships (e.g., Swiggy)
items.quote: The B2C business continues to face direct competition from some of the domestic air suppliers who differentiate pricing on their own website and apps. However, despite this competition on the B2C airfront, we've managed to stabilize the volumes and have focused on improving operating performance.

items.statement: Globe gross bookings split: 60% air, 40% hotels & packages
items.quote: In terms of the split of the acquisition between hotels and air, so Globe, again, being a large MICE-focused business, their business is split almost 60% of their gross bookings come from air and 40% of their gross bookings come from hotels and packages.

items.statement: Mid-market segment onboarding ongoing; material revenue impact expected H2 next year
items.quote: My sense is that for it to really start being material, we are looking at this to be maybe, in the second half of next year.

items.statement: Agent-dependent business only 10-12% of gross bookings (5-7% of revenue); unchanged post-Globe
items.quote: So in terms of business dependent on travel agents, that is just about maybe 10%-12% of our overall business. In terms of gross bookings, in terms of revenue, that would be more like 5%-7%. So it's a very, very small part of our overall business. It doesn't change materially post the acquisition of Globe either.

items.statement: Management expects gradual recovery over next few quarters, not sudden return to growth path in Q3
items.quote: So, our entire focus is on that. That's said we expect the recovery to be gradual and not sudden when it comes to sort of getting back on the growth path that you talked about.

items.statement: Urban consumption patterns changing, visible shift in consumer buying behavior
items.quote: There clearly seems to be some form or change in terms of consumer buying in patterns which are visible, but we genuinely want to see that and understand that as a structural change.

items.statement: Medium-term high double-digit EBITDA margin target for Mamaearth unchanged despite short-term investment skew
items.quote: But our view on being able to get to a high double -digit in the medium term for ME continues to hold strongly.

items.statement: Focus categories (face cleansing, serum, sunscreen) grew 28% in H1 FY25; aim to extend to 5-6 categories in next 3-4 quarters
items.quote: Our three strongest categories where we have the best shares and ambition also is the strongest in those 2-3 categories which is face cleansing, serum, and sunscreen have actually demonstrated 28% growth in half one.

items.statement: Investing in R&D capabilities and partnerships to make hero products beat competition in blind testing across focus categories
items.quote: Our objective here would be that we build capabilities that in all our focus categories, our hero products actually beat the competition in blind testing and that's an area where a few of our products are already

items.statement: Offline GTM transformation (Project Neev) underway; 70% of ward cells have distributors deployed, remaining 30% to be covered in 3-4 months
items.quote: Currently, in about 70% of them, we have been able to deploy distributors but there are at least 30% of the ward cells where we are still deploying distributors and that will happen over the next three to four months.

items.statement: Offline ASPs 20-25% higher than competitors, offering retailers higher margins and bill value per transaction
items.quote: One, of course, as you premiumize a category in our ASPs, in almost all categories are higher by 20% to 25%. And that gives the retailer higher bill value per transaction.

items.statement: Mamaearth investment too wide across 10+ categories; narrowing focus to few hero SKUs and categories for deeper penetration
items.quote: we realized that we were allocating our investments over 10 different categories in Mamaeart h and that was too wide a dispersion of investment which was happening

items.statement: Targeting 200,000 direct outlets for 80% of weighted distribution; not pursuing deep numeric distribution
items.quote: We just need to get 200,000 direct outlets, right? And yes, if we are able to get that, this is where 80% of the weighted distribution game is being played.

items.statement: Inventory correction impact Rs 63 crore in Q2 (vs Rs 40-50 crore estimated); included sub-stockist and trade inventory not previously visible
items.quote: The Rs. 63 crores inventory impact means this is returns coming back to the company. So, it's impacted our primary sales to an extent.

items.statement: Nielsen data shows Mamaearth gaining share in face wash and shampoo categories Y-o-Y and sequentially
items.quote: If you look at the Nielsen data in the core categories, which is face wash and shampoo, the brand actually is growing fairly well. It's growing ahead of the other brands which we are competing with, and which is where the brand is actually gaining share as well.

items.statement: Consumer demand slowdown, offline distribution transition execution risk, Mamaearth growth model structural reset needed
items.quote: Things do seem to be changing faster than what we imagined them to be it in terms of on consumption landscape or distribution landscape from Q -commerce perspective and consumer productivity.

items.statement: Young brands (ex-Mamaearth) grew 30%+ in H1 FY25; Derma Co. at Rs 25 crore+ ARR run rate; Staze early but scaling per expectations
items.quote: Of course, outside of these two things, the young brands continue to demonstrate very healthy growth. And each one of them at H1 and quarter two level also have grown at 30% +.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 50%+ YoY for FY25 and EBITDA margin target of ~8% for FY25
items.quote: In terms of overall current financial spending, as we have been mentioning in the past also, is to maintain the same spend that the company will be growing at 50% plus for the current year as compared to the previous year.

items.statement: Target ROE/ROCE of minimum 15% within 2-3 years and 17% in next 3 years if growth plans met
items.quote: So, first of all, the company is extremely confident and positive that we will achieve ROE, ROCE of minimum 15% in time to come, very shortly, within a span of two to three years, for sure.

items.statement: INR 240 crore capex over 3 years for Hisense AC facility (1.5 mn units capacity); INR 40-50 crore for existing facilities
items.quote: And the estimated capex over next three years for AC business is around INR 240-odd crores. So we said $30 million, so that's almost INR 240 crores is what we are estimating in investment to create a capacity of 1.5 million air conditions over next 3 years.

items.statement: Sricity plant at 10% utilization in H1 FY25; targeting 30% by end FY25 and 60%+ in FY26
items.quote: So, by end of this year, the overall capitalization what we are targeting should be a minimum of 30 percent from Sri City in this year. And next year onwards, we definitely look to further improve it to at least 60 % onwards.

items.statement: Washing machine capacity 25,000 units/month (200k/year); pilot done in Q2, production start late Nov/early Dec
items.quote: So first of all, in terms of setup capacity for washing machine, to begin with, we have created a capacity of almost 25,000 w ashing machines per month, which translates to almost 200k of washing machines in a full year

items.statement: AC share rose to 70%+ in Q2 FY25 (vs typical 40%); non-AC 30%; small home appliances & washing machines to improve mix
items.quote: So Bhoomika, the mix for the current quarter is, AC contributing almost again, it's 70% plus in this quarter and non-AC, nearly 30%.

items.statement: Gross margin dip in Q2 due to higher AC mix (AC ~14.5-15% gross margin; small appliances ~100bps better); H1 margins stable YoY
items.quote: So like, although we are not reporting on a segmented basis, but at the same time, the margins in small home appliances is comparatively better, or slightly more as compared to AC. So when the overall revenue mix has changed, this has led to the decline in margins on a quarterly basis.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target ~8% for FY25 (vs 8.12% in FY24)
items.quote: The guidance on margin remains the same. We have been maintaining that last year we achieved a margin of 8.12% the EBITDA margins and we are targeting to achieve similar kind of margins around 8% for the current year as well.

items.statement: Q2 margins moderated to 16% due to higher raw material costs, utilities and lower recovery for some products

items.statement: FY25 planned capex Rs 25 crore, Rs 11 crore deployed in H1; sanitaryware greenfield Phase 1 capex Rs 130 crore (incl Rs 25-30 cr land) for 1.2 mn pieces/annum yielding Rs 300 cr revenue from FY28
items.quote: Our planned CAPEX for FY25 stands at Rs. 25 crore, of which we have already deployed Rs. 11 crore by H1 FY25.

items.statement: B2B sales 37% of Q2 revenue, up 15% in last 6 months; retailer loyalty program enrolled 21,700+ retailers with 3.6 lakh invoices; 39% of Rs 97 cr retail sales eligible for rewards
items.quote: B2B sales contributed 37% of Q2 revenue, demonstrating our selective focus on project sales that align with our profitability and margin goals.

items.statement: Not concerned about new entrants (pipe/paint cos) as they bulk source basic products from Morbi targeting unorganized market; Cera has strong distribution, brand and ad spend
items.quote: We are not concerned about the competition because as you mentioned, like most of the other pipe companies, paint companies, etc. have also started with the sanitaryware and faucetware business. But we find that most of them are mostly bulk sourcing from Morbi and trying to sell within a very basic kind of product.

items.statement: Net working capital days increased to 72 from 60 YoY; inventory days 80 (vs 73), receivable days 33 (vs 29), payable days 41 (vs 42)
items.quote: In terms of the working capital management, inventory days increased from 73 days to 80 days, receivable days increased from 29 days to 33 days and payable days decreased from 42 days to 41 days. Consequently, the net working capital days increased from 60 days to 72 days in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Buyback of Rs 130 crore completed (108,333 shares at Rs 12,000/share); buyback tax of ~Rs 30 crore paid by company; consistent dividend increases maintained
items.quote: During the quarter, we successfully concluded the buyback of shares amounting to Rs. 130 crore. The buyback involved purchase of 108,333 fully paid-up equity shares at Rs . 12,000 per share, effectively returning part of the surplus cash to shareholders.

items.statement: China imports reduced to 3% of revenue (~Rs 13 cr); most items internalized or sourced from Morbi; container rates normalized after Red Sea disruptions
items.quote: For Cera, we will find that we have reduced our China imports to a great extent . Most of the items that we were importing earlier from China, we have been able to internalize, and we have started manufacturing those items within our own plant.

items.statement: Sales mix: Tier-1 34%, Tier-2 21%, Tier-3 45%; South 36%, North 33%, West 21%, East 9% in Q2
items.quote: Regarding the sales distribution, Tier-1 cities accounted for 34% of the total sales, Tier-2 cities - 21% and Tier-3 cities led with 45% of total sales.

items.statement: Cash-rich with Rs 659 cr cash equivalents; CC limit Rs 100 cr but drawing only Rs 15-20 cr; interest cost increase due to IndAS lease accounting (rentals capitalized), not actual borrowings
items.quote: Our total drawing CC limit is something like Rs. 100 crore, whereas we normally draw only to the extent of Rs. 15 to 20 crore. The data has remained static in the last few quarters . That has not changed.

items.statement: Real estate delivery cycle 5-6 years; post-COVID project completions expected FY26-27 driving demand; rural sanitaryware demand not yet visible despite FMCG uptick
items.quote: So, typically a real estate project would take five years to six years to reach the completion stage. So, we can now anticipate that with post-COVID the projects which have started sometime in 2021 should be getting completed by more or less next financial year '25-'26 and '26-'27.

items.statement: Expects H2 FY25 margins to be close to H1 levels
items.quote: Yes, I think at this time, we believe that the H1 margins more or less are in line with our expectations, and we believe that H2 would also be pretty close to that.

items.statement: Investing Rs 440 crore to add third Bretonstone line at Mekaguda facility, operational by March 2026
items.quote: We are expanding our state -of-the-art quartz manufacturing facility in Telangana by adding a third Bretonstone production line. Scheduled to be operational by March 2026, this new line will significantly enhanc e our capacity while maintaining high standards of sustainable manufacturing.

items.statement: Capex funded by Rs 300 crore debt and Rs 144 crore internal accruals
items.quote: In terms of the investment m ix, we expect to do about Rs.300 crore of debt and the balance Rs.144 crore we are expecting to fund with our internal accruals.

items.statement: New line expected to reach full optimal capacity in 12-15 months after commissioning
items.quote: See, the ramp up as we have had in the first line as well, we expect that the full optimal capacity would take at least 12 to 15 months to come.

items.statement: New line expected to generate Rs 145-165 crore EBITDA and Rs 100-110 crore PAT at steady state
items.quote: So, profitability is typically we expect that the EBITDA from this would be in the range of Rs.145 to Rs.165 crore is what we are foreseeing at this time and PAT also we are expecting it to be in the range of Rs.100 to Rs.110 crore is what we are expecting at this time.

items.statement: Targets 75% revenue from North America and 25% from rest of world in 3-5 years
items.quote: Now coming to the market share, yes, of course, next three to five years, our idea is also that we have a good amount of rest of the world coming in. So, whether it would be 25% or 20%, I think time would say, but definitely our target is that we have 25% definitely coming from the rest of the world and 75 % from probably. North America.

items.statement: Expects quarterly revenue run rate of Rs 200-225 crore from new facility at steady state
items.quote: And now coming to your quarterly revenue, I think we expect that the numbers should be in the range of Rs.200 to Rs.225 crore subject to of course the market conditions and the situations out there.

items.statement: Aspires to maintain 35% EBITDA margin with new facility, historically targets 30%+
items.quote: So, historically, we have maintained that our target is to be 30% -plus EBITDA. So, we think that 35% is maintainable , of course, subject to the market conditions, but that's what we are aspiring for.

items.statement: Internal target to maintain consolidated margins around 35% for new plant
items.quote: That is what our internal targets are that we have to look at that number and plus.

items.statement: Close to ideal product mix (30-35% high value, 30-35% medium, 20-25% basic plus hospitality), hospitality still lagging
items.quote: So, we are pretty close to the ideal mix except for that , the hospitality has still not picked up, but it is far better than what it was in last year same time.

items.statement: KREOS line commercialization in Q3 FY25, launches in Q4 FY25; CHROMIA line operational by Q4 FY25
items.quote: The Kreos Line is progressing toward commercialization in Q3 FY25, with exciting product launches planned for Q4 FY25. The Chromia Line, designed for high-definition digital printing, is expected to be operational by Q4 FY25.

items.statement: US demand recovery depends on mortgage rates stabilizing below current 6.9%; mid-to-top tier focus driving outperformance
items.quote: But then as we are positioned on a different footing compared to majority of our competition, we are focusing on mid-to-top tier products. So, there, our differential strategy is able to bring us the faith of customer and also the related sales out of it.

items.statement: Freight rates normalized to near pre-inflation levels across most US ports
items.quote: I think the freight rates what we are seeing, they are pretty close to the normal levels for most of the US ports and there are certain ports where there is still not there.

items.statement: Works predominantly with large distributors; their success drives company success
items.quote: Since we do not go like caesarstone to the end consumer or to the fabricator, we work predominantly with the large distributors and their success is our success.

items.statement: Domestic India market currently minuscule; targets 10% of turnover from domestic sales
items.quote: Our focus is that always has been export market. Now looking at the Indian market and Indian growth story, we feel that the market is now right to accept our kind of product in the market. So, let's hope that we at least achieve 10% of our turnover on the domestic front.

items.statement: Will take about one year to identify right business partners for India distribution
items.quote: We will take about one year to identify the right business partners , because the response was too good, but we have to evaluate who will be the right business partners for the growth.

items.statement: Gross debt Rs 228 crore as of Sep 2024; cost of funds ~9%
items.quote: So, the gross debt as on 30th September, it is Rs.228 crore, and the cost of funds is around close to 9%.

items.statement: Current US duties: 2.34% countervailing duty, anti-dumping duty zero for this POR; any Trump changes would apply across board
items.quote: There is already an anti -dumping duty on our product. So, we have approximately about 2.34% countervailing duty, the anti -dumping duty for this POR was set as zero.

items.statement: Gross margin dip from 67.6% to 64% QoQ due to raw material mix (imported sand usage), not concerning
items.quote: I think this decline is not really a big number to be concerned , because it also depends upon what type of raw materials you are using in that particular period. Because if you are using a lot of your imported sand in that particular quarter, then it would be… so I think the number is very negligible in our view.

items.statement: Expects 25% effective tax rate for full year FY25
items.quote: So, we are expecting 25% also for the full year.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion at existing Mekaguda facility with minimal disruption; space allocated during original design
items.quote: See, this facility is going to come up at our existing facility in Mekaguda, Telangana. So, when we had originally designed our Hyderabad Mekaguda facility, we had provided enough space for future expansion.

items.statement: Additional space available at Mekaguda for further expansion beyond third line
items.quote: Regarding the additional space availability for future expansion, we do have still some space available for further expansion.

items.statement: Asset turnover historically 1x-1.25x; expects similar for new line at steady state
items.quote: Historically we have maintained that the asset turn is about 1 x to 1.25x. So, depending upon that we will have revenues around Rs.450 crore to 525 crore is what we foresee at this time.

items.statement: Granite business near-term outlook remains cautious; implementing cost-control measures
items.quote: While the near-term outlook remains cautious, we are committed to addressing these challenges with a focused and measured approach.

items.statement: Competitive pricing pressure from India and Southeast Asia producers; differentiation strategy key
items.quote: However, we remain cautious in managing competitive pricing pressures from producers in India and Southeast Asia. Our strategic focus on innovation and differentiation positions us well to address these challenges.

items.statement: Net debt expected to be around 20% lower than current Rs. 553 crores by end of FY25
items.quote: Broadly, my personal estimate would be around 20% lower than where we sit today.

items.statement: Global trade expected to strengthen; Europe may take more than two quarters to revive
items.quote: I already answered that we expect the strong demand environment in some of the select countries to continue, and Europe may take more than two quarters to revive. But globally, there's a better momentum in the market.

items.statement: Express business EBITDA improved consistently over last three quarters; price increase announced to improve margins
items.quote: We have recently announced a general price increase which will align us to improve the revenues and therefore improve the profit

items.statement: Contract logistics revenue grew 45% YoY to Rs. 111 crores in Q2 FY25 driven by new client additions
items.quote: Contract logistics revenue for Q2 FY '25 stood at Rs. 111 crores as compared to Rs. 76 crores for the same period last year, representing a growth of 45%.

items.statement: No significant capex plans beyond ordinary; investments now focused on people rather than acquisitions
items.quote: There are no significant Cap ex plans. Even on the expansion one significant change which has happened, I would say, in a way in our strate gy is that we are now investing in people in a way rather than acquiring companies.

items.statement: Contract logistics white space increased from 3-4% to 10-11% to support growth in e-commerce, auto, engineering
items.quote: Historically our white space was possibly in the range of 3% to 4% now that is 10% to 11%, but that is required as we drive grow th and movement.

items.statement: Freight rates cyclical; short-term debt increases with rate spikes and deflates when rates fall
items.quote: The freight rates are cyclical in nature and the short-term debt kind of apes that from an amount perspective.

items.statement: Contract logistics now 23% chemical, auto/engineering equal to chemical, e-commerce largest segment
items.quote: Despite continued growth, chemical logistics today comprises only 23% of our business, which means that Company has been successful in expanding its business into new domains, auto and engineering which is now as big as the chemical in terms of the total revenue mix. And the largest section for us now is our e-commerce business.

items.statement: Onboarded new team in Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay doubling business in two months; finalized JVs in Colombia, Ecuador
items.quote: Between July to September this quarter we onboarded an entire new team in Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay, which will add to the business in the region. It is already doing well in the first two months of operations, having grown the business significantly, almost doubling the business in two months itself.

items.statement: ECU Worldwide has unmatched technology and network creating flywheel of volume, market share, competitiveness
items.quote: Today, when we look at the competitive landscape, there is nobody close to our entity ECU Worldwide from a technology and network perspective, and that's something which should continue to create the flywheel of success wherein these capabilities lead to higher volume and market share.

items.statement: Restructuring scheme received exchange no-objection, filed with NCLT; demerger and separate listing by April 2025
items.quote: We believe that we would conclude the proce ss in the estimated timelines. And by April 2025 we should have the international domestic businesses demerged and listed separately.

items.statement: US business comprises both export and import; tariff restrictions may divert trade flows to Vietnam, Indonesia
items.quote: as far as our US business is concerned, it comprises both export and import. As I was mentioning earlier, we believe that any tariff restr ictions which come in particular to a certain country, those tariff restrictions could lead to diverted tariff flows, and we might see more cargo coming in from other countries as compared to China, for instance

items.statement: Net debt Rs. 553 crores up due to working capital increase from higher freight rates; temporary in nature
items.quote: The consolidated net debt for the quarter end ed September '24 stood at Rs. 553 crores. The net debt has gone up mainly on account of a working capital increase.

items.statement: Gross debt Rs. 1,362 crores (short-term ~Rs. 850 crores, long-term Rs. 495 crores); short-term debt tracks freight rate cycles
items.quote: The gross debt is Rs. 1,362 crores, short term debt is around only Rs. 850 crores out of it, or Rs. 495 crores is long term debt.

items.statement: Non-core asset monetization estimated at Rs. 75-100 crores consolidated including Allcargo and Gati
items.quote: So, across Allcargo, on a consolidated basis, which includes Allcargo and Gati as well, broadly there could be non-core cash flows coming into the extent of Rs. 75 crores to Rs. 100 crores, that's the broad estimate.

items.statement: Latin America expansion via new team onboarding and JVs in Colombia, Ecuador; no acquisitions planned
items.quote: Also this is the quarter when we finalized our joint ventures in Colombia and Ecuador, which will bring in local expertise. And combining with the global network, we expect these markets to also grow faster.

items.statement: Capital allocation focused on debt retirement and dividends; dividend distributed in recent quarter
items.quote: We have been using capital to retire debt or to provide dividends to the shareholders. And the Company has maintained distribution of cash flows by way of dividend, as you would have seen in the quarter gone by as well.

items.statement: Staff cost up Rs. 32 crores QoQ due to ~30 new hires in Argentina, bonus payments, and ~$1M severance cost this quarter
items.quote: the increase in staff cost is primarily driv en by, one, like you rightly mentioned, onboarding new people such as about 30 -plus people in the Argentina region that I mentioned about, and a few more people in other geographies as well which have been onboarded for

items.statement: Geopolitical events (Russia-Ukraine, Middle East, US tariffs) could shape world trade; Europe economic environment subdued
items.quote: There are of course several geopolitical events happening around us and they would shape the future of world trade. But prima facie, we believe that global trade will only continue to strengthen from here.

items.statement: Freight rates expected to remain range-bound; Drewry projects net trade demand to absorb new capacity
items.quote: So, we believe that freight rates will remain range bound. There are various things pointing towards an upward movement and things pointing towards downward, some you appropriately mentioned. What we follow from various maritime research projections is that there is also a lot of capacity coming up for scraping. And on an overall basis, Drewry, which is the leading maritime research Company, publi

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 50% above industry growth rate over next 3-4 years
items.quote: we should be able to grow at least 50% more than the industry's growth rate

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to sustain at 14% for FY25
items.quote: we expect this margin to continue in Q3 and Q4 for the remaining part of the fiscal

items.statement: EBITDA margin expansion target from 14% to 15% over next 3 years
items.quote: we should be able to expand those EBITDA margins further, perhaps from 14% to 15%

items.statement: IAC EBITDA margin expected to maintain 16-18% range in H2
items.quote: we do expect a similar margin to be maintained

items.statement: Total order book INR1,050 crores with 90% new business and 40% EV contribution
items.quote: The total order book, considering the value of all product and domain categories is INR1,050 crores, out of which 90% is new business

items.statement: Order book maturity: 15% in FY25, 40% in FY26, 30% in FY27, 15% in FY28
items.quote: 15% of the order value will mature in the current financial year FY '25, 40% in FY '26, 30% in FY '27 and the remaining residual 15% in FY '28

items.statement: Capex estimated at INR120-140 crores for FY25, up from INR32 crores in H1
items.quote: the Capex outlay for the whole year is estimated to be around INR120 crores to INR140 crores

items.statement: Incremental capex of ~INR60 crores YoY expected to generate INR400 crores additional revenue in FY25
items.quote: there should be an incremental Capex of about INR60 crores. Last year was around INR80 crores. This year, we are looking at anywhere between INR120 crores to INR150 crores

items.statement: IAC capacity utilization ~85% after brownfield expansions in Pune and Nashik operational in H2
items.quote: post the investments, I would say that our capacity utilizations would still be close to around 85-odd percent

items.statement: Passenger vehicle industry expected low single-digit growth for full year
items.quote: Overall, as noted previously, we expect the passenger vehicle segment to register a low single-digit growth for the full year as an industry

items.statement: 2-wheeler segment growth momentum continuing with rural demand and premium models
items.quote: Looking ahead, we anticipate this upward trend to persist, fueled by a stronger rural economy, continued introduction of premium models and evolving consumer preferences

items.statement: Commercial vehicle demand expected to rebound in H2 with government spending resumption
items.quote: we are hopeful that the demand for CVs will rebound in the second half of the year as government spending resumes and infrastructure projects regain momentum

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 14% for Q2 and H1 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margin stands at 14% for Q2 FY '25. Absolute EBITDA for Q2 stood at INR118 crores, growth of 18% on a year-on-year basis. H1 FY '25 margin is at 14%

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin improved ~150 bps YoY in H1 due to OEM scale and price corrections
items.quote: it has grew almost by 150 basis points and which basically includes certain economies of scale due to the higher revenue in OEM and as well as certain, you can say, the price corrections from our major OEMs

items.statement: EV contribution ~40% of total order book across passenger cars and 2-wheelers
items.quote: EV contribution is approximately 40% of the total order book

items.statement: No plans to pursue EV-specific components; focusing on CNG/alternate fuels instead
items.quote: we are currently not further pursuing any opportunity in the EV specific component space. As an alternative, as I mentioned, we are a lot more bullish on the penetration of alternate fuels like CNG

items.statement: IAC won full service supplier business for Tata Motors including ambient lighting new product category
items.quote: we have won a full service supplier business for Tata Motors, not just for the plastic interior products, but also for the ambient lighting, and that's a new product category which IAC India has ventured into

items.statement: Engaged with Maruti Suzuki to expand wallet share and with Honda Car India as new potential customer
items.quote: We are continuously engaged in discussions with OEMs like Maruti Suzuki to expand and increase our wallet share and also with new potential customers like Honda Car India

items.statement: GreenFuel acquisition expected to close in Q3 FY25 with consolidation from Q3
items.quote: This partnership, as I mentioned, should be fructified sometime in quarter 3 itself and with consolidation revenues maybe kicking in from quarter 3

items.statement: GreenFuel expected INR300-350 crores annualized revenue with stronger EBITDA margins, mainly for FY26
items.quote: on a full year basis, we are expecting anywhere between INR300 crores to INR350-odd crores of revenues with a stronger EBITDA margin than what we are looking at currently

items.statement: Mechatronics revenue to more than double in FY25 and double again in FY26 crossing INR200 crores
items.quote: mechatronics, as was explained earlier, will grow at almost close to 70% to 80% this year. And next year also, we expect the revenues of mechatronics domain to double, maybe crossing the INR200 crores mark

items.statement: Lumax Mannoh targeting 12-15% YoY growth with 60-62% gear shifter market share
items.quote: We are anticipating a year-on-year growth of about 12% to 15%, depending on the OEM demand holding up

items.quote: we are going ahead with the SOP in January with a major 2-wheeler manufacturer. We are looking at supplying almost 0.5 million sensors in the next financial year

items.statement: Free cash INR387 crores exceeds long-term debt INR363 crores as of Sep 30
items.value: INR387 crores cash vs INR363 crores debt
items.quote: The company is sitting on a healthy free cash of INR387 crores as on 30th September, which is more than the long-term debt of INR363 crores

items.statement: Annual long-term debt repayment INR75 crores, half paid in H1
items.quote: Annual repayment schedule for the whole year was -- long-term debt was INR75 crores. So out of that INR75 crores, half of it has been paid in H1

items.quote: it included a substantial amount of tooling revenue in IAC amounting to INR35 crores. If we exclude that INR35 crores as a manufacturing revenue, it has increased by almost 15% to 16%

items.statement: Aftermarket H1 flat but expecting double-digit YoY growth in H2 and high single-digit for full year
items.quote: for the full year, we still expect a high single-digit growth rate for aftermarket in the current financial

items.statement: Capex guidance of Rs 80 billion for H2FY25
items.quote: We expect capex spends of Rs. 80billion in H2FY25.

items.statement: Q2FY25 capex spend was Rs 13.6 billion
items.quote: Our capex investments are gaining momentum post fund raise and in Q2FY25 we invested Rs. 13.6 billion.

items.statement: Three-year capex plan of Rs 500-550 billion
items.quote: At the cost of repetition, I am pleased to share that in September, we concluded deals worth about Rs. 300 billion or USD3.6 billion with the three global partners, namely Nokia, Ericsson, and Samsung, for supply of network equipment over a period of three years. This is one of the key steps towards the rollout of the company's transformative three-year capex plan of Rs. 500 to 550 billion.

items.statement: 4G population coverage target of 1.1 billion by March 2025 and 1.2 billion by September 2025
items.quote: The 4G expansion is in progress and our target is to achieve 4G population coverage of 1.1 billion by March 2025 and 1.2 billion by September 2025.

items.statement: 5G rollout to start in Q4FY25 in key geographies
items.quote: The rollout of 5G in key geographies will start in Q4FY25.

items.statement: Added 42,000 4G sites in Q2FY25, largest ever quarterly addition
items.quote: During the quarter, we added almost 42,000 4G sites which is the largest ever addition of 4G sites in the Company in a quarter.

items.statement: 4G data capacity increased ~14% and population coverage increased by ~22 million over last 6 months
items.quote: Resultantly, our 4G data capacity has increased by approximately 14% and 4G population coverage increased by approximately 22 million from 1.03 billion to 1.05 billion over las t 6

items.statement: Customer ARPU ex-M2M increased 7.8% QoQ; blended price increase ~16% but ARPU impact lower due to segments with no hike and subscriber downgrades
items.quote: Our customer ARPU ex M2M has increased by 7.8% QoQ.

items.statement: Entry-level tariff hike ~10%, higher consumption tiers up to 20%; further structural correction needed with higher increases at high-usage levels
items.quote: At the entry level the tariff increase was about 10% whereas at the higher levels or higher price levels, it was more pronounced or, let's say, in some cases as much as 20%.

items.statement: Lost 5.1 million subscribers with increased port-outs to BSNL (which did not hike tariffs); port-outs declining post-August per MNP data
items.quote: We registered a loss of 5.1 million subscribers with increased port outs to one operator which has not participated in the tariff hike.

items.statement: Postpaid customer base grew QoQ and YoY, driven partly by M2M; retail postpaid consistently increasing over last year
items.quote: I am pleased to report that in the postpaid segment, we have been able to increase our customer base on QoQ as well as YoY

items.statement: Revenue Rs 109.3 billion, up 4% QoQ; customer revenue up 5.6% QoQ driven by July 4 price increases
items.quote: The revenues for the quarter stood at Rs. 109.3 billion, a growth of 4% versus last quarter. More importantly, the customer revenues for the quarter grew by 5.6% versus last quarter, driven by price increases effective from July 4th this year.

items.statement: EBITDA ex-Ind AS 116 Rs 23.2 billion, up 10.5% QoQ; margin 21.3%, highest since merger
items.quote: The EBITDA excluding Ind AS 116 for a quarter was at Rs. 23.2 billion, improving by 10.5% on a quarter-on-quarter basis. This is the highest quarterly EBITDA since merger and the margin has improved to 21.3%.

items.statement: Bank debt reduced to Rs 32.7 billion from Rs 78.3 billion a year ago; cash balance Rs 136.2 billion sufficient for H2FY25 capex
items.quote: The debt from banks stood at Rs. 32.7 billion versus 78.3 billion at Q2FY24, a reduction of Rs. 45.8 billion during the last one year. The cash and bank balances stood at Rs. 136.2 billion as of September 38, 2024.

items.statement: Actively engaged with lenders for debt funding for long-term network expansion; discussions ongoing with promoters involved
items.quote: We remain actively engaged with our lenders for tying up debt funding towards the execution of our long term network expansion. I am personally involved in these discussions alongwith the promoters.

items.statement: Bank guarantee quantum ~Rs 24,000 crore over one year; industry requested waiver; not factored in business plan; awaiting government decision
items.quote: The quantum of bank guarantees is disclosed in our financials i.e. about 24,000 crores over a period of one year.

items.statement: Conversion of AGR/spectrum dues to equity permitted under 2021 reforms package if shortfall exists post-moratorium (expires in ~12 months); disclosed in notes to accounts
items.quote: Given that the moratorium expires in the next 12 months, it was considered prudent to make this disclosure.

items.statement: Raised Rs 240 billion equity in 2024 via FPO and preferential issuance
items.quote: During 2024, the company has raised Rs. 240 billion of equity.

items.statement: Launched Vi One converged broadband+mobility+OTT bundle in Mumbai, Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Kerala (via Asianet partnership); expanding to other markets
items.quote: In July, we signed a strategic partnership with Asianet, a leading broadband player in Kerala, and launched Vi One additionally across entire Kerala.

items.statement: Vi Movies & TV relaunched as multi-OTT aggregation platform on mobile and Connected TV; Vi App offers games, eSports, bill pay, shopping, OTT subscriptions, 350+ TV channels
items.quote: We have launched Vi Movies & TV in an all new avatar with all new apps for mobile on both, Android & IOS as well as for TV across almost all major operating systems.

items.statement: Vi Guarantee program offers 130GB additional data to 5G/new 4G handset customers; RED X postpaid plan at Rs 1,201 includes unlimited data, multiple OTTs, lounge access, international roaming in 29 countries
items.quote: We have received good response for Vi Guarantee program in the prepaid segment, a unique offer that provides 130GB of additional data to all 5G and new 4G handset customers.

items.statement: Industry needs further tariff rationalization to recover cost of capital; entry-level headroom limited, future hikes skewed to high-usage tiers; 5G metering will create monetization opportunity
items.quote: Hence, further tariff rationalization is needed for the industry to recover its cost of capital.

items.statement: AGR curative petition dismissed; government engagement ongoing; bank funding discussions in wait-and-watch mode pending AGR clarity; no timeline for debt raise
items.quote: Post the curative petition, everybody is in a bit of a wait and watch situation to see that how things are evolving, and so these things will move together, the engagement with the government on AGR and the banking discussions.
