items.statement: CEO Akshaya Moondra and promoters personally engaged in lender and government discussions
items.quote: I am personally involved in these discussions alongwith the promoters.

items.statement: Expect strong revenue growth in FY26 and even stronger bottom-line growth due to cost cutting measures
items.quote: I think that for financial year 26, I think as the penetration of lab-grown diamonds increases, we see revenue growth accelerating, and this coupled with the cost cutting measures that we have taken in our Customer Brand segment, we expect strong revenue growth in FY '26 and even stronger growth in bottom line because of our cost cutting measures.

items.statement: Expect meaningful debt reduction by end of FY25 and zero net debt by end of FY26
items.quote: So, as I mentioned earlier, we expect it to be significantly lower by about 150 to 180 crore by the end of this year. So, the net debt which is currently at 328 should be closer to 100 crore of net debt and subsequently by FY '26, the plan would be to be zero net debt.

items.statement: Allocated around 30 crore for infrastructure upgradation from preferential fund raise
items.quote: There is, however, some amount of upgradation of infrastructure that will take place which we have allocated I think around 30 crore for.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin from continuing operations reached 10.3% in Q2 FY25, up from 7.5% year-over-year
items.quote: On the profitability front, adjusted EBITDA expanded by 42% at Rs. 40 crore in Q2 of FY '25 versus Rs. 28 crore in the same period last year with adjusted EBITDA margins of 10.3% versus 7.5% last year.

items.statement: Owned Brands EBITDA margin reached 10.3% in Q2, a 575 bps year-over-year improvement
items.quote: In Owned Brands, our revenue grew by 7% year-over-year in Q2, while the EBITDA margin in this segment reached 10.3%, reflecting a substantial year-over-year improvement of 575 basis points.

items.statement: Customer Brands EBITDA margin improved 295 bps to 9.4% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: In the Customer Brands division, revenue in Q2 stood at 293 crore with an EBITDA margin of 9.4%, making an impressive 295 basis point improvement.

items.statement: Licensed Brand business had EBITDA margin of 16.5% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: In Q2 of FY '25, our Licensed Brand business maintained stable revenues at Rs. 57 crore on account of healthy flow of orders from our retail partners as well as the Direct-to-Consumer segment. It had an EBITDA margin of 16.5%.

items.statement: Launched cost optimization initiative expected to deliver annual savings of 40 to 50 crore, with one-time restructuring expense of 3.5 crore in Q2
items.quote: We have launched an extensive cost optimization initiative towards the end of Q2, which will extend into Q3 and is expected to deliver annual savings of 40 to 50 crore. In line with the same, we incurred a one-time restructuring expense of around 3.5 crore in this quarter.

items.statement: Expect strong consumer demand in Owned Brands segment approaching holiday season
items.quote: As we approach the holiday season, we expect strong consumer demand in this segment, setting us up for a promising end to the year.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamond penetration in B2B business currently 6%, expected to grow meaningfully in coming quarters and years
items.quote: Currently the penetration is only 6%, which we expect to grow meaningfully in the coming quarters and the years to come.

items.statement: Cost cutting measures include capacity rationalization due to less labor-intensive lab-grown diamond products
items.quote: so, you know, a lot of the cost cutting measures have actually been capacity rationalizations because as a business moves to more lab grown, we see less labor intensive product being manufactured, which means that we will be able to produce more value of orders with less manufacturing capacity

items.statement: Launched new direct-to-consumer fashion jewelry brand Renaei primarily on Amazon US targeting millennial and Gen Z consumers
items.quote: We recently launched a new direct-to-consumer fashion jewelry brand, Renaei, to be primarily sold on Amazon in the U.S. The brand is uniquely designed to meet an ever-growing affordable fashion jewelry demand among millennial and Gen Z consumers.

items.statement: Tested Enchanted Star collection with major US retail partner, extending Enchanted Disney Fine Jewelry brand with lab-grown diamonds
items.quote: Recently, we tested the Enchanted Star collection with a major retail partner in the U.S. This collection is an exciting extension of our Enchanted Disney Fine Jewelry brand brings lab-grown diamonds into our offerings, featuring engagement rings and fashion jewelry pieces.

items.statement: Plan to launch Owned Brands in UK in February for geographic expansion
items.quote: Currently, a large part of our brands is in the US. We plan to launch in February in the UK, and there will be some geographic expansion, which will lead to growth.

items.statement: Exclusive licensing arrangement with Disney provides moat in branded jewelry segment
items.quote: And then in the licensed brand segment, we have an exclusive licensing arrangement with Disney which gives us a moat and helps us sort of protect the business because Disney is a very well-recognized brand in the markets in which we operate.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity ratio at 0.27 as of September 2024, down from 0.31 in June 2024 and 0.29 in September 2023
items.quote: Our net debt-to-equity ratio stands at a healthy 0.27 as on 30th September '24 versus 0.31 in June '24 and 0.29 in September of '23.

items.statement: Total net debt at Rs. 328 crore as of September 2024, down from Rs. 370 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our total net debt stands at Rs. 328 crore against Rs. 370 crore in Q1 of FY '25.

items.statement: Completed preferential fund raise of around 168 crore, proceeds to be used for debt reduction and potential acquisitions
items.quote: So, we obviously have, we are on the lookout for an acquisition, and we have not identified any acquisition immediately. So, once a fund raise is done, debt reduction will happen immediately.

items.statement: Cash and bank balances increased to Rs. 244 crore as of September 2024, up Rs. 58 crore from June 2024 and Rs. 60 crore from March 2024
items.quote: Our cash and bank balances and current investments stand at Rs. 244 crore, which is up by Rs. 58 crore from 30th June '24.

items.statement: Inventory typically peaks in September for holiday season build, expected to reduce in December and March
items.quote: However, the absolute inventory number, obviously, this is the start of the season and September usually represents a peak in terms of our inventory numbers, because we are usually building inventory for the October, November, December holiday season. So, we would expect to see a reduction in inventory subsequently, both in December as well as in March.

items.statement: Branded segment revenue reached Rs. 92 crore in H1 FY25, up 19% from Rs. 78 crore in H1 FY24
items.quote: Our branded segment reached revenues of Rs. 92 crore during the first half of the financial year versus 78 crore in the first half of FY '24, which is upped by 19%.

items.statement: Direct-to-Consumer India brand Irasva recorded revenues of Rs. 10 crore in H1 FY25 with four stores
items.quote: Our Direct-to-Consumer India brand Irasva, with a total of four stores across Mumbai, Ahmedabad and Hyderabad, recorded revenues of Rs. 10 crore in the first half of FY '25.

items.statement: Expect significant reductions in interest rates leveraging proceeds from gold business sale and favorable rate environment from Fed rate cuts
items.quote: Additionally, we expect to see significant reductions in interest rates as we leverage the proceeds from the sale of our gold business and anticipate a more favorable interest rate environment with recent rate cuts announced by the fed.

items.statement: Acknowledge near-term challenges but remain confident in long-term potential of branded business
items.quote: While we remain mindful of near-term challenges, our outlook on the long-term potential of our branded business remains exceptionally strong.

items.statement: Seeing return to growth in all segments in Q2, anticipate trend to continue or accelerate going forward
items.quote: So, I think we are seeing sort of a return to growth in all of our segments in quarter 2. We anticipate this trend to continue or accelerate going forward.

items.statement: Expect double-digit growth in licensed brand segment in coming quarters as inflation pressures abate
items.quote: Our cadence has been to try and grow in double digits in our licensed brand segment and which we expect sort of in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 revenue growth guidance 25%-30% and EBITDA margin 17%-18%
items.quote: We are sticking to our guidance because we are expecting increase in the volumes of ductile iron pipes which are the major contributors to our topline and the bottomline.

items.statement: Target to become net term debt free within next 12 months; FY25 term debt target Rs. 225-250 crores
items.value: Rs. 225-250 crores term debt by FY25 end
items.quote: Our FY25 guidance is to reduce the term debt to Rs. 225-Rs. 250 crores of which we are very optimistic of achieving.

items.statement: Rs. 1,000 crore capex plan; Rs. 700 crores incurred; balance Rs. 300 crores over next 9 months
items.quote: Out of this, approximately Rs. 700 crores has already been incurred and the balance Rs. 300 crores is expected to be incurred over the next 9 months.

items.statement: DI pipe capacity expanding from 3 lakh to 6.6 lakh metric tons; Phase 1 (1.4 lakh tons) in FY25, Phase 2 (2.2 lakh tons) in FY26
items.quote: JBIL is expanding its DI pipes capacity from 3 lakh metric tons to 6.6 lakh metric tons. Of this, 1.4 lakh metric tons, the remaining capacity from Phase 1 that is expected to be commissioned in FY25 while the Phase 2 capacity of 2.2 lakh metric tons is expected for commissioning in FY26.

items.statement: Ferro alloy capacity increasing from 1.6 lakh to 1.9 lakh metric tons by Q1 FY26
items.quote: The ferro alloy capacity will increase from 1.6 lakh metric tons to 1.9 lakh metric tons with client capacity expansion by Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Blast furnace capacity rising from 6.3 lakh to 7.5 lakh metric tons; one revamped, second by Q1 FY26
items.quote: Additionally, 1 blast fumace has already been revamped and commissioned with the second one expected to be completed by Q1 of FY26 boosting the total capacity from 6.3 lakh metric tons to 7.5 lakh metric tons.

items.statement: Sinter capacity raised to 9 lakh tons in FY24; additional 3 lakh tons by Q1 FY26 to reach ~12 lakh tons per annum
items.quote: And the center capacity was raised to 9 lakhs tons in FY24 and an additional 3 lakh tons is expected to be commissioned in Q1 of FY26, bringing the total to approximately 12 lakh metric tons per annum.

items.statement: H1 FY25 adjusted EBITDA margin 17% vs 14% in H1 FY24
items.quote: I am also very happy to share that the adjusted EBITDA margin for HI FY25 has been increased to 17% compared to 14% in H1 FY24.

items.statement: DI pipe order book covers next 6 months; volumes to increase incrementally each quarter targeting 4 lakh tons in FY25
items.quote: Regarding volumes, we expect volumes to increase incrementally on each quarter. So we will target to achieve 4 lakh ton this year and the coming year.

items.statement: DI pipe demand robust driven by JJM, AMRUT 2.0, irrigation schemes and government infrastructure spending
items.quote: The demand for ductile pipes, it is robust and we expect it to be robust because not only are we looking at the compression of the JIM scheme, we are also looking at the AMRUT 2.0.

items.statement: Specialized ferro alloy growth slow and steady; niche market exporting to 40 countries; capacity raised to 1.9 lakh tons
items.quote: As far as the specialized ferro alloy segment, it is a very niche market. Here, we are already exporting to around 40 countries, but we are one of the only manufacturers in the country to make this product on organized basis.

items.statement: DI pipe realizations expected similar levels +/-2-3%; ferro alloy realizations similar +/-2%; pig iron, TMT, sponge iron up ~Rs. 1,000/ton in H2
items.quote: Regarding DI we expect the relations to be at similar levels, maybe plus minus 2%-3% rather because we have the order booked for the coming 6 months.

items.statement: Coking coal prices substantially down vs previous quarters; coal cooled; iron ore flat; chrome ore up substantially
items.quote: The prices of coking coal compared to the previous few quarters are substantially down. The prices of coal have cooled down and the iron prices are more or less flat, but expectation the global markets as a downward buyers. Only Chrome Ore is going up substantially.

items.statement: DI pipe exports currently <1%; target ~5% of production with capacity expansion
items.quote: Going forward, we have a plan that with the increase in the capacity expansion, here export is negligible. It s less than 5%, it is less than 1%. So we are looking at exporting around 5%. So on the export market

items.statement: Net term debt Rs. 300-350 crores currently; target net term debt free in 12 months; FY25 term debt target Rs. 225-250 crores
items.quote: The total term debt is around Rs. 300-Rs. 350 crores right now. And looking at the EBITDA and the pending CAPEX which is going to be, the pending CAPEX is around Rs. 300 crores and the total term debt pending is Rs. 300 crores.

items.statement: Deferred tax assets consumed over last 3 quarters; ~Rs. 70-75 crores pending consumption in Q3; carry forward tax losses ~Rs. 500 crores remaining
items.quote: As far as deferred tax assets, which were in our books, we have consumed it in last 3 quarters and the pending which I think in the third quarter will be consumed is around Rs. 70-Rs. 75 crores.

items.statement: Value-added products (DI pipes + ferro alloys) revenue share 45-55% currently; target 65% by FY25 end; 75-80% by Q4 FY26
items.quote: Then it should reach to 65% by the end of the current financial year, and then once the second part III of the ductile expansion is completed and it is fully operationalized, we will be north of 75, that is broad idea.

items.statement: DI pipe EBITDA Rs. 22,000/ton; ferro alloy Rs. 25,000/ton; pig iron Rs. 5,000/ton; TMT Rs. 4,000/ton; sponge iron Rs. 3,000/ton in Q2 FY25
items.value: DI pipe Rs. 22,000/t; ferro alloy Rs. 25,000/t; pig iron Rs. 5,000/t; TMT Rs. 4,000/t; sponge iron Rs. 3,000/t
items.quote: For ductile iron pipe, it was Rs. 22,000 per ton, ferro alloy was 25,000, pig iron, it was around. 5,000, TMT was 4,000 and sponge iron 3000.

items.statement: Domestic DI pipe demand estimated 6-7 million tons this year; bid pipeline extremely robust
items.quote: Our internal team is working is that the demand of ductile iron pipes, this particular year will be in the region of 6-7 million tons and the bid pipeline range with that only.

items.statement: DI pipe sales: 25-30% direct to government; balance to EPC contractors executing government projects
items.quote: In some cases, we are selling around 25%-30% of the sales, it is directed to the government. The balance is to the EPC contractors who are executing the projects for the government.

items.statement: Fund release from government slower post-election across sectors including Jal Jeevan Mission; expect robust spending in next 4-5 months
items.quote: What we are seeing is that since the funds have not been released to a great extent after in the last 15 months, actually the government has a budget requirement to meet the expenditure, so over the next 4-5 months, we are expecting very robust spending to be coming.

items.statement: No new capex plan announced beyond current Rs. 1,000 crore; future plans on drawing board; finalization by end of financial year
items.quote: Right now, there is no CAPEX plan which we have announced, but definitely we are looking at certain opportunities, but it will take time.

items.statement: Future capex finalization will take more than 3-4 months, likely by end of financial year
items.quote: It will take some time. It will take more than 3-4 months, 5 months.

items.statement: No discussion with board on capital market fundraising for larger expansion; priority is debt reduction first
items.quote: Well, we look into it. Right now, it has not been discussed over here, with the board.

items.statement: Priority last 3 years was turnaround, stabilize operations, shift to value-added products; ~90% achieved
items.quote: Last 3 years we wanted, the priority was to tum around the company, stabilize the operation, go into value added products in a big way, convert our big iron and the hot metal to ductile iron pipe and go big on ferro alloys.

items.statement: Commissioned 35 TPH blast furnace gas boiler for waste gas utilization in captive power plant, reducing carbon emissions
items.quote: Furthermore, the company has also commissioned a 35 TPH blast furnace gas boiler as part of a green energy initiative. This project integrates waste gas utilization from the blast fumace into the captive power plant, reducing carbon emissions and enhancing sustainability.

items.statement: Stock split announced: each Rs. 10 equity share divided into 5 shares of Rs. 2 face value
items.quote: When amnounced the liquidity of the stock, the company has also announced a stock split dividing each equity share value Rs. 10 into 5 equity share with a face value for Rs. 2 each.

items.statement: Signed SPA to divest 5 BOT project subsidiaries to Indian Highways Concessions Trust at enterprise value INR5,718 crore, equity value INR2,539 crore
items.quote: Ashoka Concessions Limited, a subsidiary of the company, has entered into share purchase agreement with Indian Highways Concessions Trust inter alia for divestment of its 5 subsidiaries. The aggregate enterprise value of the transaction is either INR5,718 crores, subject to adjustment of cash and debt, translating into an equity value of INR2,539 crores.

items.statement: Agreed to acquire 34% equity of ACL plus CCDs from Macquarie SBI Infrastructure Investment and SBI Macquarie Infrastructure Trust for INR1,526 crore
items.quote: The company has entered into SPA to acquire 34% of equity of ACL, along with 7,741,250 Class A CCDs and 2,00,00,000 class B CCDs from Macquarie SBI Infrastructure Investment Private Limited and SBI Macquarie Infrastructure Trust for INR1,526 crores.

items.statement: Viva Highways to acquire 26% equity in Jaora Nayagaon Toll Road Company for INR150 crore
items.quote: Viva Highways Limited, a subsidiary of the company, to acquire investments of investors totalling 7,46,20,000 equity shares, comprising of 26% equity share s held in Jaora Nayagaon Toll Road Company private Limited at an aggregate consideration of INR150 crores

items.statement: Monetized land at Hinjewadi, Pune held by Viva Highways for INR453 crore
items.quote: Monetization of land. - Land owned by Viva Highways Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, under its real estate portfolio situated at Hinjewadi, Pune, has been monetized for a total consideration of INR453 crores.

items.statement: Order book as on Sep 30, 2024 stands at INR11,104 crore; including post-Sep orders INR4,320 crore and L1 INR265 crore, total current order book INR15,424 crore
items.quote: Coming t o the order book status. As on September 30, 2024, our balance order book stands at INR11,104 crores. This excludes additional orders received from projects post September '24 worth INR4,320 crores and also excludes L1 of INR265 crores. The total of curren t order book stands at INR15,424

items.quote: The breakup as on September ' 30 is Road and railway project compromise around INR6,582 crores, which is 59.3% of the total order book. items.statement: FY25 revenue expected flattish YoY; EBITDA margin to improve by ~50 bps in H2 to ~8.5%; double-digit margins only from Q1 FY26
items.quote: So on the execution side, keeping in view the orders which have come in and their expected date of start of activities, we believe that the revenue top line may be flattish for this year, so what we have said or thought in the last quarter. As far as EBITDA concerned, we expect at least it should improve by 0.5% for the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth target 10-15% based on current and new order book
items.quote: FY '26, based on this order book, and maybe next order book, we should definitely look at after getting new orders, to grow by 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Bid pipeline INR1 lakh crore from NHAI, participating in INR65,000 crore; bids to be opened ~INR9,000 crore; expect to win INR4,000-5,000 crore in balance FY25
items.quote: So bid pipeline is there. Around INR1 lakh crore bidding is there from NHAI. Out of which, INR65,000, we'll be participating. There are bids to be opened of around INR9,000 crores which we already bid. And bid opening is yet to balance. And we hope we should pick up around INR4,000 crores to INR5,000 crores in balance part of the year.

items.statement: New projects bid at 11-12% margins; legacy fixed-price projects impacted by inflation
items.quote: We now continue to bid at double-digit margins, 11% to 12%. So these are for orders which were taken in the past, and the impact of -- as they were fixed price contract, the impact of inflation or increase in prices have had an impact on the margins.

items.statement: Consolidated debt INR6,881 crore as on Sep 30, 2024; standalone debt INR1,317 crore (INR109 cr equipment/term loans + INR1,209 cr working capital loans)
items.quote: Total consolidated debt as on 30th September 2024, stood at INR6,881 crores. The stand-alone debt is at INR1,317 crores, which comprises of INR109 crores of equipment and term loans and INR1,209 crores for working capital loans.

items.statement: Standalone working capital debt increased INR800-950 crore in 6-12 months due to elongated power sector working capital cycle; funded by subsidiary loans (INR950 cr) and bank loans
items.quote: So it's typically as one of the point s that we've given, is that working capital on the power sector which we had won a lot of contracts in '23, have been executed largely in these 2 years, 1.5 years, wherein the working capital cycle in the power sector is longer, elongated. That is the reason these working capital cycle has increased, which has been typically funded both by loan from subsidiari

items.statement: Expect working capital debt to reduce by INR300-400 crore by Mar-Jun 2025 as power projects complete
items.quote: So what we expect is by -- these projects will come to an end by March to June next year, and where we'll see this number is going down by INR300 crores to INR400 crores at least.

items.statement: Peak standalone debt reached; expect reduction from Q1 FY26 as monetization proceeds and operating cash flows materialize
items.quote: From a turnover perspective, it's a peak debt. But from perspective of realization of monetization money and a mix of new HAM projects and BOT prices coming up, we cannot immediately say what how they could peak out. But I think we should be close to a peak.

items.statement: Consolidated debt to reduce by INR3,000-3,500 crore by Mar 2025 from BOT/HAM asset sales; balance reduction post-Mar
items.quote: So by the end of this quarter -- by end of this year, we probably -- the INR6,800 will be used by debt, which is already on the 5 BOT projects of INR2,400. If that deal happens, that will go down. Certain debt on the HAM projects also will go down, which we intend to sell. So today, it's difficult to estimate what exactly, but we expect that at least of INR3,000 crores, INR3,500-odd crores of debt

items.statement: H1 FY25 capex INR33 crore; H2 FY25 planned capex INR35-40 crore
items.quote: So in H1, we did capex of approximately INR33 crores. And in H2, we may prepare another INR35 crores to INR40 crores. That's H2, sorry. Not FY, H2.

items.quote: The company has a received a completion certificate for its HAM project: Four -laning of NH-161 from Kandi to Ramsanpalle in the State of Telangana from August 2024. The project is executed by Ashoka Kandi Ramsanpalle Road Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of the company. The SPV has received a certificate for completion of entire project stretch of 39.98 kilo meters. Consequent to this,

items.statement: Toll collection Q2 FY25 INR316 crore vs INR297 crore YoY (+6%)
items.quote: In Q2 FY '25, in our toll collection division, the company recorded a gross toll collection of INR316 crores as against INR297 crores in Q2 FY '24, recording a growth of 6%.

items.statement: Order inflow FY25 YTD ~INR6,000 crore
items.quote: Around INR6,000 crores.

items.quote: So as far as NIIF SPA was concerned, it had a long stop date which has expired quite some time back. So presently, it is not on , the SPA is not live. But we continue to engage. As far as JTC L is concerned, we are still await

items.statement: Expect to sign SPA for HAM projects in next couple of weeks (Q3 FY25)
items.quote: So we are -- as we have stated in the past, an d we are constantly engaging. And we expect that in the next couple of weeks, we should be able to sign on the SPA for the HAM projects also.

items.statement: Impairment reversal expected: ~INR800 crore at ACL level, ~INR250-300 crore at ABL level post BOT asset sale
items.quote: So there will be impairment at ACL level which will be reversed once these assets are sold off, which is almost -- at ACL balance sheet of almost INR800 crores. And at ABL balance sheet, there could be a reversal of approximately INR250 crores to INR300 crores post sale.

items.statement: ACL 34% acquisition from SBI Macquarie long stop date Jun 2025; expect completion Mar-May 2025
items.quote: We expect this transaction the long stop date for this transaction is June '25, and we expect to get that done somewhere in the month of March -- April, May '25.

items.statement: Remaining land bank book value ~INR210 crore; potential market value 3-4x
items.quote: So we would have approximately INR210 crores of land bank with our subsidiaries which will be available for sale, and which could have maybe a value 3x to 4x at least. These are land banks on an average hold of 6 to 7 years.

items.statement: Power project working capital cycle elongated; trade payables converted to WIP and debtors; client payment delays (elections) partly contributed
items.quote: Largely based on the working capital cycle. Of course, partly also on these slight delays in payment being released due to various non -administrative reasons. But capital cycle plays that way. So power projects which have been which require initial capital for procurement and other things, they take up a lot of working capital requirement because on the purchase side, there's a lot of competition

items.statement: Land monetization proceeds INR453 crore upstreamed to ABL for operations
items.quote: It's 100% subsidiary. Like whatever land was monetized , this INR450 crores, most of it was upstreamed to ABL for ABL's operations.

items.statement: Targets 5,000 tenancies in FY25 and another 5,000 in FY26, reaching 15,000 total by FY26 end
items.quote: We are 100% sure we will deliver 5,000 tenancies in FY '25 and same in FY '26. We have enough business from Vodafone , BSNL. Airtel's starting users upgrade and few sites are coming from Airtel.

items.statement: Guides for 3,000 sites in FY25 with 500+ in Mumbai, and 10,000 tenancies over FY25-FY26
items.quote: So, we are going to achieve a target of 3,000 sites in FY '25, 500, out of which 500 plus will be Mumbai and we are sure of achieving 10,000 tenancies in next two financial year, FY '21, FY '26.

items.statement: Expects around 9,000 towers in overall portfolio by March 2025
items.quote: In overall portfolio, yes. We'll have around 9,000 towers by March.

items.statement: Revenue growth projected at around 30% for FY25
items.quote: The revenue for '24, '25 projection -- percentage wise around 30% of growth overall.

items.statement: Maintains FY26 organic revenue guidance of ₹320 crore despite inorganic plans
items.quote: We will keep the same guidance of ₹320 crores. It's something, which we are working on Trident. Nothing has been closed right now. So , let's wait and watch for that.

items.statement: Targets 5 lakh home passes for FTTH over 3-4 years
items.quote: Raj, we are trying around to connect 5 lakh home passes. Every home is one pass. So, we are trying to connect 5 lakh home passes down like three years to four years.

items.statement: Preferential issue of ₹350 crore (₹250 crore investors + ₹100 crore promoter) to fund organic and inorganic growth
items.quote: In terms of ₹350 crores CapEx, what we are planning around ₹250 crores will be done with the investors , plus ₹100 crores will do warrant with the promoter.

items.statement: Estimates FY26 capex at ₹400-450 crore, funded by internal accruals and debt
items.quote: Again, CapEx in FY '26 would be around ₹400 crores, ₹450 crores, out of which maximum will come from internal accruals.

items.statement: Added 102 tenancies and 80 new towers in Q2; 450 sites ready for billing; 100 km fibre added
items.quote: We have increased our by 102, where we have already started our billing. 102 tenants has been added. 80 new towers is, that which means we have created 80 towers on which we have got 102 tenancy, which has been added in the billing system. Other than that, we have added another 100 kilometres of fibre.

items.statement: Order book visibility: 3,000-3,500 towers from Vodafone, 2,500+ from BSNL; targets 4,500-5,000 tenancies in H2 FY25
items.quote: We are on 3,000, 3,500 towers loaded by Vodafone and another 2,500 towers loaded by BSNL. That's in current visibility, which keep adding month-on-month basis as and when we get a new requirement from operator.

items.statement: Targets 2,500-3,000 BSNL towers in FY25 and same in FY26; revenue impact visible from FY26
items.quote: In terms of order, we already have more than 2 and a half 3000 towers list from BSNL, which we want to erect from them. In terms of fibre, well, we will not spe ll the exact number what we are targeting. But I want this that in my presentation that we are targeting around two and half, three thousand towers of BSNL in FY '25 and same in FY '26.

items.statement: Confirms margins sustainable at 70-75% EBITDA and ~35% PAT despite capex

items.statement: Maintained FY25 EBITDA margin guidance of 20-22% for consumables and 10-12% for equipment, blended ~20-21%
items.quote: Generally, we have been able to have a consumables EBITDA margin of close to anything in the range of 20% to 22%. And then in equipment, we have set our expectation of 10% to 12%. On a blended rate, we see any EBITDA margin for the group at around 20%, 21%, and we are confident of these numbers.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 13% vs 22% YoY due to one-time contract accounting expense of INR 17-20 cr
items.quote: The EBITDA margin has been muted due to the contract accounting, leading to a onetime expense in Q2, which has been charged off in the current quarter and shall lead performance in the subsequent period.

items.statement: One-time expense of INR 17-20 cr charged in Q2 FY25 related to inventory and installation for projects
items.quote: The onetime impact will be close to about INR 17 crores to INR 20 crores.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margins expected to revert from Q3 FY25 onwards
items.quote: Yes, we are confident, both our revenue estimate and the EBITDA margin estimate what we did, we shall be able to have those things going forward from Q3 onwards.

items.statement: Group order book INR 605 cr as of Sep 2024 including orders crystallizing in next 6-7 months
items.quote: We have a firm order book at a group level of INR 605 crores as at September 2024 end vis-a-vis an order without considering the long-term orders like the NMDC order in ML.

items.statement: Shipment delays and order deferments due to geopolitical issues; confident of recouping in next 2 quarters
items.quote: There have been certain delays in shipments and deferment of orders by customers, which we are confident of recouping in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Geopolitical issues causing shipment delays; teams made more agile to address disruptions
items.quote: These are mainly due to geopolitical issues, Chirag. And we would like these to get over ASAP, but we'll not be able to tell when.

items.statement: Major capex drive of $35-40 million including Chile project and Dahej plant; additional $10 million over FY25-26
items.quote: We have gone into a major capex drive of about $35 million to $40 million, which includes this capex of Chile as well as the Dahej plant.

items.statement: Chile project construction started; targeting commercialization by June-July FY26
items.quote: Earlier we had given an estimate of June, July of the next financial year. So we currently think we should be able to have the construction complete.

items.statement: Quarterly depreciation ~INR 26 cr; expected to continue at this level subject to capex capitalization
items.quote: Yes. So, these are the quarterly numbers. And for -- you should consider these are the quarterly numbers, which will be reflected in the subsequent quarters as well.

items.statement: Chinese competitors not considered serious in consumables due to service component; some Chinese-owned mines order from Tega
items.quote: Chinese competitors in the mining, have not been able to sustain products from overseas because in the mining and the consumables that we have there, there is a very large component of service and we have sales and service team all over the world.

items.statement: Consumable segment revenue grew INR 58 cr YoY in H1; equipment segment moderated to INR 82 cr from INR 91 cr
items.quote: The total revenues of the consumable business segment grew by INR 58 crores over the same period last year, whereas the equipment business segment moderated to INR 82 crores from INR 91 crores same period last year.

items.statement: Inventory increased as of Sep 30 due to shipment delays; inventory will convert to revenue in subsequent periods
items.quote: We even have an increase in the overall inventory levels, if you see as at 30th September, because of these delays what we have been speaking -- talking about. So all of this, inventory turns into revenue in the subsequent period.

items.statement: Bullish on copper demand driven by energy transition, digital trends and traditional growth; bullish on gold prices
items.quote: We believe that the copper demand shall be increasing due to a combination of three key themes that is traditional economic growth and the newer themes of energy transition and digital, that is primarily the data centers.

items.statement: Hopes to maintain ~100% revenue growth for full FY25 and expects new TPW range starting early next year to add volumes and revenue
items.quote: We have grown by almost 100% in the first half and we are hoping to maintain this kind of growth for this year. And once we add the new range that we are looking at beginning next year, we are hopeful that that will add numbers as well as revenue.

items.statement: TPW manufacturing facility investment likely around INR 3 crores, orders placed, targeting start early next year
items.quote: This particular TPW line that we are looking at, the value of this investment is likely to be in the range of about INR3 crores.

items.statement: Disclosed plan to set up new TPW manufacturing facility in North; orders placed, aiming to start early next year
items.quote: only, we have just made a disclosure to the exchange that we are looking at setting up a manufac turing facility for TPW. That's the plastic range of table, pedestal, and wall. The orders for the plant have been placed and we are hoping to start this sometime early next year

items.statement: Seasonal product leads to full booking in season and idle capacity off-season; adding machinery at different places to enhance capacity
items.quote: Utilization, you know, as I just mentioned a while ago, this being a very seasonal product, in the season we are kind of booked. But during the off-season, we have some idle capacity.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 2.68%; BLDC fans give slightly better margin but overall improvement driven by volume growth and cost optimization
items.quote: Additionally, our EBITDA margins improved to 2.68%, underscoring our focus on operational efficiency and cost management.

items.statement: Added electric heaters and kettles to diversify portfolio and cushion fan off-season; first year in category, see potential but cannot commit numbers
items.quote: Products such as electric heaters and kettles have been added with a view to diversify our portfolio, as well as to cushion the off-season in fans.

items.statement: Short-term loans/advances up INR 2 crores due to new MSME payment legislation requiring reduced credit terms; funds used for vendor bill discounting
items.quote: Yes, this is actually a requirement that came to us because, you know, of the new legislation that MSME vendors have to be made payment in a certain number of days to meet that commitment of, you know, reduced credit t erms to our vendors, we had to increase limits, which are being used for bill discounting of our vendors

items.statement: Claims to be only listed player in OEM/ODM fan space; differentiates via R&D, quality, timely delivery, seasoned management
items.quote: Not out of place to report that we are perhaps one of the only listed companies in this space and that differentiates us from the competition.

items.statement: Combined production capacity over 12 million units per year across three plants spanning 3 lakh sq ft
items.quote: These plants have a combined production capacity of over 12 million units per year, making us one of the most capable fan producers in the country.

items.statement: Main obstacle highlighted is seasonality of fan business; managed by adding heaters/kettles for off-season utilization
items.quote: Obstacles are only that, you know, this being a seasonal pro duct, that's the main obstacle

items.statement: Indian fan market growing strongly due to urbanization, residential construction, PM Awas Yojana, rising disposable income, and preference for energy-efficient BLDC fans
items.quote: The Indian fan market is experiencing strong growth, fuelled by rapid urbanization and increased residential construction. Initiatives like PM Awas Yojana, which aims to expand affordable housing, provide us with a direct opportunity to meet the rising demand for the same, particularly energy efficient options like our BLDC fans.

items.statement: Emphasizing cost optimization and operational efficiency to achieve percentage improvement in margins
items.quote: We are also emphasizing on cost optimization and looking at ways to further improve operational efficiency where possible to achieve some percentage improvement in margins.

items.statement: Seasoned management team with over five decades industry experience; next generation equally enthusiastic about growth
items.quote: With a seasoned management team bringing over fiv e decades of industry experience and a robust vendor network, we are well-posed for sustained growth and value creation for all

items.statement: Credit cost for Q2 FY25 determined at Rs 693 crore after auditor review, higher than earlier estimate of 500-550 crore
items.quote: I would like to mention that post the review of our auditors, our actual credit cost for Q2 FY25 has been determined at Rs.693 crore.

items.statement: Gross NPA at 9.41% and net NPA at 2.41% as of September 30, 2024
items.quote: The gross NPA stands at 9.41% and net NPA stands at 2.41% .

items.statement: ECL stands at Rs 1,140 crore including Rs 59.5 crore management overlay as of September 30, 2024
items.quote: The ECL, as on September stands at 1140 crores, which includes 59.50 crores of management overlay.

items.statement: Total write-offs in H1 FY25 at Rs 254.84 crore, with Rs 196.44 crore in Q2 FY25
items.quote: We have done total write off in H1 of Rs 254.84 crores. And in Q2 we have done write off of INR 196.44 crores.

items.statement: Covenant breaches on gross NPA, net NPA and CARE rating downgrade; all Q1 waivers received, confident of further waivers
items.quote: So as far as the covenant breaches are concerned, it is largely what you have said, Abhijit one is gross NPA, second is net NPA, and third is a rating downgrade which has happened by CARE, which was in the month of September .

items.statement: Rights issue of up to INR 550 crore being fast-tracked, promoters fully backing it, filing expected within this quarter
items.quote: We have already planned additional remedial measures, including the rights issue of up to INR 550 crore, on which we have been working on the last month or so. Now that our Q2 numbers are out, we have fast tracked the process and hope to file it within this quarter.

items.statement: Raised Rs 1,513 crore in Q2 FY25 including DA of Rs 435 crore; H1 FY25 total raise Rs 4,060 crore including DA of Rs 915 crore
items.quote: In Q2 FY25 we have raised 1513 crores, including direc t assignment of 435 crores , and till H1 we are able to raise INR 4060 crores, including direct assignment of 915 crores.

items.statement: Liquidity at Rs 1,800 crore approx with sanctions in hand of Rs 1,500 crore as of September 30, 2024
items.quote: As on September 30th, our liquidity stands at 1800 crores approx. and we have sanctions in hand of approximately 1500 crores.

items.statement: NIM reduced 15 bps QoQ to 11.48% due to higher write-offs; up 37 bps YoY
items.quote: The NIM of the company has reduced by 15 bps to 11.48% from and increased by 37 bps on year-on-year basis. QoQ drop is largely due to the higher write off taken in this quarter.

items.statement: Marginal cost of fund reduced 4 bps QoQ and 53 bps YoY; average cost of fund down 50 bps YoY and 4 bps QoQ
items.quote: Our marginal cost of fund has further reduced by 4 bps on quarter -on -quarter basis, and 53 bps on year -on-year basis. Average cost of fund has decreased by 50 bps on year-on-year basis and by 4 bps on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: MFI disbursements dropped to Rs 1,661 crore from Rs 2,987 crore in Q1 due to tighter credit criteria
items.quote: This has calibrated our overall disbursements which have dropped to Rs.1661 crore from Rs 2987 crore in Q1.

items.statement: MSME AUM grown to Rs 620 crore with 78% secured portfolio
items.quote: Our MSME AUM has grown to Rs.620 crore, with almost 78% of portfolio being secured.

items.statement: Reduced customer handling per relationship officer to 380 to improve outreach and collections
items.quote: To tackle the issue of low center meeting attendance , we have already reduced our customer handling per relationship officer to 380 customers per relationship officer, so that we can improve our customer outreach on ground with strong focus on customers with irregular attendance.

items.statement: Field officer incentive ~25-30% of salary (Rs 3,500-4,000 on Rs 15,000 base); never exceeded this proportion
items.quote: I totally agree with you , we have seen in our case the incentive out of the total salary is around 25%, 30% only. It has never gone beyond that. Just to give example, if RO gets around 15,000, so around 4000, 3500 to 4000 has been our average incentive over the years.

items.statement: PAR 0 composition higher for customers with Fusion plus 3+ and 4+ lender relationships; 85% of customers in top 5 states current or up to 30 DPD
items.quote: We have looked at our customers in the top five states, and what we saw that 85% customers are still current. They are either current or up to 30, but they are still, in the last six months, they have not gone beyond 30.

items.statement: Collection efficiency ~97% on current (0 DPD) bucket, consistent across months
items.quote: So at a pan India level, we have been maintaining almost 97% collection efficiency on that particular bucket. And this has been kind of consistent across the months .

items.statement: Pre-provision operating profit Rs 284 crore in Q2 FY25, up 17.39% YoY, down 4.67% QoQ
items.quote: As on September 30th, 2024 the pre-provision operating profit is INR 284 crore s increased by 17.39% on a year-on-year basis and decreased by 4.67% on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: DA outstanding at ~11.70% of total book as of September 30, 2024; will continue DA per market conditions
items.quote: The DA outstanding as of September 30, 2024 is approximately 11.70% of the total book, and we will continue to do so as per the market condition.

items.statement: No guidance provided for H2 FY25 credit cost; management sees peak provisioning in Q2, early green shoots but remains watchful
items.quote: From here on, we should see improvement in our performance based on the steps we are taking. Having said that, things still remain dynamic and we remain watchful. Therefore, I will reserve myself from providing any guidance for H2

items.statement: Focus on enhancing IT capabilities for operational efficiency, field personnel management and risk controls over medium term
items.quote: From a medium term perspective, our focus remains on enhancing our IT capabilities to improve our operational efficiencies, field personal management and risk controls.

items.statement: New in-house loan origination and customer management platform for MSME being rolled out for better efficiency and scalability
items.quote: We have implemented new loan origination and customer management tech pl atform, which has been built in -house, once fully rolled out, it will bring in better operational efficiency and scalability.

items.statement: Customer loyalty program in early phase showing encouraging response and improved attendance where launched
items.quote: We have been working on our customer loyalty program while it is in an early phase. We have received encouraging response from our customers, and we have seen improvement in their attendance wherever this program has been launched.

items.statement: Illegal agencies influencing borrowers in pockets of Eastern UP and other areas; sector working with state administrations to curb
items.quote: the point I am trying to drive is that, yes there are some small events here and there, which keep on happening like we have seen even in Eastern UP some of these events.

items.statement: Capex guidance: INR 470 crore on existing units, INR 500 crore on Noida (spent Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26), other projects over next 3-4 years
items.quote: If you see that what we are maintaining here is that there will be about INR 470 crores of capex on the existing units. And then the INR 500 crores on the Noida which will be spend in the somewhere Q4FY25 and Q1 of the next financial year when we order major medical equipment, etcetera.

items.statement: H1 FY25 capex incurred INR 370 crore including INR 131 crore for Mumbai land acquisition
items.quote: In the first half of FY2025, INR 370 crores of capex were incurred, including INR 131 crores related to the acquisition of land in Mumbai.

items.statement: Added 118 beds in Q2 FY25 (52 Lucknow, 66 Patna); H1 FY25 added ~280 beds (150 Lucknow, 84 Patna, 50 Gurugram)
items.quote: During the quarter, we have successfully expanded our capacity by 118 beds, comprising 52 beds at Lucknow and 66 beds at Patna.

items.statement: Plan additional 50 beds in Patna in coming months; capacity for 200 more beds in Lucknow and ~150 in Patna in near future
items.quote: We are also planning an additional 50 beds in Patna, which we hope to come on board in the next coming months. Furthermore, we have capacity within our current infrastructure to add 200 more beds in Lucknow and approximately 150 beds in Patna, which we will bring online in the near future.

items.statement: Noida facility construction progressing, anticipated opening Q1 FY2026
items.quote: Construction of our Noida facility is progressing well and we anticipate opening in Q1 FY2026.

items.statement: Signed O&M agreement for 750-bed super specialty hospital in Pitampura, New Delhi, to be jointly developed over next 4 years
items.quote: I'm pleased to announce that last week we signed an Operation and Management Agreement to operate and management a state-of-the-art 750 bed super specialty hospital in Pitampura, New Delhi.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 25.3% in Q2 FY25, up 170 bps QoQ; matured hospitals 25.3%, developing hospitals improved to 29.9% from 24.5% in Q1
items.quote: EBITDA margins were at 25.3% in Q2 FY25, an improvement of 170 basis points on a sequential basis.

items.statement: Matured hospital margins stable around 25-25.5% over several quarters; management sees efficiency opportunities but prefers conservative tariff increases
items.quote: So if you look at the matured one, you will see that the margins have moved around 25%, 25.5%, 25.3%. So yes, if you look at the last several quarters, it does appear that they are reasonably stable.

items.statement: ARPOB matured hospitals grew 6.2% YoY to INR 67,059 driven by tariff increases in Gurugram/Indore and case mix; developing hospitals ARPOB declined 5.9% YoY to INR 53,724 due to payor/case mix shift
items.quote: ARPOB grew by 6.2% to INR 67,059 in Q2 FY25, driven by tariff increases in Gurugram and Indore and changes in our case mix.

items.statement: Inpatient volumes up 8.8% YoY to 45,000+; outpatient volumes up 6.6% YoY to 7.75 lakh; average occupied bed days up 9.1% YoY
items.quote: Inpatient volumes during the quarter increased by 8.8% year on year to over 45,000 and outpatient volumes increased by 6.6% year on year to 7.75 lakhs.

items.statement: Consolidated occupancy 64.3% on increased bed capacity; matured hospitals 67%, developing hospitals 60%
items.quote: Average occupied bed days increased 9.1% year on year with a strong occupancy of 64.3% on increased bed capacity.

items.statement: Lucknow enrolled in Ayushman Bharat, Deen Dayal, and CGHS schemes; no bed reservation, scheme patients ~10-15% of revenue group-wide
items.quote: Medanta Lucknow has already enrolled in the Ayushman Bharat and Deen Dayal Health Schemes providing cardiac and radiation oncology services to a wider patient base. Furthermore, as of October 2024, we have secured the empanelment of the Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS) expanding our reach within the community.

items.statement: Patna PPP revenue share ~11% (volumes ~19%); Lucknow scheme revenue negligible; group cash/TPA ~80-85%
items.quote: I think that in Patna, we started out somewhere around 10% - 11%, if I'm not mistaken, of the PPP business, which is the only kind of scheme business we have. I think now it's probably heading up a little bit more, maybe closer to 15% - 20%. But I think about 80% of our business is still cash and insurance in Patna.

items.statement: Delhi NCR viewed as multiple distinct catchments; supply additions take 3-4 years to build + 2-3 years to stabilize; demand-supply gap remains large; not worried about competition
items.quote: So I don't worry at all about the capacity because the amount of time it takes, there will be a huge demand. Today, if we comp lete all the capacity announced by every player, tomorrow morning, it's still less from a supply-demand point of view

items.statement: Onboarded 25+ doctors in Q2 FY25; Lucknow added 6 senior directors in last 3 months; aggressive hiring continues across network
items.quote: We continue to strengthen our clinical capabilities and on-boarded over 25 doctors in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Gurugram hired ~80 senior doctors in last year despite being 13-14 year old facility; Noida attracting strong clinician interest pre-launch
items.quote: In a hospital that's 13 - 14 years old, we have still hired in very senior talen t. If I recall, that was almost somewhere around 80 senior doctors that had been hired in last year in a 13 - 14-year-old facility

items.statement: DLF South Delhi project delayed ~1 year due to pollution-related construction curbs and approvals; Indore project stuck in litigation, exploring alternatives
items.quote: I would say that if you look at it on an overall basis, I think it's probably been approximately one year that this project has been delayed because of the various compliances and approvals that we've been trying to get.

items.statement: Net cash surplus of INR 7,186 million at end of September 2024; balance sheet remains strong
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains strong with a net cash surplus of INR 7,186 million at the end of September 2024.

items.statement: Group revenue mix: ~21% Cardiac, 12% GI/Gastro, 14% Cancer; Lucknow adding new specialties (Ophthalmology, Plastic Surgery) and robotic surgery
items.quote: approximately 21% is in Cardiac, 12% is GI and Gastroenterology and about 14% is Cancer.

items.statement: Pitampura O&M: society to invest INR 200-250 crore on civil structure; Medanta to invest in medical equipment, services, finishing
items.quote: As far as capex, I would assume that the partner would be putting in somewhere INR 200 crores or maybe a little bit more, INR 200 - 250 crores of capex because they'll be putting up the civil structure, etcetera. And we will be putting in the services and the medical equipment and of course, the finishing to operate it.

items.statement: Guest house at Medicity: INR 250 crore for 250 keys, timeline 3-4 years; Medical school: ~4-5 lakh sq ft, INR 250-300 crore, starting with 100 seats
items.quote: 250 keys is what we're planning right now. And we'll see how it goes. Like I said, we are building on less than half of the actual land. So if it is a success, maybe we need to scale it up.

items.statement: International patient revenue ~6% of total (down from 11-12% pre-COVID due to Lucknow/Patna dilution); expected to rise as NCR/Mumbai facilities add capacity; geopolitical factors affect Bangladesh/Afghanistan flows
items.quote: Pre -COVID was really only Gurgaon and maybe to some extent Indore and Ranchi. So international business is only really in Gurgaon. As Lucknow and Patna contribute to the total pool, the share of international business will naturally reduce.

items.statement: Indore project litigation creates ambiguity; DLF project delayed by pollution curbs; both projects have less visibility on timelines
items.quote: As far as the Indore project goes, I think there the situation is a little bit more ambiguous. And that is why we have also commenced alternative thoughts in Indore to see how we can look at expanding our capacity.

items.statement: Gurugram completed 3,000 kidney transplants; performed first CAR T-cell therapy; Da Vinci Xi robot installed at Lucknow
items.quote: Notably, Medanta Gurugram reached a significant milestone by completing 3,000 kidney transplants. Additionally, our doctors achieved a breakthrough in treating Idiopathic Chylopericardium, a rare condition using minimally invasive approaches. Medanta Gurugram also performed its first CAR T-cell therapy, an advanced cancer treatment that harnesses the power of the patient's own immune system to fig

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of ~40% for FY25 maintained; full-year EBITDA margin now expected at 20-21% vs prior 22-23%
items.quote: We should be very close to achieve the number that we quoted in our last -- in revenue calls and in last investor call. And so we are hoping, and we are quite positive that we should reach to those numbers.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin guided at 20-21% for FY25 due to Welcome brand dilution
items.quote: We are expecting that the EBITDA should stand -- the whole year EBITDA should stand around or between 20% to 21%.

items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for Q2 F Y '25 is 17.97% compared to 20%, which is our guided range. However, I want to empha size that we are taking decisive action to address these challenges

items.statement: Acrylic PU products carry 10-12% higher net margins than polyurethane
items.quote: So gross margins of acrylic products. Finally, the net margins that company get is about 10% -- 10% to 12% more than polyurethane.

items.statement: Welcome brand EBITDA margin ~15%
items.quote: EBITDA here is coming out to be about 15%.

items.quote: Our price increase and average increase has been about 3.5%.

items.quote: See, historically, always Q3 has been a little down compared to Q2 and Q4 has been more or less the same or better than Q2.

items.statement: Acrylic PU products performed excellently in Q2; gaining traction in high-quality furniture and residential
items.quote: So the acrylic PU products have performed excellent in the quarter 2 and a lot of quality furniture manufacturers, including the high-quality residential side being done by architects has used and moved to acrylic polyurethane products instead of polyurethane.

items.statement: Welcome brand revenue INR11 cr in Q2; full-year target INR60 cr (vs INR48 cr last year)
items.quote: For this year, we are eyeing, and we are eyeing a revenue close to INR60 crores.

items.statement: Oikos revenue ~INR1.2 cr in Q2 (monthly run-rate ~INR40 lakh)
items.quote: Oikos is a recent launch and it's moving more or less on the same monthly average of about INR40 lakhs. So only INR 1.2 crores was the contribution from th e Oikos

items.quote: The decorative, we are not eyeing more than about I NR36 crores, INR37 crores revenue. So last year was about INR25 crores, INR26 crores. Thi s year, INR35 crores, INR36 crores

items.quote: Currently, our facility is working at about a 60% capacity utilization once the products, which were earlier being imported now being manufactured here has ramped up and by the end of year, we are expecting it to reach about 75%.

items.statement: New Gujarat (Dahej) facility planned with INR20-25 cr capex for 16,000 tons/year economical PU capacity (INR380-400 cr revenue potential)
items.quote: we will be doing a new capex of about INR20- odd crores in the Gujarat to set up a new facility to produce another 16,000 tons a year, whi ch can generate a revenue of economic polyurethane products of about INR400 crores

items.statement: H1 FY25 capex of INR22 cr was for Welcome brand acquisition; no other capex spent
items.quote: No, that is spent for the acquisition of the brand Welcome.

items.statement: Exports currently negligible (~INR20 lakh/month each to Nepal and Sri Lanka); trial container to Russia; target EUR20 mn (~INR180 cr) from Russia, UAE, Estonia, Saudi, Qatar within 2-3 years subject to Sirca Italy QC approval
items.quote: The revenue generation, which can happen, especial ly from Russia and the Asia Pacific is estimated to be about -- conservatively about EUR20

items.statement: Sirca Italy long-term QC testing (6+ months) underway for exports; approvals expected by year-end
items.quote: So we are expecting by the year-end, we should be able to get much more clarity from Sirca about their long-term testing of the products expor ted from the Indian facility to their old distributors in these South Asia Pacific countries

items.statement: Inventory elevated due to muted Q2 demand vs higher RM/FG planning; expect normalization in 4 months to 30-day inventory
items.quote: in the next 4 months, we will be in a much bett er position because against the top 10 products will be here and the whole imported stock will be out, where we will be working at a 30 days inventory

items.statement: Delhi NCR market share: Sirca 28%, Asian Paints 42% (stable for 6 years); Sirca leads in secondary sales via contractors/architects
items.quote: if we talk about Delhi NCR, we operate a stron g market share of about 28%. items.statement: Core wood coatings INR95 cr in Q2: 60% polyurethane (clear/pigmented), 40% acrylic/waterborne (up from 25% in H1 FY24)
items.quote: out of INR96 crores, the contribution from the r egular polyurethane products clear and pigmented, especially where the pigmented side saw a real jump was about 60% and the 40% was coming from the acrylic range of products

items.statement: Second acquisition target: brand in South India; non-binding stage; expected to close within FY25; budget capped at INR100 cr
items.quote: So still, it's taking more time than normal at the nonbinding stage. So hopefully, within this financial year, we should be out with our seco nd -- regarding the second acquisition, which is planned to be brand from South

items.quote: So we are p ossibly eyeing an acquisition where the expertise -- product expertise is towards the metal side
