items.quote: Key raw material suppliers like Covestro, BYK are now setting up the facilities and making India as a hub for Asia Pacific, where the cost of goods produced in India is seeing a very downside.

items.statement: Distribution network at 2,476 nodes (excl. OEM); marketing spend 4-5% of revenue (majorly B2B); focus on South/West expansion
items.quote: See currently, again, we are more or less on the sa me percentage that we did last year, which averages between 4% to 5% of our revenue

items.statement: Revenue from operations INR105.5 cr in Q2 FY25 (+26.2% YoY, +34.1% QoQ)
items.quote: Our revenue from operations reached INR105.5 crores, representi ng a 26.2% increase year-over-year and an even more impressive 34.1% growth quarter-over

items.statement: EBITDA INR18.96 cr in Q2 FY25 (+34.7% QoQ)
items.quote: Our EBITDA has rebounded significantly quarter-over-qua rter, demonstrating a 34.7% increase from quarter 1 of FY '25

items.statement: Construction ban in Delhi NCR (pollution) to impact Q3 for 15-20 days; offset via OEM and South/West retail
items.quote: But unfortunately, it's just ticked up, and we're e xpecting another 15, 20 days in the quarter 3 to be under the ban

items.statement: Red Sea shipping delays adding 30 days lead time for high-value imports from Italy
items.quote: Again, the time of getting the high-value products, which we are still importing from Italy has again increased from 2 to 3 months. So another incr ease of 30 days

items.statement: FY25 revenue expected to be in line with FY24; H2 FY25 revenue 8-10% above H1; FY26 more promising
items.quote: Our forecast sort of shows that because of the sort of slow nature of the market, we have to sort of revise the overall forecast for the year. So, while H2 will be about 8% to 10% over H1, the overall performance for FY '25 will be more or less in line with FY '24.

items.statement: Export revenue share expected to reach ~20% in Q4 FY25 and continue in FY26
items.quote: In Q4 of FY '25, we expect revenue share from exports to be about 20% of our revenue. And that trend then will continue in FY '26.

items.statement: Mahindra Thar ROXX 4WD bookings over 170,000 units with ~30% 4WD mix; current transfer case demand over 50,000 units
items.quote: The total demand that we are seeing out of the first tranche of bookings is over 50,000 units of transfer cases.

items.statement: Export component programs transitioning to steady-state supply; systems business could push exports >30%
items.quote: If the system-level business kicks in next year, we could see exports at more than 30%. Without the systems business, the revenue -- export revenue will be well over 20%. I think it's 22% or 23%.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 28%, up 463 bps QoQ; expect to maintain margin profile
items.quote: EBITDA margins for the quarter stood at 28%, improved by 463 basis points on quarter-on-quarter basis. This quarter, we regained our margin profile level and expect to maintain going forward.

items.statement: Invoked volume-based pricing clause in contracts to compensate for lower volumes; adjusted for commodity and FX changes
items.quote: So, we took advantage of that and were able to successfully renegotiate for the lower volume. In terms of some other achievements, we recently signed an MoU with one of the world's largest Tier 1 transmission manufacturer to conduct a feasibility study for pr oducing over 200,000 automatic transmissions in

items.statement: Fresh issue proceeds earmarked for automatic transmission capacity; 2-year gestation period needed
items.quote: And it's precisely for opportunities of this magnitude that we have done this fresh issue. And so, in a way, we'll come back a full circle and realize the original goal of putting capacity for automatic transmission manufacturing in India.

items.statement: Operating at significantly less than 50% capacity utilization; EBITDA >20% at current utilization
items.quote: And remember that all this is happening with significantly less than 50% capacity utilization. We are still able to turn out an EBITDA of over 20%.

items.statement: Dedicated hybrid transmission (DHT) feasibility study underway; quoted on DHT and 3-in-1 EDU opportunities
items.quote: We are currently starting a concept feasibility study because one of the things that has to be done is these solutions being highly engineered for the engines of the OEMs. We need to examine what is the degree and extent of fuel efficiency improvement we can deliver.

items.statement: New export business secured from China; senior sales visits to explore further opportunities
items.quote: I'm also pleased to report that we secured new export business from China, a pretty significant one. And we have followed that up with some critical visits of senior members of our sales organization to China to explore further opportunities to build on this success.

items.statement: Bid submitted for 3-in-1 electric drive unit for multinational OEM in India; discussions underway
items.quote: I'm also pleased to report that we have submitted a bid for what is called a 3 -in-1 electric drive unit for a multinational OEM in India to explore the opportunity to deliver the entire powertrain system.

items.statement: Automatic transmission feasibility study committed for completion by Dec 20; investment assessment for >200,000 units underway
items.quote: We have committed to the customer that we will complete the study by the 20th of December. It may take a few days here and there. But as you can see, it's a question of weeks and months.

items.statement: Indian auto industry facing ups and downs; Tata EV demand slackening and Mahindra 4WD growth lacking affected Q2
items.quote: Recently, I think other than Mahindra, the other OEMs have faced significant either flat sales or significant downward trend. And we, in particula r, have been affected by a slackening in the EV demand at Tata, which I think is well known in the industry

items.statement: EV 3-wheeler segment gaining traction; majority expected to electrify in 2-3 years; domestic and global ATV/UTV opportunities
items.quote: EV 3 -wheeler segment is gaining traction, and it is generally acknowledged that in the next few years, 2 to 3 years, maybe the large majority of the 3-wheeler industry will be fully electrified.

items.statement: India to introduce new emission norms in 2027; OEMs under pressure for multi-pronged electrification approach
items.quote: India will introduce new emission norms in 2027. So, a lot of the OEMs are under pressure to have their multi approach, multi -pronged approach to electrification and carbon neutrality worked out before then.

items.statement: Component export approvals delayed by couple of months due to China-Plus-One programs; US Tier 1s not under launch pressure
items.quote: And there has been a little bit of a delay, a little bit meaning a couple of months or so in the whole approval process because many of these programs are China -Plus-One kind of risk mitigation assignments that we have got.

items.statement: Fresh issue completed to fund automatic transmission capacity expansion
items.quote: And it's precisely for opportunities of this magnitude that we have done this fresh issue.

items.statement: Sales team credited for deft handling of volume-based pricing renegotiation with OEMs
items.quote: But it had to be adjusted for commodity changes, foreign exchange adjusted and so it took some amount of deft handling by our salespeople to bring this through. So, I will credit them for the hard work that they did.

items.statement: Defense supply chain bottlenecks resolved; significant uptick expected in defense work in Q4 FY25
items.quote: We are also seeing that whatever bottlenecks there were in the supply chain for the defense work have been unraveled. And so, in the last quarter, we expect to see a significant uptick in our defense work.

items.statement: Global transfer case opportunities being pursued in US and Southeast Asia; Indian Army track record aiding credibility
items.quote: Work is underway to tap global opportunities on our transfer cases both in the U.S. and also Southeast Asia. And as we make progress, we will provide updates on that.

items.statement: Long-range EV transmission prototyping completed with successful NVH test results; 100/100 scorecard from Tata Motors, zero PPM
items.quote: We have very successful test results, not completed the testing yet, but the most important aspect of the test is what we call NVH, noise, vibration, harshness because that is a measure of the refinement of the gearbox.

items.statement: FY25 revenue target of INR700 crores maintained, dependent on a large government contract expected to be finalized by mid-December
items.quote: We are working hard towards that line. And actually the one of the big government contracts is under consideration. And unfortunately the finalization of that contract is taking some time because of the value of the contract. Hence, it may be expected in next one month or so.

items.statement: PAT margin guidance for FY25 maintained at 4% to 5% range
items.quote: It will be between 4% to 5%. Because earlier it was 2.5% types. So we have reduced some cost and when the business increases, we get the leverage.

items.statement: Post-FY25 target of 20% year-on-year revenue growth
items.quote: So, after this significant growth we want to maintain 20% year-on-year growth in the coming years.

items.statement: UPSRTC partnership for express parcel services expected to generate INR60 crores revenue over five years
items.quote: We were appointed as an authorized partner for Express Parcel Services by the Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (UPSRTC), securing space in 9,000 UPSRTC buses for parcel delivery services. This partnership is expected to generate ₹60 crore in revenue over the next five years.

items.statement: Government tender under finalization with estimated INR100 crores revenue in FY25 from INR500 crores contract value
items.quote: The tender is a very big tender. We have estimated its revenue to be around INR100 crores. The tender value is INR500 crores. We are expecting INR100 crores revenue in this year of this tender.

items.statement: Targeting INR100 crores annual revenue from Dalmia and UltraTech cement contracts
items.quote: The contract they are making for 3 to 5 years, and they are having the good volume of business. It is on us how much we can service them. So our target is to complete the business of around INR100 crores per annum from these two companies.

items.statement: Express parcel business currently INR2 crores per month, targeting INR4 crores per month by end of FY25
items.quote: As of now, our express parcel business is around INR2 crores per month. And your question is right and, in our industry, the margins in express business are better than our other business. So, now we are targeting at least to make it double for the e -commerce industries and like small industries are there who are using the express service. So, we are trying to make it double this year say around

items.statement: Two acquisitions in progress: one ~INR45 crores revenue company closing in Q3 FY25, another ~INR170 crores revenue company closing in Q4 FY25
items.quote: So, out of the two deals, one is in the maturity level, and it will definitely complete in this quarter, current quarter, third quarter. And the second deal will be happening in the fourth quarter.

items.statement: Planning INR25-30 crores asset purchase and INR50 crores leased assets by March 2025 for steel and cement clients
items.value: INR25-30 crores purchase, INR50 crores lease
items.quote: we have to add 50-100 vehicles, then we can add an asset of INR25 crores-INR30 crores till March 2025. Arya Mehta: How many crores asset? Sanjay Gupta: INR25 crores-INR30 crores. Himanshu Sharma: We will add an asset of INR25 crores-INR30 crores, and we may take an asset of INR50 crores

items.statement: EBITDA margin pressure due to sale-and-leaseback and operating lease model; PAT improving under light asset model
items.quote: So, EBITDA is a bit reduced due to some of the vehicle we have done a transaction of sale and lease back. That is number one. And number two, we have further explored a leasing opportunity. And we took a few vehicles into the leasing as well.

items.statement: Cement and steel clients offer similar investment margins as FMCG but with faster payment cycles (1 week to 15 days vs 75-90 days)
items.quote: No, FMCG is a bit low. But what is there in it is that in FMCG, payment terms are a little high. Like customers are paying in 75 -90 days and in this industry, the payment terms are very competitive and 1 week or 15 days. So, our margin on investments are almost same.

items.statement: Added ~15 new clients in H1 FY25 including Indian Herbs, Haldiram, Anmol Biscuits, Devyani Foods, Dalmia Cement, Everest Industries, Shyam Steel, Supreme, EPAC
items.quote: So this time we have uploaded our presentation and on page number 13, we have given the list of the new clients which we have added in our FMCG sector and other sectors. Like we have added Indian Herbs, Haldiram, Anmol Biscuits, Devyani Foods, and electronics and other items. We have Dalmia Cement, Everest Industries, Shyam steel, Supreme, EPAC. So we have added around 15 customers.

items.statement: Expanding cross-border logistics to Nepal and Bangladesh for FMCG clients like Nestle, HUL, Colgate, P&G
items.quote: We are doing for 2-3 customers li ke Nestle and HUL , we are doing for this Nepal and Bangladesh, and we are talking to some other customers also because these are the countries where the plants are not available.

items.statement: Added 121 fleets in H1 FY25 to strengthen operational capabilities
items.quote: Continuing our expansion journey we added 121 fleets in H1 FY25 to strengthen our operational capabilities to meet the growing demand and expand our market footprint.

items.statement: Promoter warrant conversion ongoing: 655,000 shares already converted, balance 25% to be paid by mid-December 2024
items.quote: promoters already invested in 655,000 shares already converted by the promoters. Rishi Kothari: And that should be converted by whom? Management: By December 15 or 20. The last date is 31st December. So 25% has been already paid. So balance we need to pay by third week or maximum third week we will complete this

items.statement: Light asset model shift: sale-and-leaseback and operating leases reducing EBITDA but improving PAT and cash conversion
items.quote: So, this is the light asset model. And in this scenario, the PAT is improving whereas EBITDA is a little bit minorly, there may be some reduction. But overall PAT is improving, and we are working towards the light asset model business that leasing is available in the market.

items.statement: Truck pricing, toll tax, and operating costs increasing daily, driving customer shift to multimodal rail solutions
items.quote: Nowadays, because of the truck pricing, toll tax cost and other operations cost are increasing day by day. So the customers are shifting towards the multi-modal, which we have already run in the seven, eight trains on long-term contract with Indian Railways.

items.statement: National Logistics Policy target to reduce logistics costs to 8-10% of GDP by 2030 creates opportunities for integrated providers
items.quote: Looking ahead, the National Logistics Policy's target of reducing logistics costs to 8 -10% of GDP by 2030 presents significant opportunities for integrated logistics providers like us.

items.statement: Management guides for approximately 18% year-on-year top-line growth for FY25, with bottom-line growth target of 15-18% before a one-time customs duty impact of INR 50-60 crore.
items.quote: we are looking at around approximately an 18% growth year-on-year. The gold prices have been on an upward trend but let us assume an 18% growth year-on-year in terms of top line. In terms of bottom line our endeavour from the very beginning was to grow about 15% to 18%

items.statement: Management expects total customs duty impact of INR 58-60 crore for FY25, with INR 29.83 crore booked in Q2 and the balance in Q3.
items.quote: our total impact is likely to be around INR 58 crore to INR 60 crore. So now that INR 29.83 crore has come in quarter 2, balance amount impact will come in quarter 3 that is H2.

items.statement: October 2024 achieved best-ever monthly sales of over INR 1,000 crore driven by Navratri, Diwali, and Dhanteras.
items.quote: I'm very happy to share that this October, we achieved the best-ever sales in Senco's history. We surpassed INR 1,000 crore in sales for the month, with Navratri, Diwali, and Dhanteras all falling within the same period.

items.statement: H1 FY25 consolidated gross margin was 14.7% (15.7% excluding customs duty impact), in line with 15-16% guidance; full-year gross margin expected at 16-17%.
items.quote: if you look at H1 gross margin, that is around 14.7% as against 12.2%. Now, if you look at quarter-to-quarter, obviously quarter-to-quarter has come down. So if you look at Q1 versus Q2 movement is significant, but we've always indicated that since our industry is quite dynamic, and due to extreme volatility in the gold prices, despite a high hedging of 95%, the IndAS does not lead to a very symme

items.statement: Q2 standalone PAT grew 40% to INR 16.8 crore; H1 consolidated PAT grew 60% to INR 63.4 crore despite customs duty hit.
items.quote: Similarly, the PAT which in H1 last year was INR 39.6 crore has grown to INR 63.4 crore, a 60% improvement. And this is despite the fact that we have taken impact of around INR 29.83 crore on account of custom duty.

items.statement: Gold value growth 30% and volume growth 7% in Q2; diamond value growth 9% but volume decline 3%; studded ratio target 15% (currently ~10%).
items.quote: we have registered a 27% retail growth in Q2 and if you want to break it up, you will see that the value growth overall in gold was about 30% and in diamond it was about 9%. And in terms of volume, when gold prices rise, we see value growth but a decline in volume. However, in this case, we've experienced a 7% growth in gold volumes, while diamond volumes have declined by 3%.

items.statement: Enabled QIP of ~INR 500 crore to fund working capital needs arising from 25% gold price rise since IPO (INR 350-400 crore) and 12-13 new owned stores (INR 240 crore).
items.quote: This QIP is purely in order to maintain the business at the same level and that is why we are raising this fund primarily for the working capital.

items.statement: Franchisee secondary sales in Tier 2-4 towns drove Q2 growth; 80% of sales from East India, 10-13% from North.
items.quote: the primary sales to franchisee and the secondary scale that we saw the franchisees getting from their markets, which is usually the Tier 2, Tier 3, Tier 4 towns and cities has been the one which has actual ly driven the Q2 growth for Senc o Gold

items.statement: H1 FY25 same-store sales growth (SSG) 12-13%; Q2 SSG ~20%; Q3 SSG expected 12-15%.
items.quote: the SSG number what we have said is usually around 60% to 70% of total growth. So even Q2, when we are talking about around 20% growth, in H1 SSG is around 12% to 13%. So similar trend will prevail in H2 and in quarter 3 or quarter 4.

items.statement: Added Kartik Aaryan as brand ambassador for men's jewellery (15% of sales) targeting younger generation; Vidya Balan and Kiara Advani remain national ambassadors.
items.quote: We are happy to inform all of you that now, along with the fact that we have Vidya Balan and Kiara Advani as our national brand ambassadors. W e wanted to focus on men's jewel lery in a big way for which we have brought in Kartik Aaryan as the brand ambassador for men's jewellery, targeting the younger crowd and the younger generation

items.statement: Gold price volatility creates asymmetric IndAS accounting impact on quarterly gross margins; management advises viewing YTD or 3-4 quarter moving averages.
items.quote: due to extreme volatility in the gold prices, despite a high hedging of 95%, the IndAS does not lead to a very symmetric result. It's always better to look at YTD, where our gross margin is 14.7%.

items.statement: Raised FY25 top-line growth guidance to 50-55% from 45-55% and aims to double FY24 revenue in two years
items.quote: Given our strong performance this quarter, we are upping our guidance to 50% to 55% growth in our top line for FY25. We are very confident of doubling our FY24 revenues in the next 2 years.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 9.8% in Q2 FY25; management targets margin expansion over time through operating leverage and cross-sell
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA for the quarter reached INR29.5 crores or INR295 million, representing a growth of 36% year-on-year. So, for the overall total revenue has been INR302.6 crores, our adjusted EBITDA is INR29.5 crores, adjusted EBITDA margin is 9.8%.

items.statement: Propel gross margins dipped to ~3.5% in Q2 due to high Amazon/Flipkart usage but will normalize to 7-9% in H2 as overriding commissions kick in
items.quote: So, the current quarter the propel margins were reduced on account of high brand usage in terms of Amazon and Flipkart plus over the year-end, the margins will be disrupted because we will get overriding commission from brands on the volumes meeting. So, from next quarter onwards, end of this year H2, we will get the margins back to normalized margins of 7 percentage to 9 percentage.

items.statement: Signed marquee clients including HDFC Ergo, Baroda BNP Paribas AMC, Blue Star, Big Basket, Can Fin Homes, Equinox India, Pirelli Tyre
items.quote: Of late, we've been onboarding marquee clients, including Big Basket, Can Fin Homes, HDFC Ergo, Baroda BNP Paribas AMC, Equinox India, Pirelli Tyre, Blue Star, amongst others.

items.statement: Revenue breakdown: SaaS/platform fees INR8.5 cr, program fees INR126 cr, Propel Points INR168 cr (gross, 7-9% margin)
items.quote: Our SaaS fee, platform fee, or service fee, the revenue contribution of this line, stood at INR85 million or INR8.5 crores in the last quarter. Program fees, the revenue stood from program fees at about INR1,261 million Indian rupees or INR126 crores. Propel Points revenue stood at INR1,679 million INR or about INR168 crores.

items.statement: Zoyer AP platform gaining traction; petty cash and BBPS bill payments are key use cases; Dr. Batra's and Berkowits signed for Zoyer BBPS
items.quote: Zoyer, our accounts payable platform, has found a high degree of acceptance, and a major use case that has emerged is petty cash expense management. We foresee high acceptance of this solution in businesses with multiple location operations.

items.statement: Fleet solution went live with Torrent Gas; addressable market INR79,000 cr; ZIP forex/remittances tied up with card networks and partners
items.quote: I'm happy to share that our first fleet solution for Torrent Gas also went live this quarter. Overall, the fleet solution space is a very large, addressable market of INR 79,000 crores as per Government of India data, and we continue to be bullish about this space.

items.statement: Completed TaxSpanner acquisition for tax services; board approved investment in Mobileware Technologies; actively pursuing fintech M&A (NBFC, payments, SaaS)
items.quote: During this quarter, we completed the strategic acquisition of TaxSpanner, which will allow Zaggle to add comprehensive tax services to our repertoire of products, which are under spend management solution. We have also received the board approval for an investment in Mobileware Technologies, a company leading the payment infrastructure development in India.

items.statement: Board approved fund raise up to INR950 cr (INR9,500 mn) via QIP, subject to shareholder approval; valid for one year for organic, inorganic, international expansion
items.quote: In line with our growth plans, we have taken approval from the Board of Directors for a fund raise up to INR950 crores, which is INR9,500 million, subject to shareholders' approval.

items.statement: Gross debt INR555 mn vs cash & bank INR1,827 mn as of 30 Sep 2024; net cash position strong
items.quote: As of 30th September 2024, our gross debt is INR555 million with a cash and bank balance of INR1,827 million.

items.statement: Trade receivables rose to INR202 cr from INR175 cr due to business growth and September invoicing; collections received in October; expected similar levels for FY25
items.quote: So, the TR largely is increased on account of one business growth. And secondly, the businesses whatever invoicing to the banks happened that has come in the last month of the segment. So, for whatever we raise invoice s in September, we have received that money in the current month as well

items.statement: Focus on large enterprise accounts to lower CAC and increase LTV; cross-sell drives deeper integration (e.g., Subway Zoyer Petty Cash, Dr. Batra's Zoyer + SAVE)
items.quote: Through this year, there has been a heightened focus to find large enterprise accounts, which helps us to sell multiple products and use cases, lowers our CAC, and increases the lifetime value of the customer.

items.statement: Competitors facing funding winter headwinds; some shutting down, allowing Zaggle to capture their customer base
items.quote: What we see is that a lot of those companies are abandoning or getting closed down which gives us another beautiful opportunity to bite into their customer pool. And that is what I meant by when I said that there are a little bit headwinds to some of the smaller companies who are trying to copy our model.

items.statement: Conservative compliance approach; integrate directly with banks and widely accepted systems (NPCI BBPS via Yes Bank); partner with Axis, ICICI, SBI Cards, BOB, Yes Bank
items.quote: We've always held on the side of caution and taken a very conservative view when it comes to compliance and regulation. We've always looked to integrate directly either with banks or systems that are very widely accepted, so that we don't end up using platforms that are in the gray area.

items.statement: US market key international opportunity; cost advantage from India operations; board approval for fund raise includes international expansion
items.quote: In the international markets, US market remains as a key opportunity due to its vast potential. There are particular segments and segues which could possibly provide us an easier landing and faster expanding. We also see that there is a strong customer demand in the US for products like ours.

items.statement: Cash PAT surged 43% YoY to INR238.17 mn in Q2 FY25 (highest ever); H1 FY25 cash PAT up 72% to INR458 mn
items.quote: Our cash PAT, which includes net profit along with depreciation/ amortisation and ESOP expenses, has surged by an impressive 43% on a YOY basis to INR238.17 million, which is highest ever.

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue INR5,548 mn (+83% YoY), adjusted EBITDA INR551 mn (+55% YoY)
items.quote: For H1 FY25, our revenue from operations surged by 83% on a YOY basis to INR5,548 million. Our adjusted EBITDA has increased a substantial growth of 55% to INR551 million.

items.statement: Incentives and cashbacks reduced significantly in Q2 vs Q1 due to repeat usage, marquee client trust, and sales team discipline to keep cashbacks low
items.quote: So there's always an attempt to encourage our sales teams to keep the cashback at as low a level as possible. So those are, things that we've done both internally and externally to be able to get the cashbacks at a lower level right now.

items.statement: ONDC card not yet launched; signed partnership, targeting Diwali season missed; expect corporates and government to use ONDC for rewards/gifting
items.quote: ONDC, the card is yet to be launched. We have signed with ONDC which was the first step. We were hoping to tap into the Diwali season, but of course, these programs and products take a certain amount of time.

items.statement: Management not averse to becoming regulated payment instrument issuer or acquiring NBFC; will pursue if it accesses profit pools and customer demand
items.quote: We are not averse to it, to be a issuer of a payment instrument or an instrument which is regulated. For us, what matters is where are the profit pools, what's the demand from our customers and where is our sustained growth going to come from.

items.statement: Dr. Raj Narayanam received Lifetime Achievement Award at International Startup Foundation 2024 and honorary doctorate from Chitkara University; FinTech Center of Excellence launched
items.quote: This quarter, our founder and chairman, Dr. Raj P Narayanam, won the Lifetime Achievement Award at the International Startup Foundation 2024. Aligned with Government of India's pivotal initiatives like Startup India, Digital India, and Make in India, ISF aims to collaborate with over 50,000 startups.

items.statement: Global spend management market growing 10.2% CAGR; India market 15.5% CAGR; demand driven by efficiency, transparency, compliance needs
items.quote: As per the industry articles, the global spend management market is expanding at 10.2% annually, while the Indian market is estimated to expand at a CAGR of 15.5%.

items.statement: Pre-sales target of Rs 850 crore for FY25 with seven new project launches totalling GDV of Rs 1,150 crore
items.quote: Looking ahead, we aim for pre-sales of Rs. 850 crores for the current financial year with plans to launch seven new projects totaling to a GDV of Rs. 1,150 crores.

items.statement: Ongoing projects sold 5.39 lakh sq ft of 6.09 lakh sq ft generating Rs 1,370 crore with Rs 767 crore receivable; unsold inventory 2.71 lakh sq ft with GDV Rs 395 crore
items.quote: In our ongoing projects, we have sold 5.39 lakh square feet out of a total of 6.09 lakh square feet, generating approximately Rs. 1,370 crores with a receivable of approximately Rs. 767 crores.

items.statement: Future pipeline of 18 projects with over 9 lakh sq ft carpet area and GDV exceeding Rs 5,000 crore; 67% value luxury, 14% luxury, 7% mix, 12% commercial
items.quote: Looking at our future pipeline, we are awaiting upcoming projects with an estimated carpet area of over 9 lakh square feet for sale, approximately 67% of this is in the value luxury projects, 14% is in the luxury, and 7% is the mix of value-luxury and luxury.

items.statement: Raised Rs 343 crore via preferential allotment (Rs 243 crore) and convertible warrants (Rs 100 crore); received Rs 269 crore in Oct 2024, balance within 18 months for land acquisition, working capital, general corporate purposes
items.quote: We have raised Rs. 343 crores via preferential allotment of equity shares amounting to Rs. 243 crores and an additional Rs. 100 crores via issue of convertible share warrants.

items.statement: Approximately 40% of raised funds allocated for new business development and land acquisition to be expended before March 2025
items.quote: So, mainly the objects of the fundraise is also for business development, so a good portion of that would be, roughly around 40% would be for new BD and land acquisition.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA grew 16% YoY to Rs 128 crore; Q2 FY25 EBITDA Rs 64 crore vs Rs 63 crore YoY; PAT grew 97% YoY in H1 and 88% YoY in Q2
items.quote: EBITDA grew 16% year-on-year to Rs. 128 crores in H1 FY '25 versus Rs. 111 crores in H1 FY '24.

items.statement: Average realization Q4 FY24 Rs 53,650/sq ft, Q1 FY25 Rs 51,116/sq ft, Q2 FY25 Rs 48,366/sq ft; unsold inventory estimated at Rs 55,500/sq ft based on last three quarters average
items.quote: So, if you see our average realization quarter-on-quarter, Q4 average realization was about 53,650, Q1 was 51,116 to be precise, and this quarter was about 48,366.

items.statement: Construction cost seeing steady labor price increases but no substantial hike; labor shortfall across industry may marginally impact costs
items.quote: In terms of construction cost, we are seeing that labor prices have been going up steadily, which obviously will impact our construction cost. But we do not see a very substantial hike in the construction cost, it's normally steady.

items.statement: Value luxury segment (Rs 1-3 crore) showing steady growth in both realization and velocity; commercial segment seeing big demand; luxury segment doing well but prices expected to stay steady
items.quote: So, the traction we are seeing right now, which has always been steady has been the value luxury concept where it is between Rs. 1 crores and Rs. 3 cores. So, that is a constant segment in which there has been steady growth.

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue mix: 40.9% from luxury units, 59% from value luxury units; upcoming pipeline 67% value luxury, 14% luxury, 7% mix, 12% commercial
items.quote: 40.9% of revenue came from sales of luxury units and 59% of revenue from sales of value luxury units.

items.statement: Marinagar project: first phase approvals received with live IoD for two buildings, five more buildings planned, design underway, targeting big launch next year; Girgaonkarwadi to commence following year
items.quote: In terms of Marinagar we have already got the first phase of approvals where we already have live IoD in two upcoming buildings there. There would be slight minor amendments in the plan in terms of adding five more buildings in the redevelopment phase.

items.statement: Bandra project: first phase approvals received, design and technical details being worked out, targeting launch between Q2 and Q3 next year
items.quote: So, things are moving positively in the Bandra planning. I think like we informed earlier, we already have the first phase of approvals. We are looking at the larger piece, so design and a lot of technical details are getting worked out as we speak.

items.statement: Suraj Vibe commercial project on Tulsi Pipe Road: ~1 lakh sq ft, RERA underway, part of launch pipeline for this year, good client interest
items.quote: So, on Tulsi Pipe Road we have approximately 1 lakh of square feet. The RERA is underway, which is also part of our launch pipeline for this year.

items.statement: RERA approvals taking longer due to increased compliances from recent circular, extending timelines for project launches
items.quote: Normally RERA approvals take some time. The number of compliances from RERA standpoint also has increased in the recent circular. So, normally it does take time to get that approval compared to earlier.

items.statement: Weighted average cost of debt at 13%; debt increased as of September due to approval-related costs for upcoming launches (Tulsi Pipe Road and Parkview 1); fundraise completed after September
items.quote: To answer your question, the cost of debt remains at the same level, 13% weighted average cost of capital.

items.statement: Collections grew 90% YoY in Q2 FY25 and 46% YoY in H1 FY25 due to new project launches and higher sales volume
items.quote: Collections grew 90% year-on-year in quarter two FY '25 and 46% year-on-year in H1 FY '25 on account of new project launches and higher sales volume.

items.statement: Pre-sales grew 26% YoY in Q2 FY25 and 13% YoY in H1 FY25 despite seasonally weak quarter; realizations grew 10% YoY in Q2 and 12% YoY in H1
items.quote: Pre-sales grew growth rate of 26% year-on-year in Q2 FY '25 and 13% in H1 FY '25 despite a seasonally weak quarter and the occurrence of some inauspicious period during the quarter.

items.statement: Combined receivables of Rs 1,162 crore from sold and unsold ongoing portfolio expected to materialize between FY25 and FY29
items.quote: The combined receivables of Rs. 1,162 crores from sold and unsold portion of our current ongoing portfolio are expected to materialize between FY '25 and FY '29.

items.statement: MMR inventory overhang steady at 14 months as of Q3 2024; affordable segment 32% of Mumbai inventory; peripheral central suburbs 30% of Mumbai available units
items.quote: Compared to the previous quarter, the inventory overhang in the MMR remained steady at 14 months by the end of Q3 2024.

items.statement: Targets ROE 20% and ROCE 25% for full year FY25
items.quote: We continue to remain on track to achieve the return on equity of 20% and ROCE of 25% for the full year with ROE of 11% and ROCE of 15% for the half-year ended September 30, 2024.

items.statement: Aims to become 1,000-bed hospital chain within next 2-3 years
items.quote: As previously announced, we are steadfast to become a 1,000-bed hospital chain within the next 2-3 years.

items.statement: Raipur Hospital to commence operations in Q4 FY25
items.quote: The Raipur Hospital, a 160-bed facility, will commence operations from Q4 FY25.

items.statement: Expects double-digit revenue growth in H2 FY25 after flat H1
items.quote: Hopefully, we should be able to deliver on that. First half was slightly out of our control because of the local issues and the floods in Tripura. Hopefully, we should be able to deliver in the second half, and especially with the Raipur hospital being commissioned in Q4, that should add more flip to the functioning.

items.statement: Maintenance capex runs INR 8-10 crore annually
items.quote: The current maintenance capex varies between INR8 crores to INR10 crores on an annual basis. This is more or less standard.

items.quote: We have already started with the PET scan for this department and we are awaiting the installation of the LINAC. Any timeline for that? Management: So, as I said, the PET scan is already on and the LI

items.statement: Howrah orthopedic surgical robot to be available by end of year
items.quote: We are in the process of procuring an orthopedic surgical robot for this hospital as well. The facility shall be available by the end of the year.

items.statement: Dum Dum plans full-fledged cardiothoracic surgery setup and clinical revamp
items.quote: The company intends to commence a full-fledged cardiothoracic surgery setup and is revamping its other clinical offerings in this hospital as well to further strengthen its scope of service.

items.statement: Group ARPOB INR 36,700 in H1 FY25
items.quote: Notably, our ARPOB stands at INR36,700, aligned with our commitment to serving the aspiring population of the society with higher disposable income in the middle to higher income segment.

items.statement: Group bed occupancy 54% on amalgamated basis
items.quote: The company-level bed occupancy rates stood at 54% on an amalgamated basis.

items.statement: Group ALOS reduced to 3.51 days in H1 FY25 from 3.98 in H1 FY24
items.quote: The ALOS has reduced from 3.98 in H1 last year to 3.51 in H1 2025. The same is on account of our continuous efforts towards changing the case mix.

items.statement: Salt Lake ARPOB rose to ~INR 39,500 in H1 FY25 from INR 33,850; inpatient volume up 13% vs trailing H2
items.quote: ILS Hospital Salt Lake is an 85-bed surgical excellence hospital. The ARPOB for this hospital has risen from INR33,850 to almost INR39,500 in H1 FY25. Additionally, there has been a 13% increase in patient volume in comparison to trailing H2.

items.statement: Salt Lake ALOS reduced to 2.77 days from 3.19 YoY
items.quote: In our pursuit of optimizing services, we have been able to reduce our length of stay to 2.77 days from 3.19 on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Agartala inpatient volumes up 12% QoQ; ALOS down to 3.08 from 3.35 days
items.quote: The inpatient volumes have increased by 12% on a quarter-and-quarter basis, combined with a reduction of length of stay to 3.08 days from 3.35 days.

items.statement: Dum Dum ARPOB ~INR 41,400 in Q2; ALOS down to 4.43 from 5.22 days YoY
items.quote: The Dum Dum Hospital has recorded an ARPOB of approximately INR41,400 for the quarter. In line with our intent to reduce the length of stay of this hospital, the length of stay has reduced to 4.43 days compared to 5.22 in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Howrah inpatient volume up ~22.8% QoQ; ARPOB up 21% YoY in H1; ALOS down to 3.31 from 3.87 days
items.quote: The inpatient volume has seen an increase of almost 22.8% from the previous quarter. ARPOB of H1 FY25 has increased by 21% on a Y-o-Y basis and the length of stay has also come down to 3.31 days compared to 3.87 days in the previous fiscal.

items.statement: Bangladesh patient flow (~5% of Agartala volumes) disrupted in Aug-Sep; recovering from Nov
items.quote: So, roughly, Bangladesh volumes in our Agartala Hospital is almost 5% of our patient volumes, which was impacted in the month of August and September. It is in November that we are seeing a re-trickling of that again.

items.statement: Local issues and floods in Tripura impacted Q2 volumes; expecting uptick from Q3
items.quote: Unfortunately, in the previous quarter, because of local issues and some natural calamities in the areas where we end up operating in, we could not get the volumes which we generally end up getting in quarter 2. But hopefully, with the situation having been corrected, we can see an uptick in the volumes from this quarter which will end up giving you that effect you are wanting to see.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 revenue INR 106 cr, EBITDA INR 26 cr, margin 24%; H1 PAT INR 25 cr, PAT margin 12%, EBITDA margin 24.2% (+80 bps)
items.quote: Revenues for Q2 FY25 stood at INR106 crores with EBITDA of INR26 crores and a margin of 24%. PAT for H1 stood at INR25 crores with a 12% PAT margin and the first six months witnessed a 5.2% year-on-year growth. EBITDA margin has increased by 80 basis points to 24.2% with a slight increase of 2% in EBITDA for the quarter to INR26.3 crores.

items.statement: Finance costs down 58% YoY due to debt reduction
items.quote: Finance costs have come down by 58% on account of reduction of debt reflecting our efficient financial management.

items.statement: 94% of patient business from cash and insurance-paying patients
items.quote: Moreover, due to our neighbourhood model, approximately 94% of our patient business continues to be from cash and insurance-paying patients only.

items.statement: Top 10 specialties contribute 80% revenue; key: gastroenterology, general surgery, nephrology, cardiology
items.quote: So, the top 10 specialties are diversified. 80% of our revenue comes from the, from 10 departments, a majority of which are gastroenterology, general surgery, nephrology, cardiology.

items.statement: Focusing on short-stay departments (gastro, urology, orthopedics, cardiology) to raise ARPOB and volumes
items.quote: We are focusing on other short-stay departments like gastroenterology, urology, and are ramping up numbers. Overall, the length of the stay coming down is a good phenomenon for us as we will be in a position to take more patients across all our hospitals.

items.statement: Manipal acquired AMRI and Medical Hospitals, becoming major force in East; no other landscape changes
items.quote: So, there has been a change in the competitive landscape with the acquisition of AMRI hospitals by Manipal. That is the only change which we have seen in the eastern part of the country. Apart from that, Manipal has also acquired Medical Hospitals. So, Manipal has become a force in the eastern part of the country over the past one or two years. Apart from that, there has not been any other change

items.quote: No, the Ranchi expansion has not been cancelled. I think we are awaiting some regulatory clearances from the government of Jharkhand. Currently, there are elections in Jharkhand. So, that process is getting delayed. As soon as we have some clarity on the regulatory approvals, we will update the investors accordingly.

items.statement: West Bengal operates Swasthya Sathi scheme (similar to Ayushman Bharat); PMJAY applies in Agartala and Raipur
items.quote: West Bengal has a scheme called Swasthya Sathi by which is very similar to Ayushman Bharat where people under a particular income category are covered by it. So, that is what is the predominant healthcare scheme in West Bengal. Apart from that, in our other hospitals of Agartala and even in Raipur, we do have PMJAY which is applicable.

items.statement: Agartala oncology block expected INR 20 cr annual revenue at maturity
items.quote: Once the oncology department is in full-fledged operations, we expect it to give a revenue of almost 20 crores annually after its maturity.

items.statement: Raipur hospital expected to break even at EBITDA level in 15-16 months post commissioning
items.quote: Generally, our hospitals, our latest hospital of Howrah broke-even in 8 months from the rate of commissioning on an EBITDA basis on a month-on-month level, but we understand Raipur will be a new market for us. We are hoping that we will be able to break even by around the 15-16 month mark, post which it should contribute positively to the EBITDA of the hospital.

items.statement: Management will not provide forward-looking revenue or margin numbers but expects H2 to be stronger than H1 based on historical seasonality and a strong order book.
items.quote: For coming 6 months I will not be able to make any forward -looking statement, but what I can assure you is that we are looking at a good order book.

items.quote: Our order book is looking very nicely placed. Our endeavor is to grow last year's number.

items.statement: No sign of recession; order booking is very strong and two large international orders (Switzerland, France) have been won recently.
items.quote: No. Mr. Arora, our order booking is very strong and our performance is there in front of you. So there is no recession, nothing which we, kind of, have to worry about.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA margin was ~10.6% (INR12.62 cr on INR119 cr); full-year margin historically ~15% due to fixed costs and H2 revenue skew.
items.quote: Our EBITDA has gone up by 94% from INR 6.5 crores last year to INR12.62 crores this year.

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue INR119 cr, up 68% YoY from INR70.91 cr.
items.quote: In terms of top line, we have done about INR119 crores as our top line, which is 68% higher than the last year's number, which was around INR70 crores.

items.statement: FY24 full-year revenue was INR237 cr, with ~70% (INR167 cr) generated in H2.
items.quote: If we compare it to last year, out of INR237 crores, we only did INR70 crores in the first half of the year. The rest of the business was in the second half.

items.quote: We've opened our Kolkata office. We've hired a new team under the leadership of a gentleman who has about 24 years of work experience in the MICE industry.

items.quote: We have increased our manpower. We have from a number of about 50 -55 till 31st of March. We are currently about 79 -80.

items.statement: Working capital increased to >INR50 cr post-IPO from ~INR30 cr a year ago; management says current level is comfortable for growth plans.

items.quote: We have a portal, which is called Book My Yatra, which is, the compliance is all done. We are in a process of hiring our leadership. There is a CTO, which needs to be hired.

items.quote: Just a ballpark figure maybe out of the 119, just about 20% would be new customers. Maybe, I could be wrong. Remaining would be the old customers.

items.quote: There are some plywood companies, the wooden companies, which have empaneled us. There are some steel TMT companies, which have empaneled us. There are other cement companies, which have empaneled us.

items.statement: Business is discretionary but historically resilient; only downturn was COVID; corporate incentive spend rises when sales slow.

items.statement: IPO proceeds removed working capital constraints and cost of funds, enabling larger order execution without bank borrowing.
items.quote: Once we have funds available, there is no cost of funds, the interest part is saved, because we used to take money from banks and we used to, there is a cost of money also.

items.statement: No dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on growth and execution.
items.quote: We would like to take this opportunity to thank our shareholders and we appreciate the trust you have given, you put in us and you are our shareholders and we look forward to doing well in future also.

items.statement: Wedding segment entered aggressively in FY25; two large wedding orders won (numbers to be disclosed later).

items.statement: Subsidiary is Mach Conventions and Voyages Private Limited; Mach Films is not a subsidiary.
items.quote: We have only one subsidiary company which is Mach Conventions and Voyages Private Limited. Mach Sales is not our subsidiary company.

items.quote: So the demand is looking good in the metal side. We are also seeing strong demand arising in FMCG, industrial chemicals, as well as MSMEs. So the demand is very strong right now, sir. items.quote: You will see that the domestic loading has been affected this year due to very heavy rains, especially in North India and Gujarat in the first half. items.quote: EBITDA has grown quite handsomely by 10.15% to INR716 million in H1 FY25 as compared to INR650 million in H1 FY24. EBITDA margins, like I said, have improved 53 basis points to 8.38% from 7.86% in H1 FY24. This is led by cost optimization, like I said.

items.quote: EBITDA margins have also improved by 50 basis points to 8.38% compared to 7.88% in Q2 of FY24. The improvement in margins is two various factors, the most important being optimization of our operations and ensuring that we reduce redundancies like detention and damage.

items.quote: So fuel costs, what happens? I want to tell you that most of the fuel costs of all our large contracts, most of them are on a DPVC basis. DPVC is diesel price variation cost. items.quote: From the top five clients, ma'am, if we include all the companies, so say for example, when I say Tata Steel, I work with several of their units, right? So the five top groups, I would say, not the five top companies, would be about 70% of revenue for us.

items.quote: Today as we speak, about 80% of our revenues have been generated for customers who have been doing business with us for over 3 years and beyond. items.quote: So, sir, working capital cycles actually started increasing from the time of Corona, sir. items.quote: No, for sure, this is going to improve, sir. items.quote: So, ma'am, there are basically two major reasons for that. items.quote: So the utilisation rate is now picking up post the monsoon, sir. items.quote: The H1 containers that we've done is 1,03,816 containers compared to 1,02,764 in H1 of last year. In absolute terms, this is a growth of over 1,000 containers and most of this growth is coming from the domestic side of the business where we've seen a large growth.

items.quote: Last year, we did about 1,300 crores. So, we have said that we will have close to 40% to 50% growth this year. We are hoping that we are able to keep a substantial level of growth even going forward next year.

items.quote: It is still being delivered and we have also got, as I mentioned, we have a total order book which is already signed of 6,000 crores.

items.statement: Actively pursuing M&A opportunities in India that are synergistic, complementary, enable components-to-systems transition, new products/sectors/geographies, and expand Make in India strategy
items.quote: In terms of M&A opportunities there are plenty of opportunities, but we are looking at opportunities which are synergistic, which are complementary and where we can significantly add value and go from components to systems, get into new products, new sectors, new geographies and also where we can expand the Make in India strategy that we have. items.statement: European and Swedish operations being downsized; committed to fixing in short period

items.quote: It is important to understand that new orders will take time to convert into revenues and may create lumpiness in quarterly performance while the business remains on the strong fundamental when dealing with the 3-to-5-year horizon.

items.quote: I would expect our revenues in India from next year to grow at a faster rate than the revenues from export simply because we are starting from a smaller base, and eventually I think domestic will become 30% to 40% over our overall business.

items.statement: Naval systems (10-15% of defense revenue) and unmanned systems identified as key domestic growth areas for next 12-24 months
items.quote: So, the naval system right now is all domestic. And what I am saying is that is the business that will grow, first domestically and then globally.

items.statement: Management expects revenue to increase commensurately with capacity utilization improvement, subject to market realizations, but declines to give formal guidance.

items.statement: Historical EBITDA margin range 4-6%; expects 200 bps improvement in better scenario; H1 FY25 EBITDA margin 4.46%.

So, that is what is the broad range that we have been able to achieve. And going forward, our endeavour will be to sort of drive the margins further by increasing the capacity utilization and improvising a product mix.

items.statement: Cost optimization project enables direct charging of billets to wire rods, eliminating reheating, reducing fuel consumption and carbon footprint; power consumption increases slightly.

items.quote: And we also generated INR100 crores of free cash flow. I think this is a big achievement for this year, mainly driven by optimization in working capital and also low capex.

items.quote: And of course, R&D, we have strong R&D around 175 people in AP R&D. They are capable to do at least INR10 crores, INR12 crores in a year.

items.quote: And as far as fiscal '25 is concerned, we should see revenues from this jurisdiction stand at between roughly just under INR100 crores.

items.statement: Brands pushing incremental business for Spring 2025 production in Q3
items.quote: Particularly with Q3 production for spring 2025, brands are pushing incremental business to suppliers like us. And are promising good set of quarters ahead.

items.statement: No pricing power this financial year due to global supply exceeding demand; expect pricing power from H1 FY26
items.quote: So, at the moment, when we are trying to ask for increased pricing for increased cost, that is not on the cards, especially for this financial year. Because there is enough, enough capacity going up again, and competing with us.

items.statement: Kenyan Shilling appreciated 20-25% from KSH 160 to 129 vs USD, increasing Atraco costs
items.quote: In addition in Atraco we also had the Kenyan Shillings, which was at an all time high . It moved from ksh 160 to ksh129 against US $, it's moving in that range. So, when Kenyan Shillings went up sharply, our cost in dollar terms went up

items.statement: ECGC covers 90% of Indian receivables; supply chain finance covers ~50% of international receivables; ~80% consolidated coverage
items.quote: For Indian operations, we do have an ECGC cover as a guarantee which guarantees are receivables from our customers. I think ECGC covers to the extent of 90% of the receivables.

items.statement: US$30 million debt in Atraco Dubai books for tax efficiency; Indian entities debt nil; plan to reduce Atraco debt by US$10 million
items.quote: The debt is in Atraco books in Dubai. It was done from a tax-efficiency point of view. So, about US$30 million debt we are carrying in Dubai books. Otherwise in Indian entities the debt is nil

items.statement: Invested Rs 80 crore in BRFL fabric processing unit (Rs 60 crore by Q2, Rs 20 crore in October)
items.quote: Until the end of Q2, it has been Rs. 60 crores. And I think in October we have infused another Rs. 20 crores. So, it is about Rs. 80 crores.

items.statement: Top 5 customers (GAP, Carhartt, Columbia, JCPenney, Abercrombie & Fitch) contribute 65-70% of revenue; top customer ~27%
items.quote: Our top five customers are GAP, Carhartt, Columbia and JCPenney, which will be the fifth one I think it is Abercrombie & Fitch. So, these are some of the customers. The combined contribution of the top five customers to our total revenue will be approximately 65% to 70%

items.statement: Global sourcing shifting from China, Vietnam, Bangladesh to India due to supply instability and supplier consolidation
items.quote: The long-term outlook is also very favorable, supported by a continued shift in global sourcing away from China, Vietnam, even Bangladesh, where there is turmoil at the moment.

items.statement: UK-India FTA progress minimal but would be very positive if implemented; Bangladesh duty advantage being forgone by buyers
items.quote: So, there has not been much progress. There is an intent on both sides, but there has not been much progress on the UK India FTA. So, we do not know what will happen or what will be the eventual outcome.

items.statement: Standalone revenue run rate ~Rs 650 crore/quarter, targeting Rs 670-680 crore in Q3; consolidated targeting Rs 1,000 crore/quarter
items.value: Rs 670-680 crore standalone, Rs 1,000 crore consolidated
items.quote: Standalone, currently we are at, I think this quart er we were at Rs. 650 crores or thereabouts. And I think in the quarter ahead, we should be closer to about Rs. 670 crores, Rs. 680 crores in that region. And at a consol basis we should probably cross Rs. 1000 crores

items.statement: Current footprint max revenue ~Rs 700 crore/quarter standalone; Bhopal Unit-2 adds Rs 175 crore annually; Atraco expansion adds Rs 70-85 crore; Matrix expansion adds Rs 100 crore
items.quote: If you ask me, if you talk about max revenue, our current footprint should yield approximately Rs. 700 crore. And if you look at Unit-2 of Madhya Pradesh that will on an annual basis yield another Rs. 175 crores of revenue.

items.statement: Biggest risk is cyclicality from retail cycles, inventory swings, and customer financial health; mitigated by customer selectivity, low-cost footprint, and product versatility
items.quote: So, we have to understand why is the cyclicality? So, the cyclicality happens for many reasons. One is of course the retail industry itself can be cyclical because of economic changes etc., etc.

items.statement: Focus on high-margin women's fashion and sportswear knits; avoid low-margin core programs; woven and high-value knit margins at par
items.quote: We tend to remain in the highly profitable women's fashion business, etc. We tend to stay away from men's, kids we use, because their the pricing will be sharper.

items.statement: Heavy absenteeism in Q1 due to elections caused production outage and air freight costs in Q2; issue resolved
items.quote: In India as well, we had some one-time air freighting because of spillover from Q1 when we had some production loss, for production outage on account of heavy absenteeism in Q1 due to elections.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target of around ₹500 crores; FY27 another ~20% addition possible
items.quote: FY '26, like earlier, we had said we will be touching somewhere around ₹500 crores of the top line. And FY '27, another addition of some 20% might be there.

items.statement: PAT target of over ₹100 crores by 2026-27 remains on track and likely to be overachieved
items.quote: yes, we are in line with what we have said for 2026 and '27. I think it is definitely doable. We will be overachieving that.

items.statement: Mumbai 300-room hotel expected to start operations by end of FY25 (March); licenses targeted by end of February
items.quote: We are working at a fast pace to complete our 300 room hotel in Mumbai and hopefully, we should be able to start operation towards the end of the current financial year.

items.statement: Surat managed property at 188 keys currently, targeting full 288 keys in ~12 months with phased opening
items.quote: we will get to the 288 keys, I would say in about 12 months from now, right? Along with each one of the room opening, the room blocks, I guess, room floors opening, a couple of new facilities are added to it.

items.statement: Management expects better margins in coming quarters as new hotels stabilize and renovations complete
items.quote: We are working to post better margin in th e coming quarter than what the company has witnessed in the recent past

items.statement: North Goa micro-market suffered due to heavy rains/weather in Q2, a one-off impact
items.quote: in one market, we did suffer in North Goa, it's very public, actually in the papers, if you read, North Goa was actually really suffering as a micro market, and it did affect us year-on-year in quarter two. But that being said, that was largely a one-off period due to weather.

items.statement: Like-for-like revenue growth of ~15% expected next year from existing hotels driven by ARR, occupancy, F&B and renovation benefits
items.quote: So overall, I feel that the revenue should go up by next year by 15% of the existing hotels.

items.statement: Healthy cash profits; Ind AS adjustments are non-cash; PAT before Ind AS would have been ₹8.72 cr vs reported ₹7.52 cr
items.quote: without Ind AS, our PAT for the quarter would have been ₹8.72 crores instead of ₹7.52 crores as reported by us. This Ind AS adjustments need to be done as per accounting standards. However, they're not cash in nature.

items.statement: Renovations funded through internal accruals, not bank loans
items.quote: Most of the renovation is being done through internally generated resources. And I think things are looking quite well.

items.statement: SEBI final order dropped allegations against promoters on share sales; penalty on accounting treatment stayed by SAT, appeal ongoing
items.quote: the SEBI, the final order has come wherein they have removed all the allegations against the promoter sale of share. That has been dropped. But they are stuck to the accounting treatment, okay? So there was a levy of penalty on three of the m anagement as well as the company. We have gone to SAT and we have filed an appeal, and we got a stay from the SAT on that

items.statement: Gurgaon hotel is a revenue-share model (100% revenue to Royal Orchid, fixed rent to landlord); no P&L expense in Q2
items.quote: It's a revenue share. It's not a share. So we will own 100% of the revenue, and we will give the landlord a fixed rent on the asset when completed.

items.statement: Mumbai hotel pre-opening costs ~₹3 cr/month starting Q3; first costs ~₹1-1.5 cr in March; Gurgaon costs start April
items.quote: Monthly costs will be around ₹3 crores. So in March, maybe ₹1 crores, ₹1.5 crores we might have to spend. But Gurgaon is going to start in April. So this year, nothing will come.

items.statement: FY25 launch pipeline revised to Rs 7,000 crore GDV from Rs 8,000 crore
items.quote: As we look ahead, our l aunch pipeline remains robust, with projects representing a total GDV of Rs. 7,000 crore planned for the fiscal year

items.statement: FY25 revenue target of ~Rs 1,800 crore with early double-digit EBITDA margin
items.quote: While the first half has been low on revenue recognition, we are on track to close the year with strong deliveries and revenue of ~Rs. 1,800 crore.

items.statement: FY25 interest cost forecast at Rs 70-75 crore
items.quote: I see that around Rs. 70 crores, Rs. 75 crores is roughly the number, as you said.

items.statement: Business development target of Rs 8,000 crore for FY25 maintained
items.quote: As far as our BD goals, in a couple of BDs we are in quite advanced stage, and we are pretty confident that this number of Rs. 8,000 crores of our guidance we will meet.

items.quote: During the half year, our pre-sales value stood at Rs. 1,481 crore with volumes of 1.99 million square feet. 24K luxury segment contributed 30% to the pre-sales by value for H1 reflecting the sustained demand for premium and high-quality residences.

items.statement: Life Republic H1 sales volumes ~1.03 msf, pending development potential 20 msf

items.quote: Here onward also, when we are selecting a couple of redevelopment projects, we are setting our strategy of margin to the team at the time of acquisition itself, which is roughly around 16% to 18%.

items.statement: Internal margin targets: outright deals 25%, JV 17-18%, redevelopment similar
items.quote: For outright deal we have expectations of around 25% of the margin, for joint v enture projects around 17%, 18% of the margins, redevelopment works around the same margin

items.statement: Net debt negative Rs 58 crore as of Sep 30, 2024 (net cash position)
items.quote: Our net debt as on 30th September stands at negative Rs. 58 crores.

items.statement: Project financing from Marubeni, Motilal Oswal at zero coupon, evaluating finance cost reduction

items.quote: We see this demand is sustained and will grow from here onward. There is absolutely no concern over the demand on those, particularly Life Republic itself. And this is one of the flagship projects. It is a preferred location. So we see that, here onward, the demand will definitely grow up there.

items.statement: Portfolio focus on mid-premium and premium segments, 24K luxury seeing uptick
items.quote: over the last 2, 3, 4 quarters, we have seen the premium demand rise. And we have benefited - our 24K luxury brand has seen an uptick in the overall sales volume. But yes, as you've mentioned, that we are quite focused on mid-premium as well as the premium segment. This will rema in our focus till coming next few more quarters, considering the demand scenario going on

items.statement: Key hires include CFO Ravi Porwal, strengthening operations and all departments
items.quote: We have hired in key positions like CFO, Ravi Porwal has been hired in this financial year. We have hired in operations. So we are rebuilding. So, that is very much a part of our strategy for strengthening

items.statement: Mumbai launch certainty dependent on post-election approvals, Pune launches on schedule

items.statement: No adverse policy impact expected from Maharashtra election outcome
items.quote: See, we have seen uplift in demand, largely from the IT spaces, those who are our target group of customers. So we see that changing in government, obviously, there are a few dependencies on the approvals. But so far, we don't see that there is any new policy strategies, so we don't foresee any adverse or any negative impact irrespective of who comes in power.

items.statement: Life Republic realizations touched ~Rs 6,900 psf
items.quote: So it continues to do well. And I think now the realizations have touched almost Rs. 6,900.

items.statement: Strong consumer sentiment in housing supported by stabilizing interest rates and rising disposable incomes
items.quote: Customer confidence indices have been reflecting optimism and we have seen strong consumer sentiment in the housing sector too. Stabilizing interest rates have further supported s ustained demand for housing

items.statement: Mumbai pipeline includes Vashi (launched), Laxmi Ratan Versova, Jal Mangal Deep Goregaon, Vishwakarma
items.quote: We have a couple of projects in the pipeline - like Vashi, as I said, already launched Laxmi Ratan in Versova, we are securing most of the sanctions now. So, we have certain visibility coming up. Jal Mangal Deep, Goregaon here also we see a certainty and certain approval progress. At the same time, Vishwakarma. So we are monitoring our approval progress. And I think once we secure that, we will be

items.statement: H1 FY25 order intake was INR 1,104 crores, up 17.5% year-on-year.
items.quote: Our orders are INR 1,104 crores, which is 17.5% over and above last year.

items.statement: Order backlog stands at INR 1,389 crores, up 14.3% year-on-year.
items.quote: Order backlog is practically up by 14.3%.

items.statement: Management expects H2 to be stronger than H1 historically due to year-end capitalization push.
items.quote: H2 is always better. H2 is always better historically for any company, and we are no different because there is a lot of impetus on actually capitalizing it.

items.statement: H1 FY25 gross margin expanded to 39.5%, up 300 basis points year-on-year.
items.quote: This has given us a material margin or a gross margin at 39.5%, which is 3 points over and above corresponding period of last year.

items.statement: H1 FY25 EBITDA margin expanded by 2.3 percentage points to 14.0% with absolute growth of 44.2%.
items.quote: So that gives us an EBITDA of INR 167.4 crores, which is up by 2.3 points over and above last year and a good absolute value growth of 44.2%.

items.statement: Strong order momentum across all segments driven by RDSS scheme, data centres, and emerging segments like solar and EV.
items.quote: Good momentum in orders across all segments and order backlog we've already talked about.

items.statement: Kolkata factory commissioning on track for Q1 next year with partial start in Q4 FY25.
items.quote: It is actually coming up sometime around the first quarter of next year. That will happen. And it will perhaps start maybe in the last quarter of this year, and we will sort of conclude the other -- installation of other furnaces by Q1 next year.

items.statement: Capacities are being ramped up in plants as per future needs.
items.quote: In fact, we have exceeded by 2 minutes. And we are ramping up our capacities as we see our needs going forward in the plants, number one.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 sales mix: Systems 70%, Transactional 19%, Services 11%, Group company 21%.
items.quote: So we have the breakup for Q2: systems is at 70%, transaction 19%, services 11%, and group company is 21%.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 order intake mix: Equipment 47%, Projects 13%, Transactional 23%, Services 17%; intergroup orders indicated at ~INR 125 crores.
items.quote: So the order intake is: equipment is at 47%, projects at 13%, transaction 23%, and services 17%. Viraj: And intergroup? Suparna Bhattacharyya: Intergroup, we do not capture orders as such, but it is -- the indicated number is close to INR125

items.statement: Channel partner contribution ~2:1 vs direct in H1 FY25 measured by number of assets supplied.
items.quote: Suparna -- under control of Suparna, it would be typically, I would say, maybe 2:1, 2 in favour of license partner. That's what we have done in H1 in terms of number of assets.

items.statement: Exports contribute approximately 14% of total sales.
items.quote: Out of our total sales, we have been 14% of that approximately contributes -- comes from the exports.

items.statement: Cash flow improved due to better payment terms, on-time collections, inventory and payables management, and higher profitability.
items.quote: There has been a lot of focus in terms of having better payment terms for the last, say, 1 year as we are evolving to improve our cash position. Our -- a lot of impetus on getting on-time collections. If the collections are a little delayed, we are practically camping at customer sites to get those collections, and inventory management has been better. Our payables management have been better.

items.statement: Services order intake at 17% in Q2 FY25 but revenue share at 11%; EcoCare subscription ramp-up expected to drive services growth.
items.quote: the services piece is cyclic. And the focus stays on services General for the business because that is where we differentiate ourselves in terms of giving a value-add services to our clients. One quarter here and there doesn't matter. But overall, our objective and alignment is to drive more and more services fees purely propelled by a new offer, which we have lost, which is EcoCare

items.statement: Draft notification on type test validity extension seen as positive for the industry.
items.quote: It will actually give -- it will have a positive impact if you are asking about that one, not only for Schneider, but the entire set of people who actually are operating in this field.

items.statement: No conflict of interest between Schneider group entities in India; SEIL offers full Schneider portfolio for 'one SE experience'.
items.quote: There is no conflict of interest between various operational entities in India of Schneider. And number two, if you ask me as to what is the budget, which people might take for being more sustainable, this is -- I would not be in a position to answer you because you see what's been happening is there are people who are taking -- today is an evolution phase, I would say.

items.statement: EV penetration timeline uncertain but long-term opportunity remains; data centre configuration variability makes per-megawatt TAM difficult to quantify.
items.quote: What I -- what is very difficult to ask is whether the EV story will happen by the time it has been projected for 2030, 30% penetration? The answer, I don't know. But what I certainly know, if not in 2030, it will happen in 2032.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement driven by better efficiency, pricing, productivity in raw material, and product mix.
items.quote: And this has come from the better efficiency, better pricing, better productivity in the raw material.

items.statement: Finance cost remained stable in H1 FY25.
items.quote: Now let me come to the finance cost. Finance cost is more or less stable.

items.statement: Deferred tax liability of INR 5.8 crores reversed in Q2 FY25 due to LTCG tax rate reduction from 20% to 12.5% and removal of indexation benefit.
items.quote: So we have reversed a deferred tax liability of INR 5.8 crores in this quarter on account of the recent amendments in the taxation of long -term capital gains. So this is -- as you are all aware that the tax on long -term capital gains has reduced from 20% to 12.5% and the indexation benefit, which has been removed.

items.statement: Employee costs rose 10.6% in H1 FY25 mainly covering inflation.
items.quote: Our employee costs have risen by 10.6%, and this is mainly covering the inflation.

items.statement: CSR expenses increased due to profitability over last 3 years vs prior loss period.
items.quote: The other expenses have risen by 38.8%. This has a component of the sales growth expenses like whatever we take as a percentage of sales growth and the other coming from the increase in CSR expenses because we've been profitable for the last 3 years as compared to the General corresponding period of last year, where it had one -- the first year, which was in losses

items.statement: Expects to be debt-free in 3-3.5 years, earlier if Fleur Hotels IPO happens
items.quote: I think we are sticking to our guidance that in the next 3 - 3.5 years, we should be debt free, but if we list Fleur before that then we will be debt free that much earlier.

items.statement: Targets 15-20% annual revenue growth minimum after renovations complete
items.quote: I would reckon that 15% - 20% growth in revenue every year is the minimum we would expect and once renovation slows down and cost flat and then this will be mostly operating leverage.

items.statement: Expects Fleur Hotels IPO within next 2-3 years
items.quote: Well, I would reckon within the next 2-3 years at most.

items.statement: Post-renovation ongoing capex expected at 1.5-1.6% of revenue
items.quote: Post this, renovation expenses are expected to be between 1.5% - 1.6% of revenue on an ongoing basis.

items.statement: Plans to invest Rs. 250-300 crore over 3 years on renovations vs normal Rs. 60-70 crore
items.quote: in 3 years, we will spend Rs. 250 - Rs. 300 crore instead of what would normally have been say, Rs. 20 crore a year, instead of Rs. 60 - Rs. 70 crore, we will be spending 3 .5x that.

items.statement: Annual renovation capex capped at Rs. 100-110 crore per year
items.quote: Because we decided we would not invest more than say Rs. 100 - Rs. 110 crore per year.

items.statement: Renovation capex peaked in Q2 FY25, will shoot up again in Q1-Q2 FY26
items.quote: In Q3 - Q4, yes, but it will shoot up again in Q1 - Q2 next year.

items.quote: As of 30th September 2024, the inventory for the group stands at 112 operational hotels with 10,318 rooms and a pipeline of 75 hotels with 5,220 rooms.

items.statement: Full Keys portfolio renovation completion expected by FY27
items.quote: I reckon that the full portfolio will open perhaps next financial year end. So, really, the impact will be felt for the full portfolio from FY27, number one.

items.quote: See Aurika Bombay, I expect will do EBITDA margin of 60% plus in H2.

items.quote: after we stabilize it, we are looking at an EBITDA of roughly Rs. 60 crores from the portfolio, which means about Rs. 6.5 lakhs a room.
