And even in this quarter, we've seen a currency loss of INR79 crores in Nigeria, which was INR99 crores in Q1. And in Mexico, we've seen a INR14 crores loss, which was INR51 crores in Q1. And in Egypt, the loss is 0, which was INR31 crores in Q1. So, while the losses ha

items.statement: BOPET exports from India down 10% QoQ in Q2 due to strong domestic prices; BOPP exports down 5% QoQ
items.quote: On an industry -wide basis, again, the BOPET exports from India in the quarter reduced by about 10% in Q2 over Q1, largely because the prices were good, domestic prices were good in this quarter. And even for BOPP, they were down 5%, Q2 versus Q1, again, largely because of the higher domestic prices, where exports contracted a bit.

items.statement: H1 FY25 consolidated EBITDA INR903 crores (+23.9% YoY) driven by packaging sales volume +13.8% and Aseptic volume +10%
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA for H1 is INR903 crores, it's gone up by about 23.9% this H1 over the last fiscal H1 and, again, driven by the packaging sales of 13.8% and Aseptic sales of about 10%.

items.statement: Restructuring (separating commodity vs value-added businesses) considered to unlock value; offshore listing first step; no non-core asset sales planned
items.quote: So, I think the best way, according to me, is to separate your commodity business from value -added business, from your packaging business would command a different multiple as compared to your packaging films business, your aseptic business, your chemicals business will come under different premium and that's also a very substantial business for us. So, restructuring may be one way to unlock that

items.statement: Dirok gas offtake fell to 15.03 mmscfd in Q2 FY25 due to floods and plant shutdowns in Assam
items.quote: Dirok gas sales for the last quarter is 22.65 million standard cubic feet per day. But the offtake in the current quarter reduced to 15.03 million standard cubic feet per day.

items.statement: Major consumer plants in Assam were shut for 19-61 days in Q2 FY25, causing low gas offtake
items.quote: And then you look at Numaligarh refinery, which was shut in for about 19 days. And the Brahmaputra Fertilizer Corporation was about 28 days, a national Namrup thermal power station was 24 days, and NECO, that was the major consumer for about 61 days.

items.statement: Management expects Dirok offtake to improve in Q3 FY25 and be much better in Q4 FY25
items.quote: This situation would reverse to a little better in the third quarter and if some progress we made, we have been in discussion with the Oil India, then fourth quarter would be much better than the third quarter, that's what we believe.

items.statement: Target to reach Rs 1000 crore revenue by FY26 with EBITDA margins slightly better than current levels
items.quote: Our endeavor is '25-26 we should be able to comfortably reach that number, and our margin remains the same what we are doing now, it's little better than that, because some of the fixed cost can be leveraged.

items.statement: North-Eastern region capital outlay for next two financial years remains at Rs 250 crores
items.quote: In North-Eastern region our capital outlay for the next two financial years continues to be at Rs.250 crores.

items.statement: Three additional wells planned for B-80 in FY27 at estimated cost of $50-60 million to ramp production above 3500 boepd
items.quote: Actually, we are expecting that the three well would be somewhere around $50 to $60 million and that's what we are planning for it.

items.statement: B-80 currently producing ~1000 bpd oil and 8 mmscfd gas, within +/-5% of 2500 boepd reference
items.quote: Oil about 1000 barrels and gas is about 8 million standard cubic feet of gas per day.

items.statement: PY-1 first development well drilling planned to commence April-June 2025 after expert review of basement reserves
items.quote: Before we commence the drilling, we would like to review the uncertainty of the gas water contact in the north and south of the fields. These studies will give more confidence on our plan for 3 development wells, and if everything goes as per plan, drilling of the first well will commence in April to June 2025.

items.statement: Declared sole bidder for DSF Block B15 (332.4 sq km, 40ft water depth) in Mumbai Offshore; award expected within a month
items.quote: We were declared as a sole bidder and on award of the block by Government of India we will embark on the development of this field. Water depth of this field is about 40 feet.

items.statement: Dirok gas sold at PPAC price ~US$8.2/mmbtu vs nominated blocks at US$6.5/mmbtu ceiling; nominated field gas sold first
items.quote: You are aware that OIL and ONGC are selling the gas at the price applicable for nominated blocks with the ceiling of US$6.5 per mmbtu, and the Dirok JV has to sell the gas at PPAC price, which is about US$8.2 per mmbtu.

items.statement: B-80 gas price realized at US$9.89/mmbtu in Q2 FY25 vs US$10.34/mmbtu in Q1 FY25; now moving toward imported LNG pricing
items.quote: During this quarter, the average gas price realized is 9.89 mmbtu compared to 10.34 mmbtu in the previous quarter. Now, the gas price in the Western region is moving back into imported LNG price.

items.statement: B-80 crude NRV fell from US$82.55/bbl to US$73.69/bbl in Q2 FY25, impacting profit
items.quote: Major reason for reduction in profit is due to reduction in offtake of gas in Dirok sales and reduction in the NRV approaching stock of crude from US$82.55 per barrel to US$73.69 per barrel.

items.statement: B-80 gas sales now >50% at exchange prices linked to LNG (at discount), balance at Brent-linked committed contracts
items.quote: Partly we are selling at exchange, and partly we are selling at the Brent price Wherever the committed contract, we are selling at the Brent price and the balance more than 50% we are selling at the exchange, which prices akin to LNG price, a little discount to the LNG price.

items.statement: B-80 can sustain operations even at $50/bbl oil price given owned facilities and cost structure
items.quote: If you take the net cost of all those things we can sustain even at an oil price of $50.

items.statement: Kharsang environmental clearance public hearing scheduled 26 Nov 2024; EC needed to drill exploration well and 18 Upper Girujan development wells
items.quote: Public hearing is mandated before the issuance of the environmental clearance, which is scheduled on 26th November 2024. On obtaining EC we will drill one exploration well to the depth of about 4000 meters, which would unlock substantial value in the block.

items.statement: Block 19 (Greater Dirok) extension granted till 1 Feb 2025; requested additional one-year extension from MoP&NG
items.quote: Extension has been granted up to 1 st of February 2025, and we have requested MoP&NG for additional one more year extension to start and complete the committed work program.

items.statement: Cambay blocks North Balol and Asjol received environmental clearance after 4 years; rig mobilization underway for two wells
items.quote: We have secured the environmental clearance after four years for North Balol and Asjol. We are in the process of securing the rig and tangibles to commence the drilling of two wells in North Balol, followed by Asjol.

items.statement: B-80 crude oil inventory at ~250,000 barrels; production ~2000 bpd; next offtake expected Q1 FY26
items.quote: 250,000 barrels. And then 2000 barrel is our current production, so you will be knowing by the 1st Quarter of the next year we will be able to make an offtake

items.statement: Term loan outstanding ~Rs 103 crores; India Ratings reaffirmed IND A rating with outlook revised to Positive for Rs 500 crore bank loan
items.quote: As on date, the term loan outstanding is about Rs. 103 crores. India Ratings have reaffirmed the rating IND A and revised the outlook from 'Stable' to 'Positive' for Rs.500 crores bank loan.

items.statement: Current cash position and continued production sufficient to meet all obligations including 3-year capital program
items.quote: With the current cash position and with the continued production, we will meet all our obligations, including the planned capital program for the coming three years.

items.statement: Monetization hampered by demand constraints in North-East and facility issues at B-80 (35-day shutdown for hawser repair in Q2)
items.quote: However, our ability to monetize quickly is hampered due to demand constrained in North East and issues faced with the facilities in B-80.

items.statement: B-80 revenue sharing contract: 12% minimum government share, up to 55% linear; total government take ~25-30% of revenue including royalty
items.quote: In a revenue sharing contract, the costs are immaterial, only the revenue is getting shared with the government. That goes with the LRP, that is 12% that is a fixed one. The balance one is proportional to you what you have quoted for it. So more you produce, you will have to pay more to the government, and that's a fact. So in our case, it is about 12% is the minimum we have to pay for whatever ou

items.statement: Acquiring 100% of Del Monte India via share swap, issuing 35% of ATFL equity to Bharti Group (21%) and Del Monte (14%), renaming company to Sundrop Brands
items.quote: What we will be doing at ATFL is to acquire 100% of the shares of Del Monte India, and in lieu of cash, we will be issuing shares of ATFL to the two shareholders of Del Monte Foods, and this will allow us to own 100% of the assets and business, including t he brand, of Del Monte India

items.statement: Targeting double-digit EBITDA margins over time, with sustainable margins safely below that level
items.quote: I think you'll see margins going up into double digits and then sustaining there at safely below this.

items.statement: Standalone ATFL and Del Monte each can improve margins to industry standards; combined synergies offer further accretion
items.quote: We certainly believe that there is a lot of those complementarities tha t can lead to margin accretion, b ut we will see over a period of time, but irrespective of that we believe that standalone itself, the two businesses can improve the margins and come to more industry standards or normalized margins

items.statement: Food business gross contribution above 45%; edible oil gross contribution lower but equally accretive at gross margin level
items.quote: Our food's gross contributions will be in excess of 45%, as we have said. Our oil's gross contribution may be lower, but at a gross margin level will be equally accretive with the food's business and we will focus on it to drive overall company's profitability.

items.statement: Del Monte FY24 revenue INR542 cr, EBITDA INR22 cr (4.1% margin); H1 FY25 revenue INR300 cr, EBITDA INR15 cr (5% margin)
items.quote: Del Monte, for the last year, FY24, was at INR542 crores of revenue, versus INR760 of revenue. If you look forward to this half year that has just passed, ending September, or for the half year ending September 2024, it's mentioned on page 16, but I'll just repeat, Del Monte has topped INR300 crores of revenue, with INR15 crores of EBITDA, which is a 5% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: ATFL H1 FY25 revenue similar to Del Monte, EBITDA margin slightly down
items.quote: Sundrop, for the half year, has broadly cracked on similar revenue level, and the EBITDA margin has actually come down slightly.

items.statement: Leveraging underutilized capacity across 7 ATFL plants and 1 Del Monte plant; no new capex highlighted
items.quote: We have seven manufacturing facilities for foods and we have two third -party edible oil plants. This ensures that we are able to serve our consumers with fresh products within a 300-kilometer reach to majority of consumers in the country.

items.statement: Combined manufacturing footprint of 7 ATFL plants plus Del Monte's Ludhiana plant; excess capacity available for cross-utilization
items.quote: We have seven plants, if you look at Genfudi, Uttarakhand, Unnao, Assam, Bangladesh, Telangana, Chittoor, and Gujarat, which is Jagadia. And a complementary set also comes with a plant in Punjab, in Ludhiana, from Del Monte.

items.statement: Portfolio now spans popcorn (ACT II), peanut butter & spreads (Sundrop), Italian sauces & pantry items (Del Monte); complementary non-overlapping categories
items.quote: So, products are complementary, distribution networks are complementary, and we can just learn from each other on it and build a stronger network.

items.statement: Channel mix rebalanced: combined entity 53% general trade, 18% food service, 15% modern trade, 11% e-commerce/quick commerce
items.quote: However, when we combine the two, it is such a balanced approach that we are tackling all the channels with relatively better weightage and de-risking dependence on any channel, with 53 % on general trade, 18 % on food service, 15% on modern trade, and about 11% on e-commerce and quick commerce.

items.statement: Nine consumer mega-trends identified: convenience, better-for-you, globalized tastes, organized shift, in-home consumption, premiumization, experiential eating, sustainability, rising protein demand
items.quote: With these three brands tackling the nine mega trends, how does the combination of two companies look? So, we have classified these in two parts. One is on the growth side.

items.statement: Edible oil pricing strategy: near-term hold 95-105 index, may reduce premium to drive volume growth
items.quote: In the near term, you are right we will try and still hold between 95 to 105, not talking about the 15th September duty impact, but in general, that is how we will keep it.

items.statement: Focus on distributor economics: expanding product range through same channels to improve distributor returns and drive network expansion
items.quote: So the biggest opportunity we see is for our distributor channels to now own or sell more products than what they were doing previously and hence improve their own unit economics, which will lead to further distribution expansion.

items.statement: Transaction is all-share swap; no cash outlay or new borrowings mentioned
items.quote: What we will be doing at ATFL is to acquire 100% of the shares of Del Monte India, and in lieu of cash, we will be issuing shares of ATFL to the two shareholders of Del Monte Foods.

items.statement: No dividend or buyback discussed; focus on long-term value creation
items.quote: And in the interest of building business o f the long term, we are not terribly concerned around quarterly performances or monthly performances

items.statement: Nitish Bajaj appointed Group Managing Director-designate effective 25 Nov 2024; four new independent directors inducted
items.quote: I think this now gives us the opportunity to welcome Mr. Nitish Bajaj, who is the new Group Managing Director-designate. Effective next Monday, the 25th, he will be joining us all.

items.statement: Food business CAGR ~17% over last 15-17 years; food gross margin contribution rose from 10% (FY12) to 55% (FY24)
items.quote: The innovation, distribution and the diversified manufacturing facilities have helped us have a very good CAGR of about 17% over the last 15 -17 years. In terms of gross margin, FY12, we had about 90% of our gross margin coming out of staples and 10% out of foods. In FY24, the contribution of food contributing to gross margin has moved up to 55% and the 45% comes from staples.

items.statement: Ready-to-cook portfolio (hot fresh popcorn) differentiated from QSR delivery; not replaceable by Swiggy/Zomato
items.quote: Even if you are delivering in 10 minutes, the popcorn would not remain hot and fresh. It may remain fresh, but not hot. So, we believe at least very strongly that in-home consumption of hot and fresh self-made is far better experience than Swiggy and Zomato are a convenience and they complement these things, they do not replace it.

items.statement: Crystal brand (commodity edible oil) franchised out; royalty income to continue
items.quote: As far as Crystal is concerned, that is a commodity brand which we have franchised and we do get a royalty on it and we intend to continue it like that.

items.statement: Board approved interim dividend of 50% (₹2.50 per share) and 1:1 bonus shares
items.quote: I am happy to announce to inform you that the company infect the board has approved to reward our shareholders as an interim dividend of 50% which is ₹2.50 per equity share on the pre-bonus paid-up capital share. Also happy to inform you that the company has also declared bonus share in the ratio of 1:1, one bonus share for every one existing share of ₹5 per each fully paid up.

items.statement: Lighting & Consumer Durables FY25 revenue growth target 12-15% with EBITDA margin stability
items.quote: Our focus remains on achieving FY25 revenue growth of approximately 12% to 15%, alongside the cautious optimism for EBITDA margin stability.

items.statement: Steel segment FY25 volume growth recalibrated to 7-8% YoY, EBITDA per ton ₹5,000-5,200

We anticipate EBITDA per ton to stabilize within the range of ₹5,000 to ₹5,200 per ton supported by our operational efficiencies and a positive demand outlook for the coming months.

And in third year Maharashtra’s full project will be completed and will be in operational

items.quote: Improved capacity utilization, working capital optimization and cost rationalization enabled us to become a zero-debt company and having cash surplus of ₹136 crores in H1 Financial Year 25.

items.statement: Water sector demand 1.5-2 lakh tons extra annually for 2-3 years from Har Ghar Jal
items.quote: There will be an extra demand of around 1.5 lakh to 2 lakh tons across the country for at least another 2-3 years.

items.quote: Because land has to be taken from the farmers, so at some places it is taking some time. I think there could be some delay in the 4 months to 5 months' time frame we had given.

items.quote: Basically they are also like our extended family. So 80% of our total Lighting and Consumer Durables products are manufactured in-house and 20% is outsourced. And 80% of that 20% is for Consumer Durables.

items.quote: And we look, you know, Q3 and Q4 w ill be buoyant, and we look for a strong financial performance going forward

items.statement: Demand will outstrip supply in luxury segment for next 3-4 years
items.quote: I have no reason to believe based on at least what I have seen that demand will not outstrip supply.

items.quote: I would, we will do everything we can to sustain it. I hope we can, yes.

items.quote: But we do not go over a debt equity ratio of 25%. And with all these projects, that will not be exceeded.

items.statement: Ranthambore renovation finishing early next year
items.quote: Yeah. That's still underway, and it'll be finished early part of next year. And it's absolutely on track.

items.statement: Luxury hotel rates have considerable upside, winter rates touch $1000

items.quote: MICE includes weddings and weddings is an important segment for us in a large number of our hot els.

items.quote: And guest feedback has been phenomenal. And we've also seen a substantial increase as a result of that in banqueting revenue.

items.quote: The UK is top 3 source markets. So our top 3 source markets are of course India for India hotels, the US and the UK.

items.statement: RevPAR consistently at 130% of STR competition set
items.quote: The RevPAR of the company is consistently at 130% over the STR competition set.

items.quote: Mashobra is sub judice in any way, so I don't really want to comment on Mashobra at this point in time.

items.quote: There is Rs. 592 crore fund which is there which is retained for future growth as well as expansion . items.quote: On a quarterly, occupancy and ARR which has grown from 69% to 72% and ARR has grown from 13,730 to 14,970.

items.quote: That said, with two major elections are now concluded and new governments firmly in place, we are optimistic that decision-making will accelerate in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Signed two significant technology-driven contracts in North America for core technology services.
items.quote: We recently signed two significant contracts in North America for core technology services. This is an important milestone, as it reflects the success of our ongoing journey to increase the digital component of our revenues.

items.statement: Agent X platform won UK G-Cloud framework approval, opening access to 24 large public sector entities and 317 provincial agencies.
items.quote: our Agent X platform, an AI-driven solution for customer experience transformation, recently achieved a major milestone by winning approval for the UK G -Cloud framework submission. This win allows the entire UK public sector to access and use Agent X throu gh G- Cloud services. It is a significant breakthrough, as it effectively opens up the UK public sector market for our technology services. Th

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin improved sequentially to 12.8% from 11.8% in Q1, but down from 15.9% a year ago.
items.quote: On the margin side, our EBITDA margins have shown an improvement on a sequential basis, up from 11.8% to 12.8%, but lower than where we were a year ago, when the margins were about 15.9%.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA margin declined to 12.3% from 15.6% a year ago.
items.quote: On a half-yearly basis, our revenues are down by about 5.8%, and our EBITDA margin is down from over 15.6% to 12.3%.

items.statement: Other Income swung by Rs 17.2 crores due to FX volatility: Q1 had Rs 8.3 crore gain, Q2 had Rs 8.9 crore loss.
items.quote: While this is primarily due to exchange rate fluctuations, in Q1 we had an FX gain of about Rs. 8.3 crores, and in Q2, that became a loss of Rs. 8.9 crores. So, on the other income side alone, there is a swing of about Rs. 17.2 crores, primarily due to the FX variation.

items.statement: H1 capex was Rs 66 crores, roughly Rs 5 crores lower than same period last year.
items.quote: The key thing to call out is that during the first half of the year, our CAPEX stands at close to Rs. 66 crores, which is roughly about Rs. 5 crores lower than the same period last year.

items.statement: Cape Town facility has 136 operational seats with capacity to scale rapidly across four floors.
items.quote: Currently, we have 136 operational seats, with the capacity to scale rapidly. The facility spans four floors, allowing us to quickly expand seating as demand increases.

items.statement: South Africa operations offer 40-60% cost savings per FTE and support English, German, French, Dutch.
items.quote: From a business perspective, South Africa offers a compelling value proposition, delivering cost savings of approximately 40% to 60% per FTE.

items.statement: Digital revenues now 21% of total; CX services 57%, digital and media 43%.
items.quote: Within this 43%, about 21% of the total revenues come from digital services, as Partha referred to in his slide on digital business, as well as from the digital operations business.

items.statement: Top client 10.6% of BPM revenue; top 5 clients 24%; top 10 clients 32%.
items.quote: The top customer accounts for about 10.6% from the BPM business. The top 5 customers account for about 24%, and the top 10 customers account for about 32%.

items.statement: DSO increased to 65 days in Sep 2024 from 62 days in Mar 2024; no concerns on receivables.
items.quote: There is an increase in the DSO days from 62 days in March 2024 to 65 days in September 2024. Clearly, there is seasonality. You can see that last year, from September 2023 to Q2 FY2024, it was 67 days, and it has come down to 62 days. So, we have no concerns about our receivables.

items.statement: Total debt reduced by Rs 49 crores to Rs 1,257 crores as of Sep 30, 2024 from Mar 2024.
items.quote: Between March 2024, when we had total debt of Rs. 1,306 crores, that debt has reduced by Rs. 49 crores to about Rs. 1,257 crores as of 30 th September

items.statement: Net cash and treasury surplus net of debt stands at Rs 5,090 crores, up Rs 77 crores from March.
items.quote: Our total net cash and treasury surplus, which is total cash and treasury surplus net of debt, stands at Rs. 5,090 crores. If you see between March and September, there is an increase of about Rs. 77 crores in the net treasury and cash surplus, driven by a reduction in debt, as well as an increase in the overall gross treasury and cash surplus.

items.statement: Paid Rs 129.5 crores in earn-out payments for TekLink acquisition during H1.
items.quote: The only other thing to call out is that we had some payments to be made for the TekLink acquisition, which continues to perform well. So, there were some earn-out payments, and during the year, we paid out roughly about Rs. 129.5 crores towards the TekLink acquisition.

items.statement: Broadband subscriber base grew 22% YoY in H1; H1 revenue Rs 608 crores vs Rs 500 crores last year.
items.quote: If you look at the topline, in the H1 of FY2024, we achieved around Rs. 500 crores, and this year, we reached Rs. 608 crores in H1 alone. That is a 22% growth.

items.quote: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has stated they will release a pricing structure by December 15th this year, just a few weeks away. We anticipate that LEO tests will start in the middle of next year.

items.statement: Show cause notice received for search/survey conducted Nov-Dec 2023; company is preparing reply.
items.quote: We have been making disclosures as required since the quarter ending December 2023. There was a search and survey conducted in November-December last year. items.statement: Massive re-skilling exercise underway across Colombia, South Africa, Philippines, and India for AI and technology skills.
items.quote: As we steer the company toward more digital frontiers, we are undergoing a massive re-skilling exercise for employees across Colombia, South Africa, the Philippines, and India to train them on AI and technology skills.

items.statement: North America tech contracts expected to scale in remainder of FY2025 with full impact in FY2026.
items.quote: We anticipate these services will scale up during the remainder of the financial year, with their full impact expected in FY 2026, starting April 1, 2025.

items.statement: Global shrimp prices improved towards end of Q2 FY25 and are continuing to increase, encouraging Indian farmers to stock more seed for upcoming crop season.
items.quote: after a prolonged period of nearly 18 months, there has been an improvement in the global prices of shrimp mainly towards the end of Q2 of FY 125, and are continuing to increase.

items.statement: US inventories have largely cleared and demand is improving, with impact expected in Q3 FY25 and beyond on realizations and global prices.
items.quote: Inventories in the U.S., a major market for shrimp, were clearing up and the demand is improving. They are — in fact, most of the inventories have been clearing and that's as informed to us.

items.statement: EU market share in sales mix increased to 51% in Q2 FY25 from 40% in Q2 FY24, and to 45% in H1 FY25 from 28% in H1 FY24, making sales mix more geographically diversified.

items.statement: Ready-to-eat product approvals for EU market are still awaited since 2020 for all seafood shrimp processing facilities commissioned since then.
items.quote: As most of you would be aware that our approvals for the ready-to-eat products to the European Union are still awaited as such with all the seafood shrimp processing facilities since the year 2020.

items.statement: Gross margin was 27% in Q2 FY25 due to higher raw material prices; H1 FY25 gross margin largely maintained at 29%. Freight cost inflation impacted EBITDA margins but freight costs are now normalizing.
items.quote: Our gross margins were at 27% in Q2 FY 25, majorly due to higher raw material prices. For H1 FY 25, the net revenue came in at INR386 crores as against INR494 crores in H1 FY "24. But the gross margin is largely maintained at 29%.

items.statement: Ocean freight rates peaked at $8,000-$8,500 per container (from ~$4,000) due to Red Sea issues, now down to $5,000-$5,500; Q2 FY25 averaged $5,000-$6,000.

But on an average, when it was 4, it has gone up to almost $8,000 to $8,500 at its peak. And now we are again seeing it back to around $5,000, $5,500.

items.statement: Average realization grew 2% QoQ to INR 695 per kg in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: Ecuador faces 3.78% CVD (no ADD); Indonesia faces 3.9% ADD (no CVD); India has existing 1.35% ADD and preliminary 5.77% CVD pending ITC confirmation.
items.quote: In the case of Ecuador, they have — they don't have any antidumping duty; however, they have been levied a countervailing duty of 3.78%. And in the case of Indonesia, they have an antidumping duty of 3.9%, and they do mot have any countervailing duty.

items.statement: CVD deposits for April-July 2024 booked as expense; management expects duties to be significantly reduced after first-year review when Government of India submits justification for RoDTEP and Duty Drawback reimbursements.
items.quote: We have not made any provision as such because we have been informed that itis going to be more of a - we have been told that it is more of effective from the time US ITC finally gives a go ahead. items.quote: We have actually initiated a revamping of our hatchery operations, and we are going well with them in this — for a start because we wanted to first get a control of our primary input. I mean, that's the primary input into our farming, which is the seeds.

items.quote: As regards our discussion for 2030, as regards to our production, our quantitative figures, we are near to our projection which we have internally discussed and tried to achieve by 2030 and we are in line with all factors as regards to our internal production. But we cannot predict the exact selling price or there may be volatility in the raw material prices.

name: S H Kelkar and Company Ltd

items.statement: Full-year revenue expected around Rs 2,100 crore, implying ~14% growth, subject to no major changes
items.quote: I would expect to reach around 2,100 or something like this number, 14% odd for the full year. This is a subject that no major changes happen between now and the end of the year.

items.statement: H2 revenue expected to be better than H1; full-year growth well in excess of 12% mid-term CAGR target
items.quote: Expect our sales to be better than 12% for the full year. Whether it is 15% in the second half, a little bit more or less, in the full-year basis we will be well in excess of our 12% target.

items.statement: H2 EBITDA margin expected similar to H1 adjusted 16.8%, slightly better, with recurring Rs 20-22 crore cost for new Creative Centres
items.quote: I expect it to be in the same range, slightly better.

items.statement: Gross margin expectation for H2 remains around 40-45% as reported in H1, but raw material shortages may necessitate price adjustments
items.quote: our gross margin expectation is still around the 40%-45% that we have reported for the first half. However, there are some raw materials where acute shortages are expected in the 4th Quarter or 1st Quarter of next year.

items.statement: European EBITDA margin 20.5% vs 21% last year; gross margin improved 350 bps but EBITDA margin down 70 bps due to smaller batch sizes from new clients
items.quote: This is purely a product mix issue. When you look at the gross margin, you look at the product level. But when we have smaller batches, then our net margin is the same.

items.statement: Global MNC account execution secured for FY25 and well underway, trending as expected with potential to expand partnership
items.quote: On the global account, we are trending as expected. So, we are on track.

items.statement: H2 FY25 capex ~Rs 50 crore; H1 FY26 another ~Rs 50 crore; ~Rs 100 crore for Vashivali reinstatement; incremental capex after insurance ~Rs 60 crore
items.quote: So, I think in the second half, we would have roughly around Rs. 50 crore and the first half next year, another Rs. 50 crore of CAPEX, out of which almost Rs. 100 odd crore would be the reinstatement of the Vashivali factory itself.

items.statement: Current utilization >85%; Vanavate and Vashivali rebuild to add 2x capacity in India; one new European factory to add ~50% capacity
items.quote: So, right now, we are at more than 85% utilization of our facilities. With the rebuilding of the Vashivali and Vanavate factory, we will add almost 2x addi tional capacity. So, that is on the domestic. And we are proposing to add one more factory which would give us roughly 50% additional capacity in the European context

items.statement: Vanavate factory expected Q4 FY25 (Q1 calendar 2025); Vashivali rebuild 9-10 months after; Mulund closure post-Vashivali
items.quote: So, the new factory in Vanavate is expected to come up in the 1st Quarter calendar next year, so 4th Quarter. Vashivali which is the rebuild of the factory will still take another 9 months to 10 months before it is rebuilt.

items.statement: Acute shortages expected in Q4 FY25/Q1 FY26 for key natural oils (orange, patchouli, vetiver ~15% of purchase basket); dialogue with customers for pass-through by Feb-Mar
items.quote: Specifically products like orange oil, patchouli oil, vetiver oil these are the key components, which is roughly I would say 15% of our purchase basket. These are under threat in terms of availability and pricing as of today.

items.statement: Domestic large FMCG customers soft; strong momentum in small/mid-sized customers and new accounts; global MNC orders driving growth
items.quote: while domestic demand for large customers remains soft, we are encouraged by strong momentum across our small, mid-sized customers and new accounts.

items.statement: European revenues grew 11.5% like-for-like; favourable dynamics from trade-down and consolidation creating vacuum for mid-sized players
items.quote: Strangely not having a very strong economic growth is favo urable for us because we are not the incumbent, we are the challengers. So, when the markets are looking for a value proposition or more private labels or different offerings it helps us to continue our growth

items.statement: Q2 gross margin muted due to ~Rs 25-30 crore lower-margin backlog carried from Q1 fire disruption; H1 gross margin representative of full business
items.quote: So, roughly Rs. 25 crore-Rs. 30 crore of business was carried over to the 2nd Quarter that was at a lower margin. Theref ore, the composite margin of 2nd Quarter is muted

items.statement: Debt expected lower by year-end from operational free cash flow and insurance payouts starting Dec-Jan
items.quote: On the debt piece, I think we expect some amount of money to come in from the insurance between now and end of the year, probably December -January we expect Insurance payout to start to flow in. So, yes, we will have lower debt in the end of the year.

items.statement: Insurance claim filed; inventory payout first, then CAPEX reimbursement on reinstatement basis; substantial payments expected Dec-Jan
items.quote: So, we have filed the claim, it is in the process. Final claims we will get in wit h the insurer any time now. And we expect by December -January substantial payments to start to come in

items.statement: Antitrust investigations against global majors (Givaudan, IFF) in EU/US creating opportunities for mid-sized players like SH Kelkar
items.quote: yes, that does open up opportunities for mid-size and other players like us.

items.statement: Raw material availability/pricing storm horizon for H1 FY26; US administration policy changes from Jan 2025 uncertain impact
items.quote: there is a sort of storm on the horizon and we are just highlighting that this may hit the industry at some point in the first half of next year. In addition, I would like to say that there is expectation of a lot of ch anges in the global economic order after the administration in the United States takes charge in

items.statement: European revenue growth 11.5% like-for-like; global MNC account scaling as expected; Ingredients division turnaround continuing
items.quote: our core European segment delivered impressive performance this quarter with revenues growing by 11.5% on a like -for-like basis.

items.statement: Creative Development Centres launched in Germany (June 2024) and Manchester (early 2025); recurring Rs 20 crore/year OPEX; revenues to start in 6-8 months
items.quote: Those are all employee and OPEX costs. So, there is a recurring Rs. 20 crore order per annum.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance for FY25 maintained at INR 3,500-4,000 crore
items.quote: Again, I would say the present our guideline still remains at INR3,500 to INR4,000, but that depends on the next 2 months to 3 months how we are working

items.statement: EBITDA margin target maintained at 10% going forward
items.quote: we will try and stick to maintain our EBITDA at 10%.

items.statement: Current order book stands at INR 6,546 crore
items.quote: Currently we are at an order book of INR 6,546 Crore

items.statement: Adani Group share of current order book is INR 232 crore
items.quote: INR232 crores approximately

items.statement: Pipeline remains at INR 7,000+ crore including Adani and government projects
items.quote: overall that order book still remains INR 7,000 +.

items.statement: Bidding for INR 1,000 crore projects each at Ahmedabad and Mumbai airports, INR 500 crore at Kandla
items.quote: we are already bidding for about INR1,000 crores projects, INR1,000 crores projects at the Ahmedabad airport, INR1,000 plus crores at Mumbai Airport, and already INR500 crores projects in Kandla.

items.statement: Discussing INR 700-800 crore at Shantigram, INR 800 crore at Ahmedabad airport, INR 1,000+ crore at Mumbai airport, INR 300+ crore at Dharavi
items.quote: About INR700 to INR800 crores of projects we are discussing at Shantigram. About INR800 crores projects we are addressing at Adani Airport in Ahmedabad. About INR1,000 plus-crores projects we are discussing at Mumbai Airport. And about I think INR300 plus-crores projects we are discussing at Dharavi

items.statement: Adani Portfolio plans USD 100 billion capex over next decade
items.quote: Adani Portfolio of Companies is looking to invest USD 100bn as capex over the course of next decade.

items.statement: Three precast plants being installed at Mundra, Mumbai, and existing Ahmedabad facility
items.quote: They are already installing three Precast Plants, one in Mundra, one in Mumbai, and one, we are already having under.

items.statement: Current precast capacity sufficient for near-term projects; expansion possible later if Shantigram projects increase
items.quote: Presently, at least we've been saying one or two months or three months, actually we don't have any idea of any calculation of expanding that because there are two or three projects which we are working on and it is at the design stage for Adani Group.

items.statement: Adani projects to use cost-plus formula with base rates for major materials (cement, steel) protecting against inflation
items.quote: the basic materials are always on a base rate. So those rates which were there in the UP were all the materials we have to bear the cost of the rising material cost. Here the base prices of the cement or steel, whatever it is, we have added today that will be paid off, whatever, whether it is minus or plus.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 10% maintained; cost-plus structure aims to preserve company-level margins
items.quote: At the company level, we would like to maintain our EBITDA till now whatever we have achieved till now. And then, by formula, we'll be working on the same kind of calculation. So more or less, the company 's EBITDA is not going to change as far as that group entering into our project.

items.statement: Partnership with Adani Group for buildings, airports, data centres, industrial projects; not exclusive, will bid for other large projects
items.quote: Presently, there is nothing binding PSP Projects from not taking or working for projects out side of Adani Group. We have clearly mentioned that we should remain in the market and execute a combination of projects.

items.statement: Transaction subject to customary and regulatory approvals including open offer completion
items.quote: Please note the transaction remains subject to customary approvals and regulatory approvals including completion of an open offer.

items.statement: Adani Infra to acquire up to 30.07% from promoters; post open offer both hold equal equity; 5-year lock-in, 10-year shareholder agreement
items.quote: As per the arrangement, Adani Infra to acquire up to 30.07% stake from the founder promoter. Post the open offer for 26%; both the companies will maintain equal equity of the company.

items.statement: Promoter family restricted from similar business for 5 years post agreement completion
items.quote: for 5 years from completion of the agreements, me and other existing promoters, are restricted in terms of doing such type of similar business separately later on or that time.

items.statement: Interest cost stable post-QIP; working capital cycles may improve with Adani projects due to better receivables
items.quote: interest cost is already, whatever impact has to come, that has already come after QIP. So, that will remain little bit standard. Yes, that can be little bit developed on the working capital side.

items.statement: Future capital needs prioritize debt over equity; equity infusion to be mutually decided if needed
items.quote: There also, we have agreed upon going for debt as a priority and then it will be equity part. When it comes to equity part at that stage it can be de cided how it should be worked out . , but the priority will be debt first because company have balance sheet well to have more debt.

items.statement: Management control remains with Prahaladbhai Patel (CMD & CEO) for 5 years; board representation for Adani; HR/organizational strengthening to be discussed post-transaction
items.quote: We have clearly mentioned that the operational part 100% remains with PS Patel, being Managing Director, Chairman and CEO till today. As far as the management is concerned, they will have a Board access and there will be we have to represent the Board.

items.statement: Focus on buildings (residential, institutional, industrial), airports, data centres; precast technology adoption to accelerate delivery
items.quote: The whole intent is to have a partnership with our firm for buildings. Adani group has presence across Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Delhi. So , in all these three centres, we have to select, go partially and strengthen ourselves. Second part is the airport, that is also part of the building. Third part is data centre, that is also part of the building.

items.statement: Precast execution of 12 lakh sq ft in past year; targeting conversion of cast-in-situ projects to precast for faster delivery
items.quote: For Precast, we have done about 12 lakhs square feet of Precast in the past one year.

items.statement: Promoter sold stake at INR 575/share vs QIP at INR 670; strategic rationale prioritized long-term growth over valuation
items.quote: It was the situation where the company is getting a benefit for the longer period. And we found that this is a better win-win situation for futuristic orders and futuristic business.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance of INR3,300 crores including INR2,700 crores from core operations and INR600 crores from subsidiaries
items.quote: Our FY25 revenue guidance stands at INR3,300 crores which includes INR2,700 crores from our core operations and an additional INR600 crores from our subsidiaries which we acquired recently.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of INR6,300 crores with INR5,000 crores from parent and INR1,300 crores from subsidiaries
items.quote: Already we have given a blended of INR3,300 crores this year and FY26 is INR6,300 crores. So, INR1,300 crores from subsidiaries and INR5,000 from the parent companies.

items.statement: Monthly production volume guidance of 375-400 kgs by end of FY25, 550-600 kgs by FY26, and 750 kgs by FY27
items.quote: So, we are at 350 kgs per month run rate in H1 and we are having [inaudible] 375 kgs, 400 kgs per month till end of the year. And by FY27, we are expecting to go to 750 kgs per month.

items.statement: Targeting 7-8% gross margin and 5-5.5% EBITDA margin long-term, with PAT margin target of 3.5% for FY25 and 4% for FY26-27
items.quote: We aim to achieve 7% to 8% gross margin through an optimized product mix and export, while maintaining a long-term EBITDA margin of 5% to 5.5%. A key driver for PAT margin expansion will be reduced interest cost and we initiated utilization of gold-metal loans, which will have meaningfully impact on our interest costs moving forward.

items.statement: Next quarter blended revenue run rate of INR1,000 crores with INR700-750 crores from parent and INR150-350 crores from subsidiaries
items.quote: So, we are expecting a totally blended INR1,000 crores revenue in the next quarter, from the parent company INR700-INR750 crores what we are going by the run rate and from the subsidiary INR150 crores-INR350 crores.

items.statement: Raised INR270 crores for product portfolio expansion in 18 carat gold and diamond jewellery, capital infusion into subsidiaries Star Mangalsutra and Sparkling Chains
items.quote: Additionally, I am excited to announce a significant milestone in our company's journey as we have successfully raised INR270 crores. This investment will be strategically allocated across broadening our product portfolio with expanded offerings in 18 carat gold and diamond jewellery to align with evolving customer preferences.

items.statement: Monthly production volume averaged 345 kgs in Q2 FY25, up 38% YoY from 250 kgs; standalone capacity utilization at 46%, subsidiaries at 30-33%
items.quote: This quarter, our monthly production volume averaged 345 kgs, significantly from 250 kgs per month last year, making a robust 38% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Strong wedding season demand with 25% more weddings YoY, gold prices down 5% from 81,000 to 76,000 boosting demand
items.quote: 100% as all our client has given the outlook is very good for the wedding season as rates are also down by 5% of gold. Rates from 81,000, has come down to 76,000. So, it is helping to boost the season already.

items.statement: Increasing studded and 18 carat jewellery mix, planning Moissanite and lab-grown diamonds post March quarter
items.quote: Yes studded and 18 Carat we are increasing, and we have infused the amount for 18 Carat and Studded only. So, in this December quarter also you will see that our Studded and 18 Carat is increasing.

items.statement: Exports at 9% of sales in Q2, targeting 12-13% this year and 15% next year, focused on Middle East, UAE, Singapore, Malaysia
items.quote: So, we were at 1%-2% last year. Now we are at 9%-10%. So, we will be majorly in India only for 80%-85%. We will take export to 15% to 20% or 17%, 18% not more than that.

items.statement: Onboarded CaratLane (1-1.5% of revenue, 50-58 kg monthly volume potential) and PN Gadgil (INR50-100 crores sales potential), targeting Tanishq and mid-size corporates in Middle East
items.quote: CaratLane contributed some, some part came in this quarter, December quarter and some part came in that quarter. So, we initially started with them with some products. So, now we are supplying 1% or 1.5% of the revenue, but in these two, three quarters, we will grow with them.

items.statement: Working capital cycle at 75 days in Q2 FY25 vs 78-80 days in March 2024; receivable days increased due to high gold prices but expected to normalize
items.quote: So, we are at a total of working capital cycle of 75 days approximately

items.statement: Gold metal loan (GML) share increased from 10% to 20-25%, targeting 50-60% by December quarter and 80-85% by March quarter at 2.75-3% blended cost
items.quote: So,. we were last quarter at 10%. We have moved approximately to 20%-22%. So, this quarter, we are hardly trying because some banks have other policies. So, I think by December quarter, we will be at 50%-60%.

items.statement: Headcount increased from 500-550 at end FY24 to 650 at parent and 150-180 at subsidiaries (total 800); hired VP Sales Akash Talesara, targeting CFO and two board members
items.quote: So, by the end of 24, we were at 500 employees-550 employees now we are at 650 employees at Sky Gold parent company and subsidiary, we are at 150 employees to 180 employees in both the subsidiaries. So, together we are at 800 employees.

items.statement: Successfully raised INR270 crores via QIP for product expansion and subsidiary capital infusion
items.quote: Additionally, I am excited to announce a significant milestone in our company's journey as we have successfully raised INR270 crores.

items.statement: Gold price volatility risk mitigated through daily MCX hedging of inventory and GML positions; no unhedged exposure
items.quote: Yes. So, already our inventory is totally hedged in the MCX, which is available in India to hedge. So, our inventory is already hedged, and we hedge every sale and purchase on a daily basis in the hedging platform MCX.

items.statement: Export gross margins blended at 6-6.5-7%, domestic gross margin target 7-8% through optimized mix
items.quote: So, exports' gross margins are blended at 6%-6.5% or 7% also. So, blended it comes to 6.5% approximately.

items.statement: Actively pursuing acquisition opportunities to strengthen market position and accelerate growth
items.quote: Additionally, we are actively pursuing acquisition opportunities to further strengthen our market position and accelerate growth.

items.statement: Gold prices spiked 20-25% in two quarters, industry expects stability for 2-3 quarters before rising again
items.quote: So, already gold prices are spiked by 20%- 25%. So, industry is hoping that it will go stable for next two to three quarters, I think.

items.statement: Export policies improved significantly over 5-10 years, easy documentation and daily export metal availability
items.quote: Exports policies are very good in this government. There was very difficulty in the exports and all. Documentations are very high. The last 5 years to 10 years, exports is very easy to do.

items.statement: Digital app for B2B ordering on trial basis, expected to go live by December quarter for real-time inventory visualization and daily ordering
items.quote: So, app we have already started with the app, but it is on a trial basis. I think by December quarter, it will be live totally. So, it will help the purchase manager of the stores, the sales heads Sky Gold Limited November19, 2024 and all can visualize each and every verticals and products

items.statement: Targets 10% revenue increase in FY25 by deepening existing customer relationships, approaching new OEMs, developing new products and seeking technology partnerships in LED space
items.quote: To drive growth, we are targeting 10% revenue increase in financial year 2025 by deepening relationships with our existing customers, approaching new OEMs, developing new products and seeking strategic technology partnerships to venture further into LED space.

items.statement: Expects defence and power segment from SKL acquisition to generate INR15-22 crores revenue by year 2025
items.quote: We expect these segments to generate INR15 to INR22 crores revenue by year 2025.

items.statement: Targets consolidated revenue crossing INR100 crores within 2-3 years with good margins
items.quote: What we are targeting is our first target is to have a consolidate crossing INR100 crores in a couple of years.

items.statement: Expects consolidated EBITDA margin of 20-22% going forward
items.quote: Somewhere around 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 13.95%, H1 FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 14.95%
items.quote: For H1 FY25, we recorded a total income of INR22.49 crores with an EBITDA of INR3.36 crores and an improved EBITDA margin of 14.95%.

items.statement: Expects sustainable and very nice profit margin by year end FY25 after expense reduction measures
items.quote: So, I can see that the year end of '25 will have a sustainable and very nice profit margin.

items.statement: Automotive lamp segment anticipating 5-8% growth in FY25, with potential for double-digit growth once LED production starts
items.quote: Automotive lamps, we are anticipating a growth of around 5% to 8%. 8% in this year, and maybe once LED will start, then the growth will be more in double-digit.

items.statement: Expects defence revenue to be around 70% of current Uravi revenue by FY26
items.quote: If we consider FY26, then I am expecting defense in terms of revenue, will be around 70% of Uravi current revenue.

items.statement: Planning INR5-7 crores capex for SKL expansion including new land, building and products like alternators
items.quote: Somewhere around INR5 crores to INR7 crores.

items.statement: EV charger investment outlook depends on final product specifications and safety standards
items.quote: So that's what I'm telling. It depends upon the product. So if the product needs something which is totally automatic, then investment will be bigger.

items.statement: Developing T10 LED lamps for speedometer illumination, strengthening retrofit LED aftermarket presence, and developing EV components for two-wheelers
items.quote: Notably, we have created a prototype of T10 LED lamps for speedometer illumination and are working to strengthen our presence in the retrofit LED aftermarket segment as well.

items.statement: EV chargers technically developed but undergoing continuous testing due to evolving technology; definite timeline by January 2025
items.quote: So, definite timeline I think by January 25, I will be able to give you the definite timeline for the implementation and production or revenue generation of EV chargers in Uravi.

items.statement: Currently 95% OEM sales, 2.75% aftermarket, rest exports; targeting South American retail market breakthrough in coming months
items.quote: So, currently we are doing somewhere around 95% of OEM sales. We have about 2.75% of aftermarket and rest is export.

items.statement: SKL supplying power supply systems to defence ancillary units; leveraging automotive contacts to introduce SKL to Tata Motors and Ashok Leyland defence divisions
items.quote: So SKL acquisition will help Uravi in growing in terms of defense where we can supply our power supply systems to all defense Uravi Defence and ancillary units which are catering to government of India and our contacts in automotive will allow us to introduce SKL to companies like Tata Motors and Ashok Leyland for their Tata Advance and Ashok Leyland defense as

items.statement: Main business is two-wheeler lamps; four-wheelers mostly converted to LEDs with low consumption; focus on volume-driven two-wheeler segment
items.quote: Mainly our business is two-wheelers only. Four-wheelers are almost converted into LEDs and their consumption is very less.

items.statement: No specific government schemes currently apart from green energy projects; striving to be preferred partner for government defence organizations
items.quote: But currently we don't have any schemes in front of us apart from venturing into some green energy project, which we are not thinking at present.

items.statement: Exports currently 3-4% of business; strategically expanding into South America where Hero and Bajaj have manufacturing plants
items.quote: While exports and aftermarket segments currently contribute to 3% to 4% of our business, we see immense growth potential in these areas and are strategically expanding our reach into South America.

items.statement: Actively exploring overseas acquisitions to enhance technology growth in various segments
items.quote: Furthermore, we are actively exploring overseas acquisitions to enhance technology growth in various segments, aligning with our strategy for long-term growth and innovations.

items.statement: SKL staff retained 100%; Uravi management joined at marketing and administrative levels; SKL owner Mr. Bhatia continues technical leadership
items.quote: The staff of SKL is retained from 1% to 50%. Whatever is the person -- each and every staff is retained. Uravi has already joined management level.

items.statement: SKL consolidation from September 25 added only one week's profit (~INR4-4.5 lakhs); full consolidation impact from December 31
items.quote: Since the transaction happened on 25th of September, we could only add around INR4 lakh or INR4.5 lakh maybe numbers I am not sure, but one week's profit of SKL only.

items.statement: EV charger development delayed due to rapidly evolving technology and safety standards; multiple model revisions and testing cycles ongoing
items.quote: However, the EV market is yet to be very much mature in technological front. So, there are a couple of changes coming after every month and which we have to incorporate in our charger and again give for testing.

items.statement: Chinese and Philippine LED partnerships for supply chain and technology transfer; developing speedometer LED samples for OEMs; finished LED headlamps for aftermarket
items.quote: So strategically, what we have done is we have had an understanding with a company in China where we can have a supply chain of LEDs as a raw material and technology to produce a finished product in India and cater to Indian market.

items.statement: US module factory inauguration in February, commercial operations by end of January
items.quote: We are going to be inaugurating it sometime in February. We should be starting the commercial operations, I would say, fairly soon here by the end of January.

items.statement: 5.4 GW cell facility commercial operations by mid-December
items.quote: We should be having commercial operations commencing, I would say, middle of December.

items.statement: 6 GW integrated facility in Odisha commercial operations in FY27
items.quote: I would say we will start commercial operations somewhere in the FY27 time frame for the 6 gigawatt facility.

items.statement: Total module capacity 15 GW by end of FY25 (13.3 GW India + 1.6 GW US)
items.quote: In 2025, as we end the year, we will be having 13.3 gigawatts in India, 1.6 in the U.S., so that will make it a total of 15 gigawatts by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: India module capacity 21 GW and cell capacity 11 GW by end of FY27
items.quote: And by the end of financial year '27, in India, we will be having 21 gigawatts of module capacity and 11 gigawatts of cell capacity.

items.statement: Electrolyser manufacturing plan to be communicated in next two months
items.quote: Our electrolyser manufacturing plan is in advanced stages, and we should be in a position to communicate the same to you in the next two months' time.

items.statement: Cell facility capex ~INR2,400 crore completed; new capex initial spend ~INR300 crore
items.quote: So basically for the cell facility, we've almost completed our capex, which is about 2,400 crore and thereabouts. And for the new capex, which is ongoing, initial spends have been made for about INR300 crores.

items.statement: Board sanctioned INR600 crore for renewable power infrastructure (land and connectivity)
items.quote: Our Board has just sanctioned INR600 crores of investment for this particular foray, which we are going to use for connectivity and for bidding.

items.statement: Current 12 GW module capacity across India; Indosolar 1.3 GW started July; US 1.6 GW module facility near completion
items.value: 12 GW India, 1.3 GW Indosolar, 1.6 GW US
items.quote: we have 12 gigawatts of capacity presently that is distributed across India. The 12 gigawatts is in the Mumbai-Surat belt in Tumb, Nandigram, Chikhli, and Surat. Chikhli being the biggest for us. Indosolar, which is in Greater Noida, is 1.3 gigawatts of capacity. It started its operations in July this year and is ramping up very, very nicely as we speak. In the United States, we have 1.6 gigawatts

items.statement: 5.4 GW cell capacity in Chikhli commissioning; dry runs begun
items.quote: Solar cells, you know, the 5.4 gigawatts as we talked about, we are actually commissioning the cell facility at this point in time. Dry runs of the cells have begun.

items.statement: 6 GW integrated facility in Odisha: 595 acres allotted, 400 acres more soon, design contracts awarded, long-lead items negotiated
items.quote: We already have 595 acres of land allotted to us. Another 400 acres is being allotted very soon. From a design perspective, we are in advanced stages. The primary contracts related to design are already awarded, and the long-lead items are being negotiated as we speak.

items.statement: Future US capacity under evaluation: 3.4 GW additional module and potentially 5 GW cell
items.quote: For the U.S., we have future capacity in mind, 3.4 gigawatts of additional module capacity and potentially 5 gigawatts of cell capacity. All of this is under evaluation.

items.statement: Order book backed by advances; sticky loyal customers reduce cancellation risk
items.quote: The way in which we look at orders and consider them as orders in Waaree is if we get advances. So almost the entire 20 gigawatts of order book is backed by advances. That's number one. Number two, Prateekji, is that we most of our orders in this order book are through sticky customers, customers who are loyal to us.

items.statement: Order inflows 5-6 GW in H1 FY25
items.quote: So it's actually been fairly robust, about 6 gigawatts or so is what I would say, 5 to 6 gigawatts is what we have got in the first half.

items.statement: US module realizations fell from $0.28-0.30 to ~$0.24; India from ~$0.21 to ~$0.17
items.quote: Last year for the US, realizations were in the region of $0.28-$0.30. And this year they are kind of approaching towards somewhere around $0.24 or so. And for India, from around $0.21 or so, they are approaching to around $0.17-odd, ballpark numbers.

items.statement: Export mix dropped from ~60% to ~27%, impacting revenue and EBITDA growth; pricing also changed
